en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Salutations to the venerable Gurus. Salutations to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī.

[The fire perfected by one hundred thousand oblations (*lakṣāhuti*) is now described. The shadow of the serpent on the day; the worship of the preceptor and the seat (*pīṭha*); where is the fruit of the preliminary service (*puraścaraṇa*) for the sake of the seat? The sacrificial pavilion is to be prepared according to the sequence of days. Today and so forth—this is the introductory formula.

I, the sacrificer, of the Mānava gotra, Śrī-Śrī-Sumatijaya-jitāmitra-malla-varman, offer this flower-vessel for the purpose of the perpetual fire-sacrifice (*nitya-yajña*) performed according to the oblations (*yathā-huti*), preceded by the propitiation of my chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*). *Śrī-saṃvarta*: "May there be success in the commencement of the rite," and so forth. I offer the flower-vessel. [Offering of water to the Sun (*sūryārgha*): Nyāsa with the root mantra. Perform the four purificatory rites (*catuḥ-saṃskāra*).
Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Hrīṃ Huṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Namaḥ. Beholding.
Aiṁ (5) Khphreṁ Sakarasatrupramathani, Phaṭ to the weapon! [This is] the sprinkling.

Aiṁ (5) Khphreṁ! O you who destroy all sins, enemies, and adversaries, and shatter the afflictions; to the independent armor, Huṃ! [This is] the veiling. Aiṁ (5) Khphreṁ! O you who crush all enemies; to the weapon, Phaṭ! [This is] the striking.
Thus ends the preparation of the ground.

The ritual of casting out [obstacles] and so forth: *Ekā plakānagāle* | *Aiṃ (5) Khphreṃ Sakaraśatrupramathani Astrāye Phaṭ*. *Bali bhevatasa*. May the various forms of spirits (*bhūta*) dwelling in the divine realms, the atmosphere, and the depths of the underworld, perish by the command of Śiva!
Aiṃ (5) Khphreṃ, Phaṭ! To the weapon against all enemies. [Recite] from the southeast to the center for the limbs.
Aiṁ (5) Khphreṁ, obeisance to the heart of Paramahaṃsinī. One should perform this very mantra at every step.
Bhavatābali || The Six Limbs (Ṣaḍaṅga): *Astrāya hṛdayāya namaḥ* || *Astrāya śirase svāhā* ||

To the weapon, for the crest, vauṣaṭ. To the weapon, for the armor, hūṃ. To the weapon, for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ. To the weapon, for the weapon, phaṭ. The offering to the spirits (bhūtabali): O spirits of various forms, whether dwelling in the divine realms, the atmosphere, or the depths of the netherworld—by the command of Śiva, may you all depart!
The field offering.
Hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ kṣuṃ! O Lord of this very place, together with your beloved Mother, accept this bali offering! Svāhā! (2)
The offering to Vaṭuka.

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! Come, come, O Devīputra Vaṭukanātha, radiant with a mass of tawny matted hair, three-eyed, flame-mouthed one! Destroy all obstacles! Accept this bali offering along with all ritual services! Svāhā! (2x)
Gaṇabali: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Gaṃ, O Gaṇapati, together with your beloved consort, accept this bali! (2) Svāhā!
The offering to the Yoginīs: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! To all the Yoginīs, to all the sacred seats (pīṭhas), and to all the guardians of the fields (kṣetrapālas), Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!

The Bali offering to the group of Mothers (Mātṛgaṇabali): Aṃ, obeisance to Brahmāyaṇī. Kaṃ, obeisance to Māheśvarī. Caṃ, obeisance to Kaumārī. Ṭaṃ, obeisance to Vaiṣṇavī. Taṃ, obeisance to Vārāhī. Paṃ, obeisance to Indrāyaṇī.
And [the offering] to Amuṇḍā: *namaḥ*. To Śrī Mahālakṣmī: *namaḥ*. This is the *bali* for them.
Aśitāṅga and the others: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Aśitāṅgabhairava; Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Rurubhairava; Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍabhairava; Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Krodhabhairava.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Unmattabhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Kapālīśabhairava.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Bhīṣaṇabhairava.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Śahārabhairava. This is the bali offering for him.

Hetukādi: Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Hetuka Bhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Tripurāntaka Bhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Agnivetāla Bhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Agnijihva Bhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Kārākṣa Bhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Kalālīna Bhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Ekapāda Bhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Bhīmarūpa Bhairava.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Dāmarabhairavī. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Kūrmmapṛṣṭhabhairavī.
This is their offering.
Lokapāla || lūṃ, obeisance to Indra; rūṃ, obeisance to Agni; muṃ, obeisance to Yama.
KṢŪṂ, obeisance to the Rākṣasa; VŪṂ, obeisance to Varuṇa; YŪṂ, obeisance to the North-West (Vāyavya).
ŚŪṂ, obeisance to Kubera. HŪṂ, obeisance to Īśāna. AṂ, obeisance to Ardhacchandana.
Oṃ, homage to the one who bestows upward fragrance. To him, this offering (bali).
The offering for the sixty-four Yoginīs.
Aiṃ (5). Jayā and Vijayā, Jayantī and Aparājitā, Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Bhīmā, and Kalā—thus is the group of eight.
Diviyoginī, Mahāyoginī, Siddhiyoginī, Gaṇeśvarī, Sākiṇī,
Kālarātrī, Ūrdhvakeśī, and Niśākarī.
Gambhīrā, Ghoṣaṇī, Sthūlā, Pavanāgī,
Ulomikā, Bhīṣaṇā, Mahānandā, and likewise Jvālāmukhī.
Piśācī, Hastinī, Jakṣaṇī, and likewise Dhūrjaṭī;
Viṣabhakṣī, Sarvasiddhi, Tuṣṭi, and likewise Icchā.
Hūṃkārī, Bhāsvarī, Dīrghā, Dhūmrākṣī, Kalahapriyā,
Mātaṅgī, Kākadṛṣṭī, as well as Tripurā and Antakī.
The Rākṣasī Ghoranādā, Raktāṅgī, Viśvarūpiṇī,
Jayaṃkarī, Vibhañcī, Suskāṅgī, and Narabhojanī.
Vīrabhadra, Mahākālī, Kaṅkālī, Vikṛtānanā, Krodhalā, Bhīmabhadra, Vāyuvegā, and Bhayānanā.
Brāhmī, Vaiṣṇavī, Raudrī, Carcikā, Īśvarī,
as well as Vārāhī, Nārasiṃhī, and Śivādūtī as the sixth.
May these goddesses always accept this offering from me in the great fire.
Hrīṃ! O sixty-four Yoginīs, accept this bali offering (2)! Grant all peace; may you bring me accomplishment, Hūṃ (3) Phaṭ (2) Svāhā!
The offering to the jar and so forth.
Aiṃ (5): Ajara, Apakumbha, Iḍācāra, as well as Indramūrti, Ulkāsya, Ūṣmāṇḍa, and Ṛpusūdala.
Ṛmukta, Ḷktakāya, Ḹlāpādaika, Draṣṭaka,
Airāvata, Oḍyāmba, and Auṣadhīśa are likewise in front.
Antaka, Arthabāhu, Kamala, Kharānana,
Gomukha, Ghaṇṭārava, Ṅanaṇa, and Caṇḍadhāraka.
Chatātoṣa, the one called Jaṭāra, Ṛṃkāla, Bhaṭeśvara,
Ṭaṅkapāṇi, and another, as well as Ṭhānusvāḍambha and Ḍāmara.
Then Ṭaḍṛkarṇa, Oṇaṭīkrānta, Tadibha, Virasta, Danturodhana, and Caṇḍavān among the Nāgakarṇas likewise departed.
Phetkāra, Vīrasiṃha, Bhṛkuṭī, Meghavāsura,
Yugānta, Raurava, Lamboṣṭha, and likewise Vatsala.
Śukatuṇḍa, Ṣaḍālāsya, Sunāsa, Hūhuka,
and Kṣayāntaka— these are declared to be the fifty Kṣetrapālas.
In the extraction of the fifty letters, the Kṣetrapālas reside in their respective locations;
those devoid of the remaining letters are the fourteen Kṣetrapālas.
In a solitary liṅga there is the syllable HŪṂ, and in the cremation ground is the terrifying one;
Mahālakṣmī dwells in the dreadful forest, and Jvālāmukha always resides there.
On a single tree or a banyan tree, Viḍālavadana shall dwell;
in a cave resounding with the ringing of bells, Padmakhaṇḍa shall dwell, clothed in water.
At Saṅgama he is Bhūridhāraugha; likewise at Parvata he is Marut;
at Nirjhara he is Śravaṇipravāha; and at Nidhāna he is Maṇibhadraka.
One should know him as the Lord of Wealth in the field of flavors, as a jackal in the sacrificial enclosures,
as a forest-dweller in the wilderness, and he is remembered as a honey-bee in the garden.
The sixty-four Mahāvīryas remain protecting the world;
one should always offer oblations and worship in that sacred field.
There, four types of guardians—beginning with the twice-born—receive the offering:
those dwelling on the earth, those moving through the air, those residing in trees, and birds, all seeking their respective shares of the oblation according to their conduct.
The four [classes] have perpetual entitlement; other people are merely meat-eaters.
They were dark-brown with tawny hair, tawny skin, and tawny eyes;
they were extremely fierce, with terrifying fangs, and resplendent with ornaments of skulls.
With Kāśmīra saffron, sandalwood, musk, fish, and Phalguṣa;
with flowers, garments, umbrellas, lamps, and guggulu incense.
By the ancient ones who have cultivated their selves and are devoted to the sequential worship,
she— who always grants desires— is propitiated with the sounding of bells, music, songs, and other offerings.

(5) Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, descend [Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ], for [Name]! O Kṣetrapāla, resplendent with a mass of tawny matted hair, three-eyed, flame-mouthed, accept this offering of fragrance and flowers, this worship with oblations! In the form of Bhairava, *turu* (2), *muru* (2), *kha* (2), *la* (2), *pheṃ pheṃ phaḥ*, to the Lord of the Great Ḍāmara, svāhā!
By reciting this mantra and offering oblations (bali) for all according to the prescribed rule,
there shall be no famine there, nor any fear from calamities and the like.
A king who is ever-joyful shall become beloved by all;
he obtains his desired objects and is always victorious in battle.
Thus concludes the bali offering for the fields beginning with Ajara.
Now follows the rite of the propitiatory offering (śāntibali).

Aiṃ! (5) O Brahman, drink the fragments of the cosmic egg; drink the blood that flows like an ever-increasing river from Sindhu; let the mountain of falling flesh of the bound soul be filled with black and red;
O destroyer of sleep within the thunderbolt, make it a grain; O Mother of the Mountain, O Śambhu, remain!
May she, whose command was saluted by the young brahmins when she herself desired to fashion the circle of goddesses, purify us.
Whether above the cosmic egg, in heaven, in the expanse of the sky, on the surface of the earth, in the void,
in the netherworld (pātāla), in fire, or in water— wherever situated,
or in sacred fields (kṣetra), seats (pīṭha), and secondary seats (upapīṭha)— the Goddesses, having established their presence there, are pleased by offerings such as flowers and incense.
May those who are worthy of worship by the lords of heroes protect us always with the rite of the auspicious offering.
And for the sake of accomplishing what is to be accomplished, accept all these offerings of liquor and flesh; grant me peace! HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. Peace-offering (*śāntibali*).
The Field Root Mantra. Three *añjali* gestures (3). The great offering for Tvaṣṭṛ. The mudrās for invocation and so forth. Incense and lamp. Recitation (*jāpa*). Praise: Śrī Saṃvartā.

In the east, south, west, and north are the auspicious goddesses; in the east and so forth, the lords of the fields (kṣetrapālas) are Vaṭu, Bhūta, Durgā, Anila, and Herambanātha. In the cremation ground (śmaśāna) is the omnipresent Lord, the primordial god of the gods, who removes the torment of grief.
The ritual procedure for worship with offerings such as bali consists of eternal bliss and bestows joy and happiness.
Herein are: the offering of fragrance and so forth, the libation (tarpaṇa), the dismissal (visarjana), the inhalation and exhalation, and the cleansing of the hands.
Now follows the worship of the bali-vessel.

Beginning with "adyādi": offering to the Sun (sūryārgha); salutation to the Gurus; ritual placement (nyāsa); worship of the water vessel and the arghya vessel; purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) and self-worship (ātmapūjā); invocation and other rites for Śrī Saṃvartānā; the three deities (trideva); the Yoginīs; their respective mudrās; and the worship of the root text (mūlapāṭa) at Kvaccha.
Three *añjali* gestures (3). The root nine-syllable mantra does not have three *añjali* gestures.

Now, the worship of the pitcher (*kalaśārccana*); salutation to the Guru; the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of Mṛtyujaya; worship of the water vessel and the *argha* vessel; purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*); self-worship; [the recitation of] "Ādhāraśakti," and so forth. (8)
Meditative absorption.
Three-eyed, six-armed, and peaceful, adorned with matted locks and the crescent moon, white in complexion, holding a skull-cup in his hand, and seated upon a yogic posture.
Rudra is clothed in a tiger skin, adorned with a great serpent as a necklace,
and holds a trident and a rosary in his right hands.
One should fashion the god Mṛtyuñjaya, the destroyer of death and disease, with two hands holding a skull-bowl, a water-pot, and the yoga-mudrā.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, homage to Mṛtyujaya, whose form bestows the fulfillment of all desires. (3) || The offering (bali).

Oṃ, salutations to Brahmā. Salutations to Viṣṇu. Salutations to Rudra. Salutations to Sadāśiva. Salutations to Īśvara. Salutations to the seven oceans beginning with the Gaṅgā. Salutations to the fortnights. Salutations to the months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa. Salutations to the seasons. Salutations to the year. Salutations to the seven oceans beginning with the salt ocean (kṣāra). Salutations to the lunar days (tithis) beginning with Nandā. Salutations to the asterisms (nakṣatras) beginning with Aśvinī. Salutations to the astrological conjunctions (yogas) beginning with Viṣkambha.

Homage to the Muhūrtas. Homage to the nine planets beginning with Āditya. Homage to the twelve zodiac signs beginning with Meṣa. Homage to the seven sages beginning with Vasiṣṭha. Homage to those who have lost their positions and whose long lives have ended. Homage to the ten world-protectors beginning with Indra.

Salutation to the eight *kula*-nāgas beginning with Ananta. Salutation to the sandals of the goddess Śrī Rudracaṇḍā, [beginning with] Rudracaṇḍā. (8) Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ. Salutation to the form that bestows complete fulfillment. Bali.
Three handfuls of joined palms.

Aiṁ (5) HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ. Obeisance to the Great Army of the Kula-tree, to the Deluder, to the Śakala-tīrtha, to the Mantra-deities, to the Kalās, to the Tattvas, and to the Lord of Tattvas; to the essence of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra; to the Tattva of Vidyā-Śiva; HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ. Obeisance to the venerable Form of the Full Jar. *Offering of Bali* *Six-limbed Nyāsa* *HNASAKANAH* Obeisance to Śrī. *Siddhramuṅa* Obeisance to Lakṣmī. *Invocation and other rites* *Dhenumudrā* *Earth-drum* *Rice grains* *Dūrvā grass* *Cow dung* *One [recitation]*
Plakā || These are the offerings. With the Astra mantra. Then the bali offering. Recitation: Oṃ juṃ saḥ svāhā. (10)
Hymn of Praise.

I take refuge in You alone, that primordial god known as Mṛtyuñjaya, the Bhairava whom the chief guardians of the worlds of the gods, led by Brahmā, have bowed to and praised with oblations and water.
Here [are] the scents and so forth. Thus ends the worship of the vase.

The Worship of Gaṇa by Godajāsa. *Oṃ namo mūśāsanāya* (Salutation to the one whose vehicle is a rat). Three *añjali*s (three times with palms joined). *gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaṃ* salutation to Kulagaṇeśvara. *Balidāna* (offering of food). Incense (*dhūpa*). Lamp (*dīpa*). Recitation (*jāpa*). *glauṃ svāhā*. (Ten times). Hymn (*stotra*): "With thick vermilion... and so forth. Here, [offer] sandalwood paste (*gandha*) and other items.
Now follows the worship with morsels of cow-food (gogrāsapūjā).

Oṃ, homage to Nandā. Oṃ, homage to Subhadrā. Oṃ, homage to Subhīmā. Oṃ, homage to Suśīrā. Oṃ, homage to Sumanoharā. [Offer] the *stotra*, the *bali*, incense, and lamps. [Recite] the *stotra* twice, and perform the mantra recitation (*jāpa*).
Hymn of Praise.
Salutation to the five mothers of the cow: Nandā, Subhadrā, Surabhi, Suśīlā, and Sumanoharā; may this pure offering lead to the destruction of sins.
In this case, there is fragrance and so forth.
Now follows the worship of the maiden (kumārī-pūjā).
Salutation to Mayūrāsanā. Caṃ cha jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ kmlvryūṃ caṃ. O Komaṛī, [this is] the sandals for Caṇḍabhairava. (3) Bali. Six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga). Incense and lamp. Kmlvryūṃ svāhā. (10)
Hymn: "O Child-nature," and so forth. Herein [are mentioned] perfumes and the like.

Now, the worship with the *sagona* [offering]. Three *añjali*s. Having cast three *añjali*s with the root nine-syllable mantra (*navākṣarī*). Śrī (3) to the western direction of Dumāju. Śrī (3) to the northern direction of Tareju. Cāśvara: 2. Trideva: Aiṃ (5) Caṃ Chaṃ Jaṃ Jhaṃ Ñaṃ KMLVRYŪṂ Śrī-Komārī Vicce Pādukāṃ. 3. Bali. Hṛdaya and so forth. Root mantra. The syllables Sa and Ha. The great *tvāka*-bali. Āvāhana and so forth. Their respective mudrās.

Nāśvara || 3 || Trideva || Oṃ hūṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ, to Nṛtyeśvara Mahābhairava, together with the power Śkṣmlvryīṃ Nṛtyalakṣmī, [I offer] the sandals. || 3 || Bali || Hṛdayādi || The great bali for Tvaṅka. Āvāhanādi || Their respective mudrās. Tu-paraju || 4 || Trideva || Aiṃ (5) Śrī(-), in the great primordial seat, the great field of Meru, in the house of Kauri, hskhphreṃ Kubjikā, hskṣmlvryūṃ, to the Lord Ambā, the Sovereign of the Glorious Wheel of the Family (Śrīkulacakreśvarī), [I offer] the sandals. || 3 ||

Bali. Aiṃ (5) Śrī-Anādimahāpīṭhi, in the great field of Meru, in the house of Kauri, HSKHPHRĪṂ KUBJIKE ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ, the sandals of the Mother, the venerable Kulacakreśvarī. 3. Bali. [Offerings to] the heart and other limbs. The great bali for Tvaṅka. Invocation and so forth.
Their respective mudrās.

Thānalaṃkhu || 5 || Trideva || Aiṃ (5) Thrauṃ: [I offer] the stone lamp, the goddess Daṃbhakī, and the great darkness; the *pādukā* of the field-protector || 3 || Bali || Hṛdaya and others || The great *tvāka*-bali || Invocation and others || The *tarjjanī*-mudrā.
O King’s messenger! O Triple-god!

Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ Kaṃrakeśvara Karaṅkabhairavīśvarī, homage! (3) Bali. [Recite] the Heart-mantra and so forth. The great *tvāka*-bali. [Perform] the invocation and so forth with their respective mudrās. Vaccharā Devī. (7) The three deities. With the root mantra of the western direction, (3) nine times. Bali. [Recite] the Heart-mantra and so forth. The great *tvāka*-bali. [Perform] the invocation and so forth with their respective mudrās.

Mūlapāta || 1 || Aśitāṅga and others || 8 || Aiṃ (5) Ṭaṃ Ṭhaṃ Ḍaṃ Ḍhaṃ Ṇaṃ KMLVRYŪṂ Śrīvaiṣṇavī Vicce Pādukāṃ || 3 || Bali. Hṛdaya and others. Tāvaka-mahābali. Āvāhana and others. Thavathava-samudrā. Incense. Lamp. Food offering. Recitation. The Three Deities. VMLVRYŪṂ.

Svāhā! HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ SVĀHĀ! HSKHPHRŪṂ ŚKHPHRĪṂ SVĀHĀ! THRAUṂ SVĀHĀ! HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ SVĀHĀ! HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ SVĀHĀ! [This is] the nine-syllable mantra. KMLVRYŪṂ SVĀHĀ! (108 times). The hymn: I always revere her who has an unbroken circle, the illustrious Saṃvartā, in the state of the day, as the sixfold one, dark-blue and red, bearing Brahmā and Tārā upon her seat in the center; she who has the luster of smoke and blazing eyes.

Dark-red in color; fully blossomed; Vaiṣṇavī, the illusory power (māyā) of Viṣṇu; facing the east-south; as in the [mantra] beginning with "vānati" and so forth; the statement; here [are offered] perfumes and so forth; the libation (tarpaṇa); [the mantra] beginning with "pitṛ-preta" and so forth.
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the offering of bali.
Beginning with "adyādi": the offering to the Sun (sūryārgha), the worship of the Preceptor (ācāryapūjā), the rite for peace (śāntika), and the book (pustikā).

Then, according to the ritual action: the inspection of the site and so forth; the four purificatory rites (*catuḥ-saṃskāra*); the cleansing and so forth; the *cāṅgyāya*; from the beginning, middle, and end of the fire and other elements; with the *thvacā* offering at the crossroads; the worship of the six limbs (*ṣaḍ-aṅga-pūjā*) of Aghora using the root mantra; and the invocation (*āvāhana*) and subsequent rites.
The Dhenu Mudrā.

The weapon-mantra is for the purpose of protection; the mantra of the feet is for the purpose of worship and for subduing spirits such as ghosts and dogs; the heart-mantra itself is for eating and drinking; and the navel-mantra is for rising.

Again: Kāpapa (12), duhācake ku (8)—these are the primary [syllables]. Duṃthukāya pu (4), duhācake ku (10). Musi calakumārako duhācake ku (14). Thaṃ vahmāgva (1), duhācake ku (8). Tiṃ, su, luḍa, sarakhi, nibuja—these are to be written on the neck of the *kalaśa*. [Then perform] the purification with water and so forth, the bathing with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*), and the sprinkling with the water from the *argha* vessel.

The Fourfold Rite (*catusaṃskāra*): (5) *Aiṃ oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ*. *Inspection* (*nirikṣaṇa*): *Khphreṃ sakalashatrupramathani astrāya phaṭ*. *Sprinkling* (*prokṣaṇa*): (5) *Aiṃ oṃ khphreṃ sakaladuritārita kleśadalani svatantra kavacāya hūṃ*. *Veiling* (*avaguṇṭhana*): (5) *Khphreṃ sakalashatrupramathani astrāya phaṭ*. *Striking* (*tāḍana*): [Perform] with the three principles (*tritatva*) and the root mantra (*mūlamantra*). [Then] with the *sodharapa* [mantra].
Oṃ hrāṃ, to the reality of the self, svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ, to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva), svāhā! Oṃ hrūṃ, to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva), svāhā!
Worship: Pithukāpa. Oṃ, homage to Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand and is presided over by the sun.
Salutation to Agni, who holds a spear in his hand and is replete with splendor and radiance.
Salutation to Muṃjamāyā, who holds a staff in her hand and is possessed by a preta.
KṢŪṂ! Salutation to Nairṛtya, who holds a sword in his hand and is mounted upon a rohit deer.
Vūṃ, salutation to Varuṇa, who holds a noose in his hand and is the lord of the waters.
Oṃ, salutation to Vāyu in the southwest, who holds a banner in his hand and presides over the wind.
Obeisance to Suṃkubera, who holds a mace in her hand and possesses the wealth of the giver of riches.
Hūṃ! Homage to Īśāna, who has the sun in his hand, the presiding lord of spirits.
Oṃ, homage to Anantā, who holds a wheel in her hand and has a nāga as her mount.
Oṃ, homage to Brahmā, who holds a lotus in his hand and presides over heaven.

Guṃ, salutation to the Gurus. Gaṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati. Saṃ, salutation to the Satya-yuga. Taṃ, salutation to the Tretā-yuga. Droṃ, salutation to the Dvāpara-yuga. Kaṃ, salutation to the Kali-yuga. Ja-vaca-laku, salutation to Brahmā.
Oṃ khavacalaku Viṣṇave namaḥ. Thaṃ Camā Sadāśivāya namaḥ. Mūṇisa Oṃ Hrāṃ Rāśyai namaḥ. Oṃ Hrāṃ Aśitāṅgabhairavāya namaḥ.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Rurubhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Candrabhairava.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Krodhabhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Unmattabhairava.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Kapāliśabhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Bhīṣaṇabhairava.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Śaṃhārabhairava.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Hetuka Bhairava.
Salutation to Tripurāntakabhairava. Salutation to Agnivetālabhairava.
Salutation to Agnijihvābhairava. Salutation to Kārākṣabhairava.
Salutation to Kalālinabhairava. Salutation to Ekapādabhairava.
Homage to Bhīmarūpa-bhairava. Homage to Dāmara-bhairava.
Salutation to Bhairava of the Tortoise-back.
Ṭi || Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the Nakṣatra. Lu ra || Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the Nāga. Ṭirajasu || Oṃ hrāṃ.

Homage to all the gods. [Offer] incense and lamps. Having sounded these [instruments], one should perform the *kāpaya* and *tāghāra* with the *sakara*. To the north of the fire-altar (*āgnyesya*), at a distance of one *lukkoṭa* and three *ohākoṭa*, there are one hundred and eight pillars. Oṃ, homage to the one seated upon the elephant (*gajāsanāya*). To the divine fire-essence (*suragnasasvāye*), to the auspicious Śiva who is the pillar of the *sāla* tree. Oṃ Hrāṃ Luṃ, I establish the pillar of Indra (*indrastambhaṃ*). Homage to the one seated upon the goat (*chāgāsanāya*). Oṃ Hrāṃ Ruṃ, I establish the pillar of Agni (*agnistambhaṃ*). Homage to the one seated upon the lotus (*padmāsanāya*).

Oṃ hrāṃ guṃ, I establish the pillar of the Guru. Homage to the one seated upon the buffalo. Oṃ hrāṃ muṃ, I establish the pillar of Yama. Homage to the one seated upon the corpse. Oṃ hrāṃ kṣuṃ, I establish the pillar of Nairṛtya.
Salutation to the one seated upon Garuḍa. Oṃ hrāṃ aṃ, I establish the pillar of non-destruction.
Homage to Mukarāsanā. Oṃ hrāṃ vaṃ, I plant the pillar of Varuṇa.
Homage to Mṛgāsana! Oṃ hrāṃ yaṃ, I establish the pillar of Vāyu. Homage to Mūsāsana! Oṃ hrāṃ, I establish the pillar of Gaṇapati. Homage to Hayāsana!
Oṃ hrāṃ suṃ, I plant the pillar of Kubera. Homage to the one seated upon a bull.
Oṃ hrāṃ hūṃ, I plant the pillar of Īśāna.
Homage to the one seated upon a swan. Oṃ hrāṃ, I plant the Brahmā-stambha.
This is the opening of all those.
Duthokāpayā || Agni || Homage to the one seated upon Garuḍa || Oṃ hrāṃ laṃ, I plant the pillar of Sadyojāta.
Nairṛtya: Homage to the one seated upon a bull. Oṃ hrāṃ vaṃ, I plant the pillar of Vāmadeva.
Vāyavya: Homage to Savāsanā. Oṃ hrāṃ raṃ, I plant the pillar of Aghora.
Īśāna. Homage to the one seated upon a swan. Oṃ hrāṃ yaṃ, I plant the pillar of Tatpuruṣa.
The offering of the *suṅā* and *kvamana*. The *balidvaṇḍuṣa*: Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Indra; Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Rudra. The *bali* and *dvaṇḍuṣa*: Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Hetuka Kṣetrapāla. Incense and lamp.
In this case, there is fragrance and so forth.

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Agni. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Īśvarī. Bali offering. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Tripurāntaka-kṣetrapāla. To the west of the southeast [direction]. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Guru. Bali offering. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Aśitāṅga-bhairava. To the east of the southwest [direction]. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Yama. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Nīrā. Bali offering. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Agnivetāla-kṣetrapāla. To the southwest. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Nairṛti. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Ugrā. Bali offering.

Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Agnijihva Kṣetrapāla. [In the] north-west and north. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Ananta. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Paśupati. [Offer] bali. Oṃ, homage to Rurubhairava. [In the] north-west and south. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Varuṇa. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Śiva. [Offer] bali. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Kālākṣa Kṣetrapāla. [In the] north-west. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Vāyu. Homage to Sthāṇu. [Offer] bali.

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Kālarūpa Kṣetrapāla. [He is] to the east of Vāyu (the northwest). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Maheśvara. [Offer] the bali. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Candabhairava. [He is] to the west of Īśāna (the northeast).
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Kubelā. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Mahādeva. Bali offering.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Ekapādakṣetrapāla in the northeast. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Īśāna in the northeast.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the deity! Balya offering! Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Bhīmarūpa Kṣetrapāla!

To the south of Īśāna: Oṃ, obeisance to Brahmā. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Śaṅkara. Bali. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Krodhabhairava. [Offer] these with the *pidhvaya* [mudrā]. With the *duṃthu* [mudrā]: Agni. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Kṛtayuga. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sadyojāta. Bali. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Unmattabhairava. Nairṛtya. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Tretāyuga. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vāmadeva. Bali.

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Kapālīśabhairava. [In the] Vāyavya [direction]. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Dvāpara Yuga. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Aghora. [Offer] the bali. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Bhīṣaṇabhairava. [In the] Īśāna [direction]. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Kṛta Yuga. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa.

Bali: Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Śaṃhārabhairava. Incense and lamp. Here, the offering of fragrance and so forth. This is the procedure for the *kāpāsvāya*. Then, the worship of the *camā*, *java*, *khava*, and *calaku* according to the rules as before. At the mandapa, [one should perform] the ritual of the honey-drinking for the sake of non-violence (*ahiṃsā*). The covering of the *vokaṇa*. The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) and the *vocaṇa*. The consecration of the jars (*kalaśābhiṣeka*) for the patron (*yajamāna*) and the dog-eaters (*svānakokā*). The waving of the incense (*dhūpa*) according to the rite. This is the procedure for the mandapa.

Then, following the sequence of days: the ritual for the placement of the feet of the fire-pit (*agnikuṇḍa*) is as before. The worship of the vase (*kalaśa*): [in] the forest of the vase-row, [and] at the three [spots] beginning with *kaṃca*, *atapā*, and *trākhi*, [one places] five jewels (*pañcaratna*) [with the seed-syllables] *kaṃ* (5), *pho* (12), *pu* (36), *kākhiṣota*, *mālako*, *vāsura*, *nyāmuṃgala*, *bali*, *hāmala*, *mvāca*, *māḍhe*, *se*, *kṣirajā*, *ke*, *kuḍa*. Worship with the weapon-mantra (*astra*). Incense, lamp, recitation (*jāpa*), and praise.
In the work of digging the earth, you take the form of a golden spade.
Salutations always to Viśvakarman’s weapon, to the one whose form is the divine missile.
Worship of the Preceptor. One should recite the *śāntika* [hymn]. The dismissal of the weapon-mantra and the curtain.

The purification of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) through sprinkling and other rites; the protection of the lamp; the fourfold consecration (*catuḥ-saṃskāra*) of the ground; for the purpose of adorning the nose with unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*); *Oṃ pṛthivyai namaḥ*; scattering [the grains]; according to the ritual procedure starting from the southeast (*āgneya*); the placement of the hand-seals (*mudrā*); the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*).
Oṃ! May the Nāgas and the World-Protectors who grant desires enter the surface of the earth;
may they always remain in this sacrificial pit, bestowing long life and portions of strength.

Oṃ śūṃ vūṃ hrīṃ svāhā || Tāḍa (8) || For the purpose of the ritual procedure and for causing [the deity] to descend. [One should worship] Korthapati and Padmacoya; likewise, Malātasa and Maṇḍalacoya. One should offer the bali-oblation starting from the southeast (āgneya): Oṃ agnaye eya balir nnamaḥ. Likewise in the southwest (nairṛtya), the northwest (vāyavya), and the northeast (īśāna). [Then follow] the ritual placement (nyāsa) and so forth, and the thread-worship (sūtrapūjā): Oṃ śriyai namaḥ | Oṃ yaśovatyai namaḥ | Oṃ kāntāyai namaḥ | Oṃ supriyāyai namaḥ | Oṃ vimalāyai namaḥ.
Oṃ, obeisance to Śivā. Oṃ, obeisance to Śuśobhā. Oṃ, obeisance to Bhānukī. Oṃ, obeisance to Cetā. This is the Vaṃhāva-sūtra.

Oṃ, homage to Dhanyā. Oṃ, homage to Dhanyā. Oṃ, homage to Viśālā. Oṃ, homage to Sthirā. Oṃ, homage to Rūtā. Oṃ, homage to Gadā. Oṃ, homage to Niśā. Oṃ, homage to Vidrumā. Oṃ, homage to Vibhavī. These are the Yaṃhāsūtras.
Having placed all these [offerings] in their respective positions for the purpose of worship: Oṃ, obeisance to Vāstupuruṣa.
Center: Oṃ, obeisance to Brahmā. Oṃ, this offering (bali) is for Brahmā; obeisance. Thus.

East: Oṃ, salutation to Amarīci. Likewise [for the others]. South: West: North: Oṃ, this one to Vivasvat; Oṃ, this one to Mitra; Oṃ, this one to Mahīdhara. Below the fire: Oṃ, this one to Savitṛ; Oṃ, this one to Sāvitrī; Oṃ, this one to Indrāṇī; Oṃ, this one to Āpa; Oṃ, this one to Āpavatsā.

From Īśāna to the end of the North: Oṃ, obeisance to Īśānā. Oṃ, obeisance to Parjanyā. Oṃ, obeisance to Jayā. Oṃ, obeisance to Indrā. Oṃ, obeisance to Ādityā. Oṃ, obeisance to Satyā. Oṃ, obeisance to Bhṛśā. Oṃ, obeisance to Antarikṣā. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni. Oṃ, obeisance to Pūṣā. Oṃ, obeisance to Vitathā. Oṃ, obeisance to Aṅgā. Oṃ, obeisance to Yamā. Oṃ, obeisance to Gandharvā. Oṃ, obeisance to Bhṛṅgā. Oṃ, obeisance to Mṛgā. Oṃ, obeisance to Nairṛtyā.

Oṃ, salutation to Nandinī. Oṃ, salutation to Sugrīvā. Oṃ, salutation to Puṣpadantā. Oṃ, salutation to Varuṇā. Oṃ, salutation to Śukrā. Oṃ, salutation to Ketavī. Oṃ, salutation to Śaniścarā. Oṃ, salutation to Vāyavī. Oṃ, salutation to Nāgā. Oṃ, salutation to Bṛhaspatī. Oṃ, salutation to Kuberā. Oṃ, salutation to Somā. Oṃ, salutation to Vaidyā. Oṃ, salutation to Diti. Oṃ, salutation to Aditi.
In that place as well, from the east to the northeast.
Oṃ, homage to Kandā. Oṃ, homage to Vidā. Oṃ, homage to Aryyastī. Oṃ, homage to Putanā.
Oṃ, homage to Jambhakā! Oṃ, homage to Pāparākṣasī! Oṃ, homage to Pilapicchā! Oṃ, homage to Carakī! [This concludes] the incense, lamp, recitation, and praise.
The body consists of sixty-four cavities, all of which are present within the form of the body;
the armpits are hollow, and it is endowed with an equal number of all the joints.
O Maheśāna, bestow upon me a plot of land for the purpose of establishing the sacrificial pit; I bow to you here in this rite, who possess the form of the Vāstu deity.
Here [are the offerings] of fragrance and so forth. The worship of Bālā. To Kulihla. To the Yakṣa who wields the weapon of the noose. The mantra.
Even if she causes [the earth] to be dug with spades or even with hundreds of millions of pegs,
let the goddess Earth be forgiven for the purpose of establishing the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa).
One should recite the words of benediction.
May Vighnī always grant well-being, and may Mārtaṇḍa likewise grant well-being;
may all the Yoginīs grant well-being, as well as Svastipīṭhā and her own constellation.
In the east, south, west, north, and likewise in the upper half,
there is the six-limbed Svasti, both hidden and manifest as the deity;
Bhairava and Bhairavī with their limbs, Svasti, Svaḥ, Svaḥ, and the various wheels (cakras).
Their own mantras, their own mudrās, and their own weapons are their retinues.
Established in the planets, lunar mansions, and zodiac signs, may she grant well-being and the attainment of all wealth.
May there be well-being from Vīrā, Amairā, the two Yoginīs, and Gaṇanāyaka;
may there be constant well-being from the Goddess, the Supreme Goddess, and the King of Mantras.
The ancestral deities of the family and the household fire are satisfied by the offerings of oblations; may they grant well-being.
May there be well-being for the King; may there be well-being for the sacrificer at all times.
In a vessel made of gourd or wood, or on a leaf of the *balisa* tree, perform the recitation (*japa*) of the Aghora mantra according to one's ability.

Wiping and so forth. [Then] the removal of the eight obstacles (*aṣṭapāpa*), the offering of water for the feet (*pādya*), the offering of water for the face (*ācamana*), the offering of shade (*chāyā*), the bath (*snāna*), the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*), the four purificatory rites (*catuḥ-saṃskāra*), the eight obstacles, *gorocana*, consciousness (*cetana*), the reversal [of obstacles], and the *svasti-vācana*. Worship: *Oṃ nandāyai namaḥ* | *Oṃ bhadrāyai namaḥ* | *Oṃ jayāyai namaḥ* | *Oṃ riktāyai namaḥ* | *Oṃ pūrṇāyai namaḥ*. Incense and so forth; here, fragrance and so forth. Dismissal of the eight obstacles. Worship of the ritual action (*vidhi-karmāpūjā*). The lineage of the masters (*vaṃśūri-aṭaviya*).

In the eastern corner of the sacrificial hall (*yajña-śālā*), having prepared a *svastika* diagram, one should worship the five jewels (*pañcaratna*) upon a grinding stone (*lupala*) or a flat slab (*ohopala*). Then, in the eight directions starting from the southeast (*āgneya*), one performs worship. [One worships] Nanda and the others (the five deities) in the [five] directions, and in the center, with the root-mantra (*mūla-mantra*) and the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*) and so forth, as well as incense (*dhūpa*) and other offerings. Here, one offers perfumes (*gandha*) and the rest.
In the Sthirahāra [treatise], from today onwards...
Oṃ Hrāṃ! May the sacrificial rites be free from obstacles; may there be auspiciousness in the preparation of the fire-pits (kuṇḍas).
As long as the work to be done has not been completed, remain steadfast.
One should recite the words of benediction.

The pouring of the *ādīnaka* water-pot; the offering of the *dānaka* flowers; the *bali* offering; the *hiṃsā* offering; the consecration of the food (*anna-saṃkalpa*); the giving of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā-dāna*); the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) of the patron (*yajamāna*); and the benediction (*āśīrvāda*) with sandalwood paste and other items—these constitute the procedure for the installation of the pedestal of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa-pāda-sthāpana-vidhi*).

Now, the ritual for the gateway (toraṇa-vidhi). [The procedures] beginning with the ritual placement (nyāsa), the inspection (nirīkṣaṇa), and so forth; the four purificatory rites (catuḥ-saṃskāra); the previous offering of strength (bali); and the mantra for one's own self: *oṃ hrāṃ śāntikadvāra sākhāropayāmi*. Having performed the worship and circumambulation of the deity, [one recites]: *oṃ hrāṃ śāntitoraṇa ropayāmi*.
In the deity's hand is a trident: Oṃ hrāṃ, I install the trident.

South door: *oṃ hrāṃ vidyākalādvāraśākhāṃ ropayāmi* (I install the branch of the door of the Vidyā-kalā). Archway: *oṃ hrāṃ bhūtitoraṇaṃ ropayāmi* (I install the archway of the Bhūti-kalā). Trident: *oṃ hrāṃ triśūlaṃ ropayāmi* (I install the trident).
In the western *balāga*: the self-mantra is *oṃ hrāṃ nivṛttikarādvāraṃ ropayāmi*. For the *toraṇa*: *oṃ hrāṃ varatoraṇaṃ ropayāmi*. For the trident (*triśūla*): *oṃ hrāṃ triśūlaṃ ropayāmi*.
In the north: Palākasi! Svāyamantra! Oṃ hrāṃ, I install the door-panels of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*. Torana! Oṃ hrāṃ, I install the *āroha-toraṇa*. Triśūla! Oṃ hrāṃ, I install the trident.
O Agni, you are the self-existent one. Oṃ hrāṃ, I plant the door-branch of Ṛddhi. In the southwest: O Devadāru, you are the self-existent one. Oṃ hrāṃ, I plant the door-branch of Kṛtti.
Vāyavya! Ārasi! Oṃ hrāṃ, I plant the branch of the Puṣṭi door.
Īśāna! You are the Lord of Form. Oṃ Hrāṃ! I install the door-leaf of the gate of accomplishment.
Below: You are the horse. Oṃ hrāṃ, I plant the branch of the gate of Pātāla.
Above: Caṃpasvānasi. Oṃ Hrāṃ, I establish the door to heaven.
Kalila, Ṭibhābhāna, Mālako, Khāyaka.

For the banners and flags: "This banner is mine; let it be raised in the east. Mantra: *Oṃ lūṃ, I raise the banner marked with a vajra.* For the flags: *Oṃ hrāṃ, I raise the Kumuda flag.* For the parasols:
Hyāṅgu || Agne || Oṃ ḍūṃ, I install the banner marked with the Śakti. Patākā || Oṃ hrāṃ, I install the Kumudākṣa banner.
Hāk! South: Oṃ mrūṃ, I install the banner marked with a staff. Flag: Oṃ hrāṃ, I install the lotus flag. Parasol:
Dhūmra | Nairṛtya | Oṃ Kṣūṃ, I erect the banner marked with a sword. Patākā | Oṃ Hrāṃ, I erect the mind-banner.
Northwest. Oṃ brūṃ. I install the banner marked with a noose.
Banner: Oṃ hrāṃ, I install the banner with ears like a stake. Umbrella:
Speech. [Dedicated to] Vāyu. Oṃ hrāṃ mrūṃ, I erect the banner marked with a banner. Banner. Oṃ hrāṃ, I erect all the banners. Parasol.
Eyu || Uttara || Oṃ mrūṃ, I install the banner marked with a mace. || Patākā || Oṃ hrā, I install the eye-banner. || Chatra ||
Vāyu || Īśāna || Oṃ Hrūṃ, I erect the banner marked with a trident. || Banner || Oṃ Hrāṃ, I erect the beautiful-faced banner. || Parasol ||
Cāru || Below: Oṃ krīṃ, I install the banner marked with the discus. Patākā: Oṃ hrāṃ, I install the triple-peaked banner.
Hyāṅ || Ūrddha || Oṃ oṃ, I install the banner marked with a lotus. || Patākā || Oṃ hrāṃ, I install the Gaṇa-banner.
In the center: Oṃ ślīṃ paśūṃ hūṃ phaṭ, obeisance to the Pāśupata weapon; I raise the great banner.
For the purpose of subduing, one should place the fire-form *yaṃ*, which is its indicator, in the southeast corner of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).
The ritual vase and the stirring of the signs.
This is the ritual procedure for the archways (toraṇa).

Then, following the sequence of days, there is the rite of formal acceptance (*adhivāsanakarma*), the shaving rite (*kṣurakarman*), the sacrifice for the deceased (*mārakoṣa*), the ritual bathing (*snāna*) and so forth, the worship of the deity (*devārccana*), and finally the offering of one hundred *vṛndikā* oblations.
The worship of Sūrya according to one's capacity. Then, he performed the worship of Sūrya.
Of this Śrīsūrya mantra, the seer is Manu, the meter is Gāyatrī, the deity is Sūrya, and the application is for the sake of attaining unperceived fruits.

On the head: *Namaḥ* to the sage Manu. On the mouth: *Namaḥ* to the Gāyatrī metre. On the heart: *Namaḥ* to the deity Sūrya. *Nyāsa*: *Hrāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*. *Hrīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*. *Hrūṃ* to the tuft (*śikhā*), *vauṣaṭ*. *Hraiṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *hūṃ*. *Hroṃ* to the three eyes, *vaṣaṭ*. *Hraḥ* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. With this [mantra], perform the *nyāsa* on the heart and other limbs (six). With this, perform the worship of the *argha* vessel and self-worship. Worship the pedestal (*pīṭha*) with "Obeisance to Ādhāraśakti," and so forth (eight).
Oṃ, homage to Dīptā. Oṃ, homage to Sūkṣmā. Oṃ, homage to Jayā. Oṃ, homage to Bhadrā.

Oṃ, salutation to Vibhūti. Oṃ, salutation to Vimalā. Oṃ, salutation to Amoghā. Oṃ, salutation to Dyutā. Oṃ, salutation to Sarvatomukhī. [In the center: Oṃ, salutation to the Saura-pīṭha, whose essence is Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.
Meditative absorption.
I worship Him who sits upon a red lotus throne, the unique ocean of all virtues, the sun, the sovereign of all worlds,
holding in his lotus-like hands a pair of lotuses, the gesture of fearlessness, and the gesture of granting boons.
[He who has] the luster of his body reddened by the crest-jewel of rubies, and who possesses three eyes.

Having meditated thus, one should worship with the ritual services beginning with water for the feet (*pādya*). [Three handfuls of water] (*triyāñjali*): *hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ sūryāya namaḥ* (3). [Six-limbed worship] (*ṣaḍaṅga*): One should worship the enclosure (*āvaraṇa*). *soṃ somamaṇḍalāya namaḥ*; *aṃ aṅgārāya namaḥ*; *vuṃ budhāya namaḥ*; *bṛṃ bṛhaspataye namaḥ*; *śuṃ śukrāya namaḥ*; *śaṃ śanaiścarāya namaḥ*; *rāṃ rāhave namaḥ*; *kaṃ ketave namaḥ*. [Worship] ending with incense, lamp, and food offering (*naivedya*). [Then perform] the recitation (*japa*).
hrāṃ hrīṃ saṃ svāhā || 10 ||
Hymn of Praise.

Salutations to Savitṛ, the sole eye of the world, the cause of the origin, sustenance, and destruction of the universe; who consists of the three Vedas, who assumes the nature of the three guṇas, and whose essence is Viriñci, Nārāyaṇa, and Śaṅkara.
Thus ends the worship of Sūrya.
Now follows the worship of the archway (toraṇa).
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Śāntidvārā. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the form of Śāntidvāra.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Śrī Nandin. [To the right.]
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to Mahākāla. [Offerings] on the left: bali, incense, lamp, and here, perfume and so forth.
O Agni! Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Ṛddhidvārā. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the form of Ṛddhidvāra. [Offer] bali, incense, lamps, and so forth; here [offer] perfumes and other articles.
On the right: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Vidyādvārā. Oṃ hrīṃ śrī, obeisance to Vidyādvāramūrti. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Bhṛgu. Dakṣa.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. [Offering] on the left: the bali offering and so forth.
Nairṛtya: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Kīrttidvārā. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the form of Kīrttidvāra. Bali. Here [are] the perfumes and so forth.
In the west: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Nivṛttidvārā; Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the form of Nivṛttidvāra.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Vṛṣa; [at] the right. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Skanda; [at] the left. Bali.
In this case, there is fragrance and so forth.
Vāyavya: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Puṣṭidvārā.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the deity who is the embodiment of the door of nourishment. Bali offering.
In this case, there is fragrance and so forth.
In the north: Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Pratiṣṭhādvārā.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the deity of the door of consecration.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the Goddess. [To] Dakṣa.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Candrā. [Offer] bali on the left.
In this case, there is fragrance and so forth.
In the northeast: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Siddhidvārā.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the embodiment of the gateway to accomplishment. [Bali offering.]
In this case, there is odor and so forth.
Half-moon: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the Half-moon (Ardhacandrā).
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the one whose form is the half-moon. Bali.
Herein [are mentioned] fragrance and so forth.
Above: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Ūrdhvacchandā.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the lunar form above. [Bali offering.]
Herein [are] scent and so forth.

Now, the invitation of the Guru. First, the sacrificer, having become pure, should perform the invitation-maṇḍala for the preceptor, the Guru. [Offering] water for the sun (sūryārgha). [Offering] the seat: *Oṃ, for the purpose of inviting the preceptor, the Guru, here is the seat; obeisance. Flowers; obeisance.* [With the mantra] *kvatarasatute tayāva*. *Oṃ, obeisance to the water for the feet (pādārgha) for the preceptor, the Guru.* [For the purpose of the invocation of the fire in which the oblations are perfected according to the pleasure of the glorious, illustrious White Deity, and for the purpose of the worship of the Guru-maṇḍala, obeisance to the water for the feet. [With the mantra] *śaṅkhaśaluṃ tayāvaluya*.

Thus: water for the hands (*hastārgha*), vermilion (*sindūra*), the patron (*yajamāna*), the dog (*śvāna*), incense (*dhūpa*), and the lamp (*dīpa*). For the purpose of the patron’s oblations and the propitiation of the established fire (*siddhāgni*), there is the invocation; for the purpose of the worship of the maṇḍala by the preceptor (*guru*) and the teacher (*ācārya*), may all rites here—consisting of the offering of perfumes, flowers, incense, and lamps for the ritual worship of the Guru-maṇḍala—be complete.
One should not abandon one's companions even when facing danger; this is the mantra.
Oṃ! You, the Earth, have been filled with the blood of Madhu and Kaiṭabha;
therefore, for the sake of purifying that impurity, I sprinkle you with fragrant water.
Having bowed,
[I offer] this mandala of parched grain, flowers, unbroken rice, incense, lamps, and perfumes.
Oṃ! The earth has been purified and smeared with fragrant water;
may the evil deeds committed in previous births become meritorious acts.
Whatever evil was committed by me in this birth or in previous births—
It is entwined by the thread of karma throughout various births and future lives.
Having formed the añjali with the backs of the hands, one should rotate them with a focused mind;
O Lord, may all that be forgiven, and may you, O Śiva, protect us at all times.
By means of flowers of various forms, one is born into various families;
one should offer the powder ground from an unbroken mandala before the Guru.
Having made a mandala one cubit in measure with yellow powder: *ṅātute*, *kevoya*.

Oṃ, homage to Indra. Oṃ, homage to Agni. Oṃ, homage to Yama. Oṃ, homage to Nairṛti. Oṃ, homage to Varuṇa. Oṃ, homage to Vāyu. Oṃ, homage to Kubera. Oṃ, homage to Īśāna. Oṃ, homage to Viṣṇu. Oṃ, homage to Brahmā. (10) This is for the first layer.
Oṃ, homage to Jayā.
Oṃ, homage to Vijayā. Oṃ, homage to Ajitā. Oṃ, homage to Aparājitā. Oṃ, homage to Jambhanī. Oṃ, homage to Staṃbhanī. Oṃ, homage to Mohinī. Oṃ, homage to Ākarṣaṇī. 8.
The second round: Oṃ, salutation to Sadyojāta; Oṃ, salutation to Vāmadeva; Oṃ, salutation to Tatpuruṣa; Oṃ, salutation to Aghora; Oṃ, salutation to Īśāna. 5.
The third round: Oṃ, salutation to the Brahma-maṇḍala. Oṃ, salutation to the Viṣṇu-maṇḍala.
Oṃ, homage to the Śiva-maṇḍala. || 3 ||
The fourth tuṃ: Oṃ akhaṇḍamaṇḍalāya namaḥ || 2 || The fifth tuṃ: svānataṃnaṃ ||

Oṃ, salutations to Gaṇapati. Oṃ, salutations to the Gurus. Oṃ, salutations to the Guardian of the Door. Oṃ, salutations to the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla). Oṃ, salutations to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti). Oṃ, salutations to Kālāgnirudra. Oṃ, salutations to the Tortoise-Throne (Kūrmāsana). Oṃ, salutations to the Infinite-Throne (Anantāsana). Oṃ, salutations to the Lotus-Throne (Padmāsana). Oṃ, [the mantra] beginning with "Ṛgveda" and so forth. Oṃ, [the mantra] beginning with "Kṛtayuga. [The mantras] beginning with "Hṛdaya" and so forth.

Sandalwood, vermilion, *jona* and *jajamakā* flowers, clothing, a dog, this is the second [offering of] sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). Incense, lamps, fruits, betel, food offerings (*naivedya*), the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*) of fruits, flowers, betel, and so forth, recitation (*jāpa*), and hymns (*stotra*).
Homage to you, O Maṇḍala, and to you, the sovereign of all principles;
homage indeed to you, the manifestation of Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ, who possesses the form of the universe.
I bow to the mandala, which extends as far as the seven oceans, is endowed with the seven continents, and possesses the form of an unbroken circle.
Thus ends the Mandala-stava.
Then one should recite the praise of the guru: Oṃ, homage to the gurus.
Salutation to that illustrious Guru, by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the nature of an unbroken circle and by which all that is moving and unmoving is pervaded.
Herein [are] scent and so forth.

Oṃ, may there be refuge in the purity of body. Oṃ, may there be refuge in the purity of speech. Oṃ, may there be refuge in the purity of mind. Oṃ Oṃ, homage to the refuge in the purity of body, speech, mind, and consciousness.
Oṃ! You are the refuge of all beings, established in both the moving and the unmoving;
having seen [all] through your movement within beings, O Supreme Lord, may you be present.
Here [are] the fragrances and so forth.
Obeisance to the one born from the heart; you are rich in the qualities of the Mantra and born of the lineage of the Ācāryas.

For the sake of bestowing grace, O Hotṛ, you have become manifest in the path of speech during this sacrifice. Herein [is the offering of] fragrance and so forth; [followed by] the dismissal of the maṇḍala.
Having offered all the auspicious substances, the seats, the lamps, and the ritual fees (*dakṣiṇā*), one should honor the preceptor as the patron (*yajamāna*). [The mantra: *adyādi*... [etc.]
Just as for Sajña, for the purpose of the rite of establishing the sacred fire.
Oṃ! O Blessed One, by your grace, this has been worshipped for the sake of the sacrifice;
grant me the bestowal of supernatural power and accomplishment. O Guru Śambhu, homage be to you!
You have been summoned for the sake of the sacrifice; may it bring you mental well-being.
On the very day you are invoked, on that day may you be victorious.
The Guru Ācārya performs the consecration of the patron, followed by the blessing with sandalwood paste and vermilion.

O Maṇḍala-druma! With a mind purified by the sixteen-fold bath, [I] offer [this] to the witness for the sake of the patron. Oṃ, obeisance with an offering (argha) to Sūrya, the witness of performed deeds. Thus ends the procedure for the worship of the Guru-maṇḍala.

The covering for the reciter (*jāpaka*): a seat of grass (*viṣṭarāsana*), water for the feet (*pādya*), the respectful offering (*argha*), water for sipping (*ācamana*), honey-mixture (*madhuparka*), clothing, sandalwood paste and so forth, incense, lamps, and [offerings] for each respective deity. Having described these, he says: "O venerable one, please remain; we shall worship you. The sacrificer (*yajamāna*) says this. "Om, you may worship," says the preceptor (*ācārya*).
Then, taking a single seat (*viṣṭara*), the sacrificer says: "Oṃ, let this seat, the seat, be accepted. The Preceptor says: "Oṃ, I accept the seat."

Then the sacrificer [says]: "Oṃ, let the water for the feet (pādya) be accepted, the water for the feet. The sacrificer says: "Oṃ, I accept the water for the feet. Having said this, the preceptor (ācārya) should wash [his] feet.
Then the sacrificer says: "Oṃ, let the arghya, the arghya, be accepted. The sacrificer says: "Oṃ, I accept the arghya," and the teacher [accepts it].
Then, the water for sipping (3): "May the water for sipping be accepted," says the sacrificer.
"Oṃ, I accept the water for sipping," says the preceptor.
Then the honey-mixture (*madhūparka*). The sacrificer says: "Oṃ, the honey-mixture (three times). May the honey-mixture be accepted. The teacher says: "Oṃ, I accept the honey-mixture."

Gazing with the root mantra: *KHPHREṂ ŚAKARAŚATRU-PRAMATHANĪ ASTRĀYE PHAṬ*. Sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*). Raising [the water] with the ring finger and thumb, [making] three drops; three sips (*triprāśana*). Sipping water (*ācamana*) according to the three principles (*tritatva*). Performing the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with one's own mantra.

Then the sacrificer should give two blades of *kuśa* grass, saying: "Oṃ gauḥ, gauḥ, gauḥ. He should say, "I accept the cow," and then cut the grass. [He should offer] the purifiers (*pavitra*), cloth, sandalwood paste, and so forth, as well as incense and lamps, according to the colors of their respective deities. [The officiant] blows upon the *agocchāvi*. [This is performed by] the *hotṛ*.
You are enriched with the virtues of being firm in mantra and endowed with the study of sacred knowledge;
O venerable one, for the sake of bestowing grace, become the Hotṛ priest at my sacrifice—you are present everywhere.
The selection of the bridegroom according to the prescribed rules; then, the construction of the pavilion, the platform, and so forth.

The Protection of the Lamp and Iron; the Nyāsa and so forth; the Four Purificatory Rites (Catussaṃskāra). Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Pheṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Namaḥ. *Inspection* (Nirikṣaṇa): Khphreṃ, O destroyer of all enemies, to the Weapon (Astra), Phaṭ! *Sprinkling* (Prokṣaṇa): Khphreṃ, O dispeller of all misfortunes and afflictions, self-dependent, to the Armor (Kavaca), Huṃ! *Veiling* (Avaguṇṭhana): Khphreṃ, O destroyer of all enemies, to the Weapon (Astra), Phaṭ! *Striking* (Tāḍana): Khphreṃ, O Supreme Haṃsī, the All-Knowing One, to the Heart (Hṛdaya), Namaḥ!
KH PHREṂ NIRVĀNAMĀRGGETIPTI ŚIRASE SVĀHĀ ||
KH PHREṂ! To the crest-lock of primordial awakening, which pacifies all calamities and adversities, VAUṢAṬ!
KHPHREṂ! O you who have subdued all misfortunes, enemies, and afflictions; svatrantra, for the armor, HŪṂ!
KHPHREṂ! To the one who is a boat across the ocean of all calamities, whose power is unimpeded, and who possesses three eyes—VAṢAṬ!
KHPHREṂ! O you who crush hundreds of enemies with your weapon, PHAṬ!
With this mantra, the worship of the pavilion is performed.

The Worship of the King: Yellow in the east, blue in the south, white in the west, red in the north, and dark green in the center. Having offered *kuśa* grass, a small boat, sprouts, and five threads; having applied sandalwood paste; [the syllables] *phuṃ*, *siṃ*, *kī*, *la*, *aṃ*, *pu*, *nyā*, *mu*, *ga*, *la*; protective herbs; and the offering (*argha*) to the Sun and others. The worship of the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). (8) One should worship the five faces and their respective limbs in their own directions. (8)
KHPHREṂ NAMAḤ SARVVASIDDHIYONIBHYAḤ PŪRVAVAKTRĀYAI PĀDUKĀM ||
KH PHREṂ NAMAḤ SARVVASIDDHIMĀTRBHYO DAKṢIṆAVAKTRĀYAI PĀDUKĀM ||
Khphreṃ. Homage to her who is eternally delighted by primordial bliss, the northern face; [I offer] the sandals.
KH PHREṂ! To the Mistress of the Śaṅkarakūṭa Cakra, the Western Face, [I offer] the sandals.
Khphreṃ! To the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī, whose face is turned upward, [I offer] the sandals.

The Śakti-mantra; the Gāyatrī; the [mantras] for the heart and other limbs; the worship (pūjā); the Aghora-gāyatrī; the [mantras] for the heart and other limbs; the recitation (japa) and the *rapa*; the offering (bali); the incense and other offerings (dhūpādi); the consecration (pratiṣṭhā); and here, the perfumes and other articles (gandhādi).
The dismissal of the Rajana and Khipa vessels.

For the purpose of laying the ritual threads upon the altar; for the offering of oblations according to the prescribed rules; for the worship of the deities residing within the sacrificial pit; and for the daily shadow-bath as well as the complete ritual worship of the deities along with their limbs and subordinate parts.

Worship of the sacrificial ground (*thaṇḍilārccana*): sprinkling with water, scattering flowers, and performing the *chāyā-snāna* (shadow-bath). The *ācamana* (sipping of water) according to the three principles (*tritatva*). Salutation to the Guru. [Recitation of] "Akhaṇḍamaṇḍalādya... and so forth. Sprinkling the sacrificial ground with water while reciting "Akhaṇḍamaṇḍalākāram... and so forth. The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of Siddhilakṣmī. The water vessel (*jalapātra*). The argha vessel (*arghapātra*). Purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). Self-worship (*ātmapūjā*). Sprinkling with water while reciting the two mantras for invocation (*āvāhana*).

*Triyāñjali*. The *Navātmākrama*. The location of the head (*mūrdhasthāna*). *Tumbeśvarī*. The *śikhā*. *Mahākāra*. *Ugracaṇḍā*. *Ugracaṇḍī*. *Śrī Siddhilakṣmī*. *Kālī*. *Tripura*. These are the mantras for the ritual union (*saṃstava*). For the invocation (*āvāhana*), [use] the *yonimudrā*. Then, for the water-offering (*arghapūjā*): *Oṃ gaṅgāyai namaḥ*; *Oṃ yamunāyai namaḥ*; *Oṃ narmadāyai namaḥ*; *Oṃ kāverīyai namaḥ*; *Oṃ kauśikyai namaḥ*.

Salutation to the Gaṇḍakī. Oṃ sararyū, the sandals. Oṃ saṃpūrṇakalaśāyai, the sandals. Aiṃ (5) Haṃ (9). To the Kula-tree Mahāsena, the Deluder of all holy sites, the deity of the mantra, the essence of the parts, the Lord of the principles, whose self is Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra, to the principles of Ātman, Vidyā, and Śiva; HSKMLVRYŪṂ ŚKMLVRYĪṂ—to the form of the Full Jar, the sandals. [Perform] the invocation and other rites. [Mudrā: The Dhenu-mudrā. [Recite] the Āgnāya-vākya and the Kāyāvahni-śakana-sa. [Perform] the bath with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).

The syllable *ū* is the seed-syllable of Vāyu; above that is Varuṇa, who holds a vajra in his hand; above that is the syllable *ka*, joined with the final letter of the alphabet (*ha*); above that is the supreme seed-syllable of Fire (*ra*), together with *sa* and *haṃ*;
[this is] the Moon (*i*) and the Bindu (*m*), ending in dissolution, from which flows a stream of nectar from the excellent white lotus eye.
But seeing a wicked person, one should always burn them away; for such evil is indeed equal to Mount Meru.
I bathe [the deity] with water, milk, curd, honey, ghee, and earth purified from the surface of the earth,
and with the eternal wish-fulfilling cow, by the command of Śiva.
Having taken curd, [one should worship] the husband of Umā, the god who is dear to the gods;
by bathing him constantly and perpetually, the deities will always be well-pleased.
O Purifier by Ghee, O Purifier of the Liṅga of the Wielder of the Pināka!
Through Agni, who is the embodiment of all things, may those three worlds and their inhabitants be auspicious.
The yellow robe.
That which is produced by the Gomukhī-śakti is beloved by the gods;
it is that bath, situated upon the wish-fulfilling tree of desires, by which [the goal] is obtained.
With this very [offering].
This sugar-candy is of great flavor and likewise cool to the mind;
the Goddess, bathed with sugar-moon, is unbroken and the bestower of boons.
Likewise, with milk and other substances beginning with the fivefold [offerings], and with the five Brahmans and so forth as the fragrance,
joined with the five jewels, I bathe [the deity] with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
To the one who wears a garland of skulls and carries a staff.
Aiṃ (5). Within the circle of the illustrious Saṃvarta, the power of bliss is established in the stages of the sequence; it is most formidable.
In the placement of emanation, there is a tetrad, then the fivefold [group] of Akula and Kula, and another hexad;
then four, another pentad, and again four—this is the reality within the mandala.
Bow down to that excellent Guru, Śrī Kujeśa Bhairava, by whom [all things] are intermingled.
For the purpose of adorning the bare ground: the syllable *ū*, the seed-syllable of wind, and so forth. For the bathing of bees: *śkṣmlvryīṃ*.
The attendant.
Divine śrīkhaṇḍa sandalwood, enchanting with its fragrance and other qualities.
When the husband is white, sandalwood with red spots is to be consumed.
Anointed with sandalwood paste, it is meritorious, purifying, and the destroyer of evil;
it constantly removes calamities and bestows fortune, sovereignty, and happiness.
Sindūra (vermilion)
O Vīreśvarī, O Great Heroine! This supreme sindūra, adorned with the ashes of heroes, is the attractor of the three worlds.
Or else.
O Mother of the World, you are the sacrifice, the garment, the supreme purifier, and the bestower of happiness and prosperity; accept this cotton cloth offered to you—salutations to you!
View.
May this *vṛṣṭika* be accepted for the sake of attaining the fruit of divine vision, which reveals the fourteen worlds— Heaven, Mortal Realm, and Pātāla.
The Ear-banner.
One should take a beautiful four-cornered banner known as the "ear" (karṇa), which has the brilliant color of pure vermilion, belonging to the supreme lords.
The five banners.
O Goddess, accept this pair of earrings and the five-colored banner;
accept this supreme flag for the sake of attaining the fruit of the five siddhis.
Unbroken.
Grant me, O Meru, that which is unimpaired, an inexhaustible space, the bestower of the accomplishment of Dharma, Kāma, and Artha, the desired object, and the supreme goal in the next world.
The sacrificers.
The sacred thread is the supreme purifier, which was born together with Prajāpati in the beginning.
May there be for you the foremost longevity, perfect renown, the sacred thread, strength, and splendor.
In the Caphumāḍha [region].
O Lord of Gods, grant me the fruit of my desire by means of this divine wish-fulfilling gem, which shines like the full moon, that you have given.
Svāhā!
One offers various flowers, fragrant substances, and so forth, which bring joy to the sacrificial pit.
O auspicious lady, this supreme ritual of offering flowers bestows the attainment of good fortune.
With a small piece of gold from the nose.
Resplendent like the full moon, pure, and the destroyer of the pride of Śatru-darpa,
may that which holds its own reflection grant victory to the tradition.
First, for the bathing and anointing of the patron (*yajamāna*), [there is] the *vārakaracchoya*.
Thus ends the procedure for bathing in the shadow.

Now, the worship on the sacrificial ground (thaṇḍilyārccana). Having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) by means of the triple reality (tritatva): Khphreṁ Hrāṁ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva). Khphreṁ Hrīṁ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva). Khphreṁ Hrūṁ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva). Khphreṁ Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ, svāhā to all principles (sarvatattva).
The *sūryārgha* [rite]: from the beginning of today... [the ritual] formula. Having extracted the seed-syllable ending with the letter *va*, one should place *Śiva* upon it.
But at the beginning, middle, and end, it is adorned by the three fires.
Having illuminated it with the *varman* mantra, one should extract this with the *sāvitrī*.
This is the most excellent of secret formulas (*kūṭa*), the supreme Mahāmārttaṇḍabhairava.
Argha, obeisance! Flower, obeisance! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hreṃ hrauṃ hraḥ hrīṃ saḥ, obeisance to the illustrious Kulamārtaṇḍa Mahābhairava, together with the Śakti Prakāśā.
RHKṢRĪṂ! Salutation to the illustrious Mahāmārtaṇḍa Bhairava.
Salutation to the Gurus. Aiṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsoṃḥ.
Salutation to that illustrious Guru, by whom that state has been revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which all that is moving and unmoving is pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the god Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—to that glorious Guru, obeisance.
Aiṃ (5). Salutation to the supreme gurus.
(5) Homage to the supreme preceptors. (5) Homage to the supreme teachers and gurus.
Pādukā to Balisa Padmāsana; Pādukā to Thavaka Kūrmāsana.
On the side, the scattering of unbroken rice grains.
Aiṁ (5) Khphreṁ! O crusher of all enemies, abode of infinite power, to the weapon—phaṭ! [Salutation to] the sandal.
The binding of the face with the vajra-mudrā.
Aiṁ (5) Khphreṁ Hūṁ Vajrapañjare Svāhā. [This is] the touching of the ten doors.
KHPHREṂ CALAMAKULE KULAMACALE HRĪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ ||
Nyāsa: Khphreṃ! O you who crush all enemies, the abode of infinite power, to the weapon-mantra, Phaṭ! Ritual purification of the water jar. (4)
KH PHREṂ Paramahaṃsinī, to the abode of the power of omniscience, homage to both thumbs!
Khphreṃ! O Goddess on the path to Nirvāṇa, to the abode of the power of satisfaction, salutations with the two index fingers.

Khphreṃ! Obeisance to the two middle fingers, the abode of the power of primordial awakening that pacifies calamities and adversities. Khphreṃ! Obeisance to the two ring fingers, the abode of the independent power that shatters all sins, enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions.
KH PHREṂ: Salutation to the one who is the boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities, the abode of unimpeded power; to the two little fingers, *namaḥ*.
KH PHREṂ | O you who crush all enemies, to the abode of infinite power, salutation to the weapon (astra) for the two buttocks. [This is the *kala* placement.]
KH PHREṂ. Homage to all the Yoginīs of Accomplishment! The sandal of the Lord of the eastern face! PĀDUKĀM.
Khphreṁ! Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment; the sandals of the Lord of the Southern Face.
Khphreṃ! Homage to Nityoditānandananditā, the Mistress of the Northern Face; [I worship] your sandals!
Khphreṃ! To the Mistress of the entire family wheel, the Lord of the western face, [I offer] the sandals.
KH PHREṂ. To the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī, the sandals of the Lord of the upward-facing mouth. [This is] the ritual placement of the faces (vaktranyāsa).
Khphreṃ! O Supreme Swan-like One, to the abode of the power of omniscience, homage to the heart!
KH PHREṂ! To the one who bestows the path to nirvāṇa, the abode of the power of satisfaction, svāhā to the head!
KH PHREṂ! To the one who pacifies adverse calamities, the abode of the power of primordial awakening, for the crest-lock (śikhā), VAṢAṬ!
KHPHREṂ! To the armor, the abode of the independent power that crushes all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions—HŪṂ!

*Khphreṃ*, to her who carries one across the ocean of all calamities, whose abode is unimpeded power, to the Three-Eyed One, *vauṣaṭ*. *Khphreṃ*, to her who crushes hundreds of enemies along with their weapons, whose abode is infinite power, to the Weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. Thus is the ritual placement of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*). *Tam* at the center of the eyebrows; *dyam* in the heart; *thām* at the navel; *oṃ* in the mouth; *hrīṃ* in the left nostril; *hūṃ* in the right nostril; *hāṃ* in the left eye; *phreṃ* in the right eye; *kṣoṃ* in the left ear; *kroṃ* in the right ear; *na* in the penis.
Maḥ Guhya. The Nyāsa of the Nine Gates.
Worship of the Water Vessel: Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the *pādukā* for the seat of the water vessel.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, the sandals for the venerable Lord of the Water Vessel (jalapātrabhaṭṭāraka).
*Khphreṃ* for the heart-mantra and so forth; the rites of invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth; the *dhenumudrā*; the *gāyatrī*.
Khphreṃ. We know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon her who possesses ninety [verses].
May that Lakṣmī inspire us. [This is] the consecration.
The Worship of the Argha Vessel: *khphreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, the *pādukā* for the seat of the argha vessel.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ! Vauṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava!
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! O Supreme Goddess, [this is] the breath; saḥ saḥ, vomit nectar, vomit, svāhā!
Purification of the substances: three handfuls. Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ. (3)

*Khphreṃ hṛdayāya tyādi*. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth with the *yonimudrā*. Perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) with the *kacchapamudrā*. Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ khphreṃ hsauṃ hsauṃ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrī aiṃ.
Self-worship: Khphreṁ! To myself, sandalwood paste, sandals, unbroken rice grains, and heroic ashes.
KH PHREṂ! The sandals that enchant all people.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kro namaḥ; [I offer] flowers and sandals to the Self.
KHPHREṂ, O crusher of all enemies, PHAṬ to the weapon!
With this mantra, one should sprinkle it upon one's own head. (3)
One should recite the Mālāmantra: Oṃ namaścaṇḍikāyai.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Aiṃ (5). O Goddess Mārīnī, may you be victorious! You are the destroyer of death in the realm free from Mara;
you are the Goddess who is the source of the power of knowledge, and you are Intelligence that increases splendor.
O Mother of all beings, established in this cycle of existence,
O Goddess Vīrāvalī, O affectionate one, grant me a son!

Victorious is she who is the manifestation of the supreme reality and Nirvāṇa, Śambhū; you are the splendorous, unmanifest form that has emerged as the supreme power of knowledge (jñāna-śakti), the powers of will (icchā) and action (kriyā),
the auspicious one, the straight line, the beautiful inscription, and once again the sleeping lord of serpents.
O Sovereign, you whose form is like a water-lily and an earring are the power of resonance (Nāda-śakti);

you sing together, radiant, the nature of light, the very essence, auspicious; you are named Jyeṣṭhā, Vāmā, Raudrī, and Manonmanī; O Mother, you are the form of the Bindu, the Daughter-in-law, and the shape of the half-moon.

The triangular [seat] is formed by the union of the syllables *a*, *u*, *ma*, and *ī*. Its primordial nature is the state of the vulva (*bhaga*). Arising from the principle (*tattva*) of *aditi* up to *kṣānta*, it is the womb whose nature is the venerable Śrīkaṇṭha; she is the mother of Rudra, the infinite power (*ananta-śakti*), exceedingly subtle, the one who receives the offerings of the three gods, Marīci, and Īśa; she is the essence of Bhārabhūti, Tithīśa, Aśubhūta, and Harākṣa; and she is worshipped for the sake of grace as the nature of Jhaṇṭhīśa, Bhautīśa, and Sadyojāta.

You are the consort of the Great Sena of cruel limbs; you who bestow the nectar of the sixteen [vowels] at their end; you who overflow with the collection of *bindus*; you who drench and flood the body with flowing [nectar]; O Bhairavī, you who grant the bliss of supreme *nirvāṇa* to Śeṣa; you who are intent on playing in the garden of Bhairava; O Supreme Mother, you who are worshipped by the garland of Rudras; you who are the power of Rudra (*rudraśakti*); you who are the mistress of yoga for the accomplishment of the *khagī* (sky-farer) siddhis; you who are the mother of all accomplishments (*siddhimātā*); you who are the pervasive one (*vibhu*); you who are the mass of sounds (*śabdarāśi*); you who move through the letters; you who are the purity of speech (*vāgviśuddhā*); you who are the auspicious Śivā; you who are the Mistress of the Speech of the Siddhas (*siddhavāgeśvarī*); you who are the ocean of the *mātṛkā*s; you who are Will (*icchā*) and Action (*kriyā*); you who are Maṅgalā; you who are the Fortune of the Siddhas (*siddhalakṣmī*); you who are sovereign splendor (*vibhūti*).
Saṃbhūti, Gati, Śāśvatā, Kṣānti, Nārāyaṇī, Raktacaṇḍā, Karālā, and Kṣaṇā.
O Rudra, you are of terrifying form, beloved in the yoga of the Great Swelling (Mahocchuṣma), victorious, unconquered, and the deluder;
you are seated upon the lap of the God known as Navātman.

O Goddess, you are worshipped by all mantra-following practitioners who are devoted to the drinking of heroes and possessed of great devotion, using the five nectars and divine drinks—O Kāpālinī, adorned with skulls and skeletons!
Those born from one birth, two births, three births, four, five, six, or seven births;

You are gratified by those men who have been taught by the Teacher, by those auspicious ones such as Phalgupa, and by those who delight in wine and meat; by those resplendent with mantras, sciences, and vows—such as the Muṇḍakas, Kaṅkālas, and Kāpālikas—who conform to divine conduct; by those who utter these mantra-syllables: *namaḥ*, *oṃ*, *svāhā*, *svadhā*, *vauṣaṭ*, *vaṣaṭ*, *huṃ*, and *phaṭ*; and by the practitioners (*sādhakas*) and spiritual sons (*putrakas*) who hold red threads in their left hands and offer oblations while reciting prayers; and by the yogis and yoginīs who have been initiated into the maṇḍalas of the Mothers.
O Goddess, you who grant the perfection of yoga, you are worshipped by hosts of *saṃyoginīs* who are intent on the play of Rudra;
with eyes like lotus petals full of affection, you look upon him.

For him, there exists unimpeded success (*siddhi*) that moves through the seven netherworlds and the celestial realms. O Goddess, whether one recites this *daṇḍaka* once, thrice, four, five, six, seven, or eight times a day with the water of devotion, or whoever, being pure, always remembers it—that person, O Goddess, is not harmed even by thieves, fire, weapons, the ocean, or the mountain peaks.

O Goddess, by remembering your face—which possesses excellent earrings of shimmering divine rubies that resemble full moons, and whose cheeks are rubbed [by the tusks] of Ganesha—those who are attached to their sons, those dear to Mahalakshmi, thieves of gold, those addicted to the wives of others, slayers of Brahmins, slayers of cows, great sinners, and the wicked are all liberated.

O Goddess Mahākālī, whose splendor is like the fire of cosmic destruction, who art adorned with garlands by Skanda, Brahmā, Indra, the Moon, the Sun, and the flower-armed Kāmadeva; O Mother of all heroes, whose beautiful golden hair is like the filaments of a lotus, O Bhairavī, I have come to you for refuge—forgive my transgression, O Śivā! Even those whose arms and toes are bound with firm serpent-nooses shall, through the recitation of your name, O Goddess, be released from terrible and great diseases, provided they remember your two lotus feet.
Having thus praised the Great Goddess by the high-souled Bhairava,
the Supreme Goddess then emerged after bursting through the linga.
Thus ends the Mālinīdaṇḍaka hymn.
Then, having offered the five-fold oblation,
one should offer the *dathupāṭa* oblation upon the leveled ground where the *dvadusapāṭa* has been performed.

(5) To the peacock-throne, the sandals! (5) Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, to the sandals of Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha! Oblation! (5) To the human-throne, the sandals! (5) Throṃ, to the sandals of the lamp-bearing Prastara, the goddess Daṃbakī, and the great Mahādhvākṣa Kṣetrapāla! Oblation! (5) To the lion-throne, the sandals! (5) Yāṃ, to the Yoginīs, the sandals! Oblation!

(5) Whatever Yoginīs there may be—those born of the *pīṭhas*, those born of the *kṣetras*, those who are innate (*sahajā*), those born of yoga (*yogajā*), and those born of the womb (*garbhajā*); whatever Yoginīs there may be—the *kṣecarīs*, *bhūcarīs*, *gocarīs*, the single-syllabled, the two-syllabled, the three-syllabled, the four-, five-, six-, seven-, eight-, or nine-syllabled ones, those who traverse the three worlds, and those who have appeared according to their nature—accept this offering! Grant me success! HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. [This is] the offering. (5) *Pādukā* for the one seated upon a corpse (*pretāsana*).

(5) *Hskhphreṃ*, the sandals of the glorious Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī. *Bali*. (5) The sandals for the one seated upon a mouse. (5) *Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaḥ glauṃ*, the sandals of Kulagaṇeśvara; *bali*. [Perform] the rites beginning with invocation (*āvāhana*). [Display] the staff, the threatening gesture (*tarjanī*), the womb-seal (*yonimudrā*), the drop-seal (*bindumudrā*), and the elephant-seal (*gajamudrā*). [Recite] the mantra: *Śrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā* (10 times); *Throṃ svāhā* (10 times); *Yāṃ svāhā* (10 times); *Hskhphreṃ svāhā* (10 times); *Glauṃ svāhā* (10 times). "Accept this recitation, *svāhā*! [Offer] the hymn (*stotra*).
To Kumāra, the son of Gaurī, who is devoid of the expanse of the sky; to the Protector of the Realm (Kṣetrapa); to Yoginī;
to Cāmuṇḍā of fierce form; and to Gaṇeśa, the Lord of Obstacles, who removes the fear of misfortune.
Adorned with flowers and the like, incense, and lamps, and anointed with various unguents— [this deity],
having worshipped the Lord of the Wheel whose limbs are thus adorned, is the cause of the removal of obstacles for those who worship him, and the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
May all that [pertaining] to the ritual of worship of the Five Powers be completely fulfilled.
Homage to the illustrious Nātha! Homage to the illustrious Siddhinātha! Homage again and again to the illustrious Kujenātha!

Having performed the purification with betel leaves and other items; [performing] the libation (*tarpaṇa*); [reciting] "O you who sit upon the satisfied spirits" (*prītapretāsana*) and so forth; bowing to the body of the Command (*ājñākāya*); sipping water (*ācamya*); [placing] three drops on the face.

Invocation: Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! She who is the supreme goddess beyond the supreme, who dwells upon the sword and possesses the form of a bird, who has gone to the realm of the gods—O gentle one, come here to this maṇḍala until the end of my life.
This is the invocation; one should invoke.
Trideva: Khphreṃ, the pādukā for Narāsanā; Khphreṃ, the pādukā for Mayūrāsanā.
Khphreṃ, pādukā to Mūśāsana. Khphreṃ thhsrauṃ, pādukā to the rock-lamp Dambhakī Devī and the great Dhvākṣa Kṣetrapāla. Bali! Khphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ, pādukā to Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. Bali!
KH PHREṂ GĀṂ GĪṂ GŪṂ GAḤ GLAUṂ! To the venerable Kulagaṇeśvara, the sandals, the offering.
*Thaṇḍilī-havana-vidhi-pāṭha-bali*. Invocation and so forth. The *tarjanī*, *daṇḍa*, and *gaja* mudrās.
Now follows the worship of the hands (*karasapūjā*). [Recite] "Ādhāraśakti," and so forth. (8)
Meditative concentration.
Three-eyed, six-armed, and peaceful, adorned with matted locks and the crescent moon,
holding a skull-cup in his hand and a shield, he is seated upon a yogic posture.
Rudra is clothed in a tiger skin, adorned with a lordly serpent,
and holds a trident and a rosary in his right hands.
One should perform the yoga-mudrā with both hands holding a skull-cup and a fire-pot;
one should worship the god Mṛtyuñjaya, the destroyer of death and disease.
Thus is meditation.
Oṃ jūṃ saḥ, salutation to Mṛtyuñjaya, who possesses a face with three full eyes. (3) || Oblation ||

Oṃ, salutations to Brahmā. Salutations to Viṣṇu. Salutations to Rudra. Salutations to Sadāśiva. Salutations to Īśvara. Salutations to the seven oceans beginning with Gaṅgā. Salutations to the fortnights. Salutations to the months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa. Salutations to the seasons. Salutations to the year. Salutations to the seven oceans beginning with the salt ocean (Kṣāra). Salutations to the lunar days (tithis) beginning with Nandā. Salutations to the constellations (nakṣatras) beginning with Aśvinī. Salutations to the astrological conjunctions (yogas) beginning with Viṣkambha.

Salutation to the Muhūrtas. Salutation to the nine planets beginning with Āditya. Salutation to the twelve zodiac signs beginning with Meṣa. Salutation to the seven sages beginning with Vasiṣṭha. Salutation to the eight long-lived ones beginning with Aśva and Sthāṇu. Salutation to the ten world-protectors beginning with Indra. Salutation to the eight primary nāgas beginning with Ananta. [Salutation to] the sandals of the goddess Śrī Rudracaṇḍā, beginning with Rudracaṇḍā. Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ, salutation to the sandals of the embodiment of the full jar. Offering of oblation (bali).

The horizontal *añjali* (3). The six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). *Hmasakana*. *Śrīnamaḥ*. *Sidhra mūṅa*. *Lakṣmī namaḥ*. Invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth. The *dhenumudrā*. Recitation (*japa*): *Oṃ juṃ saḥ svāhā*. (10 times).
Hymn of Praise.

I seek refuge in You alone, that primordial deity known as Mṛtyuñjaya, whom the chief guardians of the worlds of the gods, led by Brahmā, bow to and praise, and who is the fire for the oblations. I take refuge in You, Bhairava.
Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. Thus concludes the worship of the jar (*kalaśa*).
Now, the worship of the jar (kumbhapūjā): [I offer] a sandal for the lotus-seat.
Meditative absorption.
Resembling a cool-rayed moon, she has five faces and three eyes;
she is endowed with ten staff-like arms, brandishing various uplifted weapons.
One should meditate upon the goddess Dharā, crimson-red in hue and the bestower of all happiness;
having thus visualized the Great Goddess, who grants the fruits of all actions.
Thus ends the meditation.
Aiṁ (5) Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Namaḥ.
Gaṃ glūṃ, the sandals for Gaṇapatīnātha, together with his beloved Śakti.
(**) To the venerable Vaṭukanātha, together with his beloved Śakti, [I offer] the sandals.
