KṢĀṂ KṢŪṂ! Sandal paste for the sandals of the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla) of his own station, together with his Śakti and beloved.
Khphreṃ Mahākela Caṇḍinī Raudramukhe Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrauṃ Kā Śrī-Kākamukhi, [I worship] the sandals! Khphreṃ Cīṃ Śrī-Caṇḍamukhī, [I worship] the sandals!
Khphreṃ ṭūṃ, the sandals of Śrītāṃkālī.
Khphreṃ Tṛṃ, the sandals of Śrīrāpiṇī.
Khphreṁ Chaṁ, the sandals of Śrī Pāvakī.
Khphreṃ Yaiṃ Śrīyamaghaṇṭhī, [I invoke] the sandals!
Khphreṃ Sauṃ, the sandals of Śivādūtī.
Khphreṃ Karā Ambā, the sandals!
From the northeast (Īśāna) to the west (Argha), and in the center.
KHPHREṂ ĀṂ KROṂ PHREṂ MAHĀSIDDHISAMAYA KHPHREṂ BHAIRAVĪ GHORĀKṢĪ BALAPRADE SVĀHĀ. [Offer] three *añjali* with the root mantra. KHPHREṂ to the heart, and so forth. The *bali* offering.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! She who dwells in the divine atmosphere, the sky, the earth, and extends even to the depths of the netherworld;
she who is Kākinī and Rākinī, as well as Tāṅkālī and Tāpinī; Yamaghaṇṭhā, Śivādūtī, Kṣayāntā, and Parameśvarī.
Having taken the bali offering and the naivedya, I have devotedly offered it with the word "svāhā."
Invocation and so forth: Yonimudrā. Recitation: KHPHREṂ SVĀHĀ (ten times). Hymn of praise.
Mounted upon a lotus and a corpse, resembling a crystal gem,
five-faced and three-eyed, she deludes the three worlds; endowed with ten arms, her body is embraced by celestial women.

In her left hands, she holds a skull-cup, a trident, a jar, the gesture of granting boons, a great noose, a severed head, a bell, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a sword, the gesture of fearlessness, and a goad; I bow to Siddhilakṣmī, who wields these.
Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. Thus ends the worship of the jar (kumbhapūjā).
The worship of the Kṣatra-vaṭuka, the Gaṇas, the Yoginīs, and the water-jar.

Now, for the western *deguḷī*: the ritual site (*thaṇḍila*) has the emblems of a *karttī* and a skull-cup. On the ritual site, having offered the *javāla-aṅghri-pāṭa-bali*, [one performs] the salutation to the Guru beginning with "To the unbroken maṇḍala," and so forth. [One offers] the sandals to the Lotus Seat; the sandals to the Tortoise Seat. *Kiṇi (2) vicce koṅkanāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ*.
(5) Aiṁ hūṁ phaṭ vajrapañjare svāhā || Calamakule kulamacale hrīṁ hūṁ phaṭ svāhā || Nyāsa || Kiṇi (2) vicce koṅkanāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ pādukāṃ || (4) ||
The purification of the ritual vessel.
Homage to the Blessed Lady Hṛtkamalā! Hrāṃ Śrī! To the two thumbs, the sandals.
Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula; Hrīṁ, to the two Śrī-tarjanīs, the sandals.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, O you with the dark-red crest, hrūṃ! [I offer] the sandals to the two [deities] Śrī and Madhyemā.
Ghorā, Aghorā, Aghorāmukhī, Bahurūpā—hreṃ, [I worship] the sandals at the two ring fingers, O Śrī. Chāṃ chīṃ, [I worship] the sandals at the two little fingers, O Śrī Mahantārikā, hrauṃ.
Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkaṇāyai Hraḥ; [I offer] the sandals to the two hands, beautiful and auspicious on their backs.
The ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa): Homage to the Blessed One, to the lotus of the heart, to the venerable one with the upward face; [I invoke] the sandals.
Hsphreṁ! To Kubjikā, the Lamp of the Kula, whose face is preceded by Śrī; [I offer] the sandal-paste.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, to the one with the dark-brown crest, to the venerable Southern Face, [I offer] the sandals.
To the one who is Ghora, Aghora, and Aghorāmukhī, to the multiformed Śrī-uttaravaktrā, [I offer] the sandal.
Chāṃ chīṃ, to the Great Mother, the Glorious Western Face, the sandals.
Kiṇi (2), to Vicce Koṅkaṇā, to the venerable Parāparavaktrā, [I offer] the sandal-paste. This is the Vaktra-nyāsa.
Homage to the Blessed Lady of the Heart-Lotus; *hrāṃ*, the sandalwood for the heart.
Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula, Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, O you with the dark-blue crest, hrūṃ! To the venerable Khāyā, vauṣaṭ!
Ghorā, Aghorā, Aghorāmukhī, Bahurūpāyai; Hraiṃ, for the armor, Hūṃ!
Chāṃ chīṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes of Mahantārikā; hrauṃ.
Kiṇi (2) vicce koṅkaṇṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ. Thus is the assignment of the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
For the seat of the water-vessel, the sandals: Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to the venerable Śrījalapātra-bhaṭṭārikā, the consort of Ānandaśakti-Bhairava-Ānanda, the sovereign of heroes, Śkṣmlvryīṃ, the sandals.
Hrāṃ to the heart, and so forth; the rites of invocation (āvāhana) and the rest; the dhenu-mudrā; the Gāyatrī; and the consecration (abhiṣecana).
Aiṃ (5). We know Kubjikā; we meditate upon her, the lamp of the Kula; may that Kubjī inspire us.
Now, the worship of the argha vessel: [I offer] the sandals for the seat of the argha vessel.

Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hraḥ, quiver (2), O you of most terrible form (2), crackle (2), move about (2), roar (2), vomit (2), subdue (2), slay (2), destroyers (2)! Hūṃ (3) Phaṭ! To Kau, O Śrī Mahākaumārikā Vicce, [this] sandal-paste offering.
Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ Ānandaśaktibharai-vānanda Śrīmahāvidyālājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ. [Salutation] to the venerable *arghapātra-bhaṭṭārikā*, the sandals.
*Hrāṃ* to the heart, and so forth. [Perform] the invocation and other rites. Display the *yonimudrā*.

with one face and three eyes, his hair is tawny and stands upright on his head. (1)
With tawny eyes, hair shimmering like a brow, a massive body, and a large belly.
Clad in a tiger skin, with an elephant hide as an upper garment. (2)
Adorned with a jeweled serpent-bone headpiece and decorated on both sides with anklets.
Holding in his hands a sword, a cleaver, a skull-cup, and so forth, as well as a drop (bindu) and a khaṭvāṅga staff. (3)
Possessing the great splendor of ten million lightning bolts, he was adorned with the consumption of headless trunks.
Whose sandals are rubbed by the heads of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the Lord of the Gods. (4)
The howling of dogs and jackals, the shrieking of owls, and the cries of vultures and crows—these portend calamity.
It was filled with the tumultuous, shrieking cries of spirits, ghosts, and demons. (5)
And the cremation ground, most terrible, adorned by the assembly of yoginīs.
[He saw] Mahādeva, the benefactor of the worlds, being enveloped [in smoke]. (6)
I bow to the great Kāla, Bhairava, the Lord of the World.
Whoever recites or even hears this [text], which destroys enemies and diseases, (7) ||
She always bestows all success and increases victory.
Thus is meditation.
Three handfuls of water. Aiṃ (5) Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ, the sandals for Śikhāśvacchanda-Mahābhairava. (3) The offering.
Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ Maṃ, I worship the sandals of Mahākāla, the crusher of all enemies, the Great Terrifier. (3) The offering.

Aghora. Hrāṃ, the *pādukā* for the heart. Baliviya. Aiṃ (5) Chāṃ Chīṃ, Phaṭ Svāhā to the weapon (*astra*). Obeisance to Ahatīnasaṃkhakaṭa! Accept this offering of peace (*śānti-bali*), Svāhā! Obeisance to Vujharī, the red one. Obeisance to the dweller of the cremation ground (*śmaśānavāsinī*), the new dweller. Obeisance to Iṣṭayogni. Obeisance to Khecarī. Obeisance to Sma...

Śānavā-śṛṣṭayogini, obeisance to the beloved Bhairava, obeisance to Vikaṭodarī, obeisance to Lambakarṣaṇī. Pheṃ pheṃkāra hrīṃ sa phreṃ phreṃ phrīṃ sa! O Yoginīs, accept the bali offering (2) svāhā! [Performs] the invocation and other rites; the Yoni and Khadga mudrās; the three Bindus.
Thus ends the Śikhāmahākāla-deguli.
Then Ugracaṇḍā [spoke] to Ugracaṇḍīdeguliyā.

Worship at the sacrificial ground (*thaṇḍila*). The signs of the sword and the *pheṭaka*, and the ritual jar (*kalaśa*). At the sacrificial ground, the offering of the *khavalāṅ* and the *thupāṭa* bali. Having sipped water as if it were sacred water (*tīrtha*), perform the salutation to the Guru. [Recite] "Of the form of an unbroken mandala," and so forth. The sandals for the lotus posture (*padmāsana*). The sandals for the tortoise posture (*kūrmmāsana*). For the death-harrowing weapon: *astrāya phaṭ*. *Aiṃ hūṃ vajrapañjare svāhā*. *Aiṃ cala makule kulamacale hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
Aiṃ (5) Mṛtyuhare, Phaṭ to the weapon! Oṃ Hrīṃ Rājaprade, Namaḥ to the little finger! Hsphreṃ Ugracaṇḍe, Svāhā to the ring finger! Ripumardanī, Voṣaṭ to the middle finger!

HŪṂ PHREṂ SADĀRAKṢA (2) TARJANYĀYA HŪṂ || TVĀṂ MĀṂ JUṂ SA AṄGUṢṬHĀYA VAṢAṬ || MRITYUHARE ASTRĀYA PHAṬ || OṂ HRĪṂ RĀJAPRADE HRDAYĀYA NAMAḤ HSPHREṂ UGRACAṆḌE SIRASE SVĀHĀ || RIPUMARDANĪ ŚIKHĀYA VOṢAṬ || HŪṂ PHREṂ SADĀRAKṢA (2) KAVACĀYA HŪṂ || TVĀṂ MĀṂ JUṂ SA NETRATRAYĀYA VAṢAṬ || MRITYUHARE ASTRĀYA PHAṬ ||

Worship of the Water Vessel (jalapātrapūjā). Gāyatrī: *Hrīṃ*, let us know the fierce Caṇḍā; may we meditate upon the Goddess Durgā; may that Caṇḍī inspire us. Worship of the Argha Vessel (arghapātrapūjā). The Weapon of Ghorikā (ghorikāstra). Purification of the Elements (bhūtaśuddhi). Self-worship (ātmapūjā).

Invocation: O Śrī Saṃvartāna! O Trideva! Seat: Offering of worship; Bali offering; [Madāna?]; beginning with "To Ādhāraśakti," etc. (8). Pādukā for the buffalo-throne; Pādukā for the lion-throne; Pādukā for the Śumbha-throne; Pādukā for the Niśumbha-throne.
Now, meditation.
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ! She has the color of molten gold and is adorned with various flowers.
Clad in divine garments, she is seated upon a buffalo throne. (1)
With crowns, earrings shaped like circles, armlets, and jeweled anklets.
And with various garlands of jewels, and adorned with strings of necklaces. (2)
She is adorned with eighteen arms, and her chest and breasts are full.
Adorned with every ornament, she possesses a radiance equal to ten million flashes of lightning. (3)
The auspicious goddesses hold a sword, an arrow, a discus, a thunderbolt, and a goad.
She grants boons, holds a hand-drum, and is beautifully adorned with a trident and a vessel. (4)
With her right hands, she held these [ornaments] upon her lower lip according to what was beautiful.
She holds a *pheṭaka* and a bow in her hands, beautifully adorned with a mace and a bell. (5)
And with her hand, she holds a noose and a threatening gesture, as well as a khaṭvāṅga and a mass of hair.
The *vindumudrā* as well as the *sīdhu* [mudrā] are situated upon the lion throne. (6)
Then, standing below, Himaja cut off my head, O great Asura.
O Daitya of great strength and prowess, she emerged from his neck. (7)
Having been pierced by the trident, she was held aloft by the god Rudra.
Having meditated thus upon the Great Goddess, who bestows the fruit of all desires. (8)
The Śekharā has sixteen hands and is devoid of the khaṭvāṅga and the ḍamaru.
Rudracaṇḍā, Pracaṇḍā, Caṇḍogrā, and Caṇḍanāyikā; (9)
Caṇḍā, Caṇḍavatī, Caṇḍarūpā, and Caṇḍikā.
The Mūmrikā [is] yellowish-brown, reddish, black, blue, and white. (10)
Those who are yellow and pale should be known as being situated in the *ālīḍha* posture, O Hari.
Accompanied by their own retinues, they have arrived here at this maṇḍala. (11)
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.

Aiṁ (5) Namaḥ Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Caṇḍacogrāyai Namaḥ Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Pādukāṁ. Bali. Three añjalis. Aiṁ (5) Oṃ Hrīṁ Rājaprade Hsphreṁ Ugracaṇḍe Ripumardanī Hūṁ Phreṁ Sadārakṣa (2) Tvāṁ Māṁ Juṃ Sa Mṛtyuhare Pādukāṃ Pūjayāmi. (3) [Hṛdayādi]. Bali.

Worship of Indra and the others: Aiṃ (5) LMLVRYŪṂ LUṂ, for Indra, who holds a thunderbolt in his hand, the lord of the gods, [I offer] the sandals. RMLVRYŪṂ RAṂ, for Agni, who holds a spear in his hand, the lord of splendor, [I offer] the sandals.
MMLVRYŪṂ MUṂ:
[I offer] this sandal to Yama, who holds a staff in his hand and is the lord of the pretas.
KṢMLVRYŪṂ KṢUṂ: To the Lord of the Rākṣasas, Nairṛtya, who holds a sword in his hand, [I offer] the sandal.
Vmlvryūṃ Vuṃ, to Varuṇa, who holds a noose in his hand and is the lord of the waters, [I offer] the sandals.
YMLVRYŪṂ YUṂ: Obeisance to the one of the northwest, who holds a banner in his hand, the lord of the wind; [grant] the sandals.
SMLVRYŪṂ SUṂ, to Kubera, who holds a mace in his hand and is the lord of wealth, [I offer] the sandals.
HMLVRYŪṂ HŪṂ! To Īśāna, who holds a trident in his hand and is the lord of spirits, [I offer] the sandals.
Aṃ, to the infinite one, who holds a discus in hand, the lord of nāgas, [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Oṃ, to Brahmā, who holds a lotus in his hand and is the lord of heaven, [I offer] the sandals. To him, this bali offering.
The worship of Jayā and others: Aiṃ (5) Hmryūṃ, the sandals of Jayā; Gmryūṃ, the sandals of Vijayā.
Mmryūṃ, the sandal of Ajitā; Hmryūṃ, the sandal of Aparājitā; Rmryūṃ, the sandal of Jaṃbhanī; Smryūṃ, the sandal of Taṃbhanī; Kṣmryūṃ, the sandal of Mohanī.
I worship the *ākarṣaṇī* (attracting) sandal; this is the offering for them.

*Haṃśāsanāya*, etc. (8). Worship of Brahmāṇī and the others. Aiṃ (5) A Ā Rudracaṇḍā, I worship the sandals of Brahmāṇī. I Ī Pracaṇḍā, I worship the sandals of Māheśvarī. U Ū Caṇḍācogā, I worship the sandals of Kaumārī. Ṛ Ṝ Caṇḍanāyikā, I worship the sandals of Vaiṣṇavī. Ḷ Ḹ Caṇḍā, I worship the sandals of Vārāhī. E Ai Caṇḍavatī, I worship the sandals of Indrāṇī. O Au Caṇḍarūpā, I worship the sandals of Cāmuṇḍā.
Aiṃ (5) Aṃ Aḥ. I worship the sandals of Aticaṇḍikā Mahālakṣmī. Here is the offering for her.

The Sixfold Worship of the Ḍākinīs Aiṃ (5) Ḍāṃ Ḍīṃ Ḍūṃ Dmlvryūṃ: I worship the sandals of Ḍākinī. Rāṃ Rīṃ Rūṃ Rmlvryūṃ: [I worship] the sandals of Rākinī. Lāṃ Līṃ Lūṃ Lmlvryūṃ: [I worship] the sandals of Lākinī. Kāṃ Kīṃ Kūṃ Kmlvryūṃ: [I worship] the sandals of Kākinī. Sāṃ Sīṃ Sūṃ Smlvryūṃ: [I worship] the sandals of Sākinī. Aiṃ (5) Hāṃ Hīṃ Hūṃ Hmlvryū: I worship the sandals of Hākinī.

Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ, I worship the sandals for Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha. Hrīṁ, I worship the sandals for Jālandhara-pīṭha. Hrīṁ, I worship the sandals for Kāmarūpa-pīṭha. Hrīṁ, I worship the sandals for Oḍiyāna-pīṭha. [Offer] the *bali* to these. The *bali-mantra*: Aiṁ (5) Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrāṁ Hrūṁ Phaṭ! Yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, vetālas, and the guardians of the field (*kṣetrapālas*).
And likewise the Ḍākinī, Mālā, Pūtanā, and Kaṭapūtanā.
Those born of the seats (pīṭha), those of the fields (kṣetra), and especially those born of the families (kula).
The yoginīs, assuming various forms, move about in the sky.
Ten resident women have gathered here in this circle;
they abide by their commitments, and likewise there are others desiring the sacrificial offering.
May all those goddesses be satisfied by these offerings of perfumes, flowers, and other trifles;
may they grant me satisfaction and bestow upon me my desired objects and cherished aims.
Hrūṃ (2) Phaṭ Svāhā. [Perform] the invocation and other rites. Display the Yonibindumudrā. [Perform] the libation.
Thus ends the *Ugracaṇḍā-ugracaṇḍī-deguli*.
Oṃ, homage to the goddess Śiddhilakṣmī; homage!
Now, [this is] for the venerable Siddhilakṣmīdevaguliyā.
The Worship of the Sacrificial Ground (Thaṇḍilīsapūjana): [This consists of] the Thaṇḍiliṅgavana, the Dathupāṭa, and the Bali offerings.

Having sipped water with the triple principle (*tritattva*): *KHPHREṂ HRĀṂ ĀTMA-TATTVĀYA SVĀHĀ* *KHPHREṂ HRĪṂ VIDYĀ-TATTVĀYA SVĀHĀ* *KHPHREṂ HRŪṂ ŚIVA-TATTVĀYA SVĀHĀ* *KHPHREṂ HRĀṂ HRĪṂ HRŪṂ SARVA-TATTVĀYA SVĀHĀ*
Salutation to the Gurus. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Śphreṃ Hsauṃḥ.
Salutation to that illustrious Guru by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which all that is moving and stationary is pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—salutations to that illustrious Guru.

Aiṃ (5) Salutation to the Supreme Gurus. Aiṃ (5) Salutation to the Parameṣṭhi Gurus. Aiṃ (5) Salutation to the Paramācārya Gurus. Aiṃ (5) Pādukā to Padmāsana; offering (bali). Aiṃ (5) Pādukā to Kūrmāsana; salutation to the seat. Scattering unbroken rice (akṣata) at the sides. Aiṃ (5) Hsphreṃ, O destroyer of hundreds of enemies!

*Phaṭ* to the weapon (*astra*) for the abode of infinite power; [worship] the sandals (*pādukā*). The binding of the mouth with the *vajra-mudrā*: *aiṃ (5) khphreṃ hūṃ vajrapañjare svāhā*. Touching the ten openings: *aiṃ (5) khphreṃ cala makule kulamacare hrīṃ hrūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Perform breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the root mantra.

Now, the Nyāsa of the Seers and others (Ṛṣyādinyāsa): Oṃ. Of this Śrī Siddhilakṣmīmārāma mantra, Īśvara is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ), Śrī Siddhilakṣmī is the deity (devatā), HSKHPHREṂ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Svāhā is the power (śakti); its application (viniyoga) is for the sake of accomplishing all undertakings. I bow to the Seer Īśvara on the head. I bow to the Meter Anuṣṭubh in the mouth. I bow to the Deity Śrī Siddhilakṣmī in the heart. I bow to the Seed-syllable HSKHPHREṂ at the Mūlādhāra. I bow to the Power Svāhā in the feet.
Of the two *kalās*: the application (*viniyoga*) is for the accomplishment of all purposes and goals.

Now, the ritual placement on the hands and limbs (*karāṅganyāsa*): *Khphreṃ sakaraśatrupramathani anantaśaktidhāmne astrāya phaṭ.* (4) [This is] the purification of the water-pot (*kalaśodhana*). *Khphreṃ paramahaṃsini sarvajñātāśaktidhāmne aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ.* [Salutation] with both thumbs to the abode of the power of omniscience, O Supreme Swan-like Goddess.
KH PHREṂ! Salutation to the one who bestows the path to nirvāṇa, the abode of the power of satisfaction, with the two index fingers.

Khphreṃ! Homage to the two middle fingers, the abode of the power of primordial awakening that pacifies all calamities and adversities. Khphreṃ! Homage to the two ring fingers, the abode of the independent power that destroys all misfortunes, evils, and afflictions.
Khphreṃ. To the one who crosses the ocean of all calamities, whose abode is unimpaired power, homage to the two little fingers (kaniṣṭhā).
KH PHREṂ SAKALAŚATRU-PRAMATHANI ANANTAŚAKTIDHĀMNE ASTRĀYA KARATARAPṚṢṬHĀBHYĀṂ NAMAḤ. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (kara-nyāsa).
KH PHREṂ. Homage to all the Yoginīs of All Accomplishments! The sandal of the Lord of the Eastern Face!
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment; the sandals of the Lord of the Southern Face.
Khphreṃ! Homage to the one who rejoices in eternally arisen bliss; the sandals of the Lord of the Northern Face!
KH PHREṂ: To the Mistress of the entire wheel of families, the Lord of the Western Face, [I offer] the sandals.
KH PHREṂ | To the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī and the Lord of the Upper Face, [I offer] the sandals. Thus is the ritual placement of the faces (vaktranyāsa).
Khphreṃ! O Supreme Swan-like Goddess, to the abode of the power of omniscience, homage to the heart!
KH PHREṂ! To the giver of the path to nirvāṇa, the abode of the power of satisfaction, svāhā to the head!
KH PHREṂ! Obeisance with VAṢAṬ to the crest-lock (śikhā), the pacifier of adverse calamities, the abode of the power of primordial awakening.
KH PHREṂ! To the armor, the abode of the independent power that crushes all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions—HŪṂ!

*Khphreṃ*, to the one who carries across the ocean of all calamities, whose abode is unimpaired power, to the Three-Eyed One—*vauṣaṭ*. *Khphreṃ*, to the one who crushes all enemies, whose abode is infinite power, to the Weapon—*phaṭ*. Thus is the ritual placement of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*). *Tam* at the center of the eyebrows; *dyam* at the heart; *thām* at the navel; *oṃ* at the mouth; *hrīṃ* at the left nostril; *hūṃ* at the right nostril; *hāṃ* at the left eye; *phreṃ* at the right eye; *kṣoṃ* at the left ear; *kroṃ* at the right ear; *na* at the penis.
*Maḥ* on the anus. Thus is the Nyāsa of the nine gates.
Now, regarding *prāṇāyāma*: with the mantra "haṃ saḥ hsauṃ," one offers the living person through the *iḍā* [channel] into the *brahmarandhra*.
Then, having visualized the entire skeleton as black in color upon the surface of the left armpit, one should contemplate it as being consumed by fire.

Again: (3) *gaṇapataye* (2) on the right arm; (3) *vaṭukāya* (2) on the left arm; (3) *durgāyai* (2) on the right thigh; (3) *kṣāṃ kṣetrapālāya* (2) on the left thigh; (3) *paṃ paramātmane* (2) in the heart.

Having performed the purification of the hands with *ślīṃ paśu hūṃ phaṭ*, having struck the three-sound *tāla* to dispel obstacles, and having performed the binding of the directions (*digbandha*) with *hūṃ phaṭ*, one should perform the purification of the channels (*nāḍiśodhana*) from the *mūlādhāra* up to the *brahmarandhra* by means of the twelve-long *praṇava*, following the path of the vital consciousness residing in the heart.

Having uttered "Haṃ Saḥ" and led [the breath] to the *dvādaśānta* by means of the *saṃghaṭa-mudrā*, one should unite it with the supreme splendor (*paratejas*). Having protected it with the *astra-mantra*, one should rotate the earth-seed syllable *hlāṃ* sixty times for the portion from the feet up to the knees, while contemplating it as dissolved in water.

Having recited the syllable *hrīṃ* forty-eight times (*48*) from the Earth element (*jātv-ādi*) up to the Support (*ādhāra*), one should contemplate it as dissolved into Fire. Having recited the seed-syllable *hrūṃ*, the Fire element, twenty-six times (*26*) from the Root (*mūla*) up to the Heart (*hṛdaya*), one should contemplate it as dissolved into Air. Having recited the seed-syllable *hsauṃ*, the Air element, twenty-four times (*24*) from the Heart up to the Throat (*kaṇṭha*), one should contemplate it as dissolved into Space. Then, having recited the seed-syllable *hauṃ* twelve times from the Throat up to the Sixteenth [Cakra], one should contemplate it as dissolved into its own cause, Consciousness (*caitanya*).

Having thus contemplated, one should imagine the impurity within one's own body being dried up by the *vāyubīja* (the syllable *yaṃ*), burnt away by the *agnibīja* (the syllable *raṃ*), and flooded by the *amṛtabīja* (the syllable *vaṃ*). Then, increasing the twelve elements beginning with space (*ākāśa*)—each joined with its respective seed-syllable—up to the number sixty-two, one should contemplate them as having arisen from their respective causes in reverse order. Having remembered the crookedness [of the body] by means of the earth-seed-syllable (*laṃ*) and the pervasive emptiness by means of the space-seed-syllable (*haṃ*), one’s own body is purified of all mental sins and recreated anew through merit.

Having meditated upon the living consciousness as being of the nature of Śiva, and having recited "I am He" (*so'ham*), one should lead the *jīvahaṃsa* by means of the mantra "I am the living swan" (*jīvahaṃsa*) to its own place, the heart-lotus, and perform the installation of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*). Mantra: (3) *Āṃ kroṃ hrīṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ haṃ saḥ | O speech, mind, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and the vital breaths (*prāṇa-apāna*) of Paraśiva, come here and remain happily for a long time! Svāhā!* Recite this *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* mantra twelve times while employing the heart-gesture (*hṛdayamudrā*).

Then follows the Mātṛkā-nyāsa. For this venerable Mātṛkā-nyāsa mantra: Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), Mātṛkā Sarasvatī is the deity (*devatā*), the consonants (*hal*) are the seed-syllables (*bīja*), the vowels (*svara*) are the power (*śakti*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is for the purification of the body. *Oṃ brahmaṇe* (2) — on the head. *Oṃ gāyatrīṃ* (2) — on the tongue. *Oṃ mātṛkā sarasvatyai namaḥ* — on the heart. *Oṃ aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ* — on the two thumbs.
Oṃ iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ, svāhā to the head. [The *tarjanī* fingers.]
Oṃ uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā) in the center of the two *maya*s.
Oṃ eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ kavacāya hūṃ. [Recite] over the two ring fingers.
Oṃ oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes; [this is for] the two little fingers.

Oṃ aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aḥ astrāya phaṭ. [For] the palms and backs of the hands. Aṃ kaṃ (5) āṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ. Iṃ caṃ (5) īṃ śirase svāhā. Uṃ taṃ (5) ūṃ śikhāya vaṣaṭ. Eṃ taṃ (5) aiṃ kavacāya hūṃ. Oṃ paṃ (5) auṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ. Aṃ yaṃ 10 aḥ astrāya phaṭ. Having thus performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*).

Her body, consisting of face, arms, feet, belly, and chest, was fashioned from the fifty distinct letters; she was resplendent with a radiant crown adorned by a digit of the moon, and was as white as the moon or a jasmine flower.

I bow to Bhāratī, who holds a rosary and a jar, whose every art is depicted on her walls, who possesses the three eyes, who sits upon a lotus, who is beyond the reach of the senses, and who bears the weight of full, no-longer-slight breasts.
Having meditated thus.

Aṃ on the forehead; Āṃ on the face; Iṃ and Īṃ on the eyes; Uṃ and Ūṃ on the two ears; Ṛṃ and Ṝṃ on the nostrils; Ḷ and Ḹṃ on the cheeks; Eṃ and Aiṃ on the lips; Oṃ and Auṃ on the upper and lower rows of teeth; Aṃ on the head; Aḥ on the mouth; Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ on the right arm; Caṃ [Chaṃ Jaṃ Jhaṃ Ñaṃ] on the left arm; Ṭaṃ [Ṭhaṃ Ḍaṃ Ḍhaṃ Ṇaṃ] on the right thigh; Taṃ [Thaṃ Daṃ Dhaṃ Naṃ] on the left thigh; Paṃ Phaṃ on the two sides; Baṃ on the back.

*Bhaṃ* at the navel; *maṃ* at the abdomen; *yaṃ* at the heart; *raṃ* at the crown of the head (*kakudi*); *laṃ* at the left shoulder; *śaṃ* from the heart to the right arm; *ṣaṃ* from the heart to the left arm; *saṃ* from the heart to the right leg; *haṃ* from the heart to the left leg; *kṣaṃ* [at the anus]; *kaṃ* at the mouth.
Thus ends the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.
O Goddess of the gods, he who always recites the mantra with the proper placement [of the syllables], |||
But all that is fruitless for him, like whispering into the ears of a deaf man.
Then one should begin the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). First is the placement of the six messengers (*ṣaḍdūtīnyāsa*).
Aiṃ (5) Hsphreṃ Kāli Kāli Hrāṃ Mahākāli Hrīṃ Māṃsaśoṇitabhojinī Hūṃ Raktakṛṣṇamukhī Devī Hrauṃ Māṃ Māṃ Paśyaṃ Vaḥ Śrīhṛdayadūtī Kālikādevī Śrīpādukāṃ.

Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ! Homage to the Blessed One, Jeṣṭacāṇḍālinī, consumer of the blood and flesh of enemies, bearer of the skull-cup and the khaṭvāṅga staff! Strike (2)! Burn (2)! Vomit (2)! Cook (2)! Huṃ (3)! Kill so-and-so (2)! Devour (2)! Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! To the venerable Duṣṭacaṇḍālinī at the location of the head, [I offer] the venerable sandals.

Aiṃ (5) Aghore Hrauṃ, Aghore Hsphreṃ, Ghore (2) Tare Hrāṃ Hrīṃ, Sarvvataḥ Sarva Sarva Hskhphreṃ. Salutations to you, O Rudra-padmā! To the Śrī-Śikhā-svacchanda at the station of the crest, [I offer] the Śrī-pādukā.
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Urttāliyāsimadiyā Hrīṃ Savapūhaviyavaṭiyā Hrīṃ Diliyāsi Ulakhiyā Hrīṃ Sarvvaṭ Vṛṭ Likhiyā Śrībhelakhi, at the place of the Kākavaca, [I worship] the venerable pādukā.
Aiṁ (5) Hūṃ Guhyakubjike Hūṃ Phaṭ Hrīṃ Rakte Mahārakte Cāmuṇḍeśvarī Aiṃ Haṃ Svāhā. [I worship] the Śrīpādukā of Raktacāmuṇḍā located in the place of the eyes.

Aiṃ (5) Hskhphreṃ Śkhphrīṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ! Strike down all those who have performed, are performing, or will perform any calamity, such as the application of yantras, mantras, or powders—Hana! (2) Draṣṭrākarālī Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Phlauṃ Phlūṃ Ślīṃ Guhyakubjike Astradūtī Guhyakubjikā, [I worship] the venerable sandals (śrīpādukā). Thus ends the Ugraṣaṭka.

The Nyāsa of the Six Ḍākinīs: (5) ḌĀṂ ḌĪṂ ḌŪṂ ḌMLVRYŪṂ | ḌĀKINĪ, protect me! MAMA TVATYĀBHŪ EKṢA (2) SARVASATTVAVAŚAṂKARI ŚRĪPĀDUKĀM || [On the neck. RĀṂ RĪṂ RŪṂ RMLVRYŪṂ | RĀKINĪ, protect me! MAMA RAKTADHĀBHŪ EKṢA (2) SARVASATTVAVAŚAṂKARI ŚRĪPĀDUKĀM || [At the heart.]
Aiṃ (5) Lāṃ Līṃ Lūṃ Lmlvryūṃ!
O Lākinī, protect my flesh-element; protect me! O you who bring all beings under control, [worship] the venerable sandals at the navel.
(5) KĀṂ KĪṂ KŪṂ KMLVRYŪṂ! O Kākinī, protect me (2)! Protect my fat-tissue (medas-dhātu) (2)! [I worship] the Śrī-pādukā who brings all beings under control, upon the Liṅga.
(5) Sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ smlvryūṃ! O Sākinī, protect me! (2) Protect my bone-element! (2) O you who bring all beings under control, [protect] the Śrī-pādukā! Guḍe!
(5) HĀṂ HĪṂ HŪṂ HMLVRYŪṂ! O Hākinī, protect me (2)! Protect my marrow-element (2)! O you who bring all beings under control, [protect] the glorious sandals! [Place at] the center of the eyebrows.

Yāṃ yīṃ yūṃ ymlvryūṃ! O Yākinī, protect me; protect my white constituent (*śukladhātu*). O you who bring all sentient beings under control, [protect] the glorious sandals (*śrīpādukā*) at the thousand-petalled lotus in the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*).
Then follows the placement of the eight Mothers (aṣṭamātṛkānyāsa).
(5) At the sacred site of Prayāga: AṂ Asitāṅgabhairava, ĀṂ Brahmāṇī Ambā Śrīpā [Dvaya]. [This is] on the head.
Vārāṇasī is the sacred field, Rurubhairavaka is the mother Māheśvarī; [this is] in the mouth.
And in the field of Kolāgiri, there is Caṇḍabhairava and the Mother Kaumārī. (3) [In] the ear.
(5) In the field of Aṭṭahāsa: ṬAṂ is Krodhabhairava; ṬĀṂ is the Mother Nārāyaṇī. (3) [This is] the Heart.
(5) In the field of Jayantī, she is Unmattabhairava; [and] that Ambā is Vārāhī. (3) [She is located] in the navel.
(5) At Caritrakṣetra: Paṃ Kapālībhairava; Pāṃ Śakrānī Ambā. (3) [This is] at Svādhiṣṭhāna.
(5) In the field of Ekāmra, [I bow to] Bhīṣaṇabhairava and the Mother Cāmuṇḍā. (3) In the Ādhāra.
(5) Devīkoṭakṣetreśa, Saṃhārabhairava, and the venerable Ambā Mahālakṣmī. (3)
Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the eight Mothers.

Khphreṁ 27. Having recollected [this] with breath-retention (nirucchvāsa), one should conceive of the state of Brahmā through the subtle form of the Root Goddess (Mūladevī), the state of Viṣṇu through the intermediate [form], and the state of Rudra through the supreme [form].

Having thus generated the form of the Self, having drawn the Self—which is supreme bliss—into that form by means of inhalation (*pūraka*), and having fixed it in the heart by means of retention (*kumbhaka*), one should perform the sixfold placement (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*). Therein, first: *hrīṃ śrīṃ*, at the feet of Śrīnātha, in the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmaraṃdhra*); *hrīṃ śrīṃ*, at the feet of Ambā Mahālakṣmī, in the region of the *bindu*; (2) at the feet of Ambā Vyomavāmeśvarī, in the left eye.

(2) Khecarī Ambā Śrī—on the left nostril. (2) Dikcarī Ambā Śrī—on the mouth. (2) Gocarī Ambā Śrī—on the right nostril. (2) Bhūcarī Ambā Śrī—on the right eye. Thus ends the first, the Leftward Sequence (vāmakrama). Now, the gross placement (sthūlanyāsa): (2) Khaṃ—in the heart. (2) Phaṃ—in the throat. (2) Raṃ—in the palate. Aiṃ—in the eyebrows. Maṃ—in the remainder of the skin. Thus ends the fivefold leftward sequence.

*Khphreṃ* at the center of the eyebrows. (2) *Namaḥ sarvasiddhiyoginībhyaḥ* at the throat. *Namaḥ sarvasiddhamātṛbhyaḥ* at the heart. *Namo nityonitanandananditāyai* at the navel. *Sakalakulacakranāyikāyai* at the secret place. *Bhagavatyai caṇḍakāpālinyai* at the anus. *Taṃ* at the navel. *Dyaṃ* at the heart. *Thāṃ* at the end of the twelve [fingers]. This is the first section of the Mātṛs. *Khphreṃ* at the station of Brahmā. *Hrīṃ* at the left eye.

HŪṂ on the right eye; HĀṂ on the left ear; PHAṂ on the right ear; KṢOṂ in the left nostril; KROṂ in the right nostril; NAṂ on the mouth; MAḤ on the crest-lock. This concludes the second section of the Ārṣa [Tantra]. KHPHREṂ O Supreme Haṃsinī!

In the aperture of Brahma (*brahmaraṃdhre*): O giver of the path to Nirvāṇa! At the tip of the nose (*nāsāgre*): O pacifier of calamities and disturbances! In the palate (*tālu*): O crusher of all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions! In the throat (*kaṇṭhe*): O subduer of all foes! On the chest (*vakṣasi*): O Goddess, come (*āgaccha*)! In the heart (*hṛdaye*): Laugh (*hasa*)! In the navel (*nābhau*): Leap (*valga*)! In the heart (*hṛdaye*): O devourer of human blood, entrails, and fat! In the bulbous root (*kande*): Crush, crush my enemies!

At the three paths: *khāhi* (2). At the vulva: *bhage*. With the trident: *bhindi bhindi*. At the shanks: *chindhi chindi*. At the private parts: *khaḍgena tāḍaya tāḍaya*. At the feet: *cchedaya* (2). At the big toes: thus, at the sixteen supports, [perform this] until you accomplish all my desires (2). At the feet: *paramakāriṇī*. At the knees: *bhagavati mahābhairavarūpadhāriṇi*. At the upper part: *ūrdhvāṃ*.

O you who are measured by the thirty-three [gods], in the secret place; O mother of the mantra beginning with the letter *sa*, in the navel; O you who are affectionate toward those who bow before you, in the heart; O Goddess Mahākālī!

At the throat-pit: *kālanāśini* (O Destroyer of Time). At the mouth: *hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ prasīdamadanāturāṃ* (Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ! Be gracious, O You who are distressed by passion). At the two ears: *kuru* (Act). At the eyes: *surāsurakanyakāṃ* (The maiden of the gods and demons). At the head: [the mantra]. Thus for the twelve knots.

Hrīṃ at the aperture of Brahmā; Śrīṃ at the bindu; Hūṃ at the mouth; Phaṭ at the heart; Phaṭ at the six ādhāras; Phaṭ at the navel; Svā at the liṅga; Hā at the anus. Thus is the placement of the nine syllables according to the sequence of the staff. (3)
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Siddha Yoginīs; the sandal of the Lord of the Upper Face.
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment! The venerable sandals of the Lord of the eastern face!
KHPHREṂ. Homage to the one who is eternally delighted by primordial bliss, O Lord of the southern face, Śrī [Heruka]. (3)
KH PHREṂ. To the Mistress of the Entire Wheel of Families, the Lord of the Northern Face, Śrī. (3)
KH PHREṂ! To the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī, the Lord of the Western Face, ŚRĪṂ! (3)
Thus is the placement of the five faces.
Khphreṃ! O Supreme Delighting One, Power of Omniscience, Śrī, the Lord of the Heart!
Khphreṃ! O Śrī Śirānātha, bestower of the path to nirvāṇa, power of eternal satisfaction!
Khphreṃ! O Śrī Śikhānātha, who pacifies adverse calamities and possesses power awakened from time immemorial!
Khphreṃ! O Śrī Kavacānātha, the power of sovereignty who shatters all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions!
Khphreṃ! O Lord of the Eye, Śrī, whose power is unfailing, you are a raft across the ocean of all calamities.
Khphreṃ! O Śrīpādukā of the Lord of Infinite Power, who pacifies all enemies!
Thus ends the Khaḍga-nyāsa.

O Goddess, come! (2) O Śrī Varadanātha, laugh! (2) O Abhayanātha, at the wrist: leap! (2) O Kalaśanātha, [grant] the sandals! At the left joint: O devourer of human blood, entrails, and fat, O Kapālanātha, [grant] the feet! At the left arm: crush my enemies! (2) O Khaṭvāṅganātha, at the place of the feet! Eat! Eat! (2) O Muṇḍanātha, [grant] the feet! At the right shoulder: pierce! Pierce! (2) O Triśūlanātha, [grant] the feet!
Chindi chindi! O Ankushanatha, strike with the sword at the right joint! (2)
At the right wrist of Khaḍganātha’s feet: *chedaya*. At the right elbow of Pāśanātha’s feet: *kalatara*. Thus ends the second gross placement (*sthūlanyāsa*).

[The placement] on the forehead and so forth, in a leftward sequence: *khphreṃ* on the forehead; *hrīṃ* on the eyes; *hūṃ* on the cheek; *hāṃ* on the shoulder; *kṣauṃ* on the arm; *kroṃ* on the fingers; *namaḥ* on the side; *pratyaṅgirā* on the chest; *mahārāvā* on the shank; *mahāśaṅkhā* on the feet; *viviyānā* on the toes; *haḍḍamaḍḍā* on the right toe; *mecālinī* on the feet; *mahākālī* on the shank; *kāmarājī* on the thigh; *vivi āvi* on the side.

*Anthi hanthi* at the fingers and toes; *paramanthi* at the wrists; *soyahanthi* at the forearms; *yauhi* at the shoulders; *bhairi* at the neck; *mano* at the heart; *ca* at the action [center]; *kaṇṭhe* at the throat; *tāhi* at the cheeks; *paṃtaṃgire* at the mouth; *ni* at the eyes; *vajrasajja* at the backbone; *khphreṃ* at the spine; *hrīṃ* at the waist; *hūṃ* at the base [ādhāra]; *hāṃ* at the self-abiding [svādhisthāna]; *khphreṃ* at the jewel-filling [maṇipūraka]; *kṣoṃ* at the unstruck [anāhata]; *koṃ* at the pure [viśuddha]; *na* at the place of command [ājñā]; *maḥ* at the tip of the nose.
Thus ends the third subtle placement (sūkṣmanyāsa).
Next is the placement according to the division of others.

*Khphreṃ* in the *ādhāra*; *sphaṭ* in the *anāhata*; *ma* in the *tāruni*; *hā* in the *bindu*; *caṃ* in the *ardhacandra*; *ḍa* in the *nāda*; *ge* in the *yonirodhikā*; *śva* in the *vyāpinī*; *ri* in the *samanā*; *sphaṭ* in the *manonmanī*; *vrīṃ* in the *unmanī*, *sphaṭ* at the end of *śāmbhava*; *ḍḍīṃ hrīṃ* at the end of the sixteen; *sphaṭ* at the end of the *sūkṣma*; *rvrīṃ* at the end of *parā*, *phaṭ* in the *kula*. Thus is the supreme deposition (*nyāsa*) in due order.

*Khphreṃ* at the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*). *Sphaṭ* on the entire skin. *Ma* at the tip of the nose. *Hā* at the bindu. *Caṃ* at the navel. *Ḍa* in the left ear. *Yo* in the right ear. *Ge* in the left eye. *Śva* in the right eye. *Ri* in the left nostril. *Sphaṭ* in the right nostril. *Vrīṃ* on the left cheek. *Sphaṭ* on the right cheek. *Ḍvrīṃ* on the face. *Spaṭ* on the tongue. *Vrīṃ* on the teeth. *Phaṭ* on the crest-lock (*śikhā*).
Thus ends the fourth [section], the supreme deposition (paranyāsa), according to the sequence of the shaven-headed (muṇḍa).

Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ. At the feet of Tumbaranātha and Mother Brahmāṇī: the skin remains. (3) At the feet of Kamalodbhavanātha and Mother Māheśvarī: the blood. (3) At the feet of Gagananātha and Mother Kaumārī: the flesh. (3) At the feet of Śambhunātha and Mother Vaiṣṇavī: the fat. At the feet of Nīlāmbaranātha and Mother Vārāhī: the bones. (3) At the feet of Suranātha and Mother Aindrī: the sinews. (3) At the feet of Khecaranātha and Mother Cāmuṇḍā: the marrow.
(3) To Saṃdhāyugeśvarinātha Mahālakṣmī Ambā’s feet; at the hair. Thus is the Jyeṣṭhaka placement upon the skin.

Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Ajinanātha on the right foot; (3) the feet of Ānandāmbā on the left foot; Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Ipānātha on the right shank; Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Īśvarī Ambā on the left shank; Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Udayanātha on the right thigh; Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Ūrddhagāminī Ambā on the left thigh; (3) the feet of Ṛddhinānātha.

On the right side: (3) Ṛ, the feet of Ambā. On the left side: (3) Ḷ, the feet of Luptadevanātha. In the right hand: (3) Ḹ, Lūnāḍa. In the left hand: (3) Ekāṅganātha, on the right arm. (3) Airāvatī Ambā, the feet, on the left arm. (3) Oghanānandanātha, the feet, on the right shoulder. Au, Kalālī, the feet, on the left shoulder. (3) Aṃ, Amuranātha, the feet, on the crown of the head. (3) Aḥ, Kṛśānu Ambā, the feet, in the heart.
Thus ends the placement of the eight *yāmalas*. Thus the sixfold placement (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*) is completed.

Prajāpati is the seer (ṛṣi) of this mantra, the Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas), Śrīsiddhilakṣmī is the deity (devatā), and its application (viniyoga) is for the accomplishment of all aims; thus one should recite it.
Oṃ aṃ aṃ, salutation to the two thumbs.
Hrīṃ taṃ taṃ, salutation to the two index fingers.
HŪṂ MAṂ MAṂ MAṂ, homage to the two middle fingers.
Hāṃ naṃ naṃ naṃ, salutation to the two ring fingers.
Pheṃ Kaṃ Kaṃ, salutation to the two little fingers (kaniṣṭhā).
KṢOṂ KAṂ KAṂ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands.

*Kroṃ*, salutation to the left wrist (*vāmamaṇibandha*); *namaḥ*, salutation to the right wrist (*dakṣiṇamaṇibandha*), *vauṣaṭ*. [At the right wrist: *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ*. *Karasphālāya ṭ*. Thus is the ritual assignment of the hands (*karanyāsa*).

Oṃ at the aperture of Brahmā; Hrīṃ at the circle of the face; Hūṃ at the right ear; Hāṃ at the left ear; Phreṃ at the root of the tongue; Kṣoṃ at the heart; Kroṃ at the penis; Namaḥ at the secret circle.

Oṃ, crush my own enemies! Eat them! [Eat them! Homage to the faces of the root [directions]. Hrīṃ, pierce with the trident! Pierce! Cut! [Cut! Homage to the faces of the right [directions]. Hūṃ, strike with the sword! Strike! Sever! [Sever! Homage to the fierce faces of the right [directions]. Hāṃ, accomplish all my desires as long as they last! O you whose face is meditation! Homage to the faces of the north.

Phreṃ! Homage to the feet of Kālānala, the northern face of the Blessed One, the supremely compassionate one who assumes the form of Mahābhairava. Kṣoṃ! Homage to the southern face of Kaulottara, O Mother of all mantras, who is saluted by the best of the thirty gods.

*Kroṃ*, O Goddess of grace toward those who bow before you, to the faces of Mahotkaṭā and Uttarā, *namaḥ*. *Namaḥ* to Mahākālī, the destroyer of Time (*Kāla*), O Phetkārī; to the faces of Dakṣiṇā, *namaḥ*. *Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ*, be gracious and make me afflicted with passion; to the faces of Makaranda, the pericarp of gods and demons, *namaḥ*. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the arising of the faces.
Oṃ, to the Supreme Swan, the bestower of the path to Nirvāṇa, homage to the heart.
Hrīṃ! O pacifier of calamities and misfortunes, svāhā to the head!
HŪṂ! To the crest [mantra] that shatters all enemies of misfortune and the afflictions, SVĀHĀ!
Hāṃ! To the armor that crosses the ocean of all calamities, Hūṃ!
Phreṃ, for the pacification of all enemies, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes!
KṢOṂ KROṂ NAMAḤ | ĀGACCHA HASA VALGA NARARUDHIRĀNTRAVASĀBHAKṢAṆI ASTRĀYA PHAṬ ||

Oṃ, homage to all the Yoginīs of all accomplishments! Homage at the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra)! Homage to all the Mothers of all accomplishments! Homage to her who is delighted by eternal, arising bliss! Homage at the place of the uvula (ghaṇṭikā)! Homage to the Mistress of the entire wheel of the Kula! Homage at the hollow of the throat (kaṇṭhakūpa)! O Blessed One Candakāpālī, it is as follows:

On the right arm: *oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ*. On the shaft of the left arm: *khphreṃ*, O Supreme Haṃsinī, bestower of the path to Nirvāṇa! At the heart: O pacifier of calamities and misfortunes! On the right side: O destroyer of all evils, portents, and afflictions! On the left side: O boat for crossing the ocean of all obstacles! In the center of the navel: O subduer of all enemies! At the secret organ: *devi āgaccha (2) hasa (2)*. In the secret maṇḍala:

Leap forth! O you who consume human blood, entrails, and fat! In the foundation mandala, crush and devour my own enemies! [On] the right thigh: pierce with the trident, cut with the sword, strike, and sever! [On] the left thigh: do so until you have accomplished all my purposes, O Compassionate One of Yama! [On] the right shank: O Blessed Lady, bearer of the form of Mahābhairava! [On] the left shank: [do the same].
O Mother of all mantras, praised by the thirty-three gods, [be present] at the right ankle. O Goddess who is affectionate toward those who bow before you, [be present] at the left ankle. Mahākālī!

*Kālanāśani* | On the right foot: *Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ prasīdamadanāturā*. On the left foot: *Hrīṃ kuru surāsurakanyakāṃ*. On the sole of the right foot: *Hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Between the left feet: *Oṃ ādhāramaṇḍalebhyo namaḥ*. *Hrīṃ* to the navel-mandalas. *Hūṃ* to the heart-mandalas. *Hāṃ* to the throat-pits. *Phreṃ* to the sites of transformation. *Kṣoṃ* to the right nostril-pores. *Namaḥ*.
*Kroṃ* to the nostrils; *na* to the nose; *maḥ* to the circles in the middle of the bow—thus is the *aṅgajāti-nyāsa*.
One should contemplate the placement (nyāsa) of the body of phonemes and the body of words within the mantra, through the non-difference between the Goddess and the mind.
Oṃ, salutation to all the Siddhiyoginīs; this is the placement (nyāsa) for the eastern face. (1)
Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment! The ritual placement (nyāsa) of the right face. (2)
Homage to her who is gladdened by ever-arisen bliss; this is the ritual placement of the northern face. (3)
The placement of the western face is for the Mistress of the entire Kula-cakra. (4)
To the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī. This is the placement of the upward-facing mouth. (5)
*Taṃ* at the center of the eyebrows; *dyaṃ* at the heart; *thāṃ* at the navel. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the body.

Oṃ at the mouth; Hrīṃ in the left nostril; Hūṃ in the right nostril; Hāṃ in the left eye; Phreṃ in the right eye; Kṣoṃ in the left ear; Kroṃ in the right ear; Na at the penis; Maṃ at the anus. Thus is the placement of the doors (dvāra-nyāsa).
Oṃ, O Supreme Haṃsinī, giver of the path to nirvāṇa! [At the head.]
For the pacification of calamities caused by adverse conditions, [place it] on the crest-lock.
O armor that shatters all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions!
The ocean of all calamities has subsided within his eyes.
The destroyer of all enemies in the ten directions.
The weapon-mantra is the ritual placement (nyāsa).

Thus is the six-limbed placement (*nyāsa*). O Goddess, come! (2). One should contemplate the invocation of the Goddess Sakārā as being both within one's own body and outside of it. Hasa (2). One should contemplate her as intent on bestowing grace upon oneself. "O you who consume human blood, entrails, and fat"—one should contemplate the skull-cup (*kapāla*).

In the right hand: "Crush, crush my own enemies! Eat, eat!"—one should visualize the *khaṭvāṅga* [skull-topped staff]. In the left: "Pierce, pierce with the trident! (twice)—one should visualize the trident. "Cut, split with the sword!"—one should visualize the sword. "Cut them down" (twice)—one should visualize the hook (*aṅkuśa*). In the right [hand], as long as [the mantra is recited], fulfill all my desires (twice)—one should visualize the hand granting boons (*varada-hasta*). O you who are supremely compassionate! *Da*.

One should contemplate the hand of fearlessness on the left. O Blessed One, bearer of the form of Mahābhairava, one should contemplate a human skull. O you who are saluted by the best of the thirty gods, O Mother of all mantras, one should contemplate a bell. Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the ten weapons of the arts.
One should meditate upon the one who is affectionate toward those who bow before him; thus ends the seat and the ritual placement (nyāsa).

O Goddess Mahākālī, destroyer of Time! Contemplation of the Goddess who is formless and whose nature is Kuṇḍalinī: HŪṂ. One should contemplate the arising of the Goddess from the support of birth: KHPHREṂ. A flame.

The visualization of the Goddess Rūpā extends as far as the heart: *khphreṃ*. From the heart to the point of the *bindu*: *khphreṃ*. From the location of the *bindu* to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*): "Make the daughters of the gods and demons [who are] afflicted by passion become gracious. By this, the power of subjugating the universe is declared. *Hrīṃ* at the foundation of birth; *Śrīṃ* at the *liṅga*; *Kroṃ* at the location of the bulb (*kanda*); *Hūṃ* at the location of the navel; *Phaṭ* at the heart; *Phaṭ* at the throat; *Phaṭ* at the mouth.

*Śvā* at the station of the *bindu*; *Hāṃ* at the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*). Having thus performed the ritual of placement (*nyāsa*) for the nine syllables located in the center of the navel—this is the procedure for placement—the mantra-body is complete.
Then, [one should visualize] the body of color, resembling pure crystal, with five faces and ten arms.
Seated upon the mahāmudrā posture, she possesses a beautiful body with excellent color and form.
Adorned with a crown of matted hair holding the crescent moon, her locks are dark blue and curled.
His remaining limbs were adorned with great necklaces of various jewels and other ornaments.
White, red, black, and crimson, she is as radiant as white khadira wood.
Adorned with various jewels, with well-proportioned limbs and beautiful earrings,
she has the form of the solar disc and moon, and shines with three or five eyes.
With her tongue lolling out, she gazed with eyes blazing and turned toward him.
She who wears a garland of skulls around her neck, [trampling] various wicked beings such as Daityas.
By this, [he beheld] her whose high breasts were rubbed by necklaces fashioned from jewels.
In the middle [of that river] is the auspicious Dāmodarā, rich with the beauty of its waves.
Adorned with a network of tinkling bells and fine garments, she was decorated with tiger-skin and parrot-patterned cloth.
And you move about now with a trident and other weapons, holding a shaven head in your right hand.
Above [the first] is the Khaṭvāṅga, then the Satpātra, the Pāśa, and likewise the Ghaṇṭā in the north.
Adorned with a pair of knees that radiate the brilliance of a white silk garment and a hero’s bell.
Her two feet were adorned with the gurgling sound of anklets.
Of the one who is very white, three-eyed, two-armed, and single-faced.
And [he saw her] mounted upon the shoulder of Rudra, who was seated in the vīrāsana posture.
Resembling a blazing fire, it was a mass of gathered flames.
Light issuing from the pores of his skin made the sky resemble the color of dawn.
She stands in the midst of the eight Mātṛkās, surrounded by the six Ḍākinīs;
she is honored by the Siddhas and Yoginīs in a place crowded with many accomplished masters.
Thus is meditative absorption.
Then follows the placement of the body upon the feet.

Oṃ namaḥ. Homage to the Siddhayoginīs on the crown of the head. Homage to the Mothers of all Siddhas on the circle of the forehead. On the tip of the nose: homage to Nityoditānandananditā. On the left eye: homage to Sakalakulacakranāyikā. On the right eye: homage to Bhagavatī. On the third eye: homage to Caṇḍakāpālinī. On the left cheek: as follows. On the right cheek: Brahmakhaṇḍa. Oṃ on the left ear. Hrīṃ on the right ear. Hūṃ on the lower lip.

Hāṃ on the upper lip; Pheṃ on the lower teeth; Kṣoṃ on the upper teeth; Kroṃ on the tongue; Nama on the mouth; Viṣṇukhaḍe on the throat; Oṃ Paramahaṃsini on the left shoulder; Nirvāṇamārggade (O giver of the path to liberation) on the left arm; Viṣamopaplavapraśamani (O pacifier of adverse calamities) on the left forearm; Sakaladuritāriṣṭakeśadalani (O destroyer of all misfortunes, evils, and afflictions) on the left wrist; Sarvāpadāmbhodhitaraṇi (O ferry across the ocean of all calamities) on the fingers of the left hand; Sakalaśatruprathamani (O subduer of all enemies) on the nails of the left fingers.

O Goddess, come! (2) On the right shoulder: laugh! (2) On the right arm: *vargga*! (2) On the right wrist: O you who devour human blood, entrails, and fat! On the fingers of the right hand: crush, crush my own enemies! On the nails of the right fingers: eat, eat! In the circle of the *udala* [flower]: pierce, pierce with the trident! On the left breast: cut, cut! On the right breast: strike with the sword! (2) *Phiṃke* and vomit, O right one!

Cchedaya (2) || In the circle of the navel || Fulfill all my desires until [that time] || Kālanatve || O you of supreme compassion || In the center of the womb || O Blessed One || In the circle of molasses || O bearer of the form of Mahābhairava || On the left buttock || O you who are saluted by the best of the thirty gods || On the right buttock || O you who possess all mantras and the essence of mantras || On the left thigh || O you who are affectionate toward those who bow before you || On the left thigh, O slayer || O Goddess Mahākālī, destroyer of Time || On the left knee ||
Hūṃ. At the left ankle: "She who is distressed by the god of love, be gracious."

The two right ankles. *Kuru*. (2) The toes of the left foot. *Surāsurakanyakām*. The toes of the right foot. *Hrīṃ*. In the region below the right thigh. *Śrīṃ*. On the right knee. *Hūṃ*. On the right foot. *Phaṭ phaṭ*. The toes of the left foot. *Phaṭ svāhā*. On the back. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the body and feet.

The Worship of the Water Vessel (Jalapātrapūjā). Then, having fashioned on one's own left side a mandala consisting of a circle marked with the syllable Māyā (Hrīm) and a square, and having worshipped the syllable Aiṃ within the triangle, one places the base (ādhāra), which has been washed with the Astra-mantra, upon it and sprinkles [the water].
Raṃ, obeisance to the ten-fold essence of the fire-element; Phaṭ. (3) Having washed the water vessel.

Khphreṃ. Having established the water vessel there: Haṃ, obeisance to the solar disc consisting of twelve kalās. This is the installation of the water vessel. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kṣīṃ Klīṃ. Having filled it with water, [one worships].
O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu,
and Kāverī, please be present in these waters.
To the moon-maṇḍala, whose self consists of sixteen digits, saṃ. (2)
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Varuṇādevī Hsauṃ. (7)

The nine-syllable mantra: Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ. [Offer] the sandals to the venerable Mistress of the Water Vessel (jalapātrabhaṭṭārikā). Perform the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga). Recite the root nine-syllable mantra. Form the Dhenu-mudrā. Conceal [the vessel] with the Matsya-mudrā. Sprinkle all substances four times with the *tarjani* finger. Thus concludes the worship of the water vessel.

Now, the ritual for establishing the *śaṃyu* (the pacifier). One should fill [the vessel] with water while reciting the mantra beginning with "namaḥ. [Then follow the rites] such as "khphreṃ to the heart," and so forth. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites. One should display the *dhenu-mudrā* and the *yoni-mudrā*. [Finally, perform] the sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*).

Now, the worship of the *argha* vessel: Having placed it between the Goddess and oneself, [one should assign the mantras] to the wheels (*cakra*) as follows: *Hṛdaya* (Heart) to the southeast (*agni*), *Śiras* (Head) to the northeast (*īśāna*), *Śikhā* (Crest) to the southwest (*nairṛtya*), *Kavaca* (Armor) to the northwest (*vāyavya*), *Netra* (Eye) to the front, and *Astra* (Weapon) in the four cardinal directions. *Sarvamantrāsanāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the seat of all mantras). *Aiṃ Kāmarūpapīṭhāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the sacred seat of Kāmarūpa). *Klīṃ Pūrṇagiripīṭhāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the sacred seat of Pūrṇagiri). *Sauṃ Jālandharapīṭhāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the sacred seat of Jālandhara). *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Udyānapīṭhāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the sacred seat of Udyāna).

One should place the vessel support (pātrādhāra), which has been washed with the weapon-mantra (astramantra). [Recite: *Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I consecrate the vessel support of Siddha Mahālakṣmī.* [Offer water for the feet (*mācate*).]

*Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Rāṃ Rīṃ Rūṃ Rmlvryūṃ*, obeisance to the seat of the *argha* vessel for the fire-mandala, whose self consists of the ten digits of the *dharmapada*. Having thus worshipped the support (*ādhāra*), [one worships] upon it, proceeding clockwise: *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*, I worship the venerable sandals of the digit Dhūmrārci; obeisance. (2) *Raṃ*, the venerable sandals of the digit Nīlaraktā. (2) *Laṃ*, the venerable sandals of the digit Kapilā. (2) *Vaṃ*, the venerable sandals of the digit Visphuliṅginī. (2) *Śaṃ*, the venerable sandals of the digit Jvālinī.

(2) *Saṃ* Arccimatī-kalā Śrī; (2) *Saṃ* Havyavāhinī-kalā Śrī; (2) *Laṃ* Raudrī-kalā Śrī; (2) *Kṣaṃ* Saṃhāriṇī-kalā Śrī. Having thus worshipped [these], one should take a single vessel made of gold, copper, bell-metal, brass, or silver, and wash it with the Astra-mantra: *Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Siddhamahālakṣmī Ambā, I establish the argha-vessel; namaḥ*. [This is for] the vessel.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hāṃ Hīṃ Hūṃ Hmlvryūṃ. Salutation to the seat of the *arghapātra* for the solar disc (*sūryamaṇḍala*), which consists of twelve digits (*kalā*) and bestows strength. Upon that, in a clockwise direction: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kaṃ Bhaṃ. I worship the *śrīpādukā* of the digit Tāpinī; salutation. (2) Khaṃ Caṃ. [I worship] the digit Bhrāmarī; Śrī. (2) Gaṃ Phaṃ. [I worship] the digit Kledinī. (2) Ghaṃ Vaṃ. [I worship] the digit Tāpinī. (2) Ṅaṃ Naṃ. [I worship] the digit Śodhinī. (2) Caṃ Dhaṃ. [I worship] the digit Bodhinī. (2) Chaṃ Daṃ. [I worship] the digit Varaṇyā. (2) Jaṃ Thaṃ. [I worship] the digit Ākarṣaṇī.

(2) *Ṛṃ* is Suṣumnā; (2) *Ñaṃ* and *Ṇaṃ* are Vṛṣṭivāhā; (2) *Ṭaṃ* and *Ṭhaṃ* are Jyeṣṭhā; (2) *Caṃ* and *Ḍaṃ* are Hiraṇyā. Having worshipped them in this manner, one should offer incense with: *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Kṣīṃ Khphreṃ*. Having thus offered incense twelve times.
The worship of the argha vessel: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the pādukā for the seat of the argha vessel.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ! Voṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava!

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the breath: Saḥ Saḥ Saḥ, the Supreme Goddess, vomit nectar! Svāhā! (2) Purification of the substances: Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Namaḥ! (3) Khphreṃ to the heart, and so forth; invocation and so forth with the Yoni-mudrā.
Purification of the Elements (Bhūtaśuddhi): Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauḥ Hsauḥ Hsphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ. Thus is the purification of the elements. Self-Worship (Ātmapūjā).

Khphreṃ, salutation to sandalwood for the self. Khphreṃ, salutation to unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*). Khphreṃ, salutation to vermilion (*siṃdūra*). Khphreṃ, salutation to the enchantress of all people (*sarvajanamohanī*). [Flower offering: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ; salutation to the flower for the self. [Apply] three drops of honey (*ali*). Khphreṃ, *sakaraśatrupramathani*, *astrāya phaṭ* (O subduer of enemies with their armies, to the weapon-mantra, *phaṭ*).

Then, one should place the lineage of gurus upon one’s own head: *Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Khphreṃ*, the sandals of Śrīkaṇṭhanātha; (3) Śaṃkaranātha; (3) Anantanātha; (3) Sadākhyanātha; (3) Piṅgalanātha; (3) Khagendranātha; Vidyāmbā; Kūrmanātha; the sandals of Maṅgalāmbā; the sandals of Meghanātha; (3) the sandals of Matsyendranātha; the sandals of Koṅkaṇāmbā; the sandals of Piṅgalanātha; the sandals of Śavarī Ambā.

(3) To the feet of the Guru-nātha. (3) To the feet of the Paramaguru-nātha. (3) To the feet of the Parameṣṭhi-guru-nātha. (3) To the Pūrvācārya-nātha. (3) To the Ādisiddhi-nātha. Having thus worshipped, one should display the five mudrās: Aiṃ, the Yoni-mudrā; Hrīṃ, the Guhya-mudrā; Śrīṃ, the Drāvaṇī-mudrā; Kṣauṃ, the Kṣobhiṇī-mudrā; Klīṃ, the Jvālinī-mudrā.
Then one should recite the Kṣetrabalī: Oṃ namaḥ siddhimahākāle kālikāyai.

Salutations to you, O Trailokyā, who are bowed to by the three worlds; O Kālikā, fierce toward the universe, O Vāmā, who abide within the Vāma [path], who are praised by the best of the thirty gods—salutations to your pair of feet! (1)

To her who is short and long, who possesses the visarga, who consists of the letters a, ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, ya, śa, and kṣa; who dwells within the light, who is shaven-headed, who is HŪṂ, whose form is the universe, who is the supreme bestower of boons through prostration, and who has the serpent as her upper garment. (2)

O Koṭarākṣī, you whose earrings are the moon and the sun, shimmering and trembling; O Mother Nandā, you who are the elder sister of Trāṃhī, and the fierce younger sister with flaming crests of fire; O Sunandā! (3)

Salutations to Viriñci in the utterance of Svāhā; to the one who benefits those who bow before him; to the destroyer of disease and doubt; to Kaṅkāla; to Kālakāla; to the remover of the wrath of the Kali age; and to the one whose bow is strung, beginning with Vāma and Aghora. (4)

HŪṂ! O you who abide in my own form within the faces, you who delight in the supreme, you who dwell in the interior of the *kanda*-cakra, you who are in the void that carries the space of the heart, you who are the terrible, uneven destroyer, O rider of the corpse, shatter [them]!
O Jambhī, Mōhī, Agnijihvī, you who reside on Mount Kola in the abode of Śaśa-Śaśa-Śavara!
O Goddess, in this churning of the Lord of All, [you] destroy the effects of evil deeds. (5)
Drāṃ drāṃ drāṃ drāṃ! O Drāviṇī! Kili kili! O Rabhasā! O Carmamuṇḍā! O Prahārā! Klīṃ plūṃ! O Rata-tattva-vāhā! Kili kili! O Subhagā! O Mantra-vidyā-vagāhā!
Preṃ preṃ preṃ! O Preta-vāhā! Kala kala kahale! At the tip of the noose and the *kaṭṭārikā* knife!
In that which is perfumed by the divine and the super-divine, where ten thousand birds move about, and which is terrible with a gurgling roar. (6)

KṢĪM PHAṬ HŪM PHAṬ! O you whose nature is the *ḍamaru*—ḌA ḌA ḌA ḌA ḌAMARE! HŪM! You who triumph in the abode of the afflictions (*ādhi*), cut through [them] with your weapon! VĀME ṬHA ṬHA ṬHA ṬHA ṬHAMARE KṢEKṢEKĀRE SUBHĪME! I bow to you, Koṭarākṣī, you who grant the most excellent boons, you who are the syllable of the right-hand form.
He he! With the roar of the syllable *hūṃ*, burn, burn! O you who are intensely ablaze, release, release! (7)

O Caṇḍākṣī, you of wrathful form, rend, rend! O Supreme One, you who are intensely fond of wine, O Heroine dwelling in the fire of heroes, you who are intoxicated with the passion for honey, O Blazing One with a flaming mouth!
O Fierce One of one-pointed form, you whose terrible appearance resounds with a deep roar, O Destroyer of Fear!
Phaṭ phaṭ! O you whose form is the sound *phreṃ*, O playful woman smeared with the ashes of the dead! Kaha kaha! (8)
O Mārī, you whose form is the syllable *kroṃ*, who utter "Kaha Kaha" with your tongue, O Kṛṣṇa-Kaṅkāla-Vīṇā;
*kṣāṃ kṣāṃ kṣāṃ*! You whose form is wrath, who laughs "Ha Ha Ha Ha," I bow to you, O wielder of the fierce sword's edge!
I worship you at all times, O you whose mouth is filled with human flesh, who dwell in the seat of sacred conduct.
He he hūṃkāra-sound, la la la la, severing with the sound phaṭ! (9)

Ḍāṃ ḍāṃ ḍāṃ! O Ḍāmarī, bestow boons, bestow boons, O granter of boons! O you of terrible *hūṃkāra*-impulse, O you who bind man with man! Worship, worship at the single station, in the abode of Koṭikarṇa!
You, the hero praised by heroes, restrained by the mothers of the ṛṣis, have been praised as the seat and sub-seat of Yoga.
To him, who is eternally bestowing excellent auspiciousness, [the city] Kāmarūpa has descended. || 10 ||

O Goddess, he who recites this auspiciously renowned *Kṣetrāvalī*—this mantra-lion composed by Śubhayaśas—is freed from all divine and non-divine obstacles; indeed, O Goddess, there is no power capable of prevailing against his power in this world.
Thus ends the hymn to the Kṣetrabalipīṭha of Pratyaṅgirā, within the Vidyāpīṭha of the Jayadratha-prakāśa according to the Śrī Siddhilakṣmīmata.
(3) O Supreme Goddess, O Khecarī whose nature is space,
O Mother who acts for the welfare of all beings, come, O Supreme Sovereign!
O Goddess seated upon the Mahāmudrā throne, whose movement is the stainless moon of consciousness;
O Mother who acts for the welfare of all beings, come, come, O Supreme Sovereign!

"Be present in this maṇḍala, be well-pleased; obeisance! Having thus invoked the digit of consciousness into the form of the Goddess while recollecting the root mantra (mūlavidyā), [one should proceed].

Having performed the rites of invocation (āvāhana), presence (sannidhāna), confinement (saṃnirodha), and manifestation (saṃmukhīkaraṇa), and so forth, one should form the Avaguṇṭhana mudrā and the Dhenu-yoni mudrā, and contemplate that the Goddess has arrived.
Then, having assigned the six limbs beginning with omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) to the Goddess, one should assign the mantra-body to the Goddess.
Then, having fumigated with the nine-syllable mantra: *Āṃ phīṃ phāṃ mahāsṛṣṭi caṇḍalakṣmī siddheśvarī phreṃ phaṭ*.
Then one should recite the *daṇḍaka* in three sections: "O Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, Guhyakālikā, Tripurasundarī, I invoke you; I invoke you!"

The Worship of the Three Deities (*tridevapūjā*). *Khphreṃ*, the *pādukā* for Narāsana. *Khphreṃ*, the *pādukā* for Mayūrāsana. *Khphreṃ*, the *pādukā* for Mūṣāsana. *Khphreṃ thhsrauṃ*, the *pādukā* for the goddess Dambhakī, the great Dhvāṅka, and Kṣatrapāla, [offering] the lamp on the stone slab. *Bali* offering to Vaṭuka: *Khphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ*, three times, the *bali* for Kuraputra Vaṭukanātha. *Bali* offering to Gvaraja: *Khphreṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaḥ glauṃ*, the *pādukā* for Kulagaṇeśvara. [Perform] the invocation and other rites (*āvāhanādi*). [Display] the Tarjanī, Daṇḍa, and Gaja mudrās.

The Worship of the Goddess’s Seat (Devī-āsanapūjā) Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutations to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti). Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutations to the Seat of Ananta (Anantāsana). Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutations to the Seat of the Root-Bulb (Kandāsana). Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutations to the Seat of the Nerves (Nārāsana). Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutations to the Seat of the Petals (Patrāsana). Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutations to the Lotus Seat (Padmāsana). Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutations to the Seat of the Filaments (Keśarāsana). Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutations to the Seat of the Pericarp (Karṇikāsana). Salutations to Dharma. Salutations to the Seat of Knowledge (Jñānāsana). Salutations to Vairāgya.

Salutation to Sovereignty (Aiśvarya). Salutation to Unrighteousness (Adharma). Salutation to Ignorance (Ajñāna). Salutation to Lack of Dispassion (Avairāgya). Salutation to Lack of Sovereignty (Anaiśvarya). Salutation to the Jewel-Altar Seat (Ratnavedikāpīṭha). Luṃ, salutation to the Oḍiyāna Seat (Oḍiyānapīṭha). Vaṃ, salutation to the Jālandhara Seat (Jālandharapīṭha). Raṃ, salutation to the Pūrṇagiri Seat (Pūrṇagiripīṭha). Yaṃ, salutation to the Kāmarūpa Seat (Kāmarūpapīṭha). Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the Rudra-Preta Throne (Rudrapretāsana). Hsauṃ, salutation to the Great Preta Throne (Mahāpretāsana).
Now, meditation.
Aiṃ Khphreṃ! Mahātejomayī Lakṣmī, possessing the radiance of ten million times ten thousand rays, has five faces, ten arms, and is endowed with fifteen eyes. (1)
The Great Goddess is white in color and stands upon a great preta.
In the midst of the eight Mātṛkās, Siddhiyoginī is worshipped. (2)
Licking the corners of his gaping mouth, he has scorched the world with his flames.
By the force of his inhalations and exhalations, he caused the great boundary mountains to tremble. (3)
In some places she is seen on a tree, in some in a well, and in some she forcibly seizes [her prey].
In some places he creates, in others he protects; his independent will proceeds [thus]. (4)
Adorned with ornaments of snakes and decorated by the lords of serpents.
The goddess holds a noose and a goad, with her hands granting boons and fearlessness. (5)
With his left hands, he holds a sword that causes the three worlds to tremble.
In his left hand he holds an extremely fierce khaṭvāṅga, and in his right hand an excellent trident. (6)
Furthermore, the neck was fierce, filled with flesh, and covered in hair.
In his left hand, he indeed holds a severed head, complete with hair, dripping with blood. (7)
In the left [hand], however, is a divine flask and a lamp upon a great jewel.
This is the instruction on the King of Tantras concerning the goddess Pratyaṅgirā. (8)
Pervading the divine realm, she remains established through both her singular and manifold divisions.
The great goddess Pratyaṅgirā is Siddhilakṣmī, the bestower of victory. (9)
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.

Three *añjali* gestures: *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ*, I worship the sandals (*pādukā*). (3) The *bali* offering: *Khphreṃ*. We know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon the ninety-plus [deities];
may that Lakṣmī inspire us. The *bali* offering.
Now, the garland mantra (mālāmantra).

Oṃ, homage to all the Siddhi-yoginīs! Homage to all the Mothers of all Siddhis! Homage to the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālī, the eternal Mistress of the entire Kula-cakra, who is gladdened by perpetual bliss! It is thus: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage! Oṃ, O Supreme Haṃsinī, Goddess who bestows the path to Nirvāṇa, who pacifies calamities and misfortunes, who shatters all evils, portents, and afflictions, who is a boat across the ocean of all disasters, who crushes all enemies—Goddess, come! (2) Laugh! (2) Play! (2) O you who consume human blood, entrails, and fat, [protect] me! Svāhā!

Crush, crush the enemies! Devour! Pierce, pierce with the trident! Cut, cut with the sword! Strike! Sever! [Do this] until you have accomplished all my desires! O most compassionate Blessed One, who assumes the form of Mahābhairava, who is praised by the best of the thirty gods, the essence of all mantras!

O Goddess Mahākālī, who is compassionate toward those who bow before you, O destroyer of Time! Hūṃ! Be gracious, O you who are afflicted by passion! Fulfill the lineage, fulfill it! Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Phaṭ Svāhā! With this [is offered] the bali. Thus is the Mālā-mantra.
*Khphreṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*, and so forth.
Now follows the worship of the thousand-syllable mantra of the illustrious Śrī Siddhilakṣmī.

Oṃ hrīṃ! O Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī, whose face is ablaze, whose tongue is a flame, whose mouth is a cavern, O Bhīmā, O Mahābhīmabhīṣaṇī, O Laṃbodarī, O Viśvāntakī, O Kālagrāsaṇī, O Kālanisūdanī, Hā! (4) O Hāsinī, O Mahābhairavī, O dweller in the terrifying great cremation ground, Hūṃ! O Caṇḍamukhī, O Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī, Hrīṃ Rkṣrīṃ Rvrīṃ Phaṭ! (5) O Mahāharjjabharuṭṭī, O Mahārāvinī, O Haṃsinī, O Grāhaṇī, O Māriṇī, O Mohinī, Hūṃ Jāḥ! (2) Eat! O Vidrāviṇī, Jaḥ! (2) Go away, go away! Rkṣrīṃ! O dweller in the lap of Mahābhairava!

O devourer of great flesh! Drive away! Thrut! Thrut! He! He! O Mahākālī! Thrīṃ Dhrīṃ Hrīṃ! O you who hold a staff against the beast! O Khārvāri! O Mahānaulī! O Brahmāṇī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī, Yāmya Caṇḍamukhī, Āgneyī, Vāruṇī, Vāyavye Kolamukhī! Khphreṃ! O Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī! O Mahākāpālinī! O Bhairaveśvarī! O Caṇḍeśvarī! O Mahābharuṇṭhī! O devourer of the Great Kṛtānta! O all-youging ones! O you who bring joy to the heart! O Jvālā!

O you of blazing form! Hrūṃ (3) Rkṣrīṃ (3) Phaṭ (5)! O you clothed in the skin of a great man-eater! O you who utter the great sound of "Phaṭ"! Strike, strike! Hūṃ! O Ḍamukhi! O you whose face is a flame! O you with a neck like a water-lily! O you adorned with earrings made of serpents! O most terrifying one! O you with most terrifying armlets! O you whose mouth is a most terrifying wrath! O you whose hair and face are ablaze! O Great Caṇḍī! O Cāmuṇḍā! O you who have slain the great Caṇḍākili! O bearer of the *chuṣma* weapon! Ha, ha! Dance, dance! O you who cause the three worlds to tremble! O you who consume blood, fat, and gore! Drink, drink!
Vama (2), ghātaya (2), phe (2), phā (2), muñca (2), khalva (2), sphoṭa (2), garjja (2), ghūrṇa (2).

O dweller in the *kanavīra* cemetery, who resides in the great cremation ground; O you who cause the Great Bhairava to roar! Ha! O five-faced one, with ten staff-like arms, bearer of all weapons; O wielder of the great *ḍamaru*, trident, *khaṭvāṅga*, sword, skull-bowl, noose, goad, water-pot, boon-granting gesture, and gesture of fearlessness, holding blood in your great arms; O you whose body is adorned with great serpents; O many-faced one, thunderbolt of the sky, dweller in the body of the void; O you who cause the great *preta*s to roar; O you with terrifying, large fangs; O flame-mouthed one, with a face like a skull, devourer of vultures, moving within the lotus of the heart!

Subduer of all beings, *hana* (2) *rphrīṃ* (2) *hrūṃ phaṭ* (5). O you who are seated upon a great skull-throne, *hūṃ phaṭ* (5). O you whose body possesses the brilliance of a thousand suns, *hūṃ phaṭ*. O you who are as pure as the rays of ten million moons, *hūṃ phaṭ*. O you whose body is like the fire of the great dissolution, *hūṃ phaṭ*. *Turu hūṃ phaṭ*. Flash forth (2) *rhrūṃ* (3) *rphruṃ phaṭ*. O Sovereign Queen of the Great King of Mantras, *phaṭ phaṭ*. O Garland of Clouds, Great Illusionist, *hūṃ phaṭ*. O Maheśvarī, fierce with lightning, *kṣe hūṃ phaṭ*. Destroy all misfortunes, *hūṃ*.
Phaṭ! O Bhīme, come, come! Hrūṃ krūṃ phaṭ! (3) Hrīṃ! O Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī, hūṃ phaṭ! O you whose body and limbs are empowered by great ashes!

O Trailokyadāmarīśvarī, filled with the entrails of great *naraka* skulls and drinking the wine of blood; O devourer who swallows the three worlds, you who ride upon a buffalo, whose body is seated upon the carcass of a jar-born elephant; O Aghoreśvarī, you who are the Blue Boar, with a mouth made terrifying by most formidable tusks; O devourer of horses, elephants, and donkeys, O eater of great flesh, you who are intoxicated—slay! (2) HŪṂ! O Caṇḍamukhī, Sovereign of all Yoginīs, Great Māyā of terrible form! HRĪṂ! O Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī! TRĪṂ DHRĪṂ THRĪṂ PHAṬ! (5) You who dwell at the end of the sixteen digits!

O you who move within half of half the letter *ha*; O abode of the universe; O you who swallow the universe; O you who remember, remember, remember the terrible [one]; O beloved of the one with the staff of the *ḍamaru* drum; O you who draw forth Time (*Kāla*); O abode of all sciences; O infallible one; O unconquered one; O you whose face is the mother of all; O progenitor of great bliss; O you whose ears hear the bliss of nectar; O eternal, eternal one; O you who delight in enjoyment; *hrīṃ kroṃ mrjṃhrīṃ rvkṣrīṃ rvrūṃ dra phaṭ svāhā*. With this, the offering (*bali*) is made. Thus ends the Thousand-Syllable Vidyā of the Auspicious Siddhilakṣmī.
Then, having taken a piece of the Phalgu wood.

One should offer libations with their respective mantras, ending with "I satisfy [the name] with the venerable *pādukā*," for the lineage of gurus, the *gaṇas*, the *vaṭukas*, and so forth, along with the Goddess together with her limbs (*sāṅga-bhagavatī*). As for the Root Goddess, however, one should perform the libation with the nine-syllable mantra as much as possible. "Welcome! Welcome! (*āgataṃ svāgataṃ*).

Then, first, the water for washing the feet: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, the Mother Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, together with [her] retinue, together with [her] weapons—this water for the feet is offered to the Blessed Lady; obeisance!

Then, the offering of *argha*: *Argha*: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, the Mother Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her weapons—this *argha* is for the Blessed Lady; obeisance!

Then, the sipping of water (ācamana): Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, together with her retinue, together with her weapons—this vessel for sipping water is offered to the Blessed Lady; obeisance!

Then, the bath: With devotion, one should bathe the Goddess of the Gods, who is compassionate toward her devotees, with milk. Having done so, one is honored in the world of Indra after enjoying the earth. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O Blessed One, for you who are with your limbs, with your retinue, and with your weapons—this milk-bath is offered to the Blessed One; obeisance!
The Curd Bath:

One who bathes the Goddess, the beloved of Bhairava, with curd according to the prescribed rite, is glorified in the world of Śiva upon a silver celestial chariot. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her ocean [of attendants], together with her retinue, together with her weapons—to the Blessed Lady, this curd bath; obeisance!
Ghee, honey, and sugar.
He who bathes the Lord of Gods with ghee mixed with honey and combined with sugar attains the fruit of ten thousand Rāma sacrifices.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her weapons—this is the sugar-bath for the Blessed Lady; obeisance!
The bath with pure water.
Having bathed the goddess with pure water while endowed with devotion,
one who is afflicted by all burning sensations is liberated from great diseases.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her weapons—to the Blessed Lady, [this] water-bath, obeisance.
But.
I offer you wine as power, Śiva as meat, and their union as the unsurpassed; I grant you the merit of the vow of prosperity and accomplishment, and the bath of the bees.

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her weapons; [obeisance] to the Blessed Lady, here is the bath of bees (alīsnāna). Therein, one should recite the root mantra. Then follows the wiping of the limbs (aṅgapocchana).
Then Candana: "O Goddess of Gods, please accept this unguent for the purpose of anointing, consisting of sandalwood, saffron, and camphor derived from musk."
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her vehicle, her attendants and retinue, and her weapons—to the Blessed Lady, salutation for the application of sandalwood paste.
Sindūra (vermilion)
Vīreśvarī, the Great Heroine, is accompanied by the ashes of heroes.
O Goddess, it is the supreme attractor of the three worlds, red as vermilion.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her hosts, and her retinue, together with her weapons; sindūra to the Blessed Lady, obeisance!
O Mother of the World, accept this garment; it is pure, supreme, and bestows happiness and prosperity. It is made of cotton; salutations to you.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her hosts, and her retinue, together with her weapons—to the Blessed Lady, obeisance; [this] garment.
The sacred thread.
O Goddess of gods, the sacred thread (yajñopavīta), provided with the Brahma-knot,
was fashioned by Brahmā in ancient times as a garment for the householder.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady for the sacred thread.
View.
Please accept this vision, which reveals the fourteen worlds— Heaven, Earth, and the single Pātāla—
in order to obtain the fruit of divine sight.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady with her limbs, Dṛṣṭikā.
The ear-banner; the five banners.
O Goddess, accept this excellent banner with its pair of ear-like ends and five-colored streamers,
for the sake of attaining the fruit of the five perfections.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I offer] the ear-banner and the flag to the Blessed Lady together with her limbs.
Dūrvā grass, unhusked rice grains, and flowers.
O Mother, O Ambika of the universe, accept these dūrvā grass, unbroken rice grains, and fragrant substances, which bestow fortune, splendor, and victory,
and grant success and prosperity.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady with her limbs, along with dūrvā grass, unhusked rice, and flowers.
A garland of flowers.
O Goddess of the gods, please accept these various garlands, rich with many fragrant flowers, which have been offered by me with devotion.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her attendants, and together with her weapons; [I offer] this flower-garland.

Then, having worshipped ten times with the root mantra, the *svāmin*, the *ugrakrama*, and the *gāyatrī*, one should worship with three handfuls (*añjali*) using the root mantra. Then, one should place the sacrificial offering (*bali*) before the Goddess, separately for each member of her retinue.
Then, as an offering, flattened beans, phalgumasa, meat, liquor, and so forth should be given.
Then, having requested permission from the primary deity for the purpose of worshipping the retinue, one should worship the retinue.

Then the Krama [sequence]: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the venerable sandals of Kulagaṇapatinātha. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable Mother Vallabhā of Kramagaṇapati. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable Kramavaṭukanātha. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable Mother Vallabhā of Kramavaṭuka. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Ukārapīṭha. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Vṛkṣasaṃketa. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable Mother Sarvasaṃhāriṇī. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable feet of Mahākanavīraśmaśāna.
Thhsrauṁ hrīṁ śrīṁ, O Śrīpāda Kṣetrapāla, fierce with the power to destroy all; hrīṁ śrīṁ, the venerable sandals of his beloved Mother, Śrīpādukā.

Then, at the head of the street, the lineage of the Gurus: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Vīranātha (3). (2) Daśakaṇṭhanātha Śrī (3). (2) Krodhamuninātha Śrī (3). Vasiṣṭhamuninātha Śrī (3). (2) Jayadrathanātha Śrī (3). This is the Divine Current (Divyaugha). Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Kaṅkāla Ombī Ambā (3). (2) Mātaṅgī Ambā Śrī (3). (2) Vīrābali.
Ombinī Ambā Śrī. (2) Tribhuvanānandanātha Pāda. (2) Vijayanātha Śrī. (3) Vāmadevanātha Śrī. (3) Garbhānandanātha Śrī. (3) Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Bhadrā Gaurīśvaranātha Śrīpādukāṃ. This is the Siddhaugha.

Immediately following [the mantra] *māravaughap*, one should worship the lineage of gurus with flowers and unbroken rice (*akṣata*) as follows: *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*, the venerable feet of Pakṣānandanātha; (2) the venerable feet of Icchānandanātha; (2) the venerable feet of Ajavaktrānandanātha; (2) the venerable feet of Bindanātha; *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*, the venerable feet of Bodhānandanātha. Thus one should worship the lineage of gurus.
