Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, obeisance to Hetuka Kṣetrapāla. (3) Tripurāntaka; (3) Vahnivetāla; (3) Agnijihvā; (3) Kaṅkāla; (3) Kalālakṣetra; (3) Kapāla. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, [obeisance to] the venerable sandals of Ekapāda Kṣetrapāla.

Then, beginning with Brahmāṇī: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Aṃ 16. To the venerable sandals of Maṅgalā, the courtesan, who is Brahmāṇī, [the goddess] of Indra, at Prayāga, [seated upon] the syllable Aṃ Kṣaḥ Aḥ, and [presiding over] Aśitāṅga Bhairava, obeisance! Aiṃ (5) Kaṃ (5). To the venerable sandals of Caccikāsundinī, who is Māheśvarī, [the goddess] of Agni, at Ilā in Varuṇā, [seated upon] the syllable Ikṣaḥ, and [presiding over] Ruru Bhairava, obeisance! Aiṃ (5) Caṃ (5). To the venerable sandals of Kevatī, who is Kaumārī, [the goddess] of Yama, at Ūhā in Kolāpura, [seated upon] the syllable Ūḥ Kṣaḥ, and [presiding over] Caṇḍa Bhairava, obeisance!
Aiṁ (5) Ṭaṁ (5). To Aṭṭahāsa, to Ṛśāyī, to Harasiddhā, to Khaṭakī, to Vaiṣṇavī, to the South-West, and to the sandals of Krodhabhairava—Ṛḥ KṢa—salutation!
Aiṃ (5) Taṃ (5). Salutation to the venerable sandals of Jayantika, Ḷśāyī, Bhaṭṭāyī, Kaṃdhakī, Vārāhī, Vāruṇī, Ḷkṣaḥ, and Unmattabhairava.
Aiṃ (5) Paṃ (5). Homage to the sandals of Caritra, Airāyī, Kilakīlā, Rajakī, Māhendrī, Vāyavya, Eḥkṣa, and Kapālīśabhairava.
Aiṃ (5) Yaṃ (5). To the venerable sandals of Ohāyī, Kālarātrī, Chipinī, Cāmuṇḍā, Kauverī, Auḥ, and Kṣaḥ, who are the terrifying Bhairavas at Ekāmraka, obeisance!
Aiṃ (5) Śaṃ (4). Salutation to the sandals of the goddesses Devīkoṭa, Ahlāyī, Bhīṣaṇī, Koṣaṇī, Koṣaṭī, Mahālakṣmī, and Īśānī, and to Akṣa and Saṃhārabhairava.
Thus ends [the section on] Brahmāṇī and the others.

Then, *ṣaḍūtī* is the six *ḍākinīs*. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Dhāṃ! I worship the sandals of Mother Dhāmā. (3) Mother Dhāmavatī. (3) Mother Dhāmnī. (3) Vā Vedhyānamaṇḍalā. (3) Rāṃ Raviprabhā Ambā. (3) Viṃ Virājantī Ambā, I worship your glorious sandals; obeisance!
Aiṃ (5) Ḍmlvryūṃ, Mother Ḍākinī, protect me! Pā.
Aiṃ (3) Rmlvryūṃ, the venerable mother Rākinī, [I worship] the auspicious sandals.
Aiṃ (3) Lmlvryūṃ, the venerable sandals of the mother Lākinī.
Aiṃ (5) KMLVRYŪṂ, the venerable mother Kākinī, [I worship] the śrīpādukā.
Aiṃ (5) Smlvryūṃ, the venerable sandals of the Mother Sākinī.
Aiṃ (3) Hmlvryūṃ, I worship the śrīpādukā of the Mother Hākinī.
Thus are the six dūtīs and the six ḍākinīs.
Then, on the twelve petals: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of the Mother Śivadevī.
Aiṃ (3) the Mother Goddess Vegavatī, the sandals.
(3) Khphreṃ, Mother Māyā Śrī! Aiṃ (3) Khphreṃ, Mother Bhadrā, the venerable sandals! (3) Khphreṃ Khiṃ, Mother Khiṅkinī, the sandals! (3) Khphreṃ, Mother Viḍālī, the venerable sandals!
(3) Khphreṃ Yamajihvā Ambā, the venerable sandals.
(3) Khphreṃ, the mother Rakṣakarṇī, the venerable pādukā.
(3) Khphreṃ, Ghaṇṭodarī Ambā, the venerable sandals!
(3) Khphreṃ Caumātā Ambā, the venerable sandals.
(3) Khphreṃ, to the mother Ulūkī, the venerable pādukā.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, I worship the venerable sandals of the Mother Karaṅkiṇī; obeisance!
Thus, on the twelve petals.
Then, on the eight-petaled [lotus].
Aiṃ (3) Khphreṃ, O Mahākamacaṇḍinī of the fierce countenance, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hroṃ Kāṃ, I worship the venerable sandals of Śrī Kākamukhī.
(3) KHPHREṂ CĀṂ Śrīcaṇḍamukhī, I worship the venerable sandals; homage!
(3) KHPHREṂ ṬŪṂ Śrīṭāṅkarī pādukāṃ.
(3) KHPHREṂ BHRŪṂ Śrītāpinī, the sandal!
Aiṃ (3) Khphreṃ Pbhṛṃ, the venerable sandals of Śrī Kavakī.
Aiṁ (3) Khphreṁ Yaiḥ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Yamaghaṇṭā.
Aiṃ (3) Khphreṃ Śau, the sandals of the illustrious Śivādūtī.
Aiṃ (3) Khphreṃ Kṣaḥ Kṣaṃ, the sandals of the Mother Śrīkṣayaṃkarī.
Worship [the deities] starting from the east and ending with Īśāna, using [mantras] ending in *svāhā*.
Then, on the left side of the center and back of the six-spoked [wheel]: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Karaṅkiṇī Ambā Śrīpādukāṃ.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable sandals of the Mother Krodhinī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable mother Sakarṣaṇī, the auspicious sandals!
In the southeast [from the center]: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable Lelihānāmbā.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, Mother Khecarī! Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, the venerable sandals of Bhairavī!
These six are to be worshipped on the six-spoked wheel.
In the left triangle: Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Aiṃ Vajravaiḷacanīye Hūṃ (2) Phaṭ Svāhā. Triśakti.
In the upper corner: Oṃ hlīṃ Vagalāmukhi, paralyze the mouths and speech of all evil ones; nail down their tongues; destroy their intellect! Klīṃ oṃ svāhā!
The Brahmāstra, in the south-eastern corner.
Oṃ hrīṃ rājyaprade hsphreṃ ugracaṇḍe raṇamarddani hūṃ phe sadārakṣa (2) tvāṃ māṃ juṃ sa mṛtyuhare namaḥ svāhā. This is the sword-weapon mantra.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, to the venerable Śaṅkhinī Ambā on the right.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Śivādūtī Ambā on the left.
In the southeast: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, obeisance to the Heart, the power of omniscience. (3) Obeisance to the Head, the power of eternal contentment.
In the northeast: (3) *anādibodhitāśakti* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), obeisance.

In the southwest: *Namaḥ* to the armor (*kavaca*) of the power of self-sovereignty (*svatantratā-śakti*). In the northwest: *Namaḥ* to the eye (*netra*) of the eternally undecaying power (*nityālupta-śakti*). Between the east and the southeast: *Namaḥ* to the weapon (*astra*) of infinite power (*ananta-taśakti*). In the intermediate space between the west and the north: Then, in that intermediate space, the ten self-sisters (*svasṛ-daśaka*). In the east: *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ*, I worship the venerable sandals (*śrī-pādukā*) of Varadanātha; *namaḥ*. In the southeast: [I worship] the venerable sandals of Abhayanātha. In the south: [I worship] the venerable sandals of Kalaśanātha.

In the southwest: (3) Khaṭvāṅganātha. In the west: (3) Śrī Muṇḍanātha. In the northwest: (3) Śrī Triśūlanātha. In the north: (3) Śrī Aṅkuśanātha. In the northeast: (3) Śrī Khaḍganātha. Above: (3) Śrī Kapālanātha. Below: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, I worship the sandals of Śrī Pāśanātha. Having thus worshipped the ten [deities] of one's own [family], [one should proceed].
Then one should worship the Goddess Siddhilakṣmī in the center: *hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ pañcatattvātmaka mahāpretāya hūṃ (2) phaṭ svāhā* (3). Then one should worship Siddheśvara Śrīmahābhairava.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, I worship the sandals of Ānandabhairava Siddheśvara. (3) Then, to the Mistress of the Root-mantra: Rhrjrīṃ Mahācaṇḍa Tejasakarṣaṇi Kālī Manthānehaḥ. (17 syllables) Tivālaṃ Pū. Phreṃ Āṃ Kroṃ Phi Mahāsiddhasamaya Khphreṃ Bhairavi Ghoralakṣmī Varaprade Svāhā. (25 syllables). With that, three times. (3)

Āṃ phiṃ phāṃ mahāsṛṣṭi caṇḍalakṣmī siddheśvari phe phaṭ || (17) || Hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ haṃ phaṭ (3) svāhā || (9) || Khphreṃ namo bhagavati siddhalakṣmīśvarī phaṭ (3) svāhā || (17) || Having worshipped the five faces with these five mantras, one should then worship ten times with the Gāyatrī: Khphreṃ siddhalakṣmī vidmahe kālikāya dhīmahī tanno sakarṣṣaṇi pracodayāt ||

Then, with the one hundred and eight-syllable mantra minus ten syllables, one should worship the fivefold root-nature: *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ*. These most secret and yet most manifest Yoginīs, the venerable Bhairava, Kṣetrapāla, Gaṇa, Vaṭuka, and the rest, the dwellers of the cremation grounds—all of you, arisen within the auspicious Wheel of Siddhis (*Siddhicakra*) at Śāpūlaka, together with your siddhis, weapons, vehicles, and retinues—may you be worshipped with all the ritual offerings! *Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā*. One should perform this worship three times everywhere.

Now, the worship of the retinue: the Six Dūtīs. Aiṃ Hskhphreṃ Kāli Kāli Hrāṃ! O you who feast on flesh and blood, Hūṃ! O Goddess with red and black faces, Hrauṃ! May enemies not look upon me! O Heart-Dūtī, [worship] the Śrīpādukā; O Heart-Kālidevī!

Aiṃ! Homage to the Blessed One, the Wicked Caṇḍālī, who devours the blood and flesh of enemies, who bears a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga staff; slay (2), burn (2), vomit (2), cook (2), hūṃ (3), ṣumukanāya (2), devour (2), hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! At the location of the head is the Wicked Caṇḍālī.

Aiṁ (5) Aghore Hrau Thaghore Hsphreṁ Ghora (3) Tare Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Sarvasarvve Hskhphreṁ Namaḥste Rudrarūpe Hsauṁ. Thus at the place of the crest-lock (*śikhā*). The Crest-Lock-Svacchanda is Aghora. Aiṃ (5) Hskhphreṃ Śkhphrīṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ! Strike down all calamities, including mantras, yantras, powders, and applications, whether they have been performed, are being performed, or will be performed by anyone! Kill them all! Burn them all! O Dr̥ṣṭākarālī, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Phlauṃ Phluṃ Ślīṃ Guhyakubjikā, [grant] the sandals! O Astradūtī Guhyakubjikā, [grant] the sandals! With these, [offer] the bali.
With the Hanubhairava mantra: Oṃ rhrīṃ hūṃ bhañja (3) rhrkṣrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. The bali offering.
Nāteśvara || Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Hūṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to Nṛtyeśvara Mahābhairava, together with the Śakti Śkṣmlvryīṃ Nṛtyalakṣmī, Svāhā! Pādukāṃ! Bali!

The fifth is Vārāhī. Aiṁ (5) Glauṁ Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed One Vartālī (2), Vārāhī (2), O Vārāhīmukhī! Obeisance to Andhā, obeisance to Andherī! Obeisance to Rudhirudhanī! Obeisance to Jambhā, obeisance to Jambhanī! Obeisance to Mohanī! Obeisance to [the goddess] of all the wicked! Quickly bring all under control (2)! Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Ṭha (3) Oṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! [Salutation to] the sandals. The offering.
West: Aiṃ (5) HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda Vīrādhipataye ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ. To the venerable Bhaṭṭārikā of the Western Root Abode, [this is] the sandalwood paste. The offering.
With the *uttarā* [mantra]: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ pādukāṃ. (3)
Kāliyā: Oṃ pheṃ siddhikalāli hrīṃ chrīṃ hrūṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ svāhā. Sandals and offering.

By Tripurā: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klirhrīṃ Hskhlhrīṃ Ślhrīṃ. In the Brahma-cakra, at the Mahodyāna-pīṭha, whose essence is the venerable Caryānātha, presiding over the fourth state (turyā), [I worship] the sandals of the Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī—the power whose nature is the Supreme Brahman, who is beyond the states of waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the transcendental fourth (turyātīta), and who is the very form of will, action, tranquility, and that which transcends tranquility. Oblation (bali).
With Siddheśvarī: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, I worship the venerable sandals of Ānandabhairava Siddheśvara. (3) The offering (bali).

Pañcavaktra || RJJHRĪṂ MAHĀCAṆḌATEJASAṂKARṢAṆI KĀLI MANTHĀNEHAḤ || 17 syllables || PHEṂ ĀṂ KROṂ PHIṂ MAHĀSIDDHE SAMAYA KHPHREṂ BHAIRAVI GHORALAKṢMĪ VARAPRADE SVĀHĀ || 25 syllables || ĀṂ PHIṂ PHĀṂ MAHĀSṚṢṬICAṆḌALAKṢMĪ SIDDHEŚVARĪ PHE PHAṬ || 17 syllables || HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ HRŪṂ PHEṂ PHAṬ (3) SVĀHĀ || 9 syllables ||
*Khphreṃ namo bhagavati siddhalakṣmīśvarī phaṭ svāhā.* (17) Having worshipped the five-faced one with these five mantras, this is the *bali* offering for them.
Thus concludes the worship of the retinue.
Now follows the worship of the wheel (cakrapūjā).
In the ten directions: Aiṃ (5) Lmlvryūṃ Luṃ. To Indra, who holds a vajra in his hand, the lord of the gods, [I offer] the sandals and the bali.
Aiṃ (5) Rmlvryūṃ Ruṃ. To Agni, who holds a spear in his hand and is the lord of splendor, [I offer] the sandals and the oblation.
Aiṁ (5) Mmlvryūṁ Muṁ. To Yama, who holds a staff in his hand, the lord of the pretas, [I offer] the sandals. The bali offering.
Aiṁ (5) Kṣmlvryūṁ Kṣuṁ: to the Lord of the Rākṣasas, the Sovereign of the South-West, who holds a sword in his hand, [this is] the sandals and the offering.
Aiṁ (5) Vmlvryūṁ Vuṁ: To Varuṇa, who holds a noose in his hand and is the lord of old age, [this is] the sandals and the offering.
Aiṁ (5) Ymlvryūṁ Yuṁ: O you who hold a banner in your hand, sovereign of the wind, [I offer] the sandals; the oblation.
Aiṃ (5) Smlvryūṃ Suṃ. To Keberāya, who holds a mace in his hand and is the lord of wealth, [I offer] the sandals. The oblation.
Aiṃ (5) Hmlvryūṃ Huṃ! To Īśāna, who holds a trident in his hand and is the lord of spirits, [I offer] the sandals and the bali offering.
Aṃ Aṃ Aṃ! To Ananta, who holds a discus in his hand and is the lord of the nāgas, [I offer] the sandals. The offering.
Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ, to Brahmā, who holds a lotus in his hand and is the sovereign of heaven, [I offer] the sandals. To these, this is the bali offering.

In the four corners, beginning with the southeast (āgneya): Khphreṃ Rmyūṃ Jaṃ: Obeisance to the sandals of Jambhanī. Bali! Khphreṃ: Obeisance to the sandals of Stambhanī. Khphreṃ Kṣmyūṃ Maṃ: Obeisance to the sandals of Mohohanī. Khphreṃ Smyūṃ Āṃ: Obeisance to the sandals of Ākarṣaṇī. Bali for these [deities].
At the four gates.
KH PHREṂ: I offer my sandals to the Kṣetrapāla Sakalasaṃhārabalotkaṭa.

KH PHREṂ! To the sandals of Mahāsakalasaṃhāra Balotkaṭa Kṣetrapāla, together with his beloved wife Ambā. [Offer] the bali. In the left corner of the triangle: KH PHREṂ! To the sandals of the sacred seat (pīṭha) of Kāmarūpa. At the front of the triangle: [Offer the sandals].
Khphreṃ, the sandals for Jālandhara-pīṭha; within the triangle.
KH PHRE to the seat of Oḍiyāṇa, the sandals! With this, the offering (bali).
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, to the Lord of Heroes, Śkṣmlvryīṃ, [I offer] the sandals. (3) The offering.
Aiṃ (5) Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hraiṃ Hūṃ Saḥ Hrauṃ, O you whose form is Rudra, Hraḥ! [I offer] the sandals. The oblation.
Aiṃ (5) Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ, you who attract the three worlds! Hrīṃ, you who melt the limbs of desire! Klīṃ Strīṃ, you who cause great agitation!
Aiṃ Sauṃ Sa Pādukāṃ. Bali.

Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā! Hrāṃ hrīṃ, O Terrible One, O Non-terrible One, O You Whose Face is Non-terrible! Chāṃ chīṃ, Kini (2), Vicce! [Salutation to] the sandals. The offering.
Aiṁ (5). Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā! Śrāṁ Śrīṁ Śrūṁ! Ṅa Ña Ṇa! O you whose face is not terrible! Chāṁ Chīṁ! Kini Kiṇi! Vicce! [I offer] the sandals. The oblation.
Aiṃ! O Blessed One, O Siddhā, Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ, O Kubjikā, Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrūṃ, O Khagā, O Ghora, O Aghorā, O Aghorāmukhī, Kiṇi Kiṇi Vicce! [I offer] the sandals. The oblation.

The triple *añjali*: *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ*. [Offer] the sandals (*pādukā*). (3) *Bali*: Root mantra for the six-limb worship (*ṣaḍaṅga-pūjā*): *Khphreṃ siddhilakṣmī vidmahe navatyadhika dhīmahi | tanno lakṣmīḥ pracodayāt*. [Offer] the *bali*. Perform the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites, and display the *yonimudrā*. [Perform] the libation (*tarpaṇa*).

Then follows the offering of the bali-oblation: having worshipped each of the goddesses with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), vermilion (*siṃdūra*), and so forth, one should take the water from the special *argha* vessel held in the hand using the ring finger and thumb.
Khphreṃ, homage to the Mahārudra throne.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hraiṃ Hrauṃ Hraḥ, salutation to the seat of Mahābhairava.

Aiṃ hrāṃ śrīṃ hrāṃ! To the seat of Mahārudra, destroy all my obstacles (2)! Accomplish all my desires (2)! Accept this offering of honey, meat, rice, and cakes according to my ability (2)! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

Then, with Siddheśvarī: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ*, [obeisance] to the one seated upon the great corpse; destroy all my obstacles, accomplish all my desires! Accept this offering (*bali*) of wine, meat, and rice according to my capacity—*hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Having worshipped her three times with the nine-syllable mantra.

Oṃ sidhilakṣmī vidmahe, navatyakadhikadhīmahi, tanno lakṣmī pracodayāt. Having worshipped [the deities] tenfold with this, one should offer the bali-oblation to the feet. The offering of the bali-oblation follows the sequence of worship beginning with Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kramagaṇapatīnātha and the others.
With the substance contained in the vessel, by joining the middle finger with the left thumb.

Hrīṃ śrīṃ kmlvryūṃ, O Kulaputravaṭukanātha, destroy all my obstacles; accomplish all my desires! (2) Accept this bali offering with all its attendants! (2) Hūṃ (2) phaṭ svāhā! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! O Kṣetrapāla of great power and fierce mien, seated upon the throne of Death, together with your beloved consort: accept this bali offering accompanied by all ritual services! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Dhāṃ! Salutation to Dhāmāmbā; destroy all obstacles (2)! Fulfill all desires (2)! Accept the offering (2)! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! (3) Dhāṃ Dhāmavātī. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Dhāṃvāyī. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Vāṃ Vedhyānamaṇḍalā. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Rāṃ Raviprabhā. (3) Virājantī.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Rmlvryūṃ Rākinī. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Lmlvryūṃ Lālinī. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Śmlvryūṃ Śākinī.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Hmlvryūṁ Hākinī. Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Śivādevī Ambā, accept the *bali* offering (twice), Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā. Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Ragatyambā.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Māyāmbā. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Bhadrāmbā. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Khiṅkhinī. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Viḍālī. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Yamajihvā. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Ṛkṣakarṇī. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Ghaṇṭodarī. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Ulūkī. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Karaṅkiṇī.

In the same way: Rā Caṇḍamukhī; (4) Ṭaṃ Ṭāṅkārī; (4) Sṛṃ Śrītāpinī; (4) Pṛṃ Śrīpāvakī; (4) Yaiḥ Yamaghaṇṭhā; (4) Mau Śivādūtī; (4) Kṣaṃḥ Śrī-Jayaṃkarī Devī, accept this *bali* offering! (2) Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Thus: Krodhinī; Ḷ Saṃkarṣaṇī; (3) Lelihānī; (3) Khecarī; (3) Bhairavī.
Oṃ hrīṃ, O Varninī, bestower of all intelligence; O Ḍākinī, Vajravairocanī, bestower of all accomplishments, accept, accept this bali! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ hlāṃ, O Vagalāmukhī, paralyze, paralyze the faces and speech of all wicked people; accept the offering, accept it! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ hsphreṃ, O Ugracaṇḍā, destroy, destroy my enemy! Accept the offering! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ, O Śaṅkhinī, accept, accept this offering! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ, O Goddess Śivādūtī, accept, accept the offering! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! To the heart-powers beginning with omniscience, and to the six limbs, accept, accept the bali offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! To Varadanātha, Abhayanātha, Kalaśanātha, Khaṭvāṅganātha, Guṣṭanātha, Triśūlanātha, Aṅkuśanātha, Kapālanātha, and Pāsanātha—svāhā! To these ten, accept, accept the bali offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ balim gṛhṇa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hāṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Siddheśvara, who is the form of Ānandabhairava, accept, accept the bali offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
RHRĪṂ! O Mahācaṇḍa, O Tejaḥsaṃkarṣaṇī Kālī, accept this offering in Manthāna! HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ!

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hraiṃ Hrauṃ Haḥ! To the seat of Mahārudra, destroy, destroy all my obstacles; accomplish, accomplish all my desires; accept this offering, accept it; grant me success, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ! To these most secret Yoginīs, to those dwelling in the manifest foundations, to all the Bhairavas who reside in every cremation ground, together with their vehicles, retinues, and attendants—accept this offering! (2) Accomplish, accomplish all my desires! Forgive me, forgive me! Kṣāṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
The Bali Viṣamantra: Thaṇḍi likha valāli thupāṭa balisa.
Hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ! O Devīputra Vaṭukanātha, radiant with a mass of tawny matted hair, three-eyed, flame-faced one, destroy all obstacles! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
O Vaṭukanātha, together with Vallabhāmbā, accept this offering (bali); svāhā! Thus ends the offering to Vaṭuka.

On a clean spot of ground, having offered a handful of parched grain, one should recite: *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Thhsrauṃ Hūṃ! To the Lord of this very place, together with his beloved consort, Svāhā!* Thus is the field-oblation (*kṣetrabali*).

On the bare ground, at the edge of the fire-pit, [is placed] the *bali* for Gaṇapati: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ oṃ gaṃ, to Gaṇapati together with his wife Vayabhāmbā, accept this *bali*. Phaṭ svāhā. Thus is the *bali* for Gaṇapati.
On the bare ground, near the *javā* flower, the *laṅghu*, the *pāṭa*, and the *balisa*: *hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ sarvayoginībhyaḥ sarvapīṭhebhyaḥ sarvakṣetrapālebhyaḥ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
Thus ends the offering to the Yoginīs.
The mantra for the offering of the *thaṇḍila* (sacred ground), flowers, incense, lamps, food, and bali: the *samaya-vidyā*. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Cakrayogeśvarī.

O Candrapīṭha, O Vyomakālī, O Mātaṅgī-like Kālī, O Kāmarūpiṇī, O Siddhikālī, O Pūrṇagiri Candrakālī, O Jālandharī Caṇḍakālī, O Oḍiyāṇī Raktakālī! Grant the attainment of all samayas! (2) Excellent accomplishment! Excellent diffusion! (2) Glorious diffusion! (2) He Saḥ Svaḥ 41 Hi Hi Hrīṃ Hūṃ Vāhi (2) Kāhi (2) Khāhi (2) Khe Hūṃ Lāṃ Khāṃ Khāṃ Lāṃ Chchāṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Rāṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ Sau Hre Heṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ Kve(?).
Thus ends the Samaya-vidyā of the Fortune of the Accomplishment of the Pīṭhas.
Khphreṃ: Śivā Bhagavatī, as well as Māyā and Bhadrā;
Kiṅkiṇī and Vimalā, Yamajihvā, and Tvakkarṣaṇī.
Ghaṇṭodarī, Cauramātṛ, Kiṅkiṇī, and likewise Kākinī—
[these are] for the destruction of all obstacles and the warding off of all enemies.
May all prosperity always be completely fulfilled for me. O Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, you who are the thirteenth confluence, accept this offering! Svāhā!
The garland-mantra is *baliviyamāla*.

The rites beginning with invocation (*āvāhana*). One should display the six mudrās: the lotus (*padma*), the linga, the śakti, the arrow (*nārāca*), the *mahādbhāga*, and the womb (*yoni*). The libation (*tarpaṇa*). (3)
Thus ends the *Śrīsiddhilakṣmīdevīguhya*.

Now, for the worship of the *śrī-guhyakālī-deśaguru* on the sacrificial ground (*thaṇḍila*). [This includes] the worship of the sacrificial ground, the offering of the *karapāṭa-bali*, and the ritual rinsing of the mouth (*ācamana*) with the three truths (*tritatva*). [Then follows] the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *svāhā astrāya phaṭ*. [The assignment of mantras to the fingers]: *oṃ phreṃ* to the little fingers (*kaniṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ*); *siddhikalāli* to the ring fingers (*anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ*); *hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ* to the middle fingers (*madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ*); *strīṃ* to the index fingers (*tarjjanībhyāṃ namaḥ*); *namaḥ* to the thumbs (*aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ*).

Svāhā to the weapon; salutations to the two elbows (*kalapṛṣṭha*). [This is] the *kalanyāsa*. Oṃ Phreṃ, salutation to the heart. Siddhikalāli, svāhā to the head. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (*śikhā*). Strīṃ Phreṃ, hūṃ to the armor (*kavaca*). Namaḥ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes. Svāhā, phaṭ to the weapon. [This is] the *karāṅganyāsa* (placement on the hands and limbs).

Worship of the Argha Vessel (*arghapātrapūjā*). The sandals for the seat of the argha vessel: *oṃ phreṃ siddhikalāli hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ svāhā*. (3 times). *Phreṃ* for the heart, and so forth. *Oṃ haṃ 9 siddhikalāliśvarāya namaḥ*. (9 times). Invocation and so forth; the veiling with the *ākarṣaṇī-mudrā*. Invocation and so forth; the *dhenu-mudrā* and *yoni-mudrā*. The *Gāyatrī*: *Oṃ phreṃ mahātantrāya vidmahe, kālasaṃkarṣaṇī dhīmahi, tanno śaktiḥ pracodayāt*.

Self-Worship (*ātmapūjā*) Oṃ phreṃ, [worship] the sandals of Candra. Oṃ phreṃ, [worship] the *akṣata* grains. Oṃ phreṃ, [worship] the *siṃdūra*. Oṃ phreṃ, [worship] the sandals of Mohanī. Oṃ, [worship] the sandals of Puṣpa. The three dots (*bindu-traya*). Khphreṃ Oṃ Phreṃ, obeisance to those consisting of the full moon.
The Seat: Oṃ phreṃ, homage to the seat of the seven skulls. Oṃ phreṃ hūṃ, homage to the seat of Mahāśiva.
Now, as for meditative absorption (dhyāna).
O Mahākālī, you are exceedingly secret, ten-faced, and three-eyed;
you are black-hued, possessed of great splendor, with infinite arms and a slender waist. (1)
One should meditate upon the goddess Nānāvarṇamukhī, whose nature is the essence of the sun.
Clad in a tiger skin and adorned with ornaments of human bone. (2)
In his right hands he holds a trident, a *kuśa*-grass vajra, and a mallet;
likewise, in his left hands he holds a *khaṭvāṅga*, a noose, a vessel, a skull-cup, and a severed head. (3)
Wandering through the king of sequences, which resembles a thousand spokes, she proceeds toward the single accomplishment for the sake of the middle meaning of the eight extremes. (4)
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
Oṃ phreṃ siddhikarāli hrīṃ chrīṃ pluṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ svāhā pādukāṃ. (3) Triple añjali. Bali.
Now follows the science of enjoyment.

Oṃ, homage to Mahāmāyā! Hūṃ Phreṃ! O protector of the three worlds! Śrīṃ Cchrīṃ Siddhi! Hrīṃ Hrīṃ! Sustain, sustain! Bestow, bestow! Wherever there be wealth, grain, jewels, gold, silver, wives, servants, and great treasures—O Mahāgaurī, remember me! Grant great intelligence, fame, sovereignty, and good fortune! O you who grant all things and perform every rite, O Siddhicāmuṇḍā, fulfill, fulfill! Hrīṃ! Rain down, rain down all desires and all prosperity! Shower it down, shower it down! Cause it to fall, cause it to fall! Great Treasure!

Dada (2), and grant (2) sons, wealth, long life, good fortune, a treasure-store, grain, and gold (2). Grant (2) thus all success (2), wealth (2), hrīṁ (2), strīṁ pheṁ! Rain down (2) a shower of jewels; manifest (2) all the factions! Ājñā! (Command!)

Padma (2), bestow glory and sovereignty (2), make it free from obstacles (2). Homage to the Great Yakṣa King! Hrīṃ (3) Śrīṃ (3) Strīṃ (3)! O giver of great wealth, fulfill all my accomplishments for me! Siddhigaurī Hūṃ (2)! Homage! Svāhā! Thus ends the Knowledge-Mantra of Enjoyment (*bhogavidyā*).

The Bali offering: *Phreṃ*, may we know Kāpālinī; we meditate upon Siddhikarālī; may that Śuṣkā inspire us. [Gāyatrī mantra. The Bali offering: *Oṃ phreṃ siddhi hsphreṃ hskhphreṃ khphreṃ karāli khphreṃ hskhphreṃ hsphreṃ phreṃ oṃ svāhā*. (3) The Bali offering: *Oṃ* to the heart, and so forth.

The Worship of the Retinue (*parivārapūjā*). In the Ocean of Blood (*śoṇitārṇava*): *Oṃ hūṃ kṣīṃ klīṃ phreṃ phreṃ phreṃ śoṇitārṇava-pādukāṃ*. The Offering (*bali*): *Indrādi-daśalokapāla-pādukāṃ*. *Kṣetra-vaṭuka-yoginī-gaṇapatīnātha-pādukāṃ*. *Oṃ śrīkaṇṭhanāthādyaṣṭakalāmbādyaṣṭagurupaṃkti-śrīpādukāṃ*. *Oṃ haṃ jayāvahādyaṣṭaśmaśānayā*. *Oṃ phreṃ osadi ṣoḍaśakālī-pādukāṃ*.

Oṃ Phreṃ! Protect, protect the twelve Kālīs beginning with Sṛṣṭikālī. Oṃ Phreṃ! Protect, protect Brahmavatyājyeṣṭhakālī. Oṃ Phreṃ! [I worship] the sandals of the eight Bhairavas beginning with Asitāṅga.

Oṃ phreṃ, [I worship] the sandals of Raktādinakālī hsphreṃ Gaṇakālī. Khphreṃ, [I worship] the sandals of Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī Sṛṣṭikālikāmbā. Hskhphreṃ, [I worship] the sandals of Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī Sthitikālikāmbā.
Khphreṃ, the sandals of Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī Anāsthākālikāmbā.

KH PHREṂ MAHĀ CA YOGĪŚVARĪ BHĀSĀKĀLIKĀMBĀ PĀDUKĀM. With this, the bali offering [is made]. [The rites of] āhūnā and so forth [are performed]. The yoni-guhyamudrā [is displayed]. The tarpaṇa [offering is made].
Thus ends the Śrī-Guhyakālī-deguli.

Now, for the worship of the deity Tripurasundarī on the sacrificial ground (*thaṇḍilī*). [Perform] the offering of the *balis* with the *navāvaraṇa-pāṭha* upon the sacrificial ground. Perform the sipping of water (*ācamana*) by means of the three truths (*tritatva*). The ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *Sauḥ astrāya phaṭ* (4). The empowerment of the jar (*kalaśa*): *Aiṃ aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ* | *Hrīṃ tarjjanībhyāṃ namaḥ* | *Sauḥ madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ* | *Aiṃ anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ* | *Klīṃ kanīṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ* | *Sauḥ karatarapṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
The deposition of the parts.
Aiṃ, salutation to the heart.

*klīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *sauṃḥ* to the crest-lock, *vaṣaṭ*; *aiṃ* to the armor, *hūṃ*; *klīṃ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; *sauṃḥ* to the weapon, *phaṭ*. Thus is the ritual placement of the limbs (*kalāṅganyāsa*).

Worship of the Argha Vessel: *Namaḥ* to the seat of the argha vessel. *Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ*, [offer] the sandals. (3) *Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ*, [recite] "to the heart," and so forth. Perform the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites. Form the *yonimudrā*. Self-worship: *Aiṃ*, [offer] sandalwood and the sandals; unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*); vermilion (*sindūra*); *Mohani*, [and offer] the sandals. *Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ*, [offer] the self-flower (*ātmapuṣpa*), *namaḥ*. [Offer] the drop (*bindu*). *Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ*, [offer] the sandals. (3)
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, salutation to the one seated upon a red lotus throne.
Now, meditation.
"I worship the Supreme Goddess, who has the luster of the orb of the rising sun, who possesses four arms and three eyes, and who holds a noose, a goad, and two arrows"— thus is the visualization.

Having measured out Tripurabhairavī, then follows the worship of the Goddess’s seat: "Obeisance to the seat of the five pretas. [Three añjalis. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kilhrīṃ Hiklkṣrīṃ Sklhrīṃ, the sandals of the Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī. (3) The offering: Aiṃ, may we know Trirāyā; O Kāmeśvarī, may Thou inspire our intellect. The offering.
Worship of the retinue (parivārapūjā). Libation (tarpaṇa): Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I offer] the sandals of the Nityās beginning with Kāmeśvarī. Oblation (bali): Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, [I offer] to the Heart, etc.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals for Indra and the other ten guardians of the worlds. The offering. The deities of the weapons, Vajra and the rest. (2) Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals for the goddesses who bestow the supernatural powers, Aṇimā and the rest. (2)

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ [to] Asitāṅga and others; Āṃ [to] Brahmāṇī and others; the venerable sandals of the goddesses of mudrās beginning with Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī; Aṃ Āṃ Sauḥ, the eternal sovereign of the wheel, Tripurā, the venerable sandals.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ā Ū, the eternal digit (Kalā) of Nityā, whose form is the attractor of desire (Kāmākarṣaṇī), [I worship] the venerable sandals (Śrīpādukā).
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, Tripureśī, the Mistress of the Cakra, [is] Nītyā Śrīpā [2].

Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, [I worship] the feet of the goddess Anaṅgakusumā and the others, Śrīpādukā (2). Hrīṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, [I worship] the feet of Tripurasundarī, the Mistress of the Cakra (Cakreśvarī), the Eternal One (Nityā), Śrīpādukā (2). [I worship] the feet of the goddess who bestows all accomplishments (Sarvasiddhipradā), and so forth, Śrīpādukā.
Hsaiṃ Hsklīṃ Hsauṃḥ. Tripurā, the Sovereign of the Śrīcakra, the Eternal One, the venerable Pā (2).
[The mantra] beginning with "siddhi" for all limbs, O Goddess Śrīpā... Hrīṃ Klīṃ Hāṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of the eternal Mistress of the Wheel, Tripuramālinī.
Aṃ 16 Rv-lūṃ, the goddess Vaśinī, the deity of speech, and so forth; [this is] the venerable foot of the Goddess (Śrīpā).
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Sauṁḥ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Tripurāsiddhā, the eternal Mistress of the Cakra.
The deity of weapons such as the arrow is Śrīpā [thavatenaṃ baliḥ]. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, the sandals.

Kilhrīṃ! In the fire-chakra, in the abode of Kāmagiri, whose essence is Mitriśanātha, presiding over the waking state, [I worship] the goddess Śrī Kāmeśvarī, the power of Rudra whose nature is the will-power, at the feet of Śrīpā [dava]. (2)

Hskhlhrīṁ! In the solar wheel at the sacred seat of Jālandhara, consisting of the sixty lords, presiding over my own tenfold state, [I worship] the goddess Śrī Vajreśvarī, whose essence is Viṣṇu and whose power is Śrīpā (2).

Sklhrīṃ! In the lunar wheel (*somacakra*), within the cavern of the Pūrṇagiri seat, whose nature is Uḍḍīśa, which consists of the eight states of deep sleep (*suṣuptidaśā*), and whose essence is the power of action (*kriyāśakti*), [I worship] the Goddess Śrī Bhagamālinī, the power of the Self of Brahman, at the feet of Śrī [the Guru]. (2)
Hsaiṁ Hślīṁ Hsauṁḥ, the eternal Cakreśvarī Nityā Tripurāmbā, [is] at the feet of Śrī. (2)

Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Kilhrīṁ Skhlhrīṁ Sklhrīṁ. At the great garden-pīṭha of Brahma-yajña, whose essence is the venerable Carya-natha, presiding over the fourteenth state, O Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, whose nature is the supreme Brahman—the power whose form transcends waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the fourth state, and who is beyond will, knowledge, action, and peace—[I bow to] the venerable feet [of the Goddess]. (2)
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Krihlhskhlmklhrīṁ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Śrī Mahāsaptadaśī Nityā.

Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Sauṃḥ Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kilhrīṃ Hskhlhrīṃ Sklhrīṃ Sauṃḥ Aiṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Mahātripurasundarī Śrīpādukāṃ. (Triple añjali: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kilhrīṃ Hskhlhrīṃ Sklhrīṃ Śrīmahātripurasundarīdevī Pādukāṃ. With these [mantras], offer the *bali*. Hsauṃ Hsklrīṃ Hsauṃ Mahātripurabhairavī Pādukāṃ. *Bali*. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, "Hṛdayāya Namaḥ" and so forth. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites.
The Yoni-mudrā. The libation.
Thus ends the *Śrītripurasundarī-deguri*.
Now, the mantra for the Bali offering: On the sacrificial ground (thaṇḍilī), after the fire has been kindled, the Bali offering is placed in the western direction;
the Bali offering is for Ṅā Sukalākā.
Aiṃ (5). All the pīṭhas, as well as the gates and sub-gates, the fields, sub-fields, and gathering places, are situated throughout all directions.
All the yoginīs and the lords of the heroes of yoga assembled there.
This great wheel, the Parvva, is Śrīnātha, the bestower of boons upon me.
O Goddess, for those devotees who are intent upon the teaching and devoted to the worship of the Guru’s feet,
may my grace of all accomplishments always be theirs, O Goddess.
O Goddess, those on this earth who hate the heroes and the yoginīs— them you have granted as a sacrificial offering (bali) here, O Lady, in the assembly of the conduct of the covenant (samayācāra).
May the hosts of Yoginīs, swarming together, cut away the hearing, memory, mental nourishment, flesh, fat, bone, and life-force of the wicked.
May those [deities] crowded with hosts of Yoginīs cut away wicked ill-omens such as kuhukas, bad dreams, and evil portents, as well as the evil utterances of the malevolent.
Among the syllables beginning with Oṃ, those which are proclaimed as the three essential seats (pīṭhas)—
namely Oṣadhī, Dhātu, and Sandhohā— are located in the cardinal and intermediate directions.
In the great earth, the netherworld, the cosmic egg, and in all other places, may the practitioners,
their souls united with Yoga, abide together with the Yoginī according to the sacred convention (samaya).
O heroes of heroic deeds, O lords of great heroes, may the deities abide in truth;
and may the Siddhas, the Putrakas, the Ācāryas, and the Sādhakas lie upon the earth.
Whether in a city, or in a village, or in a forest, or at the confluence of two rivers.
Or at a pond, a well, a solitary tree, a cremation ground, or a circle of Mothers.
May the various Vaṭaja spirits, assuming manifold forms,
all be satisfied and accept the offering from every side.
Even though I have come to them for refuge, they grant all this fruit:
whatever karma has been acquired by me, whatever I shall do, and whatever has already been done.
Satisfied by the offering of oblations and flowers, may you be mindful of me;
may all my actions be successful, and may all my faults be pacified.
By the grace of Śiva and Śakti, I bow to the venerable Kukārā. This is the *samaya* offering (*samayabali*).

Three *añjali* with the root mantra. (3) The shadow of Nirvāṇa. Shaking the great power of the *tvāka*. Invocation and so forth. The *yonimudrā*. Libation (*tarpaṇa*). Thus ends the ritual procedure for the western direction.

On the bare ground, near the fire, at the base of the stūpa, and at the shrine of Tumbeśvara, there is an offering (*bali*). It is an offering for the *ṅāsukalākāyā* spirits. Oṃ khphreṁ! To the yoginīs who move through the sky, to the yoginīs who move on the earth, to the yoginīs who move in the cardinal directions, and to the yoginīs who move in the great void: this *bali*—accompanied by meat, rice, *caru*, lamps, and betel—is offered. Hrīṁ (3) svāhā!

Oṃ glauṃ glāṃ! To Gaṇapati, grant the prosperity of dharma, artha, kāma, and śrī; O Gaṇa, bestow success! Accept this worship and this bali offering; protect [us]! [Twice]! Establish peace! [Twice]! Svāhā!

Oṃ, homage to those who cause obstacles! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kṣyā Kṣya! To the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla), with tawny matted hair—accept incense, light, flowers, liquor, and meat! (Twice) O you in the form of Bhairava, forgive me and grant me boons! Svāhā! Aiṃ Hrīṃ! To the son of the Goddess, Vaṭuka, with tawny matted hair and tawny eyes—accept the sacrificial offering! (Twice) By the grace of your feet, may there be no obstacles for me! Svāhā!
The root mantra for the three *añjali* gestures; (3) the *bali* offering; the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) ritual.
Nirvāṇa; the great powerful [mantra] for subduing; the invocation and so forth; the *yonimudrā*; the libation (*tarpaṇa*). Thus ends the ritual procedure for the *deguli* of Jayatuṃbeśvarī.

On the bare ground, at the crossroads, or at the foot of a tree, this is the *bali* offering for Śikhā-Mahākāla. It is to be offered to the one whose form is like the crescent moon. OṂ KHPHREṂ PHRUṂ HŪṂ! O Raudra, Raudra Mahākāla, with fierce fangs, terrifying one, Lord of the cremation ground (*śmaśāna-pīṭha*), Great Destroyer, you who utter the *phetkāra* sound, you who gather together dogs, you who assume various forms, Sovereign, Piśāca, Bhūta, Vetāla, Preta, and Rākṣasa, you who are clothed in the directions of space, possessing a great body, with a luster like crushed collyrium, wearing a garland of severed heads, O fearsome one! [Accept this offering.]

O wielder of the khaṭvāṅga, red-eyed one, most fierce, who delights in liquor, meat, and fat; accept this entire offering! O Ali, together with Phalgu and Vaśā, along with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, I have appointed you as my servant. O protector of the assembly, be patient and grant me boons! Svāhā! Hūṃ! Namaḥ!
Three handfuls with the root mantra (2). (3). The offering (bali).

The six-limbed [rite], *nirvāṇa*, the great offering (*tvākamahābali*) for shaking off [impurities], the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth, the *yonimudrā*, and the libation (*tarpaṇa*). Thus ends the ritual procedure for the *śikhā* and the Great Kāla (*Mahākāla*) deity.
On a clean, dustless spot, this is the offering for Ugracaṇḍā and Ugracaṇḍī: "Oṃ, this is the offering for the body of the Nāga-kalā. Aiṃ! Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, and Aparājitā.
Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Bhīmā, and Kalā—thus is the group of eight.
Diviyoginī, Mahāyoginī, Siddhiyoginī,
Gaṇeśvarī, Sākinī, Kālarātrī, Ūrdhvakeśī, and Niśācarī.
Gambhīrā, Ghoṣaṇī, Sthūrā, Pavanāgī,
Ulomikā, Bhīṣaṇā, Mahānandā, and likewise Jvālāmukhī.
Piśācī, Hastinī, Jakṣaṇī, and likewise Dhūjaṭī;
Viṣabhakṣī, Sarvasiddhi, Tuṣṭi, and likewise Icchā.
Hūṃkārī, Bhāsvarī, Dīrghā, Dhūmrākṣī, Kalahapriyā,
Mataṅgī, Kākadūṣṭī, as well as Triśūlā and Antakā.
The Rākṣasī Ghoranāda, Raktāṅgī, Viśvarūpiṇī,
Jayaṃkarī, Vibhañcī, Suskāṅgī, and Narabhojanī.
Vīrabhadrā, Mahākālī, Kaṅkālī, Vikṛtānanā, Krodharā,
Bhīmabhadrā, Vāyuvegā, and Bhayānanā.
Brāhmī, Vaiṣṇavī, Raudrī, Carcikā, and likewise Īśvarī;
Vārāhī, Nārasiṃhī, Śivādūtī, and Ṣaṣṭhikā—
may these great yoginīs always accept this offering from me for the Goddess.
Hrīṃ! To the sixty-four Yoginīs, accept this bali offering! (2) Grant peace to all! (2) May they grant me accomplishment! Hūṃ (3) Phaṭ (2) Svāhā! This is the bali offering for the sixty-four Yoginīs.

Three *añjali* gestures with the root mantra (2). (3). The *bali* offering. The six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) ritual. The *nirvāṇa* rite. The great *bali* for the *tvāka* [deity] at the *dhūnaka*. The invocation (*āvāhana*) and subsequent rites. The *yonimudrā*. The libation (*tarpaṇa*).
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the deity Ugracaṇḍā.
On a clean, bare ground, the offering for Tripurasundarī is made with *khavalā* (mercury). The offering is made to the body of the digit of the moon (*ṅāsukalākāya*).

Aiṃ! O Brahman, drink the fragments of the cosmic egg like a constant river of blood; O Sadāśiva, [be] ever-pure; O Kṛṣṇaraktapaśu, [be] not hot; O Piśita, [be] a mountain-flood of flesh; O Yāga, [be] the end-maker of sleep within the thunderbolt; O Kurukaṇagiri, [be] the Tāṇḍava dance; O Śambhu, stand firm; O Devī, [you who] desire to fashion the wheel yourself—may the command thus praised purify us.

Whether above the cosmic egg, in the expanse of the sky, on the surface of the earth, in the void, in the netherworld, in fire, or in water and wind; wherever they may be stationed— be it in a sacred field (*kṣetra*),

a seat (*pīṭha*), or a secondary seat (*upapīṭha*)— may those goddesses, who have been honored with flowers, incense, and other offerings, and who are worshipped by the lords of heroes, always protect us through the rite of the auspicious *bali* offering.
Sārdya and all [you deities], accept this offering of blood and flesh; fulfill my desire for peace! HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. This is the Peace Offering.

Three *añjali* gestures with the root mantra. (3) The *bali* offering. The six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). The *nirvāṇa*. Shaking the great *bali* of the *tāva* [deity]. The invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth. The *yonimudrā*. The libation (*tarpaṇa*).
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the body of Tripurasundarī.

This is the *bali* offering for Guhyakālikā at the Javalāpāṭa forest on the *thaṇḍila*. And this is the *bali* offering for Ṅāsukalākā. Oṃ namo mahāmāye hūṃ phreṃ trailokyatrāte chrīṃ chrīṃ siddhi (2) hrīṃ (2) dhāraya (2)! O Mahāgaurī, grant here wealth, grain, jewels, gold, silver, wives, family, great treasures, prosperity, mindfulness, great intelligence, fame, sovereignty, good fortune, and all lamps; fulfill all actions, O Siddhicāmuṇḍā! Hrīṃ! (2) Fulfill! (2) Hrīṃ!

Rain down (2), cause to rain down (2) all desires and all prosperity! Bestow (2) a great treasure! Bestow (2) the eight sovereign powers! Bestow (2) sons, wealth, long life, good fortune, a storehouse, grain, and gold! Constantly grant (2) thus all success! Dharā (2) Hrīṃ (2) Strīṃ Phreṃ! Rain down (2) that which consists of jewels! Command (2) all the yakṣas! Give orders (2)! Bestow (2) glory and sovereignty! Grant freedom from obstacles (2)! Homage to the Great Yakṣa King! Hrīṃ (3) Śrīṃ (3) Strīṃ (3)! O Great Giver of Wealth, [grant] all to me!
Grant wealth! (2) Siddhigaurī hūṃ (2) namaḥ svāhā. [This is] the Bhogavidyā.

The triple *añjali* with the root mantra; (3) the *bali* offering; the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*); the *nirvāṇa*; the great *bali* for the *tva* [deity] at the *dhūnaka*; the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth; the secret mudrā of the womb (*yoniguhyamudrā*); and the libation (*tarpaṇa*).
Thus ends the ritual procedure for Guhyakālī’s liṅga.
In the forest of Thaṇḍiliṅga, there is a bali offering at the root of the Dathupāṭa tree; it is indeed a bali offering for the body of the goddess Ṅāśukalā.
Aiṃ (5). Ajara, Apakumbha, and likewise Iḍācāra;
Indramūrti, Ulkāsya, Ūṣmāṇḍa, and Ṛpusūdara.
Ṛmukta, Ḷktakāya, Ḹlāpāda, and Vadaṣṭraka; Airāvata, Oghāmba, and Auṣadhīśa are likewise in front.
Antaka, Arthabāhu, Kamara, Kharānana,
Gomukha, Ghaṇṭhala, Aṅga, Ṇa, Na, and Caṇḍadhāraka.
Chaṭātoṣa, Jaṭālākhyā, Jhaṅkārā, and Ñabhaṭeśvara.
Likewise, another has a hammer in his hand, and there is also the fierce Ṭhīṇḍabandha-Ḍāmara.
Ḍhaṭ, Ṭakarṇa, Ūrṇatīkānta, Taḍidbhā, Sthavira, likewise Dantura,
Dhanada, Nāgakarṇa, Pracaṇḍavān, Phetkāra,
Vīrasiṃha, Bhṛkuṭī, and Meghabhāsura.
Yugānta, Rauva, Lamboṣṭha, and likewise Vatsala.
Śukatuṇḍa, Ṣaḍālāsya, Sunāsa, Hūhūka,
and Kṣayāntaka— these are declared to be the fifty Kṣetrapālas.
In the extraction of the fifty letters, the Kṣetrapālas reside in their respective places;
however, there are fourteen Kṣetrapālas who are devoid of the remaining letters.
And at a solitary liṅga, one should utter the syllable *huṃ*, and in a cremation ground, that which inspires fear.
Jvālāmukha always dwells in the terrible Mahālakṣmī forest.
On a single tree, or on a banyan tree, one should dwell with the face of a cat;
in a cave-dwelling, one should sound a bell, and in a cluster of lotuses, one should be clothed in water.
At the confluence he is Bhūridhāraugha; likewise, on the mountain he is Marut;
at the spring he is Śravaṇipravāha; and at the treasure-store he is Maṇibhadraka.
In the field of flavors he is known as the Lord of Wealth (Kubera), in the sacrificial enclosures as Kroṣṭraka,
in the forest as Śavaravindya, and in the garden as Madhukara.
The sixty-four of great prowess remained protecting the world;
they constantly offered oblations and worship within that sacred field.
There, four types of beings— the twice-born and others,
those dwelling on the earth, those moving through the air, and birds— accept the offering, each desiring the oblation according to their own conduct.
The four who hold eternal authority are the eaters of raw flesh,
while other people are the barbarians with tawny hair, tawny skin, and tawny eyes;
they are most fierce, with terrifying fangs, and resplendent with ornaments of skulls.
With saffron, sandalwood, musk, civet, and fish-roe;
with flowers, garments, as well as parasols, lamps, and incense made of guggulu resin.
Worshipped by the foremost practitioners who are devoted to the sequential ritual (*kramapūjā*),
and gratified with the sounding of bells, music, and other offerings, she always grants all desires.

(5) Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, descend [Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ], for [Name]! O Kṣetrapāla, radiant with a mass of tawny matted hair, three-eyed, flame-mouthed, accept this offering of fragrance, flowers, and bali! In the form of Bhairava, *turu* (2), *muru* (2), *sva* (2), *la* (2), *pheṃ pheṃ phaḥ*, obeisance to the Lord of the Great Ḍāmara, svāhā!
By means of this mantra and the offering of oblations (bali) for all according to the prescribed rule,
there shall be no famine there, nor any fear of calamities and the like.
The king shall be eternally joyful and become the lord of all the Bhilla tribes;
he shall obtain his desired objects and always achieve victory in battle.
Thus ends the bali offering for the fields beginning with Ajara.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃḥ. Oṃ! I bow to the Goddess who is dark-hued, whose form is that of desire, who resides in the city of Puravipura at the seat of Jāla, who is victorious, who dwells in the center of the hexagon, who possesses the three paths, and who is the source of the peak-sound (śṛṅgoṭṭakārā).

I bow to the God of gods, who is joined with the host of the sixty Yoginīs in the lineage of the Ācāryas known as Siddhi, in that favorable age, and who is born from the syllables Ḍa-ra-la-ka-sa-ha within the fivefold [mantra].
5. Whether in the earth, heaven, or the intermediate space; in the ten directions, in the world, at the base of the seven netherworlds (pātāla);
in a field (kṣetra), a seat (pīṭha), a secondary seat (upapīṭha), or at the uneven four paths, or at a meeting place (melaka), or in a cremation ground (śmaśāna);

on the bank of a river, under a solitary tree, on a beautiful shore of the ocean, at Dhūmrakārāvatāra, at Kollairi, at Pūrṇagiri, and likewise in the preeminent city of Oḍḍiyāṇa—[in all these places].
In the city of Kulapati known as Jāla, the foremost of yogic seats; in Kāmarūpa, Surūpa, Urjjaṇya, Aṭṭahāsa, Paṭupaṭa, Velaḍa, and Lāḍa country— in these regions.
On Śrīśaila and Pārijāta, in the abode of Paśupati, on the Hemavindhyācala mountains, in the illustrious Mokaṣāḍa region, and on Mount Marūtapatha— there dwell the Ḍākinīs and Sākinīs.
In Kashmir, in the land of Candra, in Draviḍa and Malaya, in Brahmācāha and Kuluta, in the kingdom of women, in Hakkaḍokka, in Urasi, in Virajaka, in the Siddhakṣetra of Ḍahāla,
in Airuḍyā, on Mount Pāripātra, on the peak of the Himavat, and in the land of Kāñcī—
Whether in Saurāṣṭra at the beginning of the journey, in Madhyadeśa, in the city of Bhṛgukaccha, or in Kośala or Kāmboja;
In Kārṇāta, or in Koṅkaṇa, or in the excellent city of Magadha, in Karṇakubja, Kaliṅga, Vacchoma, Haṃsavāha, Himarajapaṭala, Pāṭala, and the place called Ḍoṅgara;
in Aṅga, O Mother, in Mātṛcakra, in the abode of the hosts of sages, in Ḍohala, Candadeśa, Rāmora, and the place called Puṣpara; and in the mountain caves and deep caverns of Abjava and Siṃhanāda.

In the land called Vaṅga, in Bhīmanāda, in the city of Śivapura, in Bhadrakūla, in Jayā, in that which is known as Śrīvidyā, under the sole umbrella [of sovereignty], on the slopes of Pravaragiri, in Yakṣa, in Kumbha, and in Laṅkā; in Vārāṇasī, in Viśāla, on the path of the three sages (Trithamunipatha), in Śuddhakula, on the Mārga road, at the end of the Mlecchas, in Mlecchamāla, in the cave of the Malaya mountains, or in a city in the land of Brahmā— [these are the places].

In Bhadrāṅga, Mūrahsthāna, Prakṛtipurālīya, Siṃhakarṇa, Śaśāṅka, Triśotra, the center of the sky, Suraverāśayana, and the place called Gahvara— may all those Mothers, praised by various wise ones, who are born from the maṇḍala of the Yoginī, being satisfied, perfected, and well-perfected, grant divine accomplishments to the various wise ones.
The sword, or the accomplishment of mantras, entry into the supreme city, or movement through the sky;

the eye-salve, or the paralyzing of enemies, the conquest of vast strength, gray hair, and wrinkles, as well as immobilization and all branches of knowledge; long life, poetic skill, the pill of alchemy, and the magical sandals.
May all these, who delight in wine and meat and are devoted to Bhairava, grant the accomplishment of all desires.

May she who is meditated upon— the Mother of Mantras, who wears a skin and a skull, who utters "cauṃ cauṃ phreṃ," laughing with "ha ha ha ha" while chewing, drinking, and dancing, and who proclaims the Kaula language with cries of "kilikilitakili"— dispel all fear in the presence of wicked men, thieves, enemies, plagues, hosts of malevolent planets, thunderbolts, battle, the royal court, or floods.

With a parched form, possessing the nature of desire, sounding with the syllables ya-ra-la-va, the drum-beat, and the cries of "ha" and "hūṃ," she is the leavings, blue-throated, the friend of the immortals, marked by the bindu on her head, and highly praised.

Making the sounds "pheṃ pheṃ pheṃ," devouring the limbs smeared with the blood of the ruru deer, licking the tip of her tongue in rage, and making the sounds "lalala lalala" as she causes [the world] to melt away, she drinks.

Kṛṣṇā, the messenger of Kāmākṣā, praised by the virtues of the immortals, merged into the end of Bindu and Nāda; bestowing success at the end of Śakti, she has reached the supreme state and increased the waves.
Bold, the protectress of the world, joined with Ga, Sa, and Pavana (Vāyu), followed by Pārthiva (Earth);
situated in the sixth place, joined with Bindu, devoted to the lotus of the Kula, she is the savior known as Kuṇḍalā.

May that renowned power of Rudra, the terrifying Bhadrakālī, who takes forms at will (*kāmarūpā*), who has entered the lineage of the *akula* and *kula*, and who removes fear from her enemies, grant auspiciousness.
May she known as the illustrious Kubjikā bestow upon me the supreme, leftward (*vāma*), divine, and unfailing [attainment].
And may Cāmuṇḍā, called Koṅkaṇā, the Kaulinī in the tradition of the *Kula* transmission within the path of the Kaulas, grant it.
Mālinī, whose abode is revealed in the Vāmamārga, whose body is the Bindu,
and who consists of both Akula and Kula within the Oṃkāra-maṇḍala, is established in the circle of yogins;
she, whose form is terrifying, rests upon the lap of Śrīnātha and is worshipped by the assembly of the most excellent sages.
That Goddess, the Mother of the World, whose face is both Śiva and the universe, is the Mother within the wheel of the venerable Lord.

Worshipped by Śrīkaṇṭha, accompanied by the four yugas, known as Ambikā in the central liṅga, established upon the sacred seat (pīṭha), filling [all things] with her shimmering arts, and possessing the splendor proclaimed in the Kaula path;
she who is named the illustrious Kubjikā, endowed with the movement of the triple-path, consisting of three syllables and three modes.
I bow with devotion to that Goddess, who has manifested her abode as the essence of the five [elements] from beginning to end.

May Kālī, in the form of saffron, whose voice is most resonant, the terrifying one who devours the sacrificial oblation—may she, Śrī Kubjikā, manifest the great knowledge of the divine, inexhaustible current. (5) (1)

Hrīṃ glūṃ hrīṃ mlūṃ hrīṃ plūṃ hrīṃ mlūṃ hrīṃ nlūṃ hsauṃ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ. Grant me supernatural power (*ṛddhi*); grant me accomplishment (*siddhi*); grant me knowledge (*jñāna*); grant me long life (*āyus*); grant me wealth (*dhana*); grant me grain (*dhānya*); grant me prosperity (*lakṣmī*). Accept this great offering (*mahābali*)! O you who are the vessel of nectar (*amṛtāvaṭya*), svāhā! Thus ends the Great Offering (*mahābali*).
Three times with joined palms, recite the root mantra: "Nirvāṇa-chāya! Tva-ka-mahābalina-dhūnake!"
Now follows the great offering (mahābali) for Tvaṣṭṛ.
Aiṁ kṣāṁ kṣīṁ kṣūṁ kṣaḥ, accept this offering for the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla); svāhā! (2)
Śrīṃ hrīṃ, accept this bali offering for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha, svāhā! (2)
Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaḥ glauṃ! O Kulagaṇeśvara, accept this offering (bali)! Svāhā! (2)
HŪṂ! To the lord of the Mahākaṇavīra cremation ground, accept this bali offering, SVĀHĀ!
Hskhphrīṁ, O Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī, accept the offering! Svāhā! (2)
Moving through the sky, accept the offering from the heavenly realms; svāhā!
"From all beings, from all piśācas, from all chosen deities, accept this offering—svāhā! Thus ends the great bali offering for Tvaṣṭṛ.
The Worship of the Jar of Detachment (virāghaṭapūjā). Homage to the Guru. The Ritual Assignment (nyāsa).
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Prasphura (2) Hṛdayāya Namaḥ.
Aiṃ (5) Ghoraghorataratanurūpa, svāhā to the head! Aiṃ (5) Caṭa Pracaṭa (2), vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock!
Aiṃ (5) kaha (2) vama (2) kavacāya hūṃ. Aiṃ (5) dama (2) ghātaya (2) netratrayāya vaṣaṭ.
Aiṃ (5) vighātaya (2) vighni (2) hūṃ (3) phaṭ astrāya phaṭ. Thus is the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).
Āsana: Aiṃ (5). "Ādhāraśakti" etc. (8). Pādukā for the Lion Throne. Trideva: Brahmāṇī etc. (8). Bali: Aśitāṅga etc. (8). Bali.
Now, meditation.
Then, in the city situated within the ocean of milk being churned by the gods and asuras,
there arose the Great Goddess, a delightful celestial maiden.
The goddess resembles lac-dye in color, with a radiance equal to a ruby;
she has eighteen arms and is adorned with ornaments of jewels.
The goddess, possessing a gentle form, has three eyes and is in the bloom of youth;
she holds a sword, a trident, a vajra, a ḍiṇḍima drum, and likewise a mallet.
In the right [hands], there shines a mace, a lotus, an excellent vessel,
a pheṭaka, a goad, a bell, a severed head, the ṣaḍaṅga [seal], and two jars.
Holding a blue lotus, the gesture of fearlessness, and a drop (bindu) in her left hand,
she wears a turban fashioned from divine jewels and is adorned with golden ornaments.
Having thus meditated upon the Great Goddess Vāruṇī of divine form, seated upon a white lotus in the bound-lotus posture (baddhapadmāsana).
Thus ends the section on meditative absorption (dhyāna).
Aghora Vajravatīśī (3). Haṃ (9) Saṃ (9), [I offer] the sandals to the one whose form is the Kula-jar. Three añjalis. Six-limbed yoga.
Aghorāstra. This is the *bali* offering for it. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth. [Display] the *dhenu-mudrā* and *yoni-mudrā*.

Worship of the Great Vessel (*mahāpātrapūjā*). *Pādukā* for the seat of *aiṃ*. Worship with the *aghorāstra* mantra. *Aiṃ* (5) *hrīṃ* (2) *glūṃ* *hrīṃ* (2) *slūṃ* *hrīṃ* (2) *plūṃ* *hrīṃ* (2) *mlūṃ* *hrīṃ* (2) *nlūṃ* *hrīṃ* (2). Salutation to the vessel of supreme nectar (*paramāmṛtapātra*). The root-vidyā. The *dhenumudrā*. Recitation (*jāpa*). For the hymn of praise (*stotra*). The three deities (*trideva*). The *yoginī*.
The Goddess resembles the juice of lac, adorned with the crimson glow of vermilion;
she is endowed with eighteen arms and decorated with weapons and ornaments.
Just as the substance of nectar arose from the churning of the Ocean of Milk,
so too did the Goddess who deludes the world arise, she who effects both creation and maintenance.
May the Goddess of the gods, who destroys the pride of her enemies,
who cuts away fear and bestows prosperity, protect the Lord of Kadambara.
This mantra, which consists of water, fire, wind, and earth, along with time,

and which includes the anusvāra and pervades the three worlds— this Tumburu, renowned among the gods— even by merely writing this mantra, may the aged man, together with his sons, go to the city of the Nāgas on his arm.
O Goddess who embodies the Kula, bestow upon me the unbroken Lord of the Vases, the axe of discernment, the purifier, the independent one, and the vibrating mantra.
In this context, [there is] perfume and so forth.
Thus concludes the worship of the Hero and the Great Vessel.
One should offer the periodic *pratibali* oblation consisting of flattened beans, meat, fish, and pieces of fruit.
After the invocation and other rites, one should display the secret mudrā of the Yonikhecarī.
Tarpaṇa. Ghaṇṭāpūjā: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ hūṃ jagadhvani mantramāte svāhā. Offering incense and lamps.
Then, for the incense: having sprinkled the incense vessel with the mantra "Phaṭ," [offer] guggulu resin mixed with clarified butter, incense, perfumes, and so forth.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! This incense, produced from the essence of trees, rich in fragrance and of supreme scent, which is worthy of being smelled by all the gods—may it be accepted.
Endowed with divine fragrance and beloved by all the gods,
may this incense be accepted as an offering for the scent of all the deities.
O Blessed One, O Viśvarūpa, O Maheśvarī, among those who subsist on incense,
may the Supreme Goddess, the Mistress of the Gods, be pleased by this incense.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her retinue, her vehicle, and her weapons—this incense is for the Blessed Lady; obeisance!
Then the lamp.
Having sprinkled the lamp-vessel with "hūṃ phaṭ," [one should purify it].
Well-illuminated, of great splendor, dispelling darkness everywhere— may this lamp, a light both internal and external, be accepted.

The Ārātrika rite: To the entire circle, *hrīṃ śrīṃ*, to the Blessed Lady together with her limbs, and so forth—this lamp, obeisance! [Offer] to the Goddess on one's left, and for the accomplishment of delusion (*mohana*) on one's right side.

Having abandoned the *bindu* of the *saraiśasa*, one should draw a triangle with five *piṇḍas* in the forest of the vessel of delusion (*mohanipātra*) and place [the mantra] *hsraiṁ hlklrīṁ hsauṁ* upon the lamp. *Khphreṁ siddhalakṣmī vidmahe kālikāya dhīmahī tanno saṃkarṣaṇi pracodayāt.*

The worship with sandalwood and other offerings: *Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ*, obeisance to Tripurā, the seat of all mantras. *Aiṁ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ*, the sandals of the venerable Oṣadhīkarmabhaṭṭārikā. (3 times). The *bali* offering.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hoṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ pādukāṃ || Bali || [Offerings to] the heart and other limbs || The six limbs || Invocation and other rites || The yoni-mudrā ||

Then, for the food offering (*naivedya*), according to one's means, [prepare] cooked rice, milk-pudding (*pāyasa*), and other sweet substances. *Hūṃ Phaṭ*. Sprinkle [them] with water from the *argha* vessel. *Vauṣaṭ*. Behold [them]. *Hūṃ*, perform the veiling (*avaguṇṭhana*). *Namaḥ*, worship. *Yā* (4), *Rā* (4), *Lā* (4), *Vā* (4). Purify the food offering with these four seed-syllables; transform it into nectar (*amṛta*) with the *dhenu-mudrā*; consecrate it three times with the nine-syllable mantra; and kindle it with *Śrīṃ*.
This fourfold food, endowed with the six tastes, has been offered by me to you; please accept it, O Supreme Goddess.
O Supreme Goddess, please accept this divine food of great flavor, endowed with the six tastes, which has been offered by me with devotion.
O Lord, please accept this food offering; make my devotion unwavering.
O Goddess, [grant] the removal of untimely death and the supreme goal in the hereafter.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the Blessed Lady together with her limbs and so forth, this food offering (naivedya), obeisance!
At the conclusion of the food offering, [present] water for sipping once more to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs: "Salutation to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs."
In that regard, [there is] the fruit and so forth.
Banana, citron, orange, and likewise pomegranate—these have been offered by me to you; accept them, O Supreme Goddess.
Then, betel.
May this betel leaf, consisting of areca nut, betel leaf, camphor and other ingredients,
combined with cardamom and cloves, be accepted.
The leaf [of the betel roll] resembles a pure gold plate, filled with pearls and lime,
and provided with pieces of nutmeg, cloves, areca nut, and camphor.
O Destroyer of Cities, O Mistress of my life, this betel-roll, which brings delight to the mouth, has been offered by me to you; accept it, O Giver of Boons, O Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, salutations to you!

Japa: LĀHĀTANATRIVAYĀ THRAUṂ SVĀHĀ (10 times). ŚRĪṂ HRĪṂ SVĀHĀ (10 times). GLŪṂ SVĀHĀ (10 times). Mālā-pūjā: Then, having again placed guggulu and other substances into the incense burner, perform the fumigation with "KHPHREṂ SAṂDHŪPYA. Perform the purification of the rosary with "JAPAMĀLI HŪṂ PHAṬ ŚODHANAM. Fumigate it again with "KHPHREṂ SAṂDHŪPYA. Worship it with sandalwood paste, vermilion, flowers, and unbroken rice grains.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, O Māṃ Māle (twice), O Mahāmāyā, be gracious (twice); grant me success (twice); Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! One should recite this sixteen times and thirty-five times, both in direct and reverse order.
The garland has three drops. (3) [It is] for the application of sandalwood and so forth.
Aiṁ (5) Ḍmlvryūṁ Hrīṁ, the sandals upon the rosary.
Oṃ, O garland, O garland, O great garland, you whose nature is all-pervading power!
The four aims of human life have been entrusted to you; therefore, grant me spiritual accomplishment.

Thus is the Mālā-pūjā. For Paścimā: HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ SVĀHĀ. (54) For Tumbheśvarī: HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ SVĀHĀ. (54) For Śikhā: HSPHRĀṂ HSPHRĪṂ HSPHRŪṂ ŚIKHĀSVACCHANDAMAHĀBAIRAVA ŚRĪ SVĀHĀ. (54) For Mahākālā: OṂ HŪṂ MAṂ MAHĀKĀLĀYA SVĀHĀ. (54) For Ugracaṇḍā: HSPHREṂ SVĀHĀ. (54) For Ugracaṇḍī: HSKHPHREṂ SVĀHĀ. (54)

To Śrī Siddhilakṣmī: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ svāhā. (108 times) To Kāliyā: Oṃ siddhikalāli hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ svāhā. (54 times) To Tripurā: Aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ svāhā. (54 times) The *nirvāṇa-yāphako* [is as follows].
O you who are the secret beyond secrets, the protector, accept this recitation performed by us;
may success be mine through your grace, for [this practice] is established in you.
Having recited this, one should offer unbroken grains (*akṣata*) together with flowers into the right hand of the Goddess while reciting her mantra: "Accept this recitation, svāhā!"

Hymn of Praise || To the Bestower of the Maṇḍala || Of what nature? Of what nature? The fivefold pranava || Ringing the bell || "The unbroken circle" and so forth || Śrī Saṃvartā and her like || The trident || Mahāmāyā || The three deities, Piṅgākṣī and so forth || Brahmāyaṇīyā ||
One should worship Brahmāṇī at the base of the petal in the direction of Indra (the East); she rides upon a swan, resembles molten gold, has two faces and three eyes,
and holds in her hands the *brahmakūrca*, a water-pot, a shining staff, and a rosary of lotus seeds,
and is adorned with beautiful attire.
I bow to her whose body is variegated with perfumes and other unguents, who bears the weight of an excellent mass of matted locks. (1)
Belonging to Maheśvara.
That Māheśī, resembling thick snow at the base of the eastern petal of the fire-diagram, holding a skull, a *ḍamaru* drum, a terrifying *ḍamaruka*, and a trident upon her staff-like arms;
she who shines with three eyes, and whose crest of matted hair is adorned by the crescent moon.
One should worship the bull with perfumes and other offerings; having mounted it, one goes to the world of the stars eternally. (2)
Belonging to Kaumārī.

One should worship Kaumārī, who is rich in youth, possessing a beautiful face, radiant with the hue of saffron, and most lovely; she holds in her own hands a spear, a noose, and a goad in the right, and the gesture of fear (*abhaya*) in the left. She is intoxicated by wine, large of form, with a pair of sparkling eyes, adorned with all ornaments, and seated at the base of the leaf in the southeast direction according to the rules of the *śikhinī* [mandala]. (3)
Belonging to Viṣṇu.
In the southwest direction, at the base of the leaf, is the Vaiṣṇavī goddess, who holds a water-vessel, a bell, a conch, a skull, and a discus with her staff-like arms;
she has pure limbs, beautiful hair, sits upon Garuḍa, and is resplendent with a crown.
One should worship her with perfumes and other offerings; she is satisfied by garlands of *nīpa* flowers, which delight those intoxicated by honey. (4)
Of Vārāhī.
In the western petal-base, one should worship Vārāhī, who has the face of a boar, who holds a shield, a mace, and a plough, whose cheeks are rubbed by jeweled earrings shining from her ear-holes,
who is eternally worshipped by the world, and who stands upon a boar as large as a mountain peak, accompanied by Gaṇanātha and others.
She, with her beautiful teeth, worshiped him whose body possessed the luster of smoke-colored ash. (5)
The hymn beginning with "indrāṇīyā."

In the direction of Vāyu, at the base of a leaf, [one should visualize] Indrāṇī, whose face is adorned with jewels resembling the orb of the moon, whose complexion has the luster of sapphire, whose eyes reach to her ears, and who wears a jeweled crown;
she holds in her four lotus-hands a bow, a conch, a trident, and an arrow.
One should constantly worship her, who is seated upon her own elephant and is praised by the best of the gods, while she herself is intoxicated. (6)
To Cāmuṇḍā.
And Cāmuṇḍā, with a face split by fierce, wide, and formidable fangs from her violent laughter, possessing three eyes, holding a sword, a trident, and a skull-cup in her lotus-like hands,
and also a shield; fleshless, with blood-red eyes, causing fear to the three worlds, she is at the base of the leaf of the gentle direction (the East).
One should worship Kālī, who is adorned with skeletons, whose hair stands erect, and who dwells in the cremation ground. (7)
Of Mahālakṣmī.

Afterwards, one should worship her who is of wondrous form, with a beautiful face, possessing the luster of pure gold, holding in her lotus-hands a rosary, the gesture of fearlessness, a lotus, and a citron fruit;
she who is adored by the clouds of the three worlds and endowed with the primary auspicious marks.
O Lord, [I see] Lakṣmī at the base of the petals of the directions, bowed down by the weight of her lofty, full breasts.
All these [are] Brahmāṇyā and so forth. Now, [the deities] Aśitāṅga and so forth.
Homage to Sitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodheśa, Unmatta, Kapāla, and Bhairava;
and in the midst of Palāśa, to the one known as Bhīṣaṇa—I bow to these Bhairavas.
[The section] beginning with "hetukā" and so forth.
He who is the causal one and the destroyer of Tripura; he who is Vahnivetāla with the tongue of fire;
he who is Kāla, Kapāla, and likewise Ekapāda; and he who indeed possesses a terrifying form and a fearsome appearance.
To Ugracaṇḍā.
O Goddess who slew Mahiṣa, who possesses great illusion, who destroyed Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa,
who took away the blood-seed (Raktabīja), O fierce Caṇḍī, I bow to you.
To Vagalā.
The King Vaiśvānara makes the eloquent mute, turns the sun into cold, calms the wrathful,
and shortens the journey for the wicked while lengthening it for the virtuous;
he diminishes pride and stupefies all who know, being restrained by the machine of Your command.
O Śrī Nityavagalāmukhī, O auspicious one, salutations to you every day!
By means of the three powers.
Red, white, and extremely sharp, possessing the movement of the triple-path, the three goddesses consist of the three measures;
having praised their own self, those who have attained the various states through the three well-known groups—
youth, strength, and old age— become awakened to time within the night.
May the mother Vetālī, who possesses a virtuous womb, who bestows victory, and whose limbs are auspicious through constant worship, be victorious.
With the Hatubhairava [mudrā].
I bow to the Supreme Lord Rudra, who has the form of Bhairava;
the God who protects the three worlds, the Master and Sovereign of the Ḍāmara.
By Nāṭeśvarī.
Squeezing the entire universe with both hands, he repeatedly pressed it until the ripe, glistening fruit-like cosmos oozed out its essence;
drinking that juice again and again, he acted like one intoxicated by the three worlds.
May Mahābhairava protect us, performing the dance of Tāṇḍava according to the ritual procedure with great majesty.
The fifth is Vālāhikā.
Homage to you, O Mahāmāyā, who bears the name Vārāhī;
you are Kolāsyā, the Great Fierce One, who possesses a face like a boar and holds a vajra-tusk.
By Siddheśvarī.
She has one face and three eyes, with a crescent moon as her crest-ornament;
she possesses four hands, O Great Goddess, two of which perform the *karañja* mudrā.
Seated upon the throne of the pretas, she is red in color and most brilliantly radiant;
the goddess, whose nature is water, possesses the splendor of ten million full moons through her great luster.
Of Chinnamastā.
At the navel, upon a white lotus, is the stainless mandala of the fierce-rayed sun;

there, within that triple-pathed center, one should meditate on the praised Chinnamastā, the sole essence of cyclic existence, the mother of the three worlds, whose nature is compassion and whose activity is Dharma. She assumes a triple form.
I bow to that Yoginī, whose form is wisdom, who removes the fear of death, and who is the mudrā of yoga.
The phrase beginning with "ukāra" (the letter *u*), etc. [is as follows].

Brahmāṇī; "madhye" [is] the weapon; "khaḍgaṃ vā"; dark blue and red; *bandhūka*; "kvā kvāsa"; *mahākāraṃ*; Mārkaṇḍeya; "yā devī"; "utphullāṃ"; *siddhiparā*; "yā sāṃtikāni tāhāka"; "aindusyaiva"; *māyākuṇḍalini*; "namaste devadevetyādi"; "yoginī siddhityādi"; "tvamasi para"; "nānyaṃ vadāmi"; "yathā vānatyādi"; here, the mantra for the offering of perfume and so forth; the sentence; the libation (*tarpaṇa*).

*Prītapretātyādi*. Homage to Śrīnātha! Homage to Śrīsiddhinātha! Homage again and again to Śrīkujeśanātha! Thus ends the ritual procedure for worship on the sacrificial ground (*thaṇḍilyārccanavidhi*).

Now, the ritual for the insertion of the ritual stake (*kīla*). As before: the destruction of the [obstructing] spirits in their respective locations. *Oṃ hrāṃ lāṃ līṃ lūṃ la* (nine times) *indrāya namaḥ*. With the word *svāhā* at the end, the offering (*bali*) is made. The patron (*yajamāna*) should cause the ritual master (*ācārya*) to perform the rite of piercing with the ritual hammer (*nyāmuśalanatāya*).
Oṃ! May the Nāgas and the World-Protectors, who grant all desires, enter into the surface of the earth.
May these [medicines], which bestow longevity and strength upon us, remain in this vessel.
Oṃ śraṃ vrūṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ svāhā. Thus, etc., the Kurūṣaṇa. The bali offering.
Oṃ, to all the Indras and to all others who depend upon them.
I offer this oblation to them; may they all, empowered by mantras, accept it.
The worship with the root mantra of the *kīla*: Oṃ! To all the fires, and to those others who have taken refuge in them, I offer this *bali*; may they all, empowered by the mantra, accept it.
Oṃ, and the Lord of the South himself, and those who are stationed in the south.
And also the lord of the Nairṛta [direction], and those Rākṣasas who are in the Nairṛta [direction].
Oṃ, homage to the Naga kings! Oṃ, homage to the Vayu kings!
And also to all the Kuberas and to those others who reside in the north.

Oṃ, and to all the Rudras as well. Then, in the center: Oṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ, [this is] the installation and worship. With the Astra-mantra, [offer] the bali. The remainder is as before. [The vessel] has five yellow threads; this is the procedure for the water-pitcher (kalaśa). Then, with the lotus-hand gesture, the conch is worshipped with river water. The placement of the arghya (arghanyāsa). The Gāyatrī. Self-worship at the arghya-vessel. The mantra for the invocation of the sacred waters (tīrtha-āvāhana).
Oṃ, the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, as well as the Mahimnā and the Narmadā,
the Sindhu and the Sarasvatī, and other sacred fords that have been forgotten.
The Worship of the Naga Kings.

Oṃ jūṃ saḥ, homage to Ananta; (2) to Takṣaka; (2) to Kulika; (2) to Padma; (2) to Mahāpadma; (2) to Śaṅkhapāla; (2) to Āstika; (2) to Karkkoṭaka; (2) to Sahasraśīrṣa. [The rites of] invocation and so forth.

The five jewels (pañcaratna), the four grains (catuḥśrama), dūrvā grass, flowers, milk, rice (brīhi), gold, and water from sacred bathing places (tīrthodaka)—these are to be placed [in the vessel]. Here, the offering of perfumes and other items follows; then the dismissal (visarjana). This ritual vessel is held by the patron (yajamāna); the preceptor (ācārya) recites the benediction (svastivākya) and performs the six-fold oblation (ṣaḍapūpa).
May she who is ever free from obstacles grant well-being; may Mārtaṇḍa likewise grant well-being;
may all the Yoginīs grant well-being, and may my own natal asterism and the sacred seats grant well-being.
In the east, south, west, north, the upper half, and the lower half—
may the sixfold *svasti* protect the one who stands upon the path, both the hidden and the manifest deities.
Bhairava and Bhairavī, together with their limbs, may they grant well-being; [may there be] heaven, heaven, and the wheel of one's own [nature];
as well as one's own mantras, one's own mudrās, and the retinue bearing their own weapons.
May those situated in the planets, lunar mansions, and zodiac signs grant well-being for the prosperity of all;
may the Yoginīs and the leaders of the Gaṇas grant well-being to the heroes and the protectors of the earth.
May there be well-being; may the God of gods and the King of Mantras be ever-present;
may those devoted to the sacrificial oblations be satisfied; and may there be well-being from the ancestral fire-gods.
May there be well-being for the king; may there be well-being for the subjects; may there be well-being for the sacrificer at all times.
The rite for the placement of the auspicious water-pot (kalaśa) within the pavilion; the root-mantra and so forth; the procedure for the five-leafed water-pot (pañcapallava-kalaśa).

Having performed the adornment, the preceptor [performs] the preliminary consecration (adhivāsana-pūjā) with colored powders. For the preliminary consecration on the sacrificial ground according to the ritual procedure, after performing the shadow-bath (chāyā-snāna), he proceeds to the subsequent rites. He observes a fast; these constitute the preliminary consecration (adhivāsa).

Morning Bath: Having performed the daily worship of the deity, exit through the southwest door of the pavilion. Wash your feet, offer the *bali* oblation, and enter. Offer the *argha* water to the Sun, remember the Guru, perform the *nyāsa*, and worship the Three Deities (*trideva*). [Worship] Brahmāṇī and the others. Oṃ hūṃ, accept this *bali* offering for all spirits, svāhā! Oṃ laṃ, accept this *bali* offering for the *cetakas*, svāhā! Oṃ sāṃ, accept this *bali* offering for all yoginīs, svāhā! Thus is the *uddiṣṭa-bali*.
Incense, lamps, recitation, and hymns of praise.
In the east, south, west, and north are Śivā, Vāmā, Śikhā, and Kṣetreśa; [and] Vaṭu, Durgā, Ghaṇṭhā, Samaya, and Herambanātha.
In the cremation ground is the Lord of the Gods (Śiva), who eternally removes grief, affliction, and torment.
Consisting of eternal bliss, she bestows joy and happiness during the ritual of worship with offerings.

Herein is the dismissal of the perfumes and other offerings; [this applies] to the sacrificial pavilion (balimaṇḍapa), the goat, the *vaho-raka*, the place of the *lekā*, and the reciter (*sāvacaka*).

The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the *pāśupatāstra* mantra: Oṃ oṃ, hūṃ phaṭ, obeisance to the heart. Oṃ ślīṃ, hūṃ phaṭ, obeisance to the head. Oṃ ṛṃ, hūṃ phaṭ, obeisance to the crest-lock (*śikhā*).
Oṃ śūṃ, hūṃ phaṭ, homage to the armor! Oṃ hūṃ, hūṃ phaṭ, homage to the three eyes!

Oṃ phaṭ astrāya hūṃ phaṭ. Thus for the heart and other limbs. [Perform] the offering of the argha vessel with *taṃ hā ra gha sa*. Sprinkle the door with the weapon-mantra (*astra*). Perform the worship: Oṃ hrāṃ glūṃ to Gaṇapati, obeisance! Oṃ śrīṃ to Sarasvatī, obeisance! Oṃ hrīṃ to Mahālakṣmī, obeisance! Oṃ hrāṃ to Nandin, obeisance! Oṃ hrāṃ to Mahākāla, obeisance! Oṃ hrāṃ to Gaṅgā, obeisance! Oṃ hrāṃ to Yamunā, obeisance! [Conclude] with a wrathful gaze.
Striking with the *astra* [mudrā], and trampling the ground with the right foot.
Oṃ! May those beings depart who are stationed here in disorder.
May those beings who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva.

The scattering [of the materials]: parched grain, sandalwood, white mustard seeds, ashes, dūrvā grass, unbroken rice, and kuśa grass. One should recite the Astra mantra seven times over them. The scattering is performed with the Astra mantra. One should enter the pavilion with the right foot first.
The worship of the sword, the weapon, and the vessel: *Aiṃ (5) Khphreṃ sakalaśatrupramathanī astrāya phaṭ*. The Hotṛ and all others should request permission upon the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*).
O Blessed One, by your grace, this [image] of yours has been worshipped for the sake of the sacrifice.
O Guru Śambhu, grant the supreme perfection of supernatural powers; homage be to you!

The statement: "For the sake of [attaining] the goal, be intent upon the command in the dust-mandala; mounted upon the seat of the syllable *Aiṃ*, [be seated] upon the pericarp of the blossoming lotus"—this is the prayer.
In the south-western direction, the offering of the *bali* for the removal of obstacles is prescribed according to the ritual rule.

Oṃ, salutations to the venerable Gurus. The Bali-pūjā. Oṃ, from this day forward... [for the sake of] the petitioner holding the flower-vessel of the sacrificer. The Arghya for the Sun. For the purpose of the worship of the Bali offering to remove obstacles for [Name] Deva. Salutation to the Gurus. The placement of the *bati* (the sacrificial vessel). Worship of the jar-vessel and the arghya-vessel. Self-worship. Invocation of Śrī Saṃvarta.
One should offer the five-fold oblation (pañcabali). Aiṃ, the sandal for Mayūṣanā.
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, the sandals of Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha; [offering of] bali.

Aiṁ (5). O son of the Goddess, Vaṭukanātha, radiant with the mass of tawny matted locks, three-eyed, Jvālāmukha, descend! (2). Come, come, O Blessed One, into the center of the maṇḍala; accept the various offerings as they have been presented! (2). Grant me my desired object, Hūṁ (3) Phaṭ Svāhā! Vaṭuka. Aiṁ (5). Sandals for Narāsanā. Kṣāṁ Kṣīṁ Kṣūṁ. Sandals for Kṣetrapāla.

Aiṁ (5). O Kṣetrapāla named [Name], lord of this very place, descend (2)! Descend into the center of the maṇḍala (2)! Four-armed, three-eyed, holding a skull-topped staff, a skull-bowl, and a trident in your hands; adorned with a great garland of skulls; possessing a radiance equal to ten million flashes of lightning; come, come, O Blessed One, in the form of Bhairava! Accept the various offerings as they are presented (2)! Destroy my obstacles (2)! Hrīṁ (2) Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā! Kṣetra.

Aiṃ (5) Pādukā to the seat of the corpse! Aiṃ (5) Pādukā to the Yoginīs!
