Aiṃ (5) Whosoever among the Yoginīs are born of the sacred seats (pīṭha), born of the fields (kṣetra), innate (sahaja), born of yoga (yogaja), born of the womb (garbha), or born of the lineage (kula), and whosoever among the Yoginīs are the sky-walkers (khecarī), earth-walkers (bhūcarī), ground-walkers (gocarī), those of one syllable, two syllables, three syllables, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, or ten syllables, and those who dwell among the animals—accept this offering as it has been presented! Grant me success! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! The Yoginīs.

Aiṁ, sandals for the corpse-seat (pretāsana). Aiṁ (5) Hskhphreṁ, sandals for the glorious Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī. Bali. Cāmuṇḍā. Aiṁ (5), sandals for the rat-seat (mūṣāsana). Aiṁ (5) Gāṁ Gīṁ Gūṁ Gaiṁ Gauṁ Gaḥ Glau, sandals for the glorious Kulagaṇeśvara. Bali.

Aiṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gai gau gaḥ! To the most formidable one, the destroyer of all obstacles, the subjugator of all worlds, Śrī Kulagaṇapati Gaṇanātha, accept this offering and worship; be well-pleased with me, svāhā! Gaṇapati!
[Perform] the invocation and so forth; one should display the gestures of the pointing finger, the staff, the womb, the drop, and the elephant.

The *saṃpāta* [mantra] for the three deities: (3) One should display their respective mudrās. To the one who has come to the seat of the sky (*khavasapīṭhiyātaṃviye*): *luṃ* to Indra, the sandals; *ruṃ* to Agni, the sandals; *muṃ* to Yama, the sandals; *kṣuṃ* to Nairṛtya, the sandals; *vūṃ* to Varuṇa, the sandals; *yuṃ* to Vāyu, the sandals; *suṃ* to Kubera, the sandals; *hūṃ* to Īśāna, the sandals; *aṃ* to Ananta, the sandals; *oṃ* to Brahmā, the sandals. To these, [offer] the *bali*.

Aiṃ (5) Haṃsāsanāya pādukāṃ || (8) || Aṃ Brahmāṇī pādukāṃ || Kaṃ Māheśvarī pādukāṃ || Caṃ Kaumārī (3) || Ṭaṃ Vaiṣṇavī (3) || Taṃ Vārāhī (3) || Paṃ Indrāṇī (3) || Yaṃ Cāmuṇḍā (3) || Saṃ Mahālakṣmī (3) || Worship and the offering (bali). O Aghorā, O Vajravatī! The syllables Ha and Sa. The triple añjali. [Salutation] to the places, the seats, and so forth.

Three-fold *añjali* gesture. Aiṃ (5) Ṭaṃ Ṭhaṃ Ḍaṃ Ḍhaṃ Ṇaṃ VMLVRYŪṂ. I worship the sandals of the Goddess Vaiṣṇavī. (3) Six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Offering with the root mantra (*mūlana baliḥ*). Invocation and other rites (*āvāhanādi*). *Yonimudrā*. The drop (*bindu*). To the one who has the mark of the *javasa* plant. Aiṃ (5). The sandals of Rājamātaṅgeśvarī. Raṇa, Vanamā, Ghora, Caṇḍa, Vīra, Jaya, Ucchiṣṭamātaṅgeśvarī. Thus is the worship. The offering (*baliḥ*). Three-fold *añjali* gesture.

Oṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ, [I worship] the sandals of Siddhimātaṅgeśvara, śkṣmlvryīṃ, and the goddess Siddhimātaṅgeśvarī. (3) The six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga). The offering (bali): Oṃ, accept this bali from those with mouths of leavings; svāhā. (2) The mudrās for invocation and so forth, and the drop (bindu). (3)

Dathvasa. To the Kṣetrapālas: Aiṃ, the pādukā for Aśitāṅga-Bhairava; Aiṃ, Ruru; Aiṃ, Caṇḍa; Aiṃ, Krodha; Aiṃ, Unmatta; Aiṃ, Bhīṣaṇa; Aiṃ, Kapālīśa; Aiṃ, Saṃhāra. Worship and offering. Pūṃ, the pādukā for the Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha; Jāṃ, the pādukā for the Jālandhara-pīṭha.
Kāṃ, the sandal for the seat of Kāmarūpa. Oṃ, the sandal for the seat of Oḍḍiyāna.

Worship. Offering. Ḍmlvryūṃ, the sandals of Ḍākinī. Rmlvryūṃ, the sandals of Rākini. Lmlvryūṃ, the sandals of Lākini. Kmlvryūṃ, the sandals of Kākini. Śmlvryūṃ, the sandals of Śākini. Hmlvryūṃ, the sandals of Hākini. Worship. Offering. Hrīṃ, Goddess Jayā. Hrīṃ, Goddess Vijayā. Hrīṃ, Goddess Ajitā. Hrīṃ, Goddess Aparājitā. Hrīṃ, Goddess Jambhanī. Hrīṃ, Goddess Stambhanī. Hrīṃ, Goddess Mohanī.

Hrīṃ, the goddess Ākarṣaṇī. Worship and the offering (bali). Aghora, Vajravatīśī. The syllables Ha and Sa. With these, the bali. With the syllable of the field (kṣetra-akṣara). Three añjalis. Aiṃ (5) Kṣāṃ Kṣīṃ Kṣūṃ Kṣmlvryūṃ, the sandals for Kṣetrapāla. (3) The six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga). Then, the bali is offered with the name-syllables. Invocation and so forth. The mudrās. The bindu (3). The stone, the ladle, and the sacrificial vessel. The three deities (3). The eight [deities] beginning with Aśitāṅga. The eight [deities] beginning with Brahmāṇī.

Aghoravajravatī. The syllables *ha* and *sa*. The triple *añjali* of the field-syllable. The six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). The offering (*bali*). The invocation and so forth. The mudrās. The drop (*bindu*). (3)
Where is the *digbali* for this [deity]? (3) The three deities; (8) from *Ādhāra* onwards; the worship of the nine grahas beginning with Āditya.

Hrāṃ, the sandals for Āditya; Sroṃ, the sandals for Soma; Krāṃ, the sandals for Aṅgāraka; Vrāṃ, the sandals for Budha; Kṣrāṃ, the sandals for Bṛhaspati; Drāṃ, the sandals for Śukra; Ṣrāṃ, the sandals for Śanaiścara; Bhrāṃ, the sandals for Rāhu; Phrāṃ, the sandals for Ketu. [Offer] worship and the bali offering. Luṃ, [the sandals for] Indra and the other ten [directional guardians].

Jayādī (8) || Aśitāṅgādī (8) || Hetukādī (8) || Brahmāṇyādī || Aghora Vajravatīsī || The syllable *Ha* with the syllable *Sa* and the triple *añjali*. The six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). The offering (*bali*): Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ, to Nṛsiṃhabhairava, accept the offering (2) svāhā.
Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ, Viśvaksena, Kṣetrapāla, accept this bali offering; svāhā! (2)
Oṃ hūṃ saḥ! Accept this bali offering for all those who create obstacles, whether mentioned or unmentioned! Svāhā! [The rites of] invocation and so forth; the mudrā is the *bindu*.
Furthermore, in the middle, one should perform the daily ritual service with the *dathupāṭasaṃ* mantra.

This is indeed the *Oṃdusapūjā* offering (*bali*). Aiṃ, obeisance to Hetuka Kṣetrapāla. Aiṃ, [obeisance to] Tripurāntaka. Aiṃ, [obeisance to] Agnivetāla. Aiṃ, [obeisance to] Agnijihvā. Aiṃ, [obeisance to] Ekākṣa. Aiṃ, [obeisance to] Karālin. Aiṃ, [obeisance to] Ekapāda. Aiṃ, [obeisance to] Bhīmarūpa. Aiṃ, [obeisance to] Ḍāmara. Aiṃ, [obeisance to] Kūrmapṛṣṭha Kṣetra. The *bali* is for these [deities]. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites.
Now, the mantras consisting of the syllables of the continents.

(5) KROṂ KMLVRYŪṂ! To Manoharā Devī of Kanyadvīpa and Viṣṇu Kṣetrapāla: accept this bali, SVĀHĀ! Likewise: (5) KHROṂ KHA (7) SĪṂ! To Kūrā Devī of Siṃhala-dvīpa and Agasti Kṣetrapāla: [the] pādukā! (5) GREṂ GA (7) SVAḤ! To Śubhrakāntī Devī of Svarṇadvīpa and Vandīnātha Kṣetrapāla: [the] pādukā!
(5) Ghoṃ gha (7) Karṇadvīpa, the goddess Ghanavarā, the yakṣa king, and the kṣetrapāla: [their] sandals.
(5) Ṅroṅ ṅam (7) Svāmukhadvīpa, Vibhūdevī, Gaṇapati, Kṣetrapāla—[their] sandals. (5) Ccoṅ caṃ (7) Kuśadvīpa, Candrīdevī, Mahājihvākṣetrapāla—[their] sandals.
(5) Chroṃ chaṃ (7) the sandals of the goddess Kālarātrī of Oḍiyāna-dvīpa and the great protector of the field (kṣetrapāla) of Bhṛgukṣetra.
Joṃ jaṃ (7) Jālandharadvīpa, Jvālinī Devī, Mahājihva Kṣetrapāla, [the] sandals!
Jhrāṃ Jhaṃ (7): [I worship] the sandals of the goddess Subhadrā of Ekapādadvīpa and the field-protector Citrāṅga.
To each [of these]: the goddess Subhaṭā of Puradvīpa, and the footprints of Dhvāṅkṣetrapāla.
(5) Ṭrāṃ Ṭaṃ (7) [I worship] the sandals of Dhoradvīpa, Mṛgādevī, Jayabhadra, and Kṣetrapāla.
(5) Ṭhrāṃ Ṭhaṃ (7) [I offer] the sandalwood-sandalwood tree goddess (comanīdevī) and the spring field-protector (vasantakṣetrapāla) sandals.
(5) Ḍroṃ ḍaṃ (7) Cañcarā Devī of Cīnadvīpa, Ḍhidhiṭha Kṣetrapāla—[grant] the sandals!
(5) Ḍhroṃ Ḍhaṃ (7) the sandals of Kumāradvīpa, the goddess Yamadaṃṣṭrā, and the Kṣetrapāla Kumāra.
(5) ṆROṂ ṆAṂ (7) Yamadvīpacarādevī Yamadaṃṣṭrakṣetrapāla, [grant] the sandals!
(5) Troṃ taṃ (7) Puṣkaradvīpa, Datturādevī, Śucipāda, Kṣetrapāla, Pādukā.

(5) THRŌṂ THAṂ (7) The sandalwood of the goddess Draṣṭrādevī and the field-protector Mahādhvāṅkṣa from Kaṭaharādvīpa. DROṂ DAṂ (7) The sandalwood of the goddess Aruṇādevī and the field-protector Mahānanda from Candradvīpa.
(5) *Dhṛāṃ dhāṃ* (7) *Janadvīpa*, Bhīmarāmbādevī, Sugandhika Kṣetrapāla—[I worship] the sandals.
(5) Nroṁ naṁ (7) the sandals of Kālādevī and Gopālakṣetrapāla from Jvālāpuradvīpa.
Proṃ Paṃ (7). Ratnadvīpa Dharmā Mahākāya Kṣetrapāla, [this is] the sandalwood.
(5) Phroṃ Phaṃ (7) The sandals of the goddess Sumanā of Suradvīpa and the field-protector Puṣpadanta.
(5) To the goddess Raktādevī of Gomadadvīpa and the field-protector Dhanada, [I offer] the sandals. (7) Broṁ baṁ.
(5) Bhoṃ bhaṃ (7) Garbhāṇḍadvīpa, Kṛṣṇādevī, Vipura-kṣetrapāla, [grant] the sandals!
(5) Mroṃ maṃ (7) the sandals of the goddess Manonmanī and the kṣetrapāla Mahānanda of Sūryadvīpa.
(5) Yroṃ yaṃ (7) Āsarvvadvīpa Hayavegā Devī, [bestow] the sandalwood of the Śukla-kṣetrapāla.
(5) Rroṃ Raṃ (7) Marudvīpa, Vidyujjihvā, Kuṣṭīdevī, Viḍājvāla, Kṣetrapāla—[grant] the sandals!
(5) Lroṃ Laṃ (7) Vasantadvīpa, Queen Ullekhādevī, and the great yakṣa field-guardian Suvarṇa—[homage to] the sandals.
(5) Vroṃ Vaṃ (7) Saradvīpa Variṣṭādevī Śubhagānanakṣetrapāla Pādukāṃ.
(5) Śroṃ Śaṃ (7) Amṛtadvīpa, Savarādevī, Ratipriya, Kāmākṣakṣetrapāla—[I worship] the sandals.
(5) ŚROṂ ŚAṂ (7) The sandals of Ānandadvīpa, Rāgādevī, Surapriya, and Vadhakṣetrapāla.
(5) Sroṃ Saṃ (7) the sandalwood of the goddess Naṭī of Gāndharvadvīpa and the kṣetrapāla Citrāgadīpeśvara.
(5) Hrīṃ Haṃ (7) O Pādukā of Madaṅgadvīpa, Nādākṣī Devī, and Viḍāla Kṣetrapāla!
(5) KṢROṂ KṢAṂ (7) OṂ ANANTA-SARVĀSU-DVĪPA SARVA-GRĀSĪ-DEVĪ PRADYUMNA-NĀNTI VALA-KṢETRAPĀLA PĀDUKĀM || (5) AṂ ĀṂ JAMBUDVĪPA ANANTĀ-DEVĪ MĀTAṄGA-KṢETRAPĀLA PĀDUKĀM ||
(5) *iṃ īṃ*, the sandals of the Goddess Īśvarī and the Kṣetrapāla Brahmaghna in Plakṣadvīpa.
(5) Um Ūm! The sandals of Kusadvīpa, Queen Udayā, and Rajākṣetrapāla.
(5) *Ṛṃ* *Ṝṃ*, the sandalwood of the goddess Ṣaḍantā, the island of Cakrabuddha, and the field-protector Gaṇḍamālaka.
(5) Ḷaṃ Ḷūṃ, Śākadvīpa, Ḷkādevī, Aruṇakṣetrapāla, the sandals!
(5) Eṃ Aiṃ! The sandalwood of Śālmalīdvīpa, the goddess Aruṇādevī, and the one-legged Kṣetrapāla. The sandals!
(5) Oṃ auṃ! To the sandals of the goddess Ovalī of Puṣkaradvīpa and the field-protector Narasiṃha.
(5) Aṃ Aḥ! To the Great Goddess of Idādvīpa and the Kṣetrapāla of Lokāloka, [I offer] the sandals.
Accept this offering, svāhā! Thus is the syllable of the name.
May you protect yourself from the power of the offering.
Aiṃ (5). Caṇḍā, Ghaṇṭā, Mahānādā, Durmukhī, and likewise Sumukhī;
Revatī, Prathamā, Ghorā, Saumyā, Bhīmā, and Mahābalā.
Jayā, Vijayā, Ajitā, Aparājitā,
Mahotkaṭā, Virūpākṣī, Śuṅgamāṃsalā, and Mātṛkā.
Jātahārī, Saṃhārī, Draṣṭrārī, Śuṣkarevatī, Piṃpalī,
Puṣpahārī, Hāsinī, and Śasyahāsinī.
Bhadrakālī, Subhadrā, Bhadrabhīmā, and Sudrikā.
Mounted upon the thirty-two mantras, he holds a knife and a skull-cup.
These thirty-two are the great yoginīs, wearing dry skulls as their garments.
O thirty-two yogis, accept this offering! Svāhā!
The mantra for the bali offering.
Aiṃ (5). Ajara, Āpakuṃbha, Iḍācāra, as well as Indramūrti, Ulkāsya, Ūṣmāṇḍa, and Ripusūdana.
Ṛmukta, Lṛptakāya, Lḹlāpa, Ekadaṃṣṭraka, Airāvata, Oghāmba, and another, Oṣadhīśa.
Antaka, Arthabāhu, Kamala, Kharānana,
Gomukha, Ghaṇṭāla, Ṅaṃṇana, and Caṇḍadharaka.
Chaṭātoṣa, Jaṭālākhyo, Jhaṅkara, Ñabhaṭeśvara, Taṅkapāṇi, as well as another, Sthāṇubandha, and Ḍāmara.
Dha-dha-kaṇṇoṇa-tīkāntas-taḍi-bhā-stha-viras-tathā.
Danturodhaṇa, Nāgakarṇa, and Pracaṇḍavān;
Phetkāra, Vīrasiṃha, Bhṛkūṭākṣa, Meghabhāsura,
Yugānta, Rorava, Lamboṣṭha, and likewise Vatsala.
Śukatuṇḍa, Ṣaḍālāsya, Sunāsa, and likewise Hūhūka.
Kṣayāntaka is the fiftieth; these are declared to be the Kṣatrapālas.
In the extraction of the fifty letters, the Kṣatrapālakas reside in their respective places;
however, there are fourteen Kṣatrapālakas who are devoid of the remaining letters.
In the Ekaliṅga shrine, in the syllable Hūṃ, in the cremation ground, and in the Vayāvahe forest,
Jvālāmukha always dwells in the terrible Mahālakṣmī grove.
On a single tree or a banyan tree, Viḍālavadana shall dwell;
Ghaṇṭārāva shall dwell in a cave-abode, and Jalāmbara in a cluster of lotuses.
At the confluence [of rivers] he is Bhūridhārogha; likewise on Mount Meru he is Nirjhara;
at Śravaṇī he is Praha; and in his abode he is Maṇibhadraka.
He is the lord of wealth in the field of flavors, and the jackal in the sacrificial enclosures.
In the forest one should recognize a Śabara; in the garden, he is known as a honey-bee.
The sixty-four Mahāvīryas remain protecting the world;
one should always offer oblations and worship in that sacred field.
O protector of the earth, four beings there—the twice-born and others—receive the offering:
the earth, the sky, the tree, and the bird, each desiring the offering intended for its own enemy.
The four [classes] have permanent entitlement, while others among the people are eaters of raw flesh.
They were dark-brown, with tawny hair, tawny eyebrows, and tawny eyes.
Daṃṣṭrākarālī, Atyugrā, Kalāpā, Bharaṇā, and Jvalā;
With Kashmiri sandalwood, śrīkhaṇḍa, musk, mīna, and phalguṣa;
with flowers, garments, umbrellas, lamps, and guggulu incense.
Propitiated by the ancient ones who have cultivated their minds and are devoted to the sequential worship,
and by means of bells, musical instruments, songs, and so forth, they always grant all desires.

Oṃ hrāṃ oṃ hāṃ hūṃ! Descend upon [Name]! O Kṣetrapāla of great power, radiant with a mass of tawny matted hair, three-eyed, with a flaming mouth, accept this incense, flowers, and offering of bali! Bhairava-form, *turu* (twice), *muru* (twice), *kha* (twice), *la* (twice), *phreṃ* (twice), *haḥ*! O Lord of the Great Ḍāmara, forgive me; grant me boons, svāhā!
By offering oblations (bali) to all according to the prescribed rule with this mantra,
that famine there, along with its attendant calamities and fears, shall cease.
May the king be eternally joyful and the protector of all;
may he obtain his desired objects and always achieve victory over his enemies.
O Ajarā and the other guardians of the field, accept this offering; svāhā!
Thus ends the offering to the Immortal and others. To Khavasaviye.

Aiṁ (5). She who is in heaven, in the intermediate space, in the ten directions, in the world, at the base of the seven netherworlds, in the sacred fields (*kṣetra*), the seats (*pīṭha*), and the secondary seats (*upapīṭha*), at the uneven crossroads, in my own [abode], or in the cremation grounds; on the banks of rivers, among thorns, on the beautiful shores of the ocean, or at the descent of Dhūmakāra—[to her I bow].
Who [is] in Pūrṇagiri, or again in the excellent Oḍḍiyāna, the foremost? (1)
In the city called Kulapati, known as Jāla, the gateway of yoga; in Kāmarūpa, which is beautiful in form;
in Ujjayinī, Aṭṭahāsa, Paṭu, Paṭaha, Ravela, and Oḍa; and in the region of Pradeśa.
On Śrīśaila, at Pārijāta, in the abode of Paśupati, on the Hemavindhyā mountains, in the region of Śrīmokāpīḍa, and on Marutpathagiri—[there dwell] the Ḍākinīs and Sākinīs. (2)
In Kashmir, in the land of Andhra, in Draviḍa and Malaya, in Brahmāvarta, in Kaluṭi, in the kingdom of Strīrājya, at Hakkaḍokka, Durasi, Virajaka, and the Siddhakṣetra of Uhāsa;
at Erudī, on the Pāripātra mountain, on the peak of the Himagiri, in the land of Kāñcī, and at Prayāga.
In Saurāṣṭra, in the Middle Country, in the city of Bhṛgukaccha, or in Kośala or Kāmbuka. (3)
In Karṇāṭa, or Koṅkaṇa, or in the excellent city of Magadha, in Karṇakubja, Kaliṅga, Vacchoma, Daṃsavāha, or in Pāṭala, which is covered in a mass of snow, or in the place called Ḍoṅgara;
In Aṅga, Hemātṛcakra, Munigaṇanilaya, Ḍohara, Candradeśa,
Rāsaura, Puṣpalākhya, Girigahvaraguhā, Cākuva, and Siṃhanāda— (4).

In the place called Ramā, in Bhīmanāda, in the city of Śivapura, in Bhadrakūla, in Jayākhya, in the one named Śrī-Vindhya, under the parasol on the slope of Pravaragiri, and in Yakṣakumbha— [these are] Valaṅgā.

In Vārāṇasī, on the vast path of the triple-streamed river, on the pure bank, on the road, at the edge of the Mlecchas, in the Mleccha garland, in the cave of Mount Maraya, in the land of Brahmā, or in a city. (5)
In Bhadrāṅga, Mūlasthāna, Prakṛtipurālīya, Siṃhakarṇa, Śaśāṅka, Triśrotra, in the midst of the sky, on the bed of the best of gods, and in the place called Gahvara— at these locations.

May all those Mothers, who are born from the maṇḍala of the Yoginīs, who are praised by various wise ones, and who are accomplished Siddhas well-pleased, grant divine accomplishment—those who are praised by various wise ones. (6)
Whether it be the sword, the accomplishment of mantras, entry into the best of cities, flight through the sky, or the eye;
the paralyzing of enemies, victory over the hosts of foes, the immobilization [of adversaries], or all branches of knowledge.

May they—those who delight in wine and writing and are devoted to Bhairava—grant all these: long life, the state of a monkey, the pill of alchemical elixir, magical sandals, and the accomplishment of all desires. (7)

Whether from wicked men, thieves, enemies, death, the poison of the hosts of planets, at the falling of a thunderbolt, in battle, at the royal gate, or in a flood of water— may Carmmamuṇḍā, when meditated upon, shatter all fear.

Making the sounds *cauṃ*, *chauṃ*, and *pheṃ*, she adorns herself with "ha ha ha ha" laughter; drinking and dancing, the Mother of Mantras utters *kili kilita kili*, proclaiming the Kaula language. (8)
The syllables *sā*, *śu*, *ṣkā*, *kāma-rūpā*, *ya-ra-la-va-pa-ṭa-hā*, the sounds *hā-hā* and *hūṃ-kāra*,
*uttiṣṭhā*, *nīla-kaṇṭhā*, *amara-su-hṛdayā*, and the *bindu* praised upon the head.
Making the sound "phreṃ phreṃ phreṃ," she is Lalalala, who causes the creeper to melt and drinks [it]. (9)
Kṛṣṇā, the messenger known as Kāmā, praised by the virtues of the immortals, merged with the Bindu and the end of Nāda;
she bestows success at the end of Śakti, has reached the supreme beyond the supreme, and has increased the limbs of the waves.
She is bold, the protectress of the world, joined with the Gaṇas and the Wind, and attended by the Earth.
The sixth [vowel] joined with the bindu, delighted in the lotus of Kula, is the savior known as Kuṇḍalā. || 10 ||

May that renowned power of Rudra, the terrifying Bhadrakālī, who takes any form at will, who has entered both the Akula and Kula lineages, and who devours those who harbor hatred, grant auspiciousness.

May she known as Sāmeśrīkubjikā bestow the supreme, leftward (vāma), divine, and infallible [power]; may Cāmuṇḍā, the Kaulinī of the Koṅkaṇa tradition, grant it within the Kula lineage and the observance of the Kaula path. 11.

Mālinī, whose abode is manifested in the Left-hand Path (vāmamārga), whose body is the Bindu, and who consists of both Akula and Kula, has been declared by you to reside within the circle of the syllable *Uṃ* or the Maṇḍala, O Yogin.

She who rests upon the lap of Śrīnātha, praised by the assembly of the most eminent sages, she of formidable form, that Goddess, the Mother of the World, whose face is a fragment of Śiva—the Mother within the circle of Śrīnātha. 12.

Worshipped by Śrīkaṇṭha, accompanied by the four yugas, known as Ambikā in the central liṅga, she dwells upon the sacred seat (pīṭha), fulfilling all desires with her shimmering arts, her splendor proclaimed by the Kaula path.

I bow with devotion to that Goddess known by the name Śrī Kubjikā, who possesses the course of the triple path, consists of three syllables, and has three modes; she whose abode is made manifest and who is differentiated by the beginning and end of the fivefold [group]. 13.
May she known as Śrī Kubjikā— the dark one, whose form is a skeleton, whose roar is most intense, the terrifying devourer— reveal the unfailing, divine flood of great knowledge.
Thus is Mahābali. In the midst of Mahābali is *saviyajuroṃ*.
The power of the fault of speed has been exhausted.
Aiṃ (5). Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, Aparājitā, Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Bhīmā, and Kālā—these are likewise the eight.
Divyayoginī, Mahāyoginī, Siddhiyoginī, Gaṇeśvarī, Sākinī,
Kālarātrī, Ūrdhvakeśī, and Niśāsvanī.
Deep-voiced, thick, and possessing a chest like wind and fire.
Bhīṣaṇā, Mahānandā, and likewise Jvālāmukhī.
Piśācī, Hastinī, Jakṣaṇī, Dhūrjaṭī,
Viṣabhakṣī, Sarvasiddhi, Tuṣṭi, and likewise Icchā.
Hūṃkālī, Bhāsvarī, Dīrghā, Dhūmrākṣī, Karahapiyā,
Mātaṅgī, Kākadiṣṭi, and likewise Tripuracātakī.
The Rākṣasī of terrible roar, red-eyed and possessing every form.
Victorious is she who brings victory, fierce and terrible, with emaciated limbs and a human-eating nature;
O Bhīrabhadra and Mahākāla, she is Kaṅkālī, with a distorted countenance.
The Krodharājas, the Bhīmabhadras, the Vāyuvegās, and the Bhayānanās.
And likewise Brāhmī, Vaiṣṇavī, Raudrī, Carcikā, and Īśvarī.
Vārāhī, Nārasiṃhī, and Śivādūtī constitute the sixty-fourth.
May these goddesses always accept this offering from me in the great fire.

O sixty-four yoginīs, accept this bali! Grant all peace! For the destruction of all obstacles, grant peace for all diseases! HŪṂ (2) PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. This is the bali offering for the sixty-four yoginīs. [End.]
Aiṃ (5). Caṇḍāghaṇṭā, Mahānāsā, and so forth are the thirty-two yoginīs. (5) [They reside] on the petals. Sa-sā-ya.

The offering of the *khavalāsa* bali: Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ! All the *pīṭhas* and *upapīṭhas*, as well as the gates and sub-gates, the fields (*kṣetra*) and sub-fields (*upakṣetra*), and the assemblies (*saṃdoha*) situated in every direction—all the *yoginīs* and the lords of *yogins* and *vīras* have gathered here according to the *tantra*.
O Great Wheel, this is the chapter; Śrīnātha has granted me a boon:
those who are devoted with faith to the teaching and intent upon worshipping the feet of the Guru and the Goddess.
May the goddess always grant me grace for the attainment of all siddhis.
Those on the surface of the earth who hate the heroes and the yoginīs—
The Goddess accepted that offered oblation at the assembly of the conduct of the *samaya*.
The Veda, the Smṛti, the mind, the nourishment, the flesh, the fat, the bone, and life itself.
But for one who has been deceived by the wicked, [the city] is crowded with hosts of Yoginīs.
May the deceit of those who harbor evil desires, bad dreams, ill omens,
and wicked speech be destroyed by the multitude of Yoginīs, who are gathered in great numbers.
Those three essences which are proclaimed to be within the syllables beginning with *uṃ*—
the collections of medicinal herbs and minerals— are present in the cardinal and intermediate directions.
O practitioners, that Yoginī whose self is united with Yoga truly abides in the earth, the netherworld, the cosmic egg, and in all other places.
The deities of the lords of the gods abide in truth through the heroic stride; likewise, the Siddhas, Putrakas, Ācāryas, and Sādhakas [abide in truth] for one who sleeps upon the ground.
Whether in a city, or in a village, or in a forest, or by an excellent river.
At a pond, a well, a single tree, a cremation ground, or in a circle of Mothers (mātṛmaṇḍala).
May those others as well, who assume various forms and dwell in banyan trees,
all being fully satisfied, accept the offering from every side.
I have come to them for refuge; all this bestows its fruit upon them.
One should protect whatever action I have performed, whatever I shall perform, and whatever has been done.
Satisfied by the offering of oblations and flowers, they are mindful of me.
May all my actions be successful; may all my faults be pacified.
By the grace of Śiva and Śakti, I bow to the venerable letter Ku.
Thus is the *samaya-bali*. This is it.

The shadow of Nirvāṇa; O Mahābali, who shakes your own abode! [Offer] the mudrās for invocation and so forth; sandalwood paste; unbroken rice grains; vermilion; flowers; incense; lamps; and food offerings.

Japa || Praise (2) Samālaka || The Three Deities || Maṇḍala || Hymn || Aiṃ (5) Having the form of an unbroken circle || Śrī Saṃvartā || I always salute her || She who possesses the knowledge of desire || The syllable Ū || Brahmāṇī || East and South || Just like an arrow.

Here [are the offerings of] fragrance and so forth. [Offerings to] the gratified *pretas*. The libation (*tarpaṇa*). Having scattered the sacrificial oblation (*bali*) upon the pavilion and the four directions, one should recite the mantra: Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Prasphura (2) Ghora (2) Taratanu Ruprapracaṭa (2) Kaha (2) Vama (2) Pracaṭa (2) Daha (2) Vama (2) Dama (2) Ghātaya (2) Vighātaya (2) Vighni (2) Hūṃ (3) Phaṭ Kroṃ Komārikā Vicce Pādukāṃ. One should offer with this mantra: Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ.
And he is not subject to bondage.

Ekāneka | Aṃbe pūrvva | Hrīṃ ācamanīyaṃ svāhā | The dismissal of the bali offering: Laṃkhachatutaye | Nosiya | Balithāye (2) Sacchoya | Sthānānurūpeṇa | Mālakoviya | Thus ends the ritual procedure for the worship of the bali offering to the obstructing spirits (vighna).
Then follows the ritual procedure for the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
Curd is to be known in the east, cow urine in the south;
milk is to be known in the west, and ghee indeed in the north.
They say that the *liṅga* belongs to Agni; a vessel for flowers is placed in the southwest (*nairṛtyāṃ*), cow dung in the northwest (*vāyavyāṃ*), and *kuśa* grass water in the northeast (*iśānyāṃ*).

In the center is the vessel for Brahman. The offering (argha) for the Sun. The ritual placement (nyāsa). The worship of oneself with the argha vessel. The oblation (bali). The presentation of the oblation. The invocation (āvāhana) and so forth. The worship beginning with cow’s urine and other substances.

KHPHREṂ Paramahaṃsinī, the omniscient heart-mantra for the deity of fire (2). [This is] the worship with cow urine. KHPHREṂ O Goddess, on the path to Nirvāṇa, Tṛpti is the head-mantra for Janārdana; [this is] for the cow dung (2). [This is] the cow dung.

KHPHREṂ! To the crest-lock (*śikhā*) of primordial awakening that pacifies the turbulent and violent floods, [I offer] milk (*payas*) to the deity Soma. (2) KHPHREṂ! To the armor (*kavaca*) that shatters all misfortunes, calamities, and afflictions, [I offer] curd (*dadhi*) to Umāpati. (2) [Curd. KHPHREṂ! To the three eyes (*netratraya*) of the Sun, whose power is unimpeded and who is the boat across the ocean of all calamities, [I offer] ghee (*sarpiṣ*). (2) [Ghee.]
Khphreṃ. To Paramahaṃsinī, the Omniscient One; to the Heart, to Varuṇa, and to the Kuśa-water, homage! [Kuśa-water.]
Khphreṃ! O bestower of the path to Nirvāṇa, obeisance to Brahma-Śiva at the head of the three. [This is] the worship of the cow-dung liṅga.
KH PHREṂ! Homage to the crest-lock (śikhā) of primordial awakening, the glorious one who pacifies the onset of calamities; [offering of] flowers and water.
Khphreṃ! Homage to the Brahmā weapon, the subduer of hundreds of enemies; [the water-pot].
O Sage, [this is] for the respective mantras of the central vessel.

In the ninth chapter on the Armor Mantra (*kavacamantro*): the worship with the Root Mantra (*mūlamantra*). For the purification of the *argha* vessel with the Weapon Mantra (*astramantra*), there is striking with the Armor Mantra; by that [mantra], the veiling (*avaguṇṭhana*); and inspection with the Root Mantra. Thus are the four purificatory rites (*catussaṃskāra*). Having divided [the water] into three parts: one part for the bathing of the Deity, one part for the fire, and one part for the patron (*yajamāna*).
The consecration of the weapon-mantra.

One should not mutter the Gāyatrī; this is the Dhāraṇā (10). Pratiṣṭhā: You are established in divinity; may there be a firm establishment for the three worlds. Through your presence, protect the sacrificer, his sons, his cattle, and his kinsmen in all circumstances. O Deśaṇabhairava, salutations to you! May they be well-established and granters of boons.
Cow dung for the ritual bath of Śiva. The five nectars (pañcāmṛta) bath.

The seed-syllable of Vāyu (ya) with the duration of a long *ū*; above that, Varuṇa (va); above that, Kāla (ma) joined with the final letter of the alphabet (kṣa); above that, the supreme seed-syllable of Fire (ra) with *saha* (sa);
[ending with] the Moon (*i*) and the Bindu (*m*), situated at the end of dissolution—[this is] the bearer of the white lotus, flowing with streams of milk.
But one who has seen a falsehood constantly burns his family with evil that is indeed like Mount Meru.
O Water! O Thou who art difficult to cross!
With milk, with *hūṃ*, and with the earth-purified water,
I constantly bathe the wish-fulfilling cow by the command of Śiva.
Curd.
O Goddess, always bathe Dadhīci, the lord of the Comās and the beloved favorite of the gods; being well-pleased, you shall always remain satisfied.
The enclosure.
O you who possess the trident purified by clarified butter, O you who possess the trident purified by the liṅga!
In the form of a serpent of fire, he [protected] that triple world and its people, making them auspicious.
The yellow robe.
Arising from the Gomukhi-shakti, it is dear and beloved to the gods.
By means of which bath, performed while standing beneath the wish-fulfilling tree of one's desires, [the goal] is attained.
With this branch.
This fragment possesses great flavor and is likewise cool to the mind.
The goddess, who grants unbroken boons, has been bathed with the crescent moon.
Likewise, with the five products of the cow and so forth, and the five Brahmans and so forth as the fragrance,
combined with the five substances, I bathe [the deity] with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
The worship of Mṛtyuñjaya.
Recitation and Hymn of Praise.
I bow down to the eternal, beautiful, pure, teacher, and terrifier of faults; to the universal Lord of the universe, the god Śaṅkara.
Here, [the ritual of] scent; dismissal with the *astra* mantra; and having placed the *vardhanī* vessel at the front of the *kalaśa*.

The five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) are for the Guru, the Ācārya, and others, as well as for the patron (*yajamāna*). [This is performed] with the *astra-mantra*. In the southwest direction (*nairṛtya*), the preparation of the *argha* vessel is performed. The placement (*nyāsa*) is the *aghora-mantra*: *oṃ hrāṃ namaste rudrarūpe hraḥ mahāpāśupatāstrāya astrāya phaṭ*.
Hrīṃ, O Aghora! Hrāṃ, salutation to the Heart, the Self of All.
Hrāṃ thaghore hrīṃ, svāhā to the head of Brahmā.
Hrāṃ, O you who are more terrible than the terrible, Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the flaming crest-lock!
Hrāṃ sarvataḥ sarvva sarvve hreṃ, [homage] to the armor of Piṅgalaka, hūṃ!
Hroṃ juṃ saḥ! O self whose form is light, Hroṃ! Vaṣaṭ to the three eyes!
Hrāṃ, salutations to you who possess the form of Rudra; Hraṃḥ, to the Great Pāśupata weapon, the weapon, Phaṭ!
Hrāṃ Kṣaṃ, salutation to Īśāna, the upward-facing one.
Hrāṃ Yaṃ, salutation to Tatpuruṣa, the eastern face.
Hrāṃ raṃ, salutation to Aghora, the southern face.
Hrāṃ vaṃ, salutation to Vāmadeva, the northern face.
Hrāṃ Kṣaṃ, salutation to Īśāna, the supreme and non-supreme face.
Hrāṃ Oṃ Hrāṃ! Salutations to you who have the form of Rudra; Hraṃḥ! To the great Pāśupata weapon, Phaṭ!

The preparation of the special *argha* vessel: water, milk, tips of *kuśa* grass, white mustard seeds, sesame, rice, *kola*, and barley—these eight substances are combined in the vessel. This is known as the "special qualification" (*paryāya-viśeṣaṇa*). One should perform the worship of the *argha* vessel with the six limbs of the Aghora mantra. After performing the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites, one should display the *dhenu-mudrā*. The mantra for sprinkling the *argha* vessel is the Aghora mantra; one should recite it starting from the first syllable. This is the preparation of the *argha* vessel.
Then follows the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
Oṃ hrāṃ hlāṃ, to the element of earth, to the principle of withdrawal (nivṛttikalā), to Brahmā Sadyojāta, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ hrāṃ hroṃ, to the principle of establishment (pratiṣṭhā-kalā), to the letter Paṃ, to the element Ākāśa, to Viṣṇu, to Vāmadeva, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ hrāṃ hūṃ, to the Vidyā-kalā, to the principle of fire (tejas-tattva), to the deity Rudra, to Aghora, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ hrāṃ hyaiṃ! To the peaceful aspect, to the wind element, to the presiding deity Īśvara, to Tatpuruṣa, hūṃ phaṭ!

Oṃ hrīṃ hvauṃ! To the digit beyond peace (śāntyatītakalā), to the principle of space (ākāśatattva), to the deity Sadāśiva, to Īśāna—hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ hrāṃ haḥ! At the wheel of command (ājñācakra). Thus is the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
The Hotṛ [performs] the adorning with all ornaments; the placement of all limbs.
Then one should begin the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). First is the ritual placement of the six messengers (*ṣaḍdūtīnyāsa*).

Aiṃ (5) Hskhphreṃ Kāli Kāli Hrāṃ Mahākāli Hrīṃ O you who devour flesh and blood! Hūṃ! O Goddess with red and black faces! Hrau! Māṃ Māṃ! Let the enemies see me! [I worship] the venerable sandals of the goddess Kālikā, the messenger of the heart of Śrī.

Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ! Salutation to the Blessed One, the fierce Cāmuṇḍālinī, consumer of the blood and flesh of enemies, bearer of the skull-cup and the *khaṭvāṅga* staff! Strike (2)! Burn (2)! Vomit (2)! Cook (2)! Hūṃ (3)! Kill so-and-so (2)! Devour (2)! Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! To the venerable Duṣṭacāṇḍālinī at the location of the head, [I offer] the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*).
Aiṃ (5) Aghore Hrauṃ Thaghore Hsphreṃ Ghora(2)tare Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Sarvvataḥ Sarva Sarvve Hskhphreṃ Namaḥ te Rudrarūpe Hsauṃ. To the seat of the crest-tuft, the venerable Śikhāsvacchanda Śrīpādukā.

Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ, O you who have been uplifted by the assembly of sages, Hrīṃ, O you who have increased the prosperity of all the earth, Hrīṃ, O you who are seen and perceived, Hrīṃ, O you who are written as the protection against all [obstacles], Śrī-Bhelakhikā, [I worship] the venerable sandals at the place of the armor.
Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ Guhyakubjike Hūṃ Phaṭ Hrīṃ Rakte Mahārakte Cāmuṇḍeśvarī Aiṃ Haṃ Svāhā. [I worship] the Śrīpādukā of Raktacāmuṇḍā located in the position of the eyes.

Aiṃ (5) Hskhphreṃ Śkhphrīṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ! Strike down all those who have performed, are performing, or will perform any calamities, such as the application of diagrams (*yantra*), mantras, or powders (*cūrṇa*). O you whose fangs are terrifying, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Ṅlauṃ Ṅlūṃ Ślū-īṃ! Guhyakubjikā, the messenger of the weapon (*astradūtī*), the venerable sandals of Guhyakubjikā! Thus ends the fierce hexad (*ugraṣaṭka*).
The ritual placement (nyāsa) of the six Ḍākinīs.
Aiṃ (5) Ḍāṃ Ḍīṃ Ḍūṃ Ḍmlvryūṃ! O Ḍākinī, protect me today; O you who bring all beings under your control, [worship] the Śrī-pādukā on the neck. (2) [End of mantra]. On the neck.
(5) RĀṂ RĪṂ RŪṂ RMLVRYŪṂ! O Rākinī, protect my blood-element! (2) O you who bring all sentient beings under control, [place] the venerable sandal (śrīpādukā) upon the heart.
Aiṃ (5) Lāṃ Līṃ Lūṃ Lmlvryūṃ! O Lākinī, protect me! Protect my marrow and flesh! O Śrīpādukā, who brings all sentient beings under control, [protect me] at the navel.

Aiṃ (5) Kāṃ Kīṃ Kūṃ Kmlvryūṃ! O Kākinī, protect me (twice); protect my fat-element (medas-dhātu) (twice). [I worship] the venerable sandals (śrīpādukā) that bring all beings under control. [To the] Liṅga.

Aiṃ (5) Sāṃ Sīṃ Sūṃ Smlvryūṃ! O Sākinī, protect me; protect my bone-element (asthidhātu). [Salutation to] the glorious sandals (śrīpādukā) that bring all sentient beings under control. [To be placed] in molasses (guḍe).
Aiṃ (5) Hāṃ Hīṃ Hūṃ Hmlvryūṃ! O Hākinī, protect me (2)! Protect my marrow-element (2)! O Śrīpādukā, who brings all sentient beings under control! [Place this] in the center of the earth.
Aiṃ (5) Yāṃ Yīṃ Yūṃ Ymlvryūṃ! O Yākinī, protect me; protect my semen-element (śukradhātu). O you who bring all sentient beings under control, [homage to] the venerable sandals (śrīpādukā)!
In the thousand-petaled [lotus] at the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra).
Then follows the placement of the eight Mothers (aṣṭamātṛkānyāsa).
(5) At the sacred site of Prayāga: AṂ Asitāṅgabhairava, ĀṂ Brahmāṇī Ambā; [I worship] the venerable sandals at the head.
(5) In the field of Vārāṇasī, [one should worship] Kaṃ, Rurubhairava, Kaṃ, and Māheśvarī on the sandals; [these are located] on the face.
(5) And at the sacred site of Kolāgiri, the sandals of Caṇḍabhairava and Kaumārī are in the ear.
In the field of Aṭṭahāsa, Ṭaṃ is Krodhabhairava and Ṭāṃ is Nārāyaṇī. [This is] the heart.
In the field of Jayantī, that Unmattabhairava [is] that Vārāhī; [the] pādukā [is] at the navel.
(5) At Caritrakṣetra, [worship] Pañcapālībhairava; at Śakrānī, Svādhiṣṭhāna.
(5) In the field of Ekāmra, [he is] Bhīṣaṇabhairava, and [she is] Cāmuṇḍā; in the Ādhāra.
(5) In the field of Devīkoṭa, [I place] Śaṃ Saṃhārabhairava and Śāṃ Mahālakṣmī on the sandals at the feet. Thus is the placement of the eight Mothers (aṣṭamātṛkā-nyāsa).

Khphreṃ (27). Having recollected [the mantra] while holding one's breath, one should conceive of the state of Brahmā through the subtle form of the Root Goddess (Āmūladevī), the state of Viṣṇu through the intermediate form, and the state of Rudra through the supreme form. Thus, having generated the form by means of the Self, one should bring the Self—which is supreme bliss—into that [form] by means of inhalation (pūraka), and having fixed it in the heart by means of retention (kumbhaka), one should perform the sixfold deposition (ṣoḍhānyāsa).
Therein, first:
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O feet of Śrīnātha, [reside] in the aperture of Brahmā (the crown of the head).
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, at the feet of Mother Mahālakṣmī, in the region of the Bindu.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Vyomavāmeśvarī Ambā at the feet; [Hrīṃ Śrīṃ] Vāmanetra at the left eye.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the feet of the Mother Khecarī are in the left nostril.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Dikcarī Ambā Śrī—[to be placed] on the face.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Gocarī Ambā Śrī, at the right nostril.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Bhūcarī Ambā Śrī—[worship] at the right eye.
Thus ends the first leftward sequence. (1)

Now, the gross placement (sthūlanyāsa): (2) *kheṃ* at the heart; (2) *phreṃ* at the throat; (2) *raṃ* at the palate; *eṃ* at the two eyebrows; *maṃ* on the skin of the remainder. Thus is the pentad of space (*vyomapañcaka*). (2) ||

Khphreṃ at the center of the eyebrows. Khphreṃ, homage to all the Yoginīs of Accomplishment (Sarvasiddhiyoginī) at the throat. Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment (Sarvasiddhimātṛ) at the heart.

Homage to her who is delighted by the eternal and non-eternal bliss—at the navel. Homage to the Mistress of the entire wheel of families—at the secret place. Homage to the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī—at the anus. Taṃ at the navel; Dyaṃ at the heart; Thāṃ at the end of the twelve (dvādaśānta). This is the first section of the Mother (Mātṛkhaṇḍa). Khphreṃ at the station of Brahmā (the crown); Hrīṃ at the left eye; Hrūṃ at the right eye; Hāṃ at the left ear; Pheṃ at the right ear; Kṣoṃ at the left nostril; Kroṃ at the right nostril; Naṃ at the mouth.

*Maṃḥ* at the crest-lock (*śikhā*). The second section of the *Ārṣa*. *Khphreṃ*, O Supreme Swan (*paramahaṃsinī*), at the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*). O Giver of the Path to Nirvāṇa, at the tip of the nose (*nāsāgra*). O Pacifier of adverse calamities, at the palate (*tālu*). O Destroyer of all misfortunes, portents, and afflictions, at the jaw (*hanu*). O Ferry across the ocean of all calamities, at the throat (*kaṇṭha*). O Pacifier of all enemies, at the chest (*vakṣas*). O Goddess, come (*āgaccha*)—twice—at the heart (*hṛdaya*). Laugh (*hasa*)—twice—at the navel (*nābhi*). Leap (*valga*)—twice—at the heart (*hṛdaya*).
O you who devour human blood, entrails, and fat! Kaṃde! Crush, crush my own enemies! Tripathe!

Eat! Eat! At the thighs: Break! Break! with the trident! At the secret parts: Cut! Cut! with the sword! At the feet: Strike! Strike! At the big toes: Sever! Sever! Thus, at the sixteen supports: Fulfill all my desires! At the feet: O Most Compassionate One! At the knees: O Blessed Lady who assumes the form of Mahābhairava! At the shanks: O You who are saluted by the best of the thirty gods! At the secret parts: [Strike!]

O Mother of all mantras! [At] the navel. O you who are affectionate toward those who bow before you! [At] the heart. O Goddess Mahākālī! [At] the pit of the throat. O destroyer of Time! [At] the mouth. Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ! Be gracious to me, who am afflicted by passion! [At] the ears. Act! [At] the eyes. [Protect] the daughters of gods and demons! [At] the head.
Thus, in the [chapter on] the twelve knots.

Hrīṃ at the aperture of Brahmā; Śrīṃ at the bindu; Hūṃ at the face, Phaṭ at the heart; Phaṭ at the six ādhāras; Phaṭ at the navel; Svā at the liṅga; Hā at the anus. Thus is the nine-syllable nyāsa performed according to the sequence of the staff (daṇḍakrama). (3)
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Siddha-yoginīs; the sandal of the Lord of the Upper Face. Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Mothers of the Siddhas; the venerable sandal of the Lord of the Eastern Face.
Khphreṃ! Homage to the one who is gladdened by eternal, ever-arising bliss; to the venerable sandals of the Lord of the Southern Face.
Khphreṃ! To the Mistress of the entire wheel of families, the Lord of the northern face, the venerable sandals!
Khphreṃ! To the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī, the Lord of the Western Face, Śrīṃ! Sandalwood sandals!
Thus is the placement of the five faces.
Khphreṃ! O Supreme Delighting One, Power of Omniscience, Glorious Lord of the Heart!
Khphreṃ! O Śrī Śirānātha, bestower of the path to nirvāṇa, power of eternal satisfaction!
Khphreṃ! O Śrī, Lord of the Crest, whose power is awakened from beginningless time, who pacifies all calamities and adversities!
Khphreṃ! O Śrī, the Lord of Armor, the power of sovereignty that shatters all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions!
Khphreṃ! O Lord of the Eye, Śrī, the boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities, whose power is never lost!
Khphreṃ! O Śrīpādukā of the Lord Anantatāśaktinātha, the pacifier of all enemies!
Thus ends the Khaḍga-nyāsa.

O Goddess, come! (2) || Varadanātha Śrī || Laugh! (2) O Abhayanātha || At the wrist: || Valga! (2) || Kalaśanātha, feet! || At the left joint: || O devourer of human blood, entrails, and fat! || Kapālanātha, feet! || On the left arm: || Crush, crush my own enemies! || Khaṭvāṅganātha, place of the feet! || Eat! (2) Muṇḍanātha, feet! || On the right shoulder: || Pierce, pierce with the trident! (2) || Triśūlanātha, feet!

Cut! (2) || At the feet of Aṅkuśanātha || At the right elbow || Strike, strike with the sword || At the feet of Khaḍganātha (? || At the right wrist || Cut, cut || At the feet of Pāśanātha || At the right palm ||
Thus is the gross placement; this is the second.

On the forehead and so forth, in counter-clockwise order: *khphreṃ* on the forehead; *hrīṃ* on the eyes; *hūṃ* on the cheek; *hāṃ* on the [other] eye; *pheṃ* on the shoulder; *kṣauṃ* on the arm; *kroṃ* on the fingers.

Salutation to Pāśvī on the side; to Pratyaṅgirā on the upper arm; to Mahārāvā on the shank; to Mahāśaṅkhā on the feet; to Viciyānī on the toes; to Haḍḍamaḍḍā on the right toes; to Mecālinī on the two feet; to Mahākālī on the shank; to Kāmarājī on the thigh; to Vivi and Āvi on the sides; to Anthi and Hanthi on the joints of the fingers; to Paramadanthi on the hands; to Soyahanthi on the arms; to Yauhi and Bhairī on the shoulders; and to Manocakarmmā on the throat.

With those [syllables], place *paṃ* on the two cheeks; *ni* on the two eyes; *vajrasajja* on the backbone; *khphreṃ* on the waist; *hrīṃ* on the foundation (*ādhāra*); *hāṃ* on the self-abiding (*svādhisthāna*); *khphreṃ* on the jewel-filling (*maṇipūraka*); *kṣoṃ* on the unstruck (*anāhata*); *kroṃ* on the pure (*viśuddha*); *na* on the station of the command (*ājñā*); and *maḥ* on the tip of the nose.
Thus ends the third subtle placement (sūkṣmanyāsa).
Next is the placement according to the division of others.

Khphreṃ is in the *ādhāra*; sphaṭ is in the *anāhata*; ma is in the *tārunī*; hā is in the *bindu*; caṃ is in the *ardhacandra*; ḍa is in the *nāda*; ge is in the *yonirodhikā*; and ge is in the *vyāpinī*.

*Śva* in *Samanā*, *ri* in *Kulakula*, *sphaṭ* in *Manonmanī*, *rvrīṃ* in *Unmanī*, *sphaṭ* at the end of *Śāmbhava*, *ḍrīṃ hrīṃ* at the end of the sixteen, *sphaṭ* at the end of *Sūkṣma*, and *rvrīṃ phaṭ* at the end of *Parā in Kula*. Thus is the supreme deposition (*paranyāsa*) in due order.

*Khphreṃ* at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*). *Sphaṭ* on the skin (*tvak*) and the rest. *Ma* at the tip of the nose. *Hā* at the *bindu*. *Caṃ* at the navel. *Ḍaṃ* in the left ear. *Yo* in the right ear. *Ge* in the left eye. *Śva* in the right eye. *Ri* in the left nostril. *Sphaṭ* in the right nostril. *Rvrīṃ* on the left cheek. *Sphaṭ* on the right cheek. *Rvyrīṃ* on the face. *Spaṭ* on the tongue. *Rvīṃ* on the teeth. *Sphaṭ* on the crest-lock (*śikhā*).
Thus, according to the sequence of mantras, the supreme fourth nyāsa is completed.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Ḍambaranātha and the Mother Brahmāṇī; [this is] on the skin.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Kamalodbhavanātha and Ambā Māheśvarī; [worship] in the red [quarter].
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of the Mother Kaumārī Gagananāthā; [worship] in the flesh.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Śambhunātha Vaiṣṇavī Ambā;
in the fat, Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, Nīlāmbaranātha Vārāhī Ambā; in the bones.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Suranātha Aindrī Ambā; [to be placed] on the sinews.
Khphreṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khecaranātha Cāmuṇḍāmbā; [in] the marrow.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O Lord Saṃdhāyugeśvarinātha, Mother Mahālakṣmī! [Be present] in the act of subjugation.
Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the eight [elements] beginning with the skin.

Oṃ juṃ saḥ. The feet of Ajinanātha on the right foot; (3) the feet of Ānandāmbā on the left foot; (3) the feet of Iḍyanātha on the right calf; (3) the feet of Īśvarī Ambā on the left calf; (3) the feet of Udayanātha on the right thigh; (3) the feet of Ūrddhagāminī Ambā on the left thigh; (3) the feet of Ṛddhimānātha on the right side; (3) the feet of Ṛtyambā on the left side; (3) the feet of Ḷ Luptadevanātha on the right hand.

(3) The feet of Ḷū Lunāḍambā on the left arm; (3) the feet of Ekāṅganāthanātha on the right arm; (3) the feet of Airāvatī Ambā on the left shoulder; (3) the feet of Oghanānandanātha on the right shoulder.
(3) Au, Karālī, on the left shoulder; (3) Aṃ, Amuranātha, on the right shoulder; (3) Aḥ, Kṛśānu, on the foot and in the heart.
Thus ends the placement of the eight *yāmalas*. Thus the sixfold placement (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*) is completed.
O Goddess of the Gods, if one should constantly recite a mantra without performing nyāsa, all of it is fruitless for him, like whispering into the ear of a deaf man. (1)

Prajāpati is the seer (ṛṣi) of this mantra, Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas), Śrīsiddhalakṣmī is the deity (devatā); its application (viniyoga) is for the recitation for the sake of accomplishing all aims.
Oṃ aṃ aṃ, salutation to the two thumbs.

HŪṂ MAṂ MAṂ, homage to the two middle fingers.

KṢOṂ KAṂ KAṂ KAṂ; salutation to the palms and backs of the hands.
Kroṃ, homage to the left wrists (2).
Salutation to the right wrists, vauṣaṭ; [this is for] the right wrist.

Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ | Phaṭ for the clapping of the hands. Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the hands: Oṃ at the aperture of Brahmā (the crown of the head); hrīṃ on the circle of the face; hūṃ in the right ear.
HĀṂ at the left ear; PHREṂ at the root of the tongue; KṢOṂ at the heart; KROṂ at the penis; NAMAḤ at the secret circle.

Oṃ, crush, crush my own enemies! Devour, devour! Homage to the primary faces! Hrīṃ, pierce with the trident, pierce! Cut, cut! Homage to the southern faces! Hūṃ, strike with the sword, strike! Sever, sever! Homage to the fierce southern faces! Hāṃ, accomplish all my desires as long as they last! Homage to the northern faces of meditation!

Phreṃ! Homage to the feet of Kālānala, the northern face of the Blessed One, who possesses supreme compassion and assumes the form of Mahābhairava. Kṣoṃ! Homage to the southern [face] of the Kaulottara, O Mother of all mantras, who is saluted by the best of the thirty gods.

Kroṃ! O Goddess of great and fierce countenance, whose grace is like that toward those who bow before you; homage to the Northern ones! Homage to Mahākālī, the destroyer of Time; homage to the Southern ones with mouths emitting the sound *phetkāra*!

Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Make her, who is afflicted by passion, gracious. Homage to the faces of the gods and asuras, whose mouths are like the *makaranda* [nectar] of the lotus center. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the emergence of the faces.
Oṃ, to the Supreme Swan, bestower of the path to Nirvāṇa, homage to the heart!
Hrīṃ! To the one who pacifies calamities and misfortunes, svāhā to the head!
HŪṂ! To the crest [mantra] that shatters all enemies of misfortune and the afflictions, SVĀHĀ!
Hāṃ! To the armor that is a raft across the ocean of all calamities, Hūṃ!
Phreṃ! To the one who pacifies all enemies, the three-eyed one, vaṣaṭ!
KṢOṂ KROṂ NAMAḤ | ĀGACCHA ĀGACCHA HASA HA VALGA VALGA NARARUDHIRĀNTA VASĀBHAKṢANI ASTRĀYA PHAṬ ||

Oṃ, salutations to all the Yoginīs of all accomplishments in the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra). Salutations to all the Mothers of all accomplishments in the circle of the face (vaktramaṇḍala). Salutations to her who is delighted by eternal, arising bliss in the location of the uvula (ghaṇṭikā). Salutations to the Mistress of the entire wheel of the Kula in the hollow of the throat (kaṇṭhakūpa). And salutations to the Blessed One, Caṇḍakālī.

Namely: on the right arm: *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ*. On the shaft of the left arm: *Khphreṃ*, O Supreme Haṃsinī, giver of the path to Nirvāṇa! At the heart: *O you who pacify all calamities and misfortunes!* On the right side: *O you who shatter all enemies, ill omens, and afflictions!* On the left side: *O you who cross the ocean of all disasters!* In the center of the navel: *O you who crush all foes!* At the secret organ: *Devī āgaccha (2) hasa (2)*. In the secret maṇḍala:

Leap forth! O you who consume human blood, flesh, and fat! In the foundation mandala, crush my own enemies! Devour them! On the right thigh: pierce with the trident! Cut! Strike with the sword, strike! Cut, cut! On the left thigh: [do so] until you have accomplished all my desires! O you of supreme compassion! On the right shank: O Blessed One, bearer of the form of Mahābhairava! On the left shank: [do so].
O Mother of all mantras, praised by the thirty-three gods; O Goddess who is affectionate toward those who bow before you, [I worship you] at the right ankle.
At the left ankle: Mahākālī, destroyer of Time (Kāla). At the right foot: [Mahākālī].
Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! O you who are afflicted by passion, be gracious with your left foot!
Hrīṃ kuru (2): [place] the daughter of the gods and asuras at the sole of the right foot.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ (3) Svāhā on the sole of the left foot.
Oṃ, homage to the foundation maṇḍalas. Hrīṃ, homage to the navel maṇḍalas. (2)
HŪṂ, homage to the heart-mandalas! HĀṂ, homage to the throat-pits!
Pheṃ, salutation to the nostrils; kṣoṃ, salutation to the right nostril-passage.

*Kroṃ*, salutation to the nostrils; *naṃ*, salutation to the nose; *maṃḥ*, salutation to the circles in the middle of the bow; thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the limbs and classes (*aṅgajāti*).
Oṃ, homage to all the Siddhas and Siddhayoginīs; this is the ritual placement (nyāsa) for the eastern face. (1)
Homage to all the Mothers who have attained perfection. The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the right face. (2)
Homage to her who is gladdened by eternal, ever-arisen bliss! This is the ritual placement (nyāsa) for the northern face. (3)
To the Mistress of the entire circle of families. This is the ritual placement for the western face. (4)
To the Blessed One, Caṇḍakāpālinī. This is the placement for the upward-facing mouth. (5)
*Taṃ* at the center of the eyebrows; *dya* at the heart; *thā* at the navel—thus is the deposition (*nyāsa*) upon the body.

Oṃ at the mouth; Hrīṃ in the left nostril; Hūṃ in the right nostril; Hāṃ in the left eye; Phreṃ in the right eye; Kṣoṃ in the left ear; Kroṃ in the right ear; Na at the penis; Maḥ at the anus. This is the door-assignment (dvāra-nyāsa).
Oṃ, O Supreme Swan-like One, bestower of the path to Nirvāṇa! [To] the head.
[The mantra] for pacifying calamities caused by uneven [circumstances], [to be placed] on the crest-lock.
O armor that shatters all enemies, misfortunes, calamities, and afflictions!
A boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities; [it is] in the eyes.
The destroyer of all enemies in the ten directions.
The weapon [mantra] is the placement; thus is the placement of the six limbs.

O Goddess, come! (2) One should contemplate the invocation of the Goddess Sakārā as being both within one’s own body and externally. Hasa (2)! One should contemplate her as intent on bestowing grace upon one’s own self. [She who is] human blood, entrails, and fat...

[Recite] "bhakṣaṇi. Visualizing the skull-bowl [in the right hand]: "Crush, crush my enemies; devour, devour! Visualizing the khaṭvāṅga [in the left hand]: "Pierce [them] with the trident, pierce [them]! Visualizing the trident: "Cut [them], cut [them] with the sword! Visualizing the sword: "Strike, strike! Visualizing the noose: "Sever, sever! Visualizing the goad [in the right hand]: "Accomplish all my desires, accomplish [them]! [Recite this] as many times as necessary.

One should contemplate the right hand as bestowing boons (*varada*). O most compassionate one! Having contemplated the left hand as granting fearlessness (*abhaya*), one should contemplate a human skull (*naramuṇḍa*) [in the left hand], O Blessed One who assumes the form of Mahābhairava! O Mother of all mantras, who are saluted by the best of the thirty gods! One should contemplate a bell (*ghaṇṭā*).
Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the ten weapons of the arts (kalā).
One should meditate upon [the deity] who is affectionate toward those who bow down; thus is the seat and the ritual placement (nyāsa).
Goddess Mahākālī, destroyer of Time; she who is formless; she whose form is Kuṇḍalinī.

The visualization of the Goddess: *Hūṃ*. One should visualize the Goddess arising from the *janmādhāra* (the source of birth). *Khphreṃ*: the visualization of the Goddess in the form of a flame extending as far as the heart. *Khphreṃ*: from the heart as far as the *bindu* (drop). *Khphreṃ*: from the location of the *bindu* as far as the *brahmarandhra* (cranial aperture). "Be gracious; make the daughters of the gods and demons afflicted with passion. By this, the power of subjugating the universe is declared. *Hrīṃ* at the *janmādhāra*; *Śrīṃ* at the *liṅga*; *Kroṃ* at the location of the *kanda* (bulb).

HŪṂ at the site of the navel; PHAṬ at the heart; PHAṬ at the throat; PHAṬ at the mouth; SVĀ at the site of the bindu; HĀṂ at the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra). Having thus performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the nine syllables located in the middle of the navel according to this procedure of placement, [one attains] the mantra-body.
Then, the body of color.
Resembling pure crystal, with five faces and ten arms,
she is mounted upon Mahārudra, possessing a beautiful body and a radiant form.
Adorned with a crown of matted hair holding the crescent moon,
her remaining locks are decorated with various jewels, great necklaces, and other ornaments.
White, red, and black, crimson and brilliant white like khadira wood,
it is adorned with various jewels, possesses well-proportioned bones, and is beautifully encircled by earrings.
Having the reddish form of the solar disc, blazing with three or five eyes,
with a slightly open mouth and a lolling tongue, she shines intensely as she faces the beholder.
She who wears a garland of the throats of various wicked Daityas and other enemies.
By this, [he beheld] her whose high breasts were rubbed by necklaces fashioned from jewels.
In the center, she was auspicious, with a slender waist, and adorned with the beauty of many ornaments.
Clad in garments adorned with networks of tinkling bells, she was decorated with tiger skins and parrot-patterned waistbands.
O Muṇḍa, you hold an excellent sword, a trident, and so forth in your right hands;
likewise, in your left hands, you hold a skull-topped staff, an excellent vessel, a noose, and a bell.
The pair of knees is beautifully adorned by the clanging of the hero’s bell,
and the two feet are graced by the resonant sound of the gurgling anklets.
Of the one who is brilliantly white, three-eyed, two-armed, and single-faced.
And she was mounted upon the shoulder of Rudra, who was seated in the vīrāsana posture.
Blazing like a fire, it was a mass of gathered flames.
And emerging from the pores of his skin, it was as beautiful as the dawn sky.
Situated in the midst of the eight measures, five-faced and endowed with the four quarters.
She who dwells in the center of the eight Mātṛkās, surrounded by the six Ḍākinīs,
is honored by the fire of the Siddhis in a place crowded with many accomplished masters.
Thus is meditative absorption.
Then follows the placement (nyāsa) of the body and the feet.

Oṃ, homage! Homage to all the Siddhas and Yoginīs at the head. Homage to all the Mothers of the Siddhas on the surface of the forehead. At the tip of the nose: homage to her who is gladdened by eternal bliss. At the left eye: homage to the Mistress of the entire Kula-cakra. At the right eye: homage to the Blessed Lady (Bhagavatī). At the third eye: homage to Caṇḍakāpālinī. At the left cheek: as follows; at the right cheek: the Brahma-section. Oṃ at the left ear; Hrīṃ at the right ear.

HŪṂ on the lower lip; HĀṂ on the upper lip; PHREṂ on the lower teeth; KṢOṂ on the upper teeth; KROṂ on the tongue; NAMAḤ on the mouth. Viṣṇukhaṇḍa! OṂ Paramahaṃsinī! On the throat. O giver of the path to Nirvāṇa! On the left shoulder. O pacifier of calamities and misfortunes!

On the left arm: *sakaladuritāriṣṭakleśadalani* (O crusher of all evils, misfortunes, and afflictions)! On the left wrist: *sarvāpadāmbhodhitaraṇi* (O savior from the ocean of all calamities)! On the fingers of the left hand: *sakalaśatrupramathani* (O subduer of all enemies)! On the nails of the left fingers: *devi āgaccha āgaccha* (O Goddess, come, come)! On the right shoulder: *hasa hasa* (Laugh, laugh)! On the right arm: *valga valga* (Leap, leap)! On the right wrist: *nararudhirāntavaśābhakṣaṇi* (O devourer of human blood, entrails, and marrow)! On the fingers of the right hand: *mama svaśatrūn marda marda* (Crush, crush my own enemies)! On the nails of the right fingers: [silence].

Eat! Eat! In the circle of the rising sun! Pierce! Pierce! with the trident! In the left breast! Cut! (2) In the right breast! Strike! Strike! with the sword! On the left and right buttocks! Cut! (2) In the circle of the navel! Accomplish! Accomplish! all my desires until then! O Kālānala! O Supreme Compassionate One! In the center of the womb! O Blessed Lady! In the circle of molasses! O You who assume the form of Mahābhairava! On the surface of the left buttock!

*Tridaśavara-namite* (O you who are saluted by the best of the thirty [gods])—on the right buttock. *Sakalamantra-māta* (O Mother of all mantras)—on the left thigh. *Praṇatajana-vatsale* (O you who are compassionate toward those who bow down)—on the left thigh. *Devī Mahākālī Kālanāśanī* (Goddess Mahākālī, destroyer of Time/Kāla)—on the left knee. *Hūṃ* (3)—on the left ankle. *Prasīda madanāturām* (Be gracious to me, who am afflicted by passion)—on the right ankle. *Kuru* (2)—on the toes of the left foot. *Surāsura-kanyakām* (O daughter of the gods and demons)—on the toes of the right foot. *Hrīṃ*—on the lower part of the right thigh. *Śrīṃ*—on the right knee. *Hūṃ*—on the right foot. *Phaṭ Phaṭ*.
*Phaṭ svāhā* on the toes of the left foot. *Phaṭ svāhā* on the back. Thus ends the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the body consisting of the feet.
Furthermore, there is the placement of the limbs (aṅganyāsa) upon the hands and face using the Aghora root-mantra.
Alternative reading: The placement of all limbs (sarvaṅgānyāsa); the placement of the hands, face, and limbs (karavaktrāṅganyāsa); the placement of Mālinī (mālinīnyāsa).

Aiṃ (5) La! O Pinākīśa, [place] the sandal upon the flesh.
Aiṃ Va Khaḍgānanda, [I place] the sandal upon the midst of the sinews.
Aiṃ (5) Śa Vakānanda, [place] the pādukā within the marrow of the bones. (5)
O Ānanda, he gave me a sandalwood slipper.
Aiṃ (5) Sa Bhṛgo Śukre Pādukāṃ.
Aiṃ (5) Ha! O Kulīśa, place the sandals upon the support of the vital breath.
Aiṁ (5) Kṣaḥ: the sandal [is placed] upon the center of the joint of the big toe of Saṃvarta-krodha.
Aiṃ (5) Alūṃ, I worship the sandals of Śabdarāśi Bhairavabhaṭṭārikā. (5)
Aiṃ (5). To the Supreme One (Parā) residing in the domain of the Śiva-tattva, [I offer] the sandals to the head (5).
Aiṃ (5). In the section on the principle of the Self (ātmatattva): Aiṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hsauṃ Phaṭ. To Aparā, the heart-sandalwood slipper (hṛdayapādukāṃ) (5).

Aiṃ (5). Aghore Hrīṃ Paramaghore Hūṃ Ghorarūpe Haḥ! O Ghorāmukhī, Bhīmabhīṣaṇī, vam (2), piva (2), ruru (2), rara (2), phaṭ hsauṃ hūṃ phaṭ! To the Parāparā [Devi] presiding over the principle of Vidyā (vidyā-tattva), at the secret place (guhya-sthāna), [I offer] the sandals (pādukā) (5). Thus is the Nyāsa of the Three Vidyās.
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Ru Aghore Hrīṃ Śauṃ; the sandals for the head of Aghoryā.
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Ru Paramaghore Śauṃ, [I offer] the sandals to Paramaghoryā at the location of the mouth.
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Ru Ghorarūpe Haḥ Śau Ghorarūpe, [I offer] the sandals to the Heart. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Ra Ghorāmukhī Śau, [I worship] the sandals at the navel for Ghorāmukhī.
Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ Ru Phaṭ Bhīme Śauṁ, [I offer] the sandals to Bhīmā on the right arm.
Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ Ru Bhīṣaṇyai Śau Bhīṣaṇyai; [I offer] the sandal-paste upon the left arm.
Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ Ra Huṁ Haḥ Vama Śau; [I offer] the sandals to Vamanā on the right thigh. (5)
Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ Ra Phaṭ! O Pibanā, drink! Place the sandals upon the left thigh and the toes of the feet.
Thus ends the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the eight Ghorikās.
Aiṃ (5) Aghore Hrāṃ, obeisance to the heart.
Aiṃ (5) Thaghore Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Aiṃ (5) Ghora-ghorantare Hūṃ, Vauṣaṭ to the Śikhā.
Aiṃ (5) Sarvataḥ sarva sarve hreṃ kavacāya hūṃ.
Aiṃ (5) Juṃ Saḥ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes, whose nature is light, Hrauṃ!
Aiṃ, salutations to you in the form of Rudra; Hraḥ, Phaṭ to the weapon!
Thus ends the Aghora-nyāsa.
Aiṁ (5) Śaṁ, [I offer] the sandals to Siddhā on both feet.
Śāṃ, for the two knees, the sandals of prosperity.
Aiṃ (5) Śiṃ, the sandals for the two thighs of Vidyuttā (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śīṃ, [salutation] to Lakṣmī, the secret sandal (guhyapādukā) (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śūṃ, [I offer] the sandals to Dīptā at the navel. (5)
Aiṁ (5) Śūṁ, [I place] the sandal-paste upon the heart of Mālinī.
Aiṁ (5) Śeṁ, the sandals for Śivā at the throat.
Aiṃ (5) Śaiṃ, the sandals at the mouth for Vasumukhā.
Aiṃ (5) Śoṃ, [I offer] the sandals to Nāsāmbumāyā at both nostrils. (5)
Aiṁ (5) Śauṁ, [I place] sandals upon the two ears for Kaṭakā (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śaṃ Harikeśī, the three-syllabled one, [bestows] the sandals (5).
Aiṁ (5) Śaṁḥ, the pādukā on the face and head (5).
Thus ends the twelve-limbed ritual placement (dvādaśāṅganyāsa).
Aiṃ (5) Śāṃ, the sandal-powder for the heart of omniscience (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śīṃ, to Amṛtatejomālinī Tṛpti, svāhā to the head!
Aiṃ (5) Śūṃ! To the crest-lock (śikhā) of primordial awakening, which proclaims the non-Vedic [truth], vauṣaṭ (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śaiṃ, to Vajriṇī, the bearer of the vajra; to the independent armor, Hūṃ (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śauṃ! To the one who possesses the unceasing power of Tombo, endowed with a thousand splendors, and possessing three eyes—vaṣaṭ (5).
Śaṃ! Homage to you, O Ananta-śakti Śili! Hūṃ! To the Great Pāśupata weapon, to the Thousand-eyed One, hūṃ phaṭ! (5)
Thus concludes the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
The *granthinyāsa* and the *ratnapañcakanyāsa* are written here as well.
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ, the sandal-shoe upon the two feet of Anantagranthi.
Hāṃ! To the two ankles, the Kālagranthi, the sandals. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Hiṃ: the Rudra-knot on the two shanks, the sandals (5).
Aiṁ (5) Hīṁ, the Jyeṣṭhagranthi on the two thighs, the Pādukā (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ: the left knot; Pādukāṃ (5) on both hips.
Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ! The Kāmagranthi is at the tip of the liṅga; [I worship] the pādukā (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hṛṃ; [I worship] the Pādukā at the location of the penis, which is the knot of the physical body. (5)
Aiṁ (5) Hraṁ, the Brahma-knot at the station of Brahma—[I worship] the sandals (5).
Aiṁ (5) Hḷṁ! [I offer] the sandal-paste at the solar knot; [I offer] the sandals below. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Hḹṃ, the lunar knot at the navel; [I worship] the sandals (5).
Aiṃ (5) Heṃ, [I worship] the Pādukā at the knot of the vital breath in the abdomen. (5)
Aiṁ Haiṁ: the life-knot in the heart, the sandals. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Hoṃ, the Viṣṇu-knot at the throat; the pādukā (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hauṃ, the Rudra-knot at the palate, the pādukā (5).
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ: I place the sandals at the location of the Īśvara-knot on the head.
Aiṃ (5) Haḥ! [I place] the sandal of Sadāśivagranthi in the location of the head. (5)
Thus ends the placement of the knots.

Aiṃ (5). O Vāgīśvarī, Glūṃ! O you who reside in the womb of enjoyment in the world of the jewel-sky, O you who move through the nectar of the sky-world, O goddess Gaganānanda, O Mother of the Sky (Gaganāmbā)! [I worship] the sandals of the sixty-four lakhs and crores of Siddhas and the sixty-four lakhs and crores of Yoginīs. (5). [To be placed] between the eyebrows.

Aiṃ (5). To Māyā, mlūṃ: O you who enter the womb of the enjoyments of the jewel-like heavenly world; O you who move through the nectar of the heavenly world; O Goddess who grants the bliss of heaven; O Mother of Heaven; [to the sandals] of the sixty million Siddhas and the sixty million Yoginīs—[I worship] the sandals at the heart.

Aiṃ (5). O Mohanī! Plūṃ! You who enter the womb of the enjoyments of the world of wind; you who move through the nectar of the world of wind; O Pavanānandadeva, O Pavanāmbā! The sandals of the sixteen hundred thousand crores of Siddhas and the sixteen hundred thousand crores of Yoginīs. (5). [The navel.]

Aiṁ (5). To Jñānā, to Mlūṁ, to the one who enters the womb of the enjoyments of the jewel-like mortal world, to the one who moves as nectar in the mortal world, to the goddess who gives joy to mortals, to Mortyambā, to the eight hundred thousand million Siddhas, to the eight hundred thousand million Yoginīs—[I offer] the sandals at the Liṅga.

Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Gāyatrī Nlūṃ, O you who go to the foremost portion of the enjoyments of the world of the jewel-serpents, O you who move through the nectar of the world of serpents, O divine joy of the serpents, O Mother of Serpents, O you who possess forty million times ten million *siddhas*, O you who possess forty million times ten million *yoginīs*, [I worship] the sandals (5). In the molasses.

Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Alūṃ! O you who enter the womb of infinite worldly enjoyments [as] the Ratna-Indranīla; O Anandāloka, you who move through the nectar; O Infinite Ananda-deva, O Infinite Mother, O Siddha of infinite lakhs and crores, O Yoginī of infinite lakhs and crores, [I worship] the sandals (pādukāṃ) (5).
Thus concludes the ritual placement of the five jewels.
Furthermore, there is the placement of the Aghora root-vidyā upon the hands, the face, and the limbs.

The Hand of Śiva. [Offering] the consciousness of the branches of the *khavalāsana* for the worship of the *thotha*. In the center with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*). For the *śikhā*, *svacchanda*, and the *deguli* [deities], [offer] to the *khāṅa*. The three deities; Hetukā and others (10); Aśitāṅga and others (8); the *śikhā-mantra* (3); the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*); the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth; the mudrās; the *ācātrasyaṃ*; for the purpose of worship—perform the invocation, the installation (*sthāpana*), and so forth. This [liquid] is to be held upon the head.

Having performed worship with all the limbs [of the body], one should meditate upon this very self as Śiva. This is the procedure for the *svacchandabhairava-ṭāṃthamabhāra* according to Ācārya. Thus ends the ritual of the Hand of Śiva (*śivahastavidhi*).

Then follows the practice for the sword of knowledge (*jñānakhaḍga-sādhana*). Having fashioned [the handle] from thirty-six *kuśa* grass blades by striking them with *darbha* grass, and having recited the *Śivāstra* mantra seven times, one should bind the braid [of the handle] with that supreme sword. [Recite: *saṃthuṅāthyaṃthuya* | *Aghorāstra*: *oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraḥ prasphura 2 hṛdayāya namaḥ*.

(2) *Ghora ghoratara-tanu-rūpa*, to the head, *svāhā*. (2) *Caṭa pracaṭa*, to the crest (*śikhā*), *vauṣaṭ*. (2) *Kaha vama*, to the armor (*kavaca*), *hūṃ*. (2) *Dama ghātaya*, to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*. (2) *Vighni*, *hūṃ* (3), to the weapon (*astra*), *hūṃ phaṭ*. Again, with the Aghora-weapon mantra, one should maintain the recitation for seven [days]. With a vajra in hand, holding it with the left hand, one should brandish the sword of the knowledge of the sky-lotus (*khavalāna*). Thus is the *Jñānakhaḍgasādhana*.

Then, the purification of the pavilion (*maṇḍapa*): [the ritual] placement (*nyāsa*). With the Heart-mantra, the establishment of the earth: *oṃ hrāṃ laṃ pṛthivyai namaḥ*. With the Root-mantra, inspection (*nirīkṣaṇa*). With the Weapon-mantra (*astra*), sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*). With the Weapon-mantra, striking (*tāḍana*). With the Armor-mantra (*kavaca*), pouring water (*siñcana*). With the Weapon-mantra, digging (*khanana*). With the Topknot-mantra (*śikhā*), lifting up (*uddharaṇa*). With the Heart-mantra, filling (*pūraṇa*). With the Head-mantra (*śiras*), leveling (*samīkaraṇa*). With the Armor-mantra, sprinkling (*abhyukṣaṇa*). With the Weapon-mantra, pounding (*kūṭana*). With the Weapon-mantra, sweeping (*saṃmārjana*). With the Armor-mantra, smearing (*lepana*). [The application of] the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*).
At the eastern gate, the installation of the Ṛgvedin: having prepared a seat of *kuśa* grass for the Four Vedas, [one proceeds] to the center.
Oṃ hrāṃ, to the one who has transcended the stage of tranquility; in the east.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Śāntikalā. [To the] right.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Vidyākalā in the west.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Nivṛttikalā in the north.
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the power of establishment (pratiṣṭhā-kalā).

For the Ṛgveda, this seat and so forth. Installation on the altar. Offering of water for the hands and so forth. One should offer a garment, a blue cloth, a wooden seat, sandals, a water vessel, a vessel for worship, and ornaments. First, the Ṛgveda. (1)

Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā. [Tie] the knot with *kuśa* grass. Oṃ phreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the form of Brahmā. Oṃ khphreṃ, salutation to the heart of Paramahaṃsinī. [Perform] worship, incense and other offerings, and recite the hymn: Oṃ, the *Ṛgveda* is the personified form of Tantra, possessing a luster like that of a sapphire.
His limbs were anointed with divine perfumes, and he was adorned with celestial ornaments.
Situated in the eastern quarter, blazing with great splendor; here [are] the perfumes and so forth.
At the southern gate, the installation of the Yajurvedī is performed; the offering of water for the hands and other rites are as before.

One should offer white garments, an umbrella, a seat, and so forth, all as previously described. *Oṃ siddheśvarāya namaḥ*. [Offer] a knot of *kuśa* grass with three threads. *Oṃ siddhilakṣmīmūrtaye namaḥ*. *Oṃ khphreṃ paramahaṃsinī hṛdayāya namaḥ*. [Perform] worship, incense and other offerings, and recite the hymn of praise.
On the right was the Yajurveda, resembling pure crystal,
wearing divine earrings, with a massive body and great arms.
Established in the southern quarter, O Yajurveda, salutations to you. Here [are offered] perfumes and other [substances].

The installation of Sāmavedī at the western gate. The hand-offering (argha) and other rites are as before. A red cloth and an umbrella. The seat and other items are as before. Oṃ khphreṃ hrīṃ Śivādevī Ambā pādukāṃ. [Tie] a knot with kuśa grass. Oṃ khphreṃ hrīṃ to the form of Śivādevī, obeisance. Oṃ khphreṃ to the heart of Paramahaṃsinī, obeisance. Worship. Incense and other offerings. Hymn of praise.
The eternal Sāmaveda is situated in the western quarter.
The glorious one, wearing red garments, possesses a luster like that of a ruby.
The Brahmin, adorned with garlands and ornaments and graced by radiant auspicious marks, [should be honored] here with perfumes and other offerings.

In the north, the installation of the Artharva-vedi [altar]. The *hastārgha* (hand-water offering) and so forth are as before. A black cloth and an umbrella. The seat (*āsana*) and so forth are as before. Oṃ khphreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the form of Māyādevī. Oṃ khphreṃ, obeisance to the heart of Paramahaṃsinī. [Perform] worship, incense and so forth, and the hymn of praise (*stotra*).
Then Atharvan stood facing west, dark-complexioned, while Uttara Taras stood facing east.
The great sage Piṅgākṣa, who has a neck like a snake and golden hair; here [are offered] perfumes and so forth.

Having had the experts in the four Vedas perform their respective recitations, hymns, and so forth, [the following rites are performed] again within the pavilions (*maṇḍapas*): the worship of the heart-mantra (*hṛdayamantra*) with five threads, a rope of *kusarajju*, sprouts, and flower garlands; the "thunderbolt-making" (*vajrīkaraṇa*) with the weapon-mantra (*astramantra*); the making of the crossroads (*catuṣpathikaraṇa*) with the heart-mantra; the securing of protection for the gateway path with the armor-mantra (*kavacamantra*); and the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*) of the pavilion.
Thus are the eighteen purificatory rites (saṃskāras).

The southern rice and the northern king [of grains]. In the center, perform the sweeping and worship: Oṃ hrīṃ, to the one who is peaceful, the embodiment of the weapon, hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ hrīṃ, to the one who bestows nourishment, the embodiment of Lakṣmī, hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ hreṃ, to Brahmā, for the destruction of all misfortunes, hūṃ phaṭ!
The scattering of kings by means of a weapon.

Taking the *arghapātra* (offering vessel), proceed to the front of the *śiva-śakti-kalaśa*. Perform the purification (*mārjana*) with the right hand by wiping [the vessel] with the *astra-mantra*. Perform the worship of the seat (*velāsana*) for the *śiva-śakti-kalaśa*. Perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the *astra* and the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Perform the self-worship (*ātmapūjā*) beginning with the *arghapātra* and so forth: Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the moving throne (*calāsana*). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the moving bull-throne (*calavṛṣāsana*). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the moving lion-throne (*valasiṃhāsana*). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to You who have the form of Rudra; hras, salutation to Śiva, the Great Pāśupata Weapon.

In this manner, [perform] worship with the six limbs of the *astra* for Śakti. Worship with the *pāśupatāstra* in the *vardhanī* vessel. [Perform] incense, lamps, recitation (*japa*), and hymns (*stotra*). [Offer] gems, medicinal herbs, and so forth. Herein [are included] perfumes and other such items.
The worship of the eastern gate.

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Peaceful Archway (śāntitoraṇa). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Ṛgveda. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Kṛta Yuga. At the trident (śūla): Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Pūṣan. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Dhātṛ. Oṃ, obeisance to Vidhātṛ. Then, on the two branches (śākha): Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Praśānta. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Śiśira. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Bhūrloka. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Bhuvarloka. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Soma. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Aṅga.

Oṃ hrāṃ, to the letter-group *a* (avarga), to Brahmāyaṇī, obeisance! Oṃ hrāṃ, to the letter-group *ka* (kavarga), to Māheśvarī, obeisance! Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Pratyūṣa! Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Prabhāsa! Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the door of the Śāntikalā! Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the presiding deity Īśvara! [At] the upper *udumbara* wheel: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati! Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī! Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Mahālakṣmī!

Then the branch: *Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Nandin*. *Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Mahākāla*. *Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Gaṅgā*. *Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Yamunā*. The banner: *Oṃ hrāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to the Vajra with its hood*. The flag: *Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Kumuda*. *Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Indra, whose vehicle is the elephant*. Meditation on the jar (*kalaśa-dhyāna*).
Mounted upon Airāvata, holding a thunderbolt in his hand, and most beautiful to behold.
I behold the Lord of Śacī, whose body resembles the color of yellowish-red.
Oṃ hrāṃ lūṃ, homage to Indra! Bali! Oṃ hrāṃ, accept this bali from Prayāga, Hetu, and Aśitāṅga! Svāhā! [Perform the rites] from incense up to the end of the hymn of praise.
Salutations to you, O Lord of Sacī, Sovereign and Master of the East;
be present at the sacrifices and ritual acts for the sake of protection.

Here [are] the scents and so forth. [At the] front (? || Oṃ, obeisance to Riddhitoraṇa. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Riddhidvāra. Obeisance to the Khaḍira tree. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Agni, whose seat is the goat. Visualization of the jar (kalaśa).
O God of great strength, you whose seat is the back of a goat and whose hand holds a spear.
I bow to Vaiśvānara, who is red in color and possesses limbs of great splendor.

Oṃ hrāṃ rūṃ, obeisance to Agni. [The Banner. Oṃ hrāṃ rūṃ, obeisance to Śakti. Phaṭ namas. [The Pennant. Oṃ, obeisance to Kumudākṣa. [The Bali offering. Oṃ hrāṃ, to Varuṇa, Tripurāntaka, and the Rurus, accept this bali! (twice) Svāhā. [The rites from incense to the end of the hymn of praise.]
Salutations to you, the seven-rayed one, the sovereign lord of the fire-god;
O protector of the sacrifice, be present here for the sake of our protection.
In this case, there is fragrance and so forth.

Southern Gate: Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Bhūtitoraṇa; Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Yajurveda; Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Tretāyuga. At the Trident: Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Ugra; Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Indra; Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Argha. On the Branches: Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Pradyumna; Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Aśvaka; Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Svarloka; Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Maharloka; Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Budha.

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Bṛhaspati. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Komārī, the goddess of the ca-group. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vaiṣṇavī, the goddess of the ṭa-group. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Ajaghanya. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Jaghanyā.

At the door: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the door of the Vidyā-kalā. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Rudra, the presiding deity. Above: Duṃ, the bali offering. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Lakṣmī. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Bhṛṅgin. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vināyaka.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Mahī. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Narmadā.
The Banner: Oṃ hrāṃ mū daṇḍāya phaṭ namaḥ. The Pennant: Oṃ hrāṃ puṇḍarīkāya namaḥ. Oṃ hrāṃ yamāya mahiṣāsanāya namaḥ.
Meditative absorption (dhyāna).
Seated upon a buffalo throne, holding a staff in his hand, he is indeed resplendent.
Obeisance to the one whose body resembles black collyrium; obeisance to Dharmarāja.
Hrāṃ Oṃ Muṃ, salutation to Yama.
Bali: Oṃ hrāṃ, to the fierce ones of Kolāpura with fire-tongues, accept this bali! Svāhā. [Recite] from the incense offering up to the hymn of praise.
Homage be to Yamarāja, the sovereign lord of the southern direction; for the sake of protection, be present here as the destroyer of obstacles to knowledge.
Herein are the perfumes and so forth. Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the worship of the southern gate.
Then, in the southwest: *Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the archway of Fame! Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the door of Fame! Homage to the Devadāru tree! Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the corpse-seat of Nairṛti!*
Meditative absorption.
I beheld with my own eyes the Lord of the Rākṣasas, smoke-colored and of great splendor, mounted upon the back of a corpse, holding a sword in his hand, and possessing great excellence.
