Oṃ hrāṃ kṣūṃ, homage to Nairṛtya. [The banner: Oṃ hrāṃ śūṃ, homage to the sword.
On the banner: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vāmana.
Bali: Oṃ hrāṃ! To the wrathful deities Aṭṭahāsa and Agnijihva, accept this bali—svāhā! [Offer] incense and so forth, ending with praise.
Homage to you, O Lord of the Night, and to the Lord of the southwestern quarter.
For the sake of protecting and guarding the sacrifices, remain present here.
Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. Thus is the ritual procedure for the worship of the southwest gate.

Then follows the worship of the western gate: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Valatolana. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sāmaveda. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Dvāpara Yuga. On the trident (śūla): Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Arghamna (?). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Mitra. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Tvaṣṭṛ. On the branch (śākhā): Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Bhūsaṃjīvana. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Amṛta. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Janaloka. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Tapaloka. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Śukra.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Śanaiścara. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Vārāhī, the goddess of the ṭa-group of consonants.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Indrāṇī of the Pavarga class. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Dhātṛ. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vidhātṛ.

The Door: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the door of the Nivṛtti-kalā. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu, the presiding deity. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Mahālakṣmī. Then, for the two side-branches: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vṛṣabha. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Skanda. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sindhu. Oṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī.
The Banner: *Prūṃ*, obeisance to the Noose (*pāśa*). The Pennant: *Oṃ hrāṃ*, obeisance to Śaṅkukarṇa; *Oṃ hrāṃ*, obeisance to Varuṇa, whose vehicle is the Makara.
Meditative absorption (dhyāna).
Seated upon the Makara-throne, and holding a noose in her hand.
One should always meditate upon Varuṇa, who is as white as cow’s milk and gold.
Vūṃ, salutation to Varuṇa.
Bali: Oṃ hrāṃ, to those who conquer death by time, accept this bali (2) svāhā! [Perform] from the incense offering up to the hymn of praise.
Salutations to you, O Lord of the Waters, the protector of the sacrifice from evil.
And for the sake of protection, O Mahādeva, be present here along with Varuṇa. [Here, offer] perfumes and so forth.
Then, in the northwest: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Puṣṭi-gate; Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Puṣṭi-door; obeisance to the mango tree; Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vāyu, whose seat is the deer.
Meditative absorption.
The god, seated upon a deer-throne, holds a banner in his hand and possesses great strength.
And the green-bodied Vāyavya, the lord of the wind, possessed of brilliant splendor.
Oṃ hrāṃ yūṃ, homage to Vāyu.
The Banner: Dhūṃ, obeisance to the Banner, Phaṭ Namah. The Pennant: Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Sarva.
Bali: Oṃ hrāṃ, to Caritra, Karāla, and Kapālīśa, accept this bali! (2) Svāhā. [Recite] from the incense offering up to the hymn of praise.
Salutations to you, O Vāyu, sovereign lord of the vital breaths!
For the destruction of obstacles to the sacrifice and for the sake of protection, be present here. [Here, the offering of] fragrance and so forth.
Thus ends the worship of Vāyu.
Then follows the worship of the northern gate.
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Arch of Health (Ārogyatoraṇa). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Atharvaveda. On the trident: Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu.

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Savitṛ. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Aṃśumat. [To] the two branches: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Dhanada. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Śrīpada. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Satyaloka. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Dhruvaloka. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Rāhu. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Ketu. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Cāmuṇḍā, the letter-group *ya*. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Mahālakṣmī, the letter-group *śa*. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Āvaha. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vivaha.
At the gate.

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the door of the *pratiṣṭhā* stage. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Brahmā, the presiding deity (*adhidevatā*). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Mahālakṣmī. On the two branches: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Goddess. Oṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍa. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Gaṇḍakī river. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Kauśikī river.
Dhvajā: Grūṃ, obeisance to the mace. Patākā: Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to the eye; Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Kuvera, who is seated upon a ram.
Meditative absorption.
One should meditate upon the Lord of Wealth, the master of riches, who is yellow in color and possesses a massive body, mounted upon a yakṣa-steed and holding a mace in his hand.
Oṃ hrāṃ suṃ, homage to Kubera.
Bali: Oṃ hrāṃ, to the terrifying ones with one foot at Ekāmra, accept this bali (2) svāhā! [The ritual continues] from the incense offering up to the end of the hymn of praise.
Salutations to you, O Kubera, the presiding lord over wealth;
salutations to Vaiśravaṇa, who protects the sacrifices here. [Here, one offers] perfumes and other offerings.
Then, for Īśāna: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Siddhitora; Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Siddhidvāra; obeisance to Nāgavṛkṣa; Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Īśāna, whose seat is the bull.
Meditative absorption.
One should meditate upon Sadāśiva, the Lord who is seated upon a bull-throne, peaceful, with limbs as white as crystal, and holding a trident and a rosary.
Oṃ hrāṃ hūṃ, homage to Īśāna.
The Banner: Oṃ hrāṃ hrauṃ, obeisance to the Trident (śūla). The Pennant: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the One with a Beautiful Face (sumukha).
Bali: Oṃ hrāṃ, to the goddesses of Koṭa and those of terrifying form who bring about destruction, accept this bali! Svāhā! (2)
From the incense offering up to the hymn of praise.
Salutations to you, O Lord of Beings; and in the northeast is the Lord who is the Master.
For the purpose of protecting the sacrifice and for its defense, be present here. [Here, the offering of] scents and so forth.
Then follows the worship of the lower [direction]: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Lower Door; obeisance to the Aśoka tree; Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu, whose seat is the tortoise.
Meditative absorption.
Mounted upon the back of a tortoise, with a discus in hand, he is most beautiful.
O Janārdana, dark-complexioned one of great splendor, salutations be to you!
Klīṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu.
The Banner: *klīṃ* to the Discus, *phaṭ* *namaḥ*. The Flag: *oṃ hrāṃ* to Delight, *namaḥ*.
Bali: Oṃ hrāṃ, accept this bali offering for Hāṭakabhairava, svāhā! (2)
From the incense offering up to the hymn of praise.
Salutations to you, O Viṣṇu, the lord of Pātāla, who possesses the ten meters as your vehicle.
Be present for the sake of protecting and guarding the sacrifices.
In this case, there is fragrance and so forth.
Above that: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the upper archway (ūrdhva-toraṇa). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the upper door (ūrdhva-dvāra). Obeisance to the campaka tree.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Brahmā, who is seated upon a swan.
Meditative absorption.
The god is seated upon a swan-throne, holding a lotus in his hand, and is most beautiful.
The supreme Śiva, appearing white and reddish, is situated upon the crown of the head.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Brahmā.
The Banner: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Padma with the hood. The Pennant: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇa.
Bali: Oṃ hrāṃ, accept this bali offering for Acalabhairava, svāhā. [Recite] from the incense offering up to the hymn of praise.
Salutations to you, O Īśāna above, the Lord and Sovereign of heaven, the protector of sacrifice; for the sake of all protection, be present here. [Here, the offering of] fragrance and so forth.
Then follows the worship of the center.
Oṃ hrāṃ ślīṃ paśūṃ hūṃ phaṭ, homage to the Pāśupata weapon!
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the pavilion whose essence is all-pervading.
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the pavilion whose essence consists of the five principles.
Then follows the rising of Śiva-Śakti, the circumambulation of the pavilion, and the threefold circumambulation.
Oṃ! Ho, ho! World-protectors, together with your own weapons, be present here!
Oṃ! For the sake of protecting the sacrifice and for the destruction of obstacles, you, together with your vehicles and weapons, have taken your seats by the command of Śiva.

The recitation of auspicious verses (*svastivācana*). The filling with water. [The mantra] beginning with "from all the oceans" (*sarvasamudrāt*) and so forth. Worship (*pūjana*). The ritual placement (*nyāsa*). Worship of the vessel for the offering-water (*arghapātra*). [The mantra] beginning with "to the foundational power" (*ādhāraśakti*) and so forth. Salutation to the bull-throne (*vṛṣāsana*). Salutation to the lion-throne (*siṃhāsana*).
Meditative absorption.
Oṃ Hrāṃ! Shining above the pericarp, blazing with great splendor, possessing five faces and three eyes, and holding [attributes] with fourteen arms.
His body is somewhat dark-limbed and green, and he wears a forest garland.
Above the crown and tiara, it was adorned with seven hoods.
One should meditate upon the Lord Śikhāśiva, who has matted hair hanging down from his head,
holding a conch, a discus, a mace, a lotus, a skull-cup, and a khaṭvāṅga staff.
One should contemplate the weapons in his hands: a battle-axe, a trident, a hand-drum, a rosary of beads, a citron fruit, and the gesture of granting boons.
With his other two arms, he held a shield and a sword, his body covered by them.
And roaring most terribly, he was joined by thirty-two Śaktis.
Just like the form of the God [Brahmā], he has four faces and eight arms;
[he holds] a skull-bowl, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a parśu knife, a trident, a ḍamaru drum, and a rosary.
The Supreme Goddess holds a citron and a lotus as her weapons;
the meditation on the excellence of Śiva and Śakti is performed with the mudrā marked by the vulva and the phallus.
Having meditated thus, one should worship the deity and perform the sacrificial rite that brings about auspiciousness.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.

The worship with the *Vardhanī* vessel using the *Pāśupatāstra* mantra. Three *añjali*s with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) together with the *Śakti*. Having performed the worship of the heart and other limbs, the worship of the faces: *Oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*, *Oṃ hrāṃ viṣṇave namaḥ*, *Oṃ hrāṃ sadāśivāya namaḥ*, *Oṃ hrāṃ amṛtīśāya namaḥ*.
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Mṛtyuñjaya. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the nine planets beginning with Āditya.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the lunar mansions beginning with Kṛttikā.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the yogas beginning with Viskambha.
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the lunar days beginning with the first day (pratipad).
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the twelve zodiac signs beginning with Aries.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Gaṅgā. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Yamunā. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī.
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Godāvarī.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Narmadā. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Tuṅgabhadrā.
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Kāverī. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the eight long-lived ones beginning with Aśvasthāman.

Oṃ hrāṃ, salutations to the seven sages beginning with Vasiṣṭha. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutations to the eight nāgas beginning with Ananta. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutations to Śānti. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutations to Vidya. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutations to Nivṛtti. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutations to Pratiṣṭhā. [Perform] three handfuls of offerings (añjali) with the root mantra, together with the Śakti. Perform the six-limbed worship (ṣaḍaṅga-pūjā), the invocation (āvāhana) and so forth, the Liṅgayoni mudrā, incense (dhūpa), and lamp (dīpa). Perform the strewing of kuśa grass, the consecration with the Astra mantra, and the installation (pratiṣṭhā).
You are established. You are established.
Praise.

Pure, peaceful, and brilliant, consisting of crystal jewels, provided with sprouts and a parasol, it is joined with the eight sacred sites (tīrthas) and all the oceans, as well as the five gems and medicinal herbs;
employed in the sacrifice of the Sacrificer, it is served by the entire assembly of sages in every way.
I bow to you and praise you with devotion, O Lord who possesses the gait of Śiva; salutations to you in the form of the Water-jar (Kumbha).
Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. Thus ends the worship of the Śiva-Śakti vessel.
The offering of the sword of wisdom. Today, at the time of the ascent. The statement.
To Umā, who possesses the form of the bhaga and who bears the form of the liṅga.
Salutations to you, Śaṅkara, who bestows grace through devotion.
Thus is the transformation into the *bhaga* and *liṅga*. "For he is the lordship of this sacrifice; by his power, he is this very form.
This is your sword of knowledge (*jñāna-nistriṃśa*); take up your own weapon. Thus is the offering.
One should pray.
"O Blessed One, this sacrificial pavilion is being constructed with great effort."
O Lord of the World, you must protect the universe from all adversaries. Oṃ hsauṃ, salutation to Śiva and Śakti. Thus ends the worship of the hands of Śiva and Śakti.
Then follows the worship of the jars dedicated to Indra and the other deities.

Oṃ lūṃ, obeisance to Indra. Oṃ rau, obeisance to Hetukabhairava. Oṃ rau, obeisance to Tripurāntakabhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the wind element (vāyutattva). Oṃ hai, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the 'A' group of vowels (avarga).

Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Ka-group of consonants. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the salt ocean. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Aśitāṅga. The strewing with kuśa grass. [The rite of] installation: "You are installed."

Now, for Agni: Oṃ hrāṃ ruṃ, obeisance to Agni. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the *ivargga* (the *i*-vowels). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the *cavargga* (the *ca*-consonants). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Kṣīroda. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Ruru.

South: Oṃ hrāṃ muṃ, obeisance to Yama. Oṃ rau, obeisance to Pāvakabhairava. Oṃ rauṃ, obeisance to Jamajihvābhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the fire element (agnitattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Aghora. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the *u*-varga. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the *ṭa*-varga. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Ocean of Curds (dadhisamudra). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍa.

Southwest: Oṃ kṣuṃ, obeisance to Nairṛtya. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Ṛ-varga. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Ta-varga. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Ocean of Ghee (Sarppi-samudra). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Krodha.
In the west: Oṃ hrāṃ vūṃ, homage to Varuṇa.

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the earth element (pṛthvī-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sadyojāta. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the *ḷ*-group of consonants. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the *pa*-group of consonants. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to sugarcane and curd. Oṃ, obeisance to Unmatta.
Vāyavya: Oṃ hrāṃ yuṃ, obeisance to Vāyavya. Oṃ e va rga āya, obeisance. Oṃ hrāṃ ya va rga āya, obeisance. Oṃ hrāṃ su rā dhvaṃ ya, obeisance.

In the north: Oṃ hrāṃ sūṃ, obeisance to Kubera. Oṃ rauṃ, obeisance to Ekapādabhairava. Oṃ rau, obeisance to Bhīmarūpabhairava. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Āptatva. Oṃ phiṃ, obeisance to Vāmadeva. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the group of vowels (ovargga). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the group of sibilants (śavargga). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the ocean of nectar (rasasamudra). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Bhīṣaṇa.

Īśāna. Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Īśāna. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the group beginning with ‘a’. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the two groups beginning with ‘kṣa’. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Śivasamudra. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Saṃhārabhairava. [Perform] the strewing with *kuśa* grass.
The foundation. You are firmly established.
The Worship of Gaṇaka and Lakṣaṇa || Oṃ, obeisance to the one whose vehicle is an elephant.
Meditative concentration.
Oṃ! To the one with a single tusk, of massive body, white in color, and of great splendor.
One should meditate upon the god Gaṇādhipa, the great hero with the face of an elephant.
Oṃ Gaṃ, homage to Gaṇapati. [The hymn of praise] beginning with incense.
The elephant-faced one of great heroism, holding a root and a sweetmeat in his hands.
O son of Gaṅgā, salutations to you; may there be freedom from obstacles in all undertakings.
Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. Thus ends the section on the gaṇa-vessel.
The Worship of the Guru’s Vase. Oṃ, homage to the lotus seat.
Meditative absorption.
Born from the color of saffron, he holds a rosary and a book.
One should visualize the form of the Guru situated in the northeastern direction.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the Guru.
Praise of incense and other offerings.
And [this applies] to all the deities and the sages, as well as humans and others.
Obeisance to you, O embodiment of the Guru, who are proficient in all the scriptures.
Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. Thus is the worship with the hand of the Guru.
The worship of the field and the vase: Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the human throne.
Meditative absorption.
Tawny in complexion, with reddish-brown hair, reddish-brown eyebrows, and reddish-brown eyes,
he holds a staff, a hand-drum, a skull-topped staff, and a trident, and carries a skull-cup.
Oṃ hrāṃ kṣāṃ, obeisance to Kṣatra. [This is] the praise beginning with incense (dhūpa).
Seated upon a human corpse, stationed to the south of Vāyu,
presiding over all the planets— homage to you, O Kṣetrapāla!
Here [are] the incense and so forth. Thus ends the worship of the field-vase (*kṣetrakalaśa*).
The worship of the Yoginī flask.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the fire-seat.
Meditative absorption.
White in color, greatly radiant, and endowed with all the auspicious marks,
one should always meditate upon the Yoginī stationed in the direction between the south-west and the east.
Oṃ hrāṃ yāṃ, homage to the Yoginī! [This is] the praise beginning with incense.
O Goddess who pervades the three worlds, who bears the curved knife and the skull-cup,
O Goddess who crushes obstacles, O Yoginī, salutations to you!
Here [are] the fragrance and so forth. Thus [ends] the Yoginī flask.
The Auspicious Worship of the Vase (Śrīkalaśapūjā). Homage to the One Seated upon the Crocodile-Throne (Makarāsana).
Meditative concentration.
The goddess stands upon a lotus, possessing the luster of the petals of a blue lotus;
she holds vermilion and a lotus in her hands, and abides in the fullness of beauty and youth.
Oṃ hrāṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the Embodiment. [This is] the incense offering and subsequent hymn of praise.
I bow down to the Goddess Śrī, who is established in all her limbs, worshipped by the three worlds,
and who holds vermilion and a blue lotus in her two hands.
Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. Thus concludes the venerable worship of the flask (kalaśa-pūjā).
The Worship of the Lakṣmī-Vase: Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Tortoise Seat (kūrmmāsana).
Meditative absorption.
Seated upon a lotus lion-throne, resembling snow, cow’s milk, or moonlight,
she has three eyes, her limbs possess a divine form, and she is adorned with golden ornaments.
Holding a sword and a shield in her hands, and bearing a lotus and a battle-axe—
having thus meditated upon the Great Goddess Mahālakṣmī, I bow down to her.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the form of Lakṣmī. [The offering of] incense and so forth, and the hymn of praise.
Seated upon the tortoise-throne, radiant as the white water-lily of the enemy, and holding a lotus and a mirror— I bow to Goddess Lakṣmī.
Here [are] the fragrance and so forth. Thus ends the Lakṣmī-vase.
The [sections on] missiles, architecture, propitiatory rites, and books.
The Worship of the Āditya Vessel. Homage to the Lotus Seat.
Meditative absorption.
Seated upon a red lotus throne, joined with his chariot drawn by seven horses,
he is red in color, possessed of great splendor, and has the luster of a pomegranate flower.
Thus one should meditate upon the Sun, the destroyer of all sins.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Āditya, whose presiding deity is Īśvara and whose secondary presiding deity is Agni.
Praise beginning with incense and other offerings.
He possessed a thousand rays and great splendor, adorned with jeweled earrings;
he had beautiful feet, lovely hands, and a beautiful head, his form being composed of jewels.
Here [are offered] fragrance and so forth. Thus ends the worship of the Āditya jar.
Nāgakumbha: Oṃ blūṃ, homage to Varuṇa! Homage to you, Varuṇa!
The Worship of the Death-Conquering Vase (Mṛtyuñjaya-kalaśa-pūjā). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the one seated upon the bull.
Meditative absorption.
The Lord Maheśvara is seated upon a bull and a lion, resembling milk, the kunda flower, and the moon;
he has one face, three eyes, and four arms.
O God, you hold a trident and a rosary, and you bear the excellent weapon;
the goddess, with two arms and a water-pot, rests upon your left thigh.
One should meditate upon the Lord of Immortality, who destroys all sins, whose limbs are adorned with golden ornaments and who is decorated with white garments.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to Mṛtyuñjaya, the Lord of Immortality.
Salutations to Aśvatthāman and the other eight long-lived ones. [This concludes] the incense offering and the hymn of praise.
O Amṛteśī, to the Great Lord, the destroyer of the suffering of the universe;
O you whose nature is both supreme and non-supreme, salutations to you, O Three-eyed One!
Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. Thus ends the worship of the Mṛtyuñjaya vessel.
In the north, there is the worship of the yakṣas and yakṣiṇīs.
Meditative absorption.
The hand [of the deity] is mounted upon a horse, possesses an elephant's trunk, and is embraced by a Yakṣiṇī.
And one should always meditate upon Kubera, who bestows all peace, as being situated at the site of the dwelling.
Oṃ hrāṃ mlūṃ, homage to the Yakṣa. Oṃ hrāṃ mlūṃ, homage to the Yakṣiṇī.
Praise of the incense and other offerings.
To Yakṣeśvara, the Lord of Yakṣas, for the destruction of obstacles.
By the command of Śiva, you and they, along with your vehicles, shall remain in close proximity.
Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. Thus ends the worship of the yakṣas and yakṣiṇīs.

Then, in due order, one should perform the worship of the sacrificial ground (*sthaṇḍila*), the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and so forth, and the self-worship (*ātmapūjā*). According to the prescribed rule, one should cause the worship of the central deity along with the limbs (*aṅga*) and sub-limbs (*upāṅga*) to be performed in the northeast corner. One should perform the worship of the sacrificial ground with water offerings, incense, and so forth, followed by praise: *Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Śrī; Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Lakṣmī*.
The worship of the water-pitcher with the *upādika* [mantra].
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, homage to the one who performs all actions.
The Jar of Sleep: Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Nidrā, the womb of the gods.

Śaryyākalaśa || Oṃ Hrāṃ, salutation to Śaryyā. Salutation to the fortnights. Salutation to the months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa. Salutation to the seasons. Salutation to the year. Salutation to the lunar days (tithis) beginning with Nandā. Salutation to the asterisms (nakṣatras) beginning with Aśvinī. Salutation to the yogas beginning with Viṣkambha. Salutation to the muhūrtas.
Now, the worship with the *sagona* [offering]: having gazed at the root [mantra] with three *añjali*s, there is the worship of the site and the *bali* offering.

The worship of the vessel containing the root-mantra (mūlapātra) in the pure [space]; the *natasiya* of the three principles (*tritatva*); obeisance to the Guru; the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the *vatīśi*; the worship of the water and the *arghapātra* vessel; the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*); self-worship (*ātmapūjā*); the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites for Śrī Śaṃvarttāna; the three deities and the Yoginīs; and their respective mudrās.

*Brahmānyādi* || (8) || *Aghora* || *Vajra* || *Vatīśi* || Root mantra with three *añjali*s || *Āvāhanādi* || To the *piśāca*s || To the beings on the left, accept this *bali* offering (2) *svāhā* || To the *piśāca*s on the left, accept this *bali* offering (2) *svāhā* ||
Cāśvara || Trideva || Aiṃ (5) Caṃ Chaṃ Jaṃ Jhaṃ Ñaṃ KMLVRYŪṂ Śrī Komārī Vicce Pādukāṃ || (3) || Bali || Hṛdayādi || Mūlamantra || Hakāra Sakāra || Tvākamahābali || Āvāhanādi || Svasvamudrā ||
Nāśvara | Trideva | Oṃ hūṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ, the sandals for Nṛtyaśvaramahābhairava, for Bhairava, together with Śkṣmlvryīṃ Nṛtyalakṣmī and her consort. (3)
Bali; the heart-mantra and so forth; the great bali for the individual deities; the invocation and so forth; their respective mudrās.
Uparāju || Trideva || Aiṃ (5) Śrī-Anādimahāpīṭha, in the great field of Meru, in the house of Kauri, HSKHPHŪṂ Kubjikā, HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ, O Śrī-Kulacakreśvaranātha and Ambā, [I offer] the sandals! Bali!

Aiṃ (5). At the great primordial seat (mahāpīṭha), the great field of Meru, in the house of Kauri: Śkhphrīṃ Kubjikā Śkṣmlvryīṃ. To the sandals of the venerable Mother, the Sovereign of the Wheel of the Kula (Śrīkulacakreśvarī Ambā). (3). The offering (bali). The heart-mantra and so forth. The great bali for Tvaṅka. The invocation and so forth. Their respective mudrās. Thānalaṃkhu, the three deities.

Aiṁ (5) Thrauṁ. The sandals of the goddess Dambhakī and the great Dhvāṅkṣa Kṣetrapāla of Prastaradvīpa. (3) Bali. The heart-mantra and so forth. The great bali for Tvaṅka. The invocation and so forth. The tarjanī mudrā.
O King’s messenger! O Triple God!

Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, homage to Karaṅkeśvara and Karaṅkabhairavīśvarī. (3) [Offer] the *bali*. [Recite] the heart-mantra and so forth. [Offer] the great *bali* for the *tva* syllable. [Perform] the invocation and so forth. [Display] their respective mudrās.

Queen Vaccharā; the three deities; with the western face of Mūran; (3); the nine-syllable [mantra]; (3); the offering (bali); the heart-mantra and so forth; the great offering for Tvaṣṭṛ; the invocation and so forth; their respective mudrās.
*Togaṇa* || *Trideva* || *KMLVRYŪṂ Śrīkaumārī Vicce Pādukām* || (3) || *Bali* || *Āvāhanādi* || [Offer] their respective *mudrās*.

*Phelaju* || *Tirdeva* || *Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ Śrīśikhāsvacchandabhairavāya pādukāṃ* || (3) || *Bali* || *Āvāhanādi* || [Offer] one's respective *mudrās*. To the western door of the stomach, [offer] *khāṅāvayāya*. *Galāla* || *Dumāju* || *Āvāhanādi* || [Offer] one's respective *mudrās*. *Dhūpa*, *dīpa*, *naivedya*, *japa*: *Trideva vmlvryūṃ svāhā* || *kmlvryūṃ svāhā* || *ha (9) sa (9) svāhā* || *hskhphrūṃ* ||

ŚKHPHRĪṂ SVĀHĀ || THROṂ SVĀHĀ || HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ SVĀHĀ || HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ NAVĀKṢARĪ || KMLVRYŪṂ SVĀHĀ || HSPHRĀṂ SVĀHĀ || GALALA || DUMĀJU || STOTRA || AKHAṆḌAMAṆḌALĀKĀRAM, etc. || ŚRĪSAṂVATTĀ || VAIṢṆAVĪ VIṢṆUMĀYĀ CA || PŪRVVAṂ DAKṢIṆA || VĀRABHĀVE || BRAHMĀTĀRADHARE || PĪṬHE MADHYANI || VAṂDE SADĀ || DHŪMĀBHAṂ DĪPANETRAṂ ||

Dark red. Fully blossomed. Āṃ Kroṃ Kliṃ, Komārī. Kvākāsa. To the Red One. Tawny-eyed. As in the *Vānati* and other [texts]. Libation (*tarpaṇa*). Worship of the cow-dust with the assembly (*gaṇa*). Homage to the one seated on a rat (*mūsāsana*). Three handfuls of water (*añjali*). Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Ga, homage to Kulagaṇeśvara. Offering (*bali*). Incense (*dhūpa*). Lamp (*dīpa*). Recitation (*japa*). Glauṃ Svāhā. (10) Hymn (*stotra*): "With thick vermilion, wine," and so forth. Here, [offer] perfume (*gandha*) and the rest.
Now, the worship of the cow-portion (*gogrāsapūjā*): *Oṃ*, obeisance to Nanda; *Oṃ*, obeisance to Subhadra; obeisance to Surabhi.
Homage to Suśīra. Homage to Sumanohara. [Offer] two *thava* and *bali*. Incense and lamp. [Offer] two *thava* and perform the recitation (*jāpa*) of the mantra.
Hymn of Praise.
Nandā, Subhadrā, Surabhi, Suśīlā, and Sumanoharā.
Salutation to the five products of the cow, the purifier for the destruction of sin. Herein [are offered] scent and the other [articles].

Now, the worship of Komārī. *Mayūrāsanāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the Peacock-Throne). *Tiryāñjali* (Horizontal *añjali* gesture). *Caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ kmlvryūṃ caṃ komārī caṇḍabhairavāya pādukāṃ* (3). *Ṣaḍaṅga* (Six-limbed ritual). *Bali* (Offering). *Dhūpa* (Incense). *Dīpa* (Lamp/Light). *Jāpa* (Recitation): *kmlvryūṃ svāhā* (10 times). *Stotra* (Hymn): "Vārabhāva... and so forth. Herein [are offered] sandalwood paste (*gandha*) and other articles.
Now follows the Sugha-nāga-pūjā. Herein: "Homage to the Kula-nāgas and the Nāga-kings."
One should meditate upon him who has infinite lotus-like eyes, who is endowed with ten thousand hoods,
who resembles a flash of lightning, and who is seated upon a tortoise.
In this case, there is odor and so forth.
Kevopūjā || Salutations to the illustrious Śrī Sūrya. Salutations to the illustrious Paśupati Bhaṭṭārika. Salutations to the illustrious Garuḍanārāyaṇa.

Salutations to the glorious Īśvarī, the chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*). Salutations to one’s own chosen deity. (4) Salutations to the glorious Varuṇa, the kings of the *nāgas*. [This concludes] the preliminary worship (*muṅapūjā*). Salutations to Śrī. Salutations to Śakti. Incense, lamps, food offerings (*naivedya*), betel leaves (*tāmbūla*), and so forth. Installation (*pratiṣṭhā*). Recitation (*jāpa*) and hymns (*stotra*). "O chosen deity, salutations to you," and so forth. Herein [are offered] perfumes (*gandha*) and other articles.

The worship of the sequential maṇḍala. Then, by the patron (*yajamāna*), the invitation of the [deities] residing in the field (*kṣetrimāvāhana*). At the entrance, the cleansing (*nirmmārjana*). The lamp and the protection with iron. Sandalwood and so forth, together with the sword. Having performed the circumambulation of the fire-pit (*kuṇḍa*) with an uninterrupted stream of water, one should place [the deity] facing north in the southwest (*nairṛtya*). Here, the seat and so forth, the foot-water (*pādārgha*), the hand-water (*hastārgha*), sandalwood, the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), and all other offerings are presented. Here, the incense and so forth; the Hotṛ recites.
Oṃ, come! You who ward off the seizing obstacles of the sacrifice at the gateway.
In the worship within the complete sacrifice, there is no desire for adornment.
O Narāyaṇa, protect me always; be the dispeller of obstacles.
"May it be so for the Kṣatriyas. Thus ends the invocation of the Kṣatriyas.
Then the Hotṛ, standing near the sacrificial pit, should recite: "Oṃ, Blessed One!"
O Lord, together with your retinue, I perform the fire-ritual joined with sacrifice;
remove all obstacles and grant me this boon and your command.

The four purificatory rites for the lion-throne: inspection with the root mantra; sprinkling with the weapon mantra; veiling with the armor mantra; and striking with the weapon mantra. Having sat upon the lion-throne, one should recite: "May all beings in the three worlds, both stationary and moving—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and Śārṅgin—always grant me protection."
Gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Pannagas.
The Meṣayas, the Manavas, the cows, and likewise the Devamātṛs.
And may all the Samādharas, filled with joy, provide protection.
Perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the root mantra. Perform the worship of the water vessel and the *argha* vessel.

Then, the purification of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*): *khphreṃ paramahaṃsinī sarvajñāta hṛdayāya namaḥ*. This is the installation [of the heart-mantra]. *khphreṃ śakaladuritāritaḥ kleśadaranī svatantra kavacāya hūṃ*. This is the installation of the girdle (*mekhalā*). The installation of the altar (*vedī*) with the armor-mantra (*kavaca*). The touching of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with the armor-mantra.

In the northeast of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), there is the worship of the nine steps: *aiṃ (5) hskṣmlvryūṃ khphreṃ pādukāṃ*. Then follows the worship of the cow-dung liṅga (*gomayaliṅga*) with the *Mṛtyuñjaya* mantra, beginning with incense (*dhūpa*) and ending with hymns of praise (*stuti*), starting from "Pure, peaceful... (*śuddha śāntaṃ*). Thereafter, one should perform the sacrifice. The patron (*yajamāna*) [offers] a flower vessel (*puṣpabhājana*) with the following formula: "Today... [and so forth]... O patron of such-and-such lineage (*amukagotra*), for the purpose of the sacrifice of the perfected fire (*siddhāgni*) according to the oblations, preceded by the propitiation of my own chosen deity (*sveṣṭadevatā*), I offer this flower vessel."

Śrī Saṃvartā! Utphullā! May there be success at the commencement of the ritual, and so forth. I offer a water-pot and a vessel of flowers to the Preceptor. Again, I offer a vessel of flowers to the Preceptor.

The ritual rinsing (*ācamana*) with the three *tattvas*. The offering to the Sun (*sūryārgha*). The statement beginning with "Today and so forth" (*adyādi*). *Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ śrīmārttaṇḍamāhābhairavāya prakāśaśaktisahitāya kuru māhāmārttaṇḍamahābhairavāya namaḥ.* The seed-syllable situated at the end of the letters and in the middle, etc. The salutation to the Guru, etc. The verse beginning with "Of the form of an unbroken circle," etc. The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the root mantra. "Homage to the Ocean in the jar for rinsing. "Homage to Vārāha, the bearer of flowers and fragrance. This is the worship of the water vessel.

Oṃ hrāṃ, the *pādukā* for the seat of the venerable water-vessel (*śrī-jalapātrāsana*). Aiṃ (5) hskṣmlvryūṃ, the *pādukā* for the venerable lady of the water-vessel (*jalapātra-bhaṭṭārikā*). Khphreṃ, *namaḥ* to the heart, and so forth. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites. [Form] the *dhenumudrā*. [Perform] the sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*). [Recite] the *Gāyatrī*: Hrīṃ śrīṃ, we know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon her who possesses ninety [forms]; may that Lakṣmī inspire us. With the water from the *arghapātra*, sprinkle oneself and all other objects.
Then, the worship of the Arghapātra (the vessel of offering): Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, the pādukā for the seat of the Arghapātra. Hrīṃ śrīṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ, voṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava.

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the breath: Saḥ Saḥ Saḥ, Parādevī, vomit nectar (2), Svāhā. Purification of the substances: Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Namaḥ (3). Khphreṃ, obeisance to the heart, and so forth. Invocation and other rites. Yonimudrā. Purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi): Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃḥ Hsauṃ Hsphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ. Self-worship (ātmapūjā): Khphreṃ, obeisance to the self with sandalwood paste; Khphreṃ, obeisance with unbroken rice grains (akṣata).

*Khphreṃ sinduraṃ namaḥ.* *Khpreṃ sarvajanamohanī namaḥ.* [Flower] *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ ātmane puṣpaṃ namaḥ.* With honey (*alī*), offer three drops (*bindu*). (3) *Khphreṃ sakalaśatrupramathani astrāya phaṭ.* Thus is the self-worship (*ātmapūjā*).

Observing the ritual preparations: To Kuśa grass, salutations to Soma; To the wooden ladle, salutations to Yama; To the fuel-stick, salutations to Vanaspati; To the sacrificial substance, salutations to Yakṣa; To the fruit, salutations to Śiva; To all grains, salutations to the Aśvinīkumāras; To food and edibles, salutations to Mādhava; To the sacrificer, salutations to Rudra; Sprinkling water once more, salutations to Vidyeśa.
Hotṛ: Homage to Śrīkaṇṭha. In the sacrifice, homage to that which consists of the five elements. In the jar, homage to the Earth. With the Astra-mantra, the dispersal of the king [of obstacles].

Then, the eleven consecrations (*saṃskāra*) for the fire-pit (*agnikuṇḍa*): (1) *Aiṃ (5) Khphreṃ sakalaśatrupramathani hūṃ hūṃ astrāya phaṭ* — Sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*). (2) *Aiṃ (5) Khphreṃ sakaladuritārita kleśadaranī kavacāya hūṃ kavacāya pādukāṃ* — Veiling (*avaguṇṭhana*). (3) *Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ unmūlanaṃ* — Striking (*tāḍana*). (4) *Aiṃ (5) Khphreṃ pūraṇaṃ* — Filling (*pūraṇa*). (5) *Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ klīṃ samakaranaṃ* — Equalizing (*samakarana*).
The rising of the rays through the wandering of the sun's orb.

KH PHREṂ—Sprinkling. (6) HS PHREṂ—Crushing. (7) AIṂ (5) HS AUṂ—Wiping. (8) AIṂ (5) HSKH PHREṂ HRĀṂ HRĪṂ HRŪṂ—Smearing. (9) AIṂ (5) OṂ PARAMAHAṂSINI KH PHREṂ—Sprinkling with water. (10) AIṂ (5) KH PHREṂ NIRVĀṆAMĀRGADE ŚRĪ—Drying. (11) Thus, the eleven consecrations of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) must be performed.

Aiṁ (5) Hraiṁ, *hūṃ* for the armor (*kavaca*). Wrapping with three threads or five threads, at each girdle: "Obeisance to this seat for such-and-such sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*). Having thus worshipped with these offerings: "Obeisance to Ananta for the deity of the pit; obeisance to Vasava for the navel; obeisance to Keśava for the neck; obeisance to Agni for the excavation; obeisance to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara for the three girdles; obeisance to Kāmākṣī for the womb; obeisance to Kāmeśā for the stalk."

The sprinkling with water while reciting the *astra-mantra*; the fetching of clay with that same mantra; *aiṃ* (5); O Supreme Swan (*paramahaṃsinī*), [draw] three lines with *kuśa* grass—namely, the *sāttvikī*, the *rājasī*, and the *tāmasī*.

The sprinkling with the *gāyatrī* [mantra] and with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). With the seventeen-syllable mantra: *aiṃ khphreṃ vajrikaraṇi rjjhrīṃ mahācaṇḍatejasaṃkarṣaṇi kālimanthāne haḥ*. The [seventeen] syllables.

With the *Kuśa* mantra, [one offers] *gāyatrī* at the crossroads. (5) With the *Aiṃ* mantra, one scatters red grain; with the *Aghora* mantra, one scatters rice; with the nine-syllable mantra, one prepares the seat of clarified butter (*ghṛtāsana*). Having placed gold, silver, a lotus, and the nine jewels using that very same mantra, one offers a flower with the *astra* mantra.

With the *kavaca* [mantra], the sacrificial fuel (*samidh*); with the *astra* [mantra], the *kuśa*-grass seat; with the *kavaca* [mantra], the extensive seat (*vistarāsana*); with *aiṃ* (five times) and the *śakti-astra*, the sandals (*pādukā*). Having placed the *kuṇḍalinī* in the center with the nine-syllable [mantra], I worship the *yonyāsana-śrīpādukā*.
One should meditate upon the Śrīcakra, the seat of accomplishment. Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, the venerable pādukā.
Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ, the venerable sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Khphreṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ, salutation to the three forms—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Īśvara—and to the triple protector.

Aiṃ (5) Kuṇḍalini Vicce, [I worship] the venerable sandals. Having established the *liṅga* in the center of the *yoni* with HSKṢPHREṂ, Aiṃ (5) SAḤ, [is] the festival of semen; HRAIṂ is the consciousness. Aiṃ, in the midst of the semen.
Aiṁ: by means of the heart-mantra, the rite of conception (garbhādhāna).

The Worship of Vāgeśvarīpūrī Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Yogapīṭha beginning with Maṇḍūka and ending with Paramātman. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Jayā. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Vijayā. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Ajitā. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Aparājitā. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Nityā. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Dogdhī. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Vilāsinī. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Aghorā. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Maṅgalā.
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutations to the lotus-seated one who possesses all powers.
Meditative absorption.
Resembling the *ataśī* flower and endowed with all the [auspicious] marks,
one should meditate upon the goddess Vāgīśvarī as being in her menses and then invite her.

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vāgīśvarī. She should be worshipped with the ritual services beginning with invocation (āvāhana). Likewise, one should worship Vāgīśvara. After performing the invocation and other rites, one should display the Dhenu and Yoni mudrās. The patron (yajamāna) should take up eight pieces of wood. The Hotṛ priest, having sprinkled them with water for the arghya offering, should sprinkle the wood with the Astra mantra and recite the mantra over the wood as follows: Aiṃ (5) hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ khphreṃ (17) kāyaṣṭaṃ nidhāya || Sikā (4) nase (2) || Sikāsva (3) svatā (3) tāne ||

Aiṁ (5). Having worshipped that wooden post with the principle of the Three (Tritatva), [one worships] in the center: Aiṁ (5). Śrī Namaḥ to all the Siddhi-yoginīs, the Śrī-pādukā. Having worshipped in the center: Aiṁ (5). To the Mothers of all Siddhis, the Pādukā. In the southern corner of the wooden post: Aiṁ (5). Namaḥ to her who is delighted by eternally arisen bliss, the Śrī-pādukā. In the left corner: Aiṁ (5). To the Mistress of the wheel of the *sakara*-family, the Śrī-pādukā. In front of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*): the sprinkling [of water] with *kuśa* grass using the five-syllable mantra.
The yogis who hold the mind steady possess a pure radiance.

Then, at the entrance, the sacrificer’s wife brings the fire kindled by the sacrificer. Aiṁ (5) HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ KHPREṂ, the fire is brought forth. Aiṁ (5) HRŪṂ SAḤ, sandals for the circle of light. [Perform] the ritual wiping (*nirmmarchana*) and so forth, the raising of the lamp, protection, and the blessing with sandalwood paste and other substances. Having entered the pavilion with a stream of water, the *hotṛ* priest shall cause [the offerings] to be given. Drawing [the fire] into another vessel with the weapon-mantra (*astra*), perform the ritual wiping and so forth.

Oṃ hrroṃ hrāṃ kravyādetyo hūṃ phaṭ ṭha ṭha || To Matānapikā || Oṃ hrāṃ kravyādāgnaye svāhā || Three oblations (3). Likewise, an oblation of clarified butter. Having cast away the fire for raw-flesh eaters with the mantra, [perform] the ritual sipping of water (upasparśaṇa).

The fourfold consecration of the fire. *Hṛdayanyāsa*: *Rāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*. *Rīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*. *Rūṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vauṣaṭ*. *Raiṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *hūṃ*. *Rauṃ* to the three eyes, *vaṣaṭ*. *Raṃ* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*.

The Vahni-Gāyatrī: "We know Vaiśvānara; we meditate upon Jātavedas; may Agni inspire us. Sprinkle [the materials] thoroughly. Inspect them with the root mantra. Strike them with kuśa grass while reciting the Astra mantra. Sprinkle them again with the Kavaca mantra. Joining consciousness (*caitanya*) into the fire with the syllable *Raṃ*, contemplate the unity of the gross (*audāryya*), lunar (*vaindava*), earthly (*pārthiva*), and fiery (*vahnī*) elements. Consecrate them with the Praṇava (*Oṃ*). Transform them into nectar using the syllable *Vaṃ* and the Dhenu-mudrā. Protect them with the Astra mantra and veil them with the Kavaca mantra.

Oṃ raṃ, salutation to Vahni (the Fire-god). Having worshipped him with perfumes and other offerings, and having recited the purpose of the rite, one should perform the circumambulation of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) while reciting the armor-mantra (kavaca). Then follows the installation of the fire: Oṃ hrāṃ rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ, svāhā to the consciousness of Vahni. One should then recite the benediction (svastivācanam).

Having rotated [the fire] within the womb (*yoni*) and having grasped the fire with the nine-syllable mantra: *Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ*, [perform] the threefold rotation while circling the fuel. *Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ Aiṃ Hskhphreṃ*: the installation of the fire (*agnisthāpanaṃ*). *Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ*: the venerable *Saṃvartā*. *Utphullāṃ*. [Recite] the words of benediction (*svastivākya*). Perform the worship with the six limbs, beginning with the heart: *Aiṃ Hrāṃ Śrīṃ Gneṃ Hūṃ Śrūṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā*. One should recite the words of benediction (*svastivākya*).
May there be well-being at all times, free from obstacles; may there be well-being from Ārttaṇḍa himself;
may there be well-being from all the Yoginīs, and well-being from one's own sacred seats and constellations.
In the east, south, west, north, above, and likewise in the doorways—
may the six-limbed Svasti, with her hidden and manifest deities, remain present.
Bhairava and Bhairavī, together with their limbs, may they grant well-being;
[they who possess] their own wheels, their own mantras, their own mudrās, and their own weapons, along with their retinues.
May she who dwells within the planets, constellations, and zodiac signs grant well-being for the prosperity of all.
May the heroes, the immeasurables, the yoginīs, and the leaders of the hosts grant well-being!
May there be well-being; may the King of Mantras, who is the presiding deity of the Goddess, be ever-present;
may those devoted to the sacrificial offerings be satisfied; and may there be well-being for the deities of the family fire.
May there be well-being for the king and his subjects; may there be constant well-being for the sacrificer.
One should recite the Kṣetrābali.
Oṃ, homage to Siddhi-Mahākālī, the Kālikā!

Salutations to you, O Trailokyā; salutations to you, O Kālikā, who are bowed to by the three worlds; O Viśvacaṇḍā, O Vāmā, who abide within the left; salutations to the pair of feet praised by the best of the thirty gods. (1)

In the short, the long, and the visarga; in the pairs of *ka*, *ca*, *ṭa*, *ta*, *pa*, and *ya*; when the eye is situated within another light; in the shaven head (*mūṇḍa*); *hūṃ*; in the region of the boon-granting *ti* at the end of the universe; and in the upper garment of the serpent—(2).
O you whose earrings are the moon and the sun, flickering and trembling; O cave-eyed one, protect me!
O elder sister, O fierce one, O you with the crests of blazing fire, O Mother Nandinī, O Sunandā! (3)

Obeisance to Viriñci in the utterance of Svāhā; to the one who brings welfare to those who bow; to the destroyer of disease and doubt; to Kaṅkāla; to the time of Time; to the remover of the impurity of the world; to the one with the strung bow; to the primordial Vāmā; to the Terrible One. (4)
O you who abide in my own form within the faces, O you who delight in excellent practice, O you who reside in the interior of the *kanda* and the *cakra*,
O you who flow through the space of the heart-space, O you who are more formidable than Hara and Hara, shatter [all obstacles], O you who carry the spirits!
O Jambhe, O Moha, O Agnijihve, O Śaśaśaśaśavare, O you who dwell on Mount Kāla, O Vicce, O Viśveśvarī, O crusher of the wicked! O Goddess, [destroy] those who have committed evil deeds! (5)
Drāṃ drāṃ drāṃ! O Drāviṇī, Kili Kili-rasasphurati, Carmamuṇḍe, O you who strike!
Klīṃ Plūṃ Ra! O bearer of the principles (tattva)! Kili Kili! O Subhaga, you who plunge into the knowledge of mantras!
Preṃ Preṃ Preṃ! O rider upon the corpse! Kala Kala Kahale! At the tip of the noose and the ṭārikā weapon!
O divine one, O you whose dwelling is divine, kha kha kha kha, O you who move through the sky with a fierce, gurgling roar! (6)

KṢĪṂ PHAṬ HŪṂ PHAṬ! O you whose nature is the syllable *svarūpa*, ḌA ḌA ḌA ḌA ḌAMARE HŪṂ! O you who dwell in Jayantī, cut through [the bonds] with the weapon! VĀMA ṬHA ṬHA ṬHA ṬHA ṬHAMARE KṢAKṢAKĀRE! O most terrifying one, I bow to you, Koṭarākṣī, whose teeth grant the best boons, whose eyes are the syllables of the letter *dakṣa*.
HE HE HŪṂKĀRARĀVE! COOK, COOK! O burner! RELEASE, RELEASE! O you who are intoxicated with power! (7)
O Caṇḍākṣī, you of wrathful form, supreme destroyer of Darada, you who are intoxicated by the essence of excellent wine;
O Heroine, whose abode is fire, you who are radiant with the intoxication of honeyed liquor, O Jvālinī, whose very weapons are aflame!
O Caṇḍā, you of one-pointed form, you who possess a thundering roar, you of terrible aspect, the dispeller of fear!
Phaṭ phaṭ! O you whose form is the sound *phetkāra*, who exclaim "kaha kaha," who delight in [the cremation ground], and who are smeared with the ashes of the *preta*s! (8)
O Māri, you whose form is the syllable *kroṃ*; O Mistress of the *kaṅkāra* of Kṛṣṇa, who utters "kaha kaha" with your tongue;

O you of wrathful form, *kṣāṃ kṣāṃ kṣāṃ*; O you who laugh "ha ha ha ha," I bow to you, Caṇḍāsidhārā! I worship you at all times, O you whose mouth is filled with human flesh, you who dwell in the seat of conduct.
He he hūṃkāra-sound, la la la la, you whose foot is the desire for the leap, O you whose form is the sound phaṭ! (9)
Ḍāṃ ḍāṃ ḍāṃ ḍāṃ, O Ḍāmarī! Bestow, bestow, O Giver of Boons! O You of terrible *hūṃ* sounds and speed!
O You who wear a garland of human entrails! Victory, victory to Your feet! O You who dwell upon ten million ears!
That hero, honored by heroes, who proceeds by the path of the sages from the seat of yoga to the supreme seat.
Having become his constant companion, O auspicious one, grant him boons, having descended into the realm of desire and form. || 10 ||
By name Kṣatrāvalī, she recites the auspiciously famous Mantrasiṃha; O Goddess, by your power, divine and other obstacles have no influence here in this battle.
Thus ends the hymn to the Pīṭha of the Kṣattrābalī of Pratyaṅgirā within the Vidyāpīṭha of the Jayadratha, in the illustrious Prakāśa of the Siddhilakṣmīmata.

The five-fold offering (pañcabali): the offering for the pit (kuṇḍa), the offering for the sky-dweller (khecaras), the offering for the one who dwells in the pit (kuṇḍastha), the offering for the tree (vaṭa), the field (kṣetra), the yoginīs, Cāmuṇḍā, the gaṇas, the recitation (japa), the hymn of praise (stotra), the three deities (trideva), the worship of the seat (āsana-pūjana), and the ritual gesture (mudrā).

Having offered water for sipping with the *hṛdaya* [mantra], having worshipped with that [same mantra], and having covered [the fire] with fuel using the *kavaca* [mantra], [one recites]: *oṃ hrāṃ cit piṅgala hana (2) paca (2) daha (2) sarvajñā jñāpaya svāhā*.
Oṃ, I pay homage to Agni, the blazing one, the knower of all beings, the consumer of oblations—
golden-hued, stainless, fully kindled, and facing in every direction.
Sprinkling with the Astra-mantra.

Akṣapātanam | Vedī āsanam | Aiṃ pādukām | Hrīṃ pādukām | Śrīṃ pādukām | Hsphreṃ pādukām | Kusagranthi is placed upon the head. To the East: Brahmaṇe namaḥ | Brahmamūrtaye namaḥ. Heart mantra: Aiṃ (5) Glūṃ Oḍiyānapīṭha.

The venerable sandals (śrīpādukā). The offering (bali) in the south: Oṃ, obeisance to Siddheśvara; Oṃ, obeisance to the form of Siddhilakṣmī. The heart-mantra: Slūṃ, the venerable sandals of the Jālandhara-pīṭha. The offering (bali). In the west: Oṃ Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Śiva; Oṃ, obeisance to the form of the goddess Śivā. The heart-mantra: Aiṃ Plūṃ, the venerable sandals of the Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha. The offering (bali). In the north.

Aiṁ Khphreṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, salutation to the form of Māyādevī. [This is] the heart mantra. Aiṁ Mlūṁ, the venerable sandals of the sacred seat Kāmarūpa. [Offer] the sacrificial oblation (bali). (4) In the ten directions: Aiṁ (5) Lāṁ Līṁ Lūṁ Lmlvryūṁ, the sandals of Indra, who holds a thunderbolt in his hand, who is joined with Śakti, together with his limbs and retinue. Aiṁ (5) Rāṁ Rīṁ Rūṁ, [the sandals] of Agni, who holds a spear.
Aiṃ (5) Māṃ Mīṃ Mūṃ, [salutation] to Yama, the Staff-bearer.
Aiṃ (5) Kṣāṃ Kṣīṃ Kṣūṃ, to the Nairṛta, a sword.
Aiṃ (5) Vāṃ Vīṃ Vūṃ, the noose for Varuṇa.
Aiṃ (5) Yāṃ Yīṃ Yūṃ, the wind [element] hook.
Aiṃ (5) Sāṃ Sīṃ Sūṃ, [the weapon] mace for Kubera.
Aiṃ (5) Hāṃ Hīṃ Hūṃ, [this is] for Īśāna, the trident.
Aiṃ (5) Aṃ Ā: the lotus above. Aiṃ (5) Aṃ: the wheel below.
This is their offering (bali).
The two syllables *du* and *dva* are difficult to pronounce.
Aiṁ (5) Worship of Svarga and the other [realms].
Aiṁ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṁ, the venerable sandals of Śrī Siddheśvara Mahābhairava.
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, I worship the sandals of the deity Agni.
O Śakra and other guardians of the quarters, protect [me], with your own weapons raised!

With effort directed toward the fire for the sake of the daytime empowerment of the youth, one should offer two pieces of fuelwood—one with the syllable *praṇava* (oṃ) and one silently. One should perform the rite of facing the fire with the *hṛdaya-mantra*.
Aiṃ (5). I worship this seat and sandals for Brahmā. Brahmā.
Aiṁ (5). This oblation is for Praṇītā; salutation to Praṇītā. || Praṇītā ||

Aiṃ, the *pādukā* for the seat of the Self (*ātmasanāya*). Thus is the moving seat (*calāsana*). [The *pādukā*] for the seat of Brahmā (*brahmāsanāya*). [The *pādukā*] for the seat of the consecrated water (*praṇītāsanāya*). The consecration of the consecrated water (*praṇītasaṃskāraṃ*). Aiṃ, sprinkling with the water of the offering (*arghodaka*) by means of the weapon-mantra (*astreṇa*). Satisfying [the vessel] with the armor-mantra (*kavacena*). Cleansing with *kuśa* grass by means of the weapon-mantra (*astreṇa*). Aiṃ Hrīṃ, the *pādukā* for the Amṛtagaṅgā. At the place where speech is free from blemish and sin, worship. Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ, the *pādukā* for Brahmā.
Aiṁ (5) Hrauṁ, the sandals for the Four-faced One. Aiṁ (5), the sandals for the Creator of Emanation.

The worship of the *praṇītā* vessel: Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ, the *pādukā* for the *praṇītā*; Hrīṁ, obeisance to Viṣṇu; Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ, the *pādukā* for the Supreme Self (*paramātman*). Having again placed [the vessels] in their respective places: Oṃ Hrāṁ, obeisance to Brahmā, whose seat is the *haṃsa*.
Meditative absorption.
Seated upon a lotus throne is the Swan (Haṃsa), and upon the Swan is the one with the beautiful face;
he is full-bodied, yellow-hued, four-armed, and holds a water-pot, a trident, a rosary, and a book.
To the south of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), upon a seat of dried cow dung,
one should meditate thus on Brahmā and worship him as the Supreme Lord.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Brahmā. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Prajāpati. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Creator.
The offering of an excellent seat and so forth: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu, whose seat is Tārkṣya.
Meditative absorption (dhyāna).
Seated upon a lotus and mounted on Garuḍa, resembling a monkey while seated on Tārkṣya,
holding a conch, discus, mace, and lotus— this is at the northern side of Viṣṇukuṇḍa.
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Lord of Waters. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to all the gods.
To the south, the installation of Brahmā upon a seat (viṣṭara).
The worship is as before.
One should place darbha grass with its tips pointing eastward upon the consecrated water.

The strewing of *kuśa* grass; the worship of the fire according to the prescribed rule; and the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *Oṃ*, salutation to Bhṛgu, the seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head. *Oṃ*, salutation to Gāyatrī, the meter (*chandas*), on the mouth. *Oṃ*, salutation to Agni, the deity (*devatā*), on the heart. *Oṃ*, salutation to Raṃ, the seed-syllable (*bīja*), on the private parts. *Oṃ*, salutation to Svāhā, the power (*śakti*), on the feet. Having thus performed the ritual placement (*vinyasya*).

The application (*viniyoga*) is for the *pratiṣṭhāṅga-homa*. With palms joined in reverence (*kṛtāñjali*), one should recite: Upon the *liṅga*: *oṃ sryūṃ hiraṇyāyai namaḥ* | In the secret place (*guhya*): *ṣryūṃ gagaṇāyai namaḥ* | On the head: *oṃ śryūṃ raktāyai namaḥ* | On the mouth: *oṃ vryūṃ kṛṣṇāyai namaḥ* | On the nose: *oṃ lryūṃ suprabhāyai namaḥ* | On the two eyes: *oṃ rryūṃ bahurūpāyai namaḥ* | On all the limbs: *oṃ yryūṃ atiraktāyai namaḥ* | Having thus performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seven tongues of fire (*saptajihvā*).
Oṃ, salutation to the heart, the thousand-rayed one. Oṃ, svāhā to the head, the fullness of light. Oṃ, to the Puruṣa who has arisen.

*Śikhāyai vaṣaṭ.* Oṃ *dhūmavyāpine kavacāya hūṃ*. Oṃ *saptajihvāya netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*. Oṃ *dhanurdharāya astrāya phaṭ*. Thus [the mantras for] the heart and so forth are applied to the head. Oṃ *agnaye jātavedase namaḥ*—on the left shoulder. Oṃ *agnaye saptajihvāya namaḥ*—on the left side. Oṃ *agnaye havyavāhanāya namaḥ*—on the left hip. Oṃ *agnaye aśvodarajāya namaḥ*—on the generative organ (*liṅga*).

Oṃ, obeisance to Aṅgaya Vaiśvānara; on the right hip. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Kaumāratejas; on the right side. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Viṣṇumukhāya; on the right shoulder. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Vasumukhāya; in the center of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*). Having prepared the worship pedestal (*pūjā-pīṭha*) of the Fire-god, which consists of an eight-petaled lotus surrounded by three squares, containing a six-cornered [triangle] within its pericarp and filaments, and provided with four seasonal [lotuses]: [The mantras for the petals follow: Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Sadyojāta; on the eastern petal. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Vāmadaiva; on the northeastern petal. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Aghora; on the southern petal. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Tatpuruṣa; on the western petal. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Īśāna; on the northwestern petal. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Ananta; on the southeastern petal. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Ūrdhvavaktra; on the upper petal. [The mantras for the corners follow: Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Soma; on the southeast corner. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Rudra; on the southwest corner. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Brahmā; on the northwest corner. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Viṣṇu; on the northeast corner. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Śakti; on the lower corner. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Śiva; on the upper corner. [The mantras for the gates follow: Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Pūrva-dvāra; at the eastern gate. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Dakṣiṇa-dvāra; at the southern gate. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Paścima-dvāra; at the western gate. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Uttara-dvāra; at the northern gate. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Ūrdhva-dvāra; at the upper gate. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Adho-dvāra; at the lower gate. [The mantras for the intermediate directions follow: Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Āgneya; in the southeast. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Nairṛtya; in the southwest. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Vāyavya; in the northwest. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Aiśānya; in the northeast. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Pātāla; in the nether region. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Svarga; in the celestial region. [The mantras for the guardians follow: Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Indrāya; to Indra. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Yamāya; to Yama. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Varuṇāya; to Varuṇa. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Kuberāya; to Kubera. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Īśānāya; to Īśāna. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Anantāya; to Ananta. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Brahmaṇe; to Brahmā. [The mantras for the weapons follow: Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Śaktaye; to the spear. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Daṇḍāya; to the staff. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Khadgāya; to the sword. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Pāśāya; to the noose. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Aṅkuśāya; to the goad. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Gadayai; to the mace. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Triśūlāya; to the trident. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Cakrāya; to the discus. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Padmāya; to the lotus. [The mantras for the seats follow: Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Siṃhāsanāya; to the lion-throne. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Vṛṣabhāsanāya; to the bull-throne. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Garuḍāsanāya; to the eagle-throne. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Mayūrāsanāya; to the peacock-throne. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Mahiṣāsanāya; to the buffalo-throne. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Gajendrāsanāya; to the lordly elephant-throne. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Haṃsāsanāya; to the swan-throne. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Garuḍāsanāya; to the eagle-throne. [The mantras for the attendants follow: Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Gaṇeśāya; to Gaṇeśa. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Kumārāya; to Kumāra. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Durgāyai; to Durgā. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Vighneśāya; to Vighneśa. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Kṣetrapālāya; to Kṣetrapāla. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Yoginībhyo; to the Yoginīs. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Bhairavāya; to Bhairava. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Śmaśānādhipataye; to the Lord of the Cremation Ground. [The mantras for the offering vessels follow: Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Arghyapātrāya; to the vessel of respectful offering. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Pādyapātrāya; to the vessel of water for the feet. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Ācamanīyapātrāya; to the vessel of water for sipping. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Madhuparkapātrāya; to the vessel of the honey-mixture. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Snānapātrāya; to the vessel of bathing water. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Vastrāya; to the garment. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Upavītāya; to the sacred thread. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Gandhāya; to the perfume. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Akṣatebhyaḥ; to the unbroken grains. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Puṣpebhyaḥ; to the flowers. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Dhūpāya; to the incense. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Dīpāya; to the lamp. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Naivedyāya; to the food offering. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Tāmbūlāya; to the betel nut. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Namaskārāya; to the prostration. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Pradakṣiṇāya; to the circumambulation. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Stotrāya; to the hymns of praise. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni Jap
Oṃ, salutation to the Yoga-pīṭha, beginning with Maṇḍūka and ending with Paramātman. On the filaments: Oṃ, salutation to Prītā; Oṃ, salutation to Śvetā; Oṃ, salutation to Aruṇā.

Oṃ, obeisance to Kṛṣṇā. Oṃ, obeisance to Dhūmrā. Oṃ, obeisance to Tīvrā. Oṃ, obeisance to Visphuliṅginī. Oṃ, obeisance to Ruciśayā. Oṃ, obeisance to Jvālinī. Oṃ, obeisance to the Lotus-Seated One who possesses all powers.
Meditative absorption.
Oṃ, I praise the three-eyed Fire-god, who holds a boon-granting gesture, a svastika, a spear, and the gesture of fearlessness;
who stands upon a lotus, is the color of vermilion, adorned with golden ornaments, and whose crown is graced by a shining crescent moon.

Having thus meditated upon the fire and displayed the seven-tongued mudrā, one should join the hands in triple añjali and recite: *oṃ vaiśvānara-jātaveda iha āvaha lihitākṣa sarvakarmaṇi sādhaya svāhā*.

Oṃ, obeisance to Agni. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni; this is the seat. Likewise [offer] the arghya, pādya, ācamanīya, madhuparka, again ācamanīya, bathing water, ācamana, garment, sacred thread, ācamana, and perfumes and flowers. In the six corners, starting from the front and ending at the center: Oṃ Hiraṇyā and so forth. In the filaments: Agni at the heart; Īśāna at the head; Nairṛti at the tuft of hair (śikhā); Vāyu at the armor (kavaca); in the front, the eyes (netra); in the four directions, the weapon (astra).

On the weapon-petals (astradala), beginning from the front, one should worship the eight forms of the Fire-god (vahni-mūrtis). Having worshipped Indra and the other guardians of the directions along with their weapons within the square enclosure (caturasra), one should offer three handfuls (añjali) with the root mantra. After offering incense, lamp, food offerings (naivedya), water for sipping (ācamana), and betel leaf (tāmbūla), one should bow to the fire. Then follows the accomplishment of the *argha* vessel; to the right, one places the water-pot (kamaṇḍalu) and the flower-vessel.

The cutting of the *tripavitra* (three-fold strainer) and so forth; the *prokṣaṇī* vessel, the *ājyasthālī* (clarified butter pot), the *carusthālī* (oblation pot), the dry *śruva* ladle, the *saṃmārjana* (cleaning) materials, the two *upayamana* (supporting) fuel sticks, the mortar and pestle, the black antelope skin (*kṛṣṇājin*), the winnowing basket (*śūrpa*), clarified butter, sesame seeds, rice grains, the rosary for recitation (*jāpyamālā*), the vessel for the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), and pairs [of items]; the touching of these in pairs. With the *Hṛdaya-mantra*, the cutting of the *pavitra* with the *Astra-mantra*; the binding of the *pavitra* with the *Hṛdaya-mantra*; washing the *prokṣaṇī* vessel with the *Astra-mantra*; and the sprinkling [of water] with the *Hṛdaya-mantra*.

Sprinkling with the *kavaca* mantra using the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*); sweeping with the *astra* mantra; filling with water using the *hṛdaya* mantra; stirring with a purifier (*pavitra*) using the *śiras* mantra; and three times sprinkling the courtyard with the *netra* mantra. Having drawn the water from the *praṇītā* vessel into another vessel, one places it into the *prokṣaṇī* vessel.
Sprinkle with the root mantra. Sprinkle all the ritual substances with the root mantra. One should place the *prokṣaṇī* vessel between the *agni* and the *praṇītā*.

Then, the purification of the *śruk* and *śruva* ladles consists of four consecrations (*catuḥ-saṃskāra*). Having washed them and so forth as before, one should heat their two mouths at the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*) and the Buddhas. Sprinkle them with water from the *prokṣaṇī* vessel while reciting the *kavaca* mantra. Touching the base, middle, and tip of those two [ladles] with the base, middle, and tip of *kuśa* grass, and touching them with a reed (*śara*), one should place the Lord of Reality (*Tattveśvara*) in each respective location through the process of emanation and withdrawal (*sṛṣṭi-saṃhāra*). Then, having wrapped the necks of the two with a triple-thread (*trisūtrī*) and bound them with the *varma* mantra, place them upon a bed of *kuśa* grass to the left.

The clarified butter vessel (*ājyasthālī*) and the oblation vessel (*carusthālī*): [perform] the purifications. Having washed them with the *astra-mantra*, perform the sprinkling with the *hṛdaya-mantra*. Perform the sprinkling with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) using the *kavaca-mantra*. Perform the wiping with the *astra-mantra*. Taking the ghee, perform the four purifications beginning with inspection (*nirīkṣaṇa*). Having placed it in the vessel with the *hṛdaya-mantra*, place it in the fire with the *hṛdaya-mantra*. Sprinkle [the ghee] with the tips and roots of two blades of *kuśa* grass using the *hṛdaya-mantra*. Having washed the two blades of *kuśa*, cast them into the clarified butter with the *hṛdaya-mantra*.
Having washed two blades of *kuśa* grass and having whirled them around the clarified butter vessel with the *kavaca* mantra.

Sprinkle [the ghee] with the heart mantra; sprinkle it again with the armor mantra. Stir the clarified butter (*ājya*) with the crest mantra. Having kindled the *kuśa* grass, heat the clarified butter with the heart mantra. Purify it by splashing with the two sacred blades (*pavitra*) using the weapon mantra. Having thrice splashed the ghee with the two sacred blades, place it in the center of the vessel for the clarified butter with the tips pointing eastward, using the heart mantra. Perform the worship: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ hsauṃ pañcapraṇave namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrāṃ surāyai namaḥ*. [Offer] sandalwood paste and so forth. [Display] the cow-seal (*dhenumudrā*).
The gazing at the clarified butter.
Having seen that clarified butter (ājya) removes sin, clarified butter is the supreme remover of sin;
all the hosts of gods reside in clarified butter, for everything is established in clarified butter.

The *prokṣaṇī* waters are prepared as before. One should sprinkle the fire with the root mantra. One should circumambulate the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) while reciting the *kavaca* mantra. Having offered oblations into the fire: *oṃ bhuvapataye svāhā*, *oṃ bhuvanapataye svāhā*, *oṃ bhūtānāṃ pataye svāhā*. Then, one should pour the remaining water into the *praṇīta* vessel.
Then, the sprinkling of the *śruk* and *śruva* ladles with the *astra-mantra*, and the inspection with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*).

Covering with the *kavaca* mantra; striking with the *astra* mantra; purifying with the *tritatva* [mantra] using the root, middle, and tip [of the blades]; [reciting] "KHPHREṂ Siddheśvara Mahābhairava, the *śruk* [ladle] is the *śrīpādukā* of Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, the *śruvā* [spoon] is the *śrīpādukā* of Śrī Siddhilakṣmī; ṄAṂ HSRĀUṂ, obeisance to Śiva and Śakti. Having taken the supporting *kuśa* grass with the *astra* mantra, [perform] the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) and the *yonimudrā*.
The rite of the ten fires. Aiṃ (5). To the heart, for the rite of impregnation, svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to the rite for obtaining a male child. Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to the extraction of the secret mantra by means of the mantra on the head.
Aiṃ (5) Svāhā! To the rite of birth by means of the crest-lock. Aiṃ (5) Svāhā! To the first emergence by means of the armor.

Aiṁ (5) HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ KHPHREṂ! To the one named *Śrīsiddhāgni*, whose nature is fire, for the naming ceremony (*nāmakaraṇa*) of the illustrious *Siddhāgni*, svāhā! Aiṁ (5)! With the upward-facing mouth, for the animation of the fruit [of existence], svāhā! Aiṁ (5)! With the supreme and non-supreme mouth, for the animation of food, svāhā! Aiṁ (5)! With the eastern-facing mouth, for the tonsure ceremony (*cūḍākaraṇa*), svāhā! Aiṁ (5)! With the eastern-facing mouth, for the piercing of the ears (*karṇavedha*), svāhā! Aiṁ...

(5) Svāhā! With the southern face, for the making of a *vaṭuka*, svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Svāhā! With the northern face, for the release from vows, svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Svāhā! With the western face, for marriage, svāhā!

Aiṃ (5). To the one with four faces, the higher and lower, svāhā! The installation of the fire should be performed. With the nine-syllable mantra, the five-faced one, the fire is filled. Aiṃ (5). Beginning from the rite of conception (garbhādhāna) and so forth, it is endowed with the ten groups, complete with ritual acts, possessed of all ornaments, consisting of all qualities, and indeed accompanied by the seven tongues of flame.

O Lord, may the glorious Bhairava-fire, together with the nine obstacles and accompanied by the fire of accomplishment, be constantly well-satisfied through oblations of a handful of parched grain (*lāja*) mixed with clarified butter, according to the prescribed rite. This is the dismissal of the fire’s parents. Thus ends the procedure for the rites concerning the fire-priest (*agnīdh*).
To Vāgīśvarī, salutation. To Agni, meditation.
Mounted upon Aries, surrounded by flames, with a sacrificial fire in his hand,
he stands at the northern face of the sacrificial pit, blazing with the splendor of the sun.

The tongue shall be seven-colored; in the right hand is the *śruva* ladle, and in the left stands Svāhā, the consort. Come for the rites of pacification (*śāntikarma*). Oṃ, salutation to the flower of meditation upon Agni.

The meditation: Bhairava, Aśitāṅga, and the others; surrounded by the eight fields such as Karavīra and the eight cremation grounds; encircled by the six Ḍākinīs, the six Yoginīs, and the [eight Mothers] beginning with Brahmāṇī; [he visualizes] the Siddha fire.

Eighteen [oblations]. Sixteen oblations with fuel-sticks (*samidh*). Having offered one with the *praṇava* (Oṃ), and having placed one in the *praṇītā* vessel, the Brahman priest, remembering [the rite], should perform the threefold *saṃvīrya* with *kuśa* grass: "Oṃ namaḥ prajāpataye svāhā. [Then] water for sprinkling (*prokṣaṇī*) is poured from the vessels: "This obeisance to Prajāpati. The binding of the *upayamana* grass is performed in the left hand: "Oṃ hrīṃ to Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand," and so forth.

Then, having meditated upon Prajāpati as the deity, Brahmā performed the worship of the gods during the subsequent oblations, accompanied by the Vedas he had brought forth and the guardians of the world. Oṃ Hrāṃ, salutation to the fifteen-fold one. Salutation to the fourfold-fifteen-fold one, to the god Agni, to the knower of the sacrificial ground, to Svarga, to Martya, to Pātāla, to Gaurī, to Dhātrī, to Skandā, to Sūrya, to Yogīśvara, to Mahāyogīśvara, to the Tīrthakṛts among the gods, to the Ṛṣis, to the deities of the oblation, to the Praṇīta, and to all the gods—salutation! Salutation to the three gods!
Homage to the gods in the north; *svadhā* to the ancestors in the south. *Oṃ*, *svāhā* to Indra; this is for Indra.

The *cakṣuhoma* (eye-oblation): Taking clarified butter from the right side with the *hṛdaya-mantra*, [offer it] to the right eye: *oṃ hrāṃ agnaye svāhā*. This [is for] the left eye. Likewise, taking [butter] from the left side: *oṃ hrāṃ somāya svāhā*. This [is for] the third eye in the middle, taking [butter] from the central portion: *oṃ hrāṃ agnīṣomābhyāṃ svāhā*. This [is for] the mouth of the Fire, taking clarified butter together with the *pavitra*: *oṃ hrāṃ sviṣṭakṛte svāhā*. This [is for] Agni.
The tongue-homa: Aiṁ (5) Plūṁ, svāhā to Rājadāyī. [This is] the eastern [direction].
Aiṃ (5) Ślūṃ, svāhā to Dāghadājananī. [This is] the Āgneya [mantra]. (2)
Aiṃ (5) Blūṃ, svāhā to Mṛtyudāyī. [In the] south. (3) ||
Aiṃ (5) Ślūṃ, svāhā to Śatrukārikā! [Direction: Nairṛtya. (4) ||
Aiṁ (5) Blūṁ, svāhā to Balikā. In the western direction. (5) ||
Aiṁ (5) mlūṁ, svāhā to Uccāṭanī in the northwestern direction. (6)
Aiṃ (5) Hrūṃ, svāhā to Arthapadā. In the northern direction. (7)
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ, svāhā to Muktidāyā (the Giver of Liberation). [In the] Īśāna [direction]. (8) ||
Aiṃ (5) Kṣrīṃ, svāhā to the Giver of All Siddhis. [End of] the middle [section]. (9)
Thus ends [the section on] Navajihvā.
Salutation to the joining of the tongue.
Aiṃ (5) Plūṃ! To Rājadāyī, the mother of Śrūdāghadāja, svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Brūṃ, svāhā to Mṛtyudāyā; Ślūṃ, svāhā to Śatrukārikā.
Aiṃ (5) Brūṃ, svāhā to Vaśikā; Mrūṃ, svāhā to Uccāṭinī.
Aiṃ (5) Hrūṃ, svāhā to Arthapadā; Hrīṃ, svāhā to Muktidā.
Aiṃ (5) Kṣrīṃ, svāhā to the giver of all accomplishments. [In the center.]
Astrāye phaṭ svāhā. Chendana. Aiṃ (5) Kṣmlīṃ Sarvasiddhidāyai svāhā.
aiṃ (5) hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ khphreṃ svāhā ||

Then, for the purpose of purifying the faces: *Oṃ haṃ sadyojātāya svāhā* — in the west. *Oṃ hiṃ vāmadevāya svāhā* — in the north. *Oṃ hūṃ aghorāya svāhā* — in the south. *Oṃ heṃ tatpuruṣāya svāhā* — in the east.

Oṃ hoṃ īśānāye svāhā. [Offering] in the center. Having thus worshipped, one performs oblations of clarified butter ending with "svāhā" and performs the sprinkling (abhighāra). Then, for the sake of reconnection: Oṃ haṃ hi sadyovāmābhyāṃ svāhā. [The syllables] *yu*, *vi*, *ne*, *na*, *yaṃ*, *thaṃ*, *ne* [are placed]. [The ritual] abandonment is together [with them]. Oṃ huṃ heṃ aghora-tatpuruṣābhyāṃ svāhā. [The syllables] *ye*, *vi*, *ne*, *na*, *yo*, *thaṃ*, *ṅa* [are placed] in the middle of the stream of clarified butter (*ghṛtadhāra*). [This is done] with the *śruva* ladle. Oṃ heṃ hoṃ tatpuruṣa-īśābhyāṃ svāhā.

Likewise, for the purpose of unifying those faces: *Oṃ hoṃ hiṃ hūṃ heṃ hoṃ sadyo-vāmā-ghora-tatpuruṣeśānebhyaḥ svāhā*. Then, from the southeast (Āgneya) to the southwest (Asura), [the faces] ending with Īśāna are placed within the mouths, starting from the mouth of Sadyojāta and ending with the middle one, which has a stream of ghee flowing from it. Thus, there is the internal inclusion of the faces within the desired mouth.
The full verse.
Clad in kanavīra flowers, she who always dwells in the cremation ground, seated upon a corpse-throne, is the one whose heart is captivated by those who bow before her.
She who is moon-like and white as snow, five-faced, beginning with Amogha, and possessing ten arms— she is Śrī, the Goddess of Success and Prosperity.
Aiṃ (5). Rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ: the red-colored, three-eyed Bhairava, the burner, possessing seven tongues;
seated there is Siddhilakṣmī, holding in her four hands the *śakti*, the *śruva* ladle, and the letter 'sa' and so forth;
with one face resting upon a corpse, O Eater of the Unborn, having kindled and made it blaze intensely—upa ūha.
May the god Agni, who brings peace and dwells in the ten directions, come and protect you.

Then follows the oblation to the Vedas: *oṃ hrīṃ brahmaṇe svāhā*. [The renunciation (*tyāga*) together with it. Likewise: *oṃ hrāṃ pṛthivyai svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ agnaye svāhā*; *oṃ hrīṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*; *oṃ hrāṃ prajāpataye svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ devebhyaḥ svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ ṛṣibhyaḥ*; *oṃ hrāṃ chandobhyaḥ svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ śraddhāyai svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ medhāyai svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ sadasaspataye svāhā*.
Oṃ hrāṃ Anumati, svāhā!

Oṃ siddheśvarāya svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ antarikṣāya svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ vāyave svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe, etc. || Oṃ hrāṃ śivāya svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ dive svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ sūryāya svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe, etc. (9) || Oṃ hrāṃ māyāyai svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ digbhyaḥ svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ candramase svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe, etc. (9) ||

Then, the offering of fifteen oblations: *Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā* | This is for Agni. *Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā* | This is for Vāyu. *Oṃ svaḥ svāhā* | This is for Sūrya. *Oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ svāhā* | This is for Prajāpati. *Oṃ vaiśvānara jātaveda ihāvaha lohitākṣa sarvakarmāṇi sādhaya svāhā* | (3) This is for Agni. The six-limbed [mantras]: *Oṃ sahasrārciṣe hṛdayāya svāhā* | Renunciation. *Oṃ svasti pūrṇāya śirase svāhā* | Renunciation.

Oṃ, to the rising person, the crest [mantra], svāhā! Oṃ, to the smoke-pervading one, the armor [mantra], svāhā! Oṃ, to the seven-tongued one, the eye [mantra], svāhā! Oṃ, to the bow-bearer, the weapon [mantra], svāhā! [The word] "renunciation" is included.
Oṃ, svāhā to Agni Havyavāhana!

[Perform] the renunciation together. Oṃ, svāhā to Agni born from the belly of the horse. Oṃ, svāhā to Agni Vaiśvānara. Oṃ, svāhā to Agni, the splendor of Kumāra. Oṃ, svāhā to Agni, whose face is the universe. Oṃ, svāhā to Agni, whose face is the gods. Oṃ luṃ, svāhā to Indra. Oṃ ruṃ, svāhā to Agni. Oṃ muṃ, svāhā to Yama. Oṃ kṣuṃ, svāhā to Nairṛti. Oṃ vuṃ, svāhā to Varuṇa. Oṃ yuṃ, svāhā to Vāyu. Oṃ suṃ, svāhā to Kubera.

Oṃ hūṃ īśānāya svāhā || Oṃ aṃ anantāya svāhā || Oṃ oṃ brahmaṇe svāhā || [Offering] with the *tyāga*. Oṃ hrīṃ lrūṃ vajrāya phaṭ svāhā || [Offering] with the *tyāga*. Oṃ hrūṃ śaktaye phaṭ svāhā || Oṃ mrūṃ daṇḍāya phaṭ svāhā || Oṃ grūṃ khaḍgāya phaṭ svāhā || Oṃ prūṃ pāśāya phaṭ svāhā || Oṃ dhrūṃ dhvajāya phaṭ svāhā || Oṃ grūṃ gadāya phaṭ svāhā || Oṃ haiṃ śūlāya phaṭ svāhā ||
Oṃ oṃ padmāya phaṭ svāhā || Oṃ klīṃ cakrāya phaṭ svāhā ||

Then, taking clarified butter with the *sruva* ladle and pouring it into the *sruk* four times, placing the *sruk* face down upon the *sruva*, standing up and reciting the previously mentioned fire-mantra (*vahni-mantra*) while uttering "Vauṣaṭ," one should offer oblations into the fire with the *sruva* while remaining standing; then, having sat down: Oṃ svāhā. Oṃ śrīṃ svāhā. Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ svāhā. Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ svāhā. Oṃ (5) svāhā. Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye svāhā. Oṃ (5) gaṃ gaṇapataye varavarada svāhā.

Oṃ (5) Gaṃ, to Gaṇapati, the bestower of excellent boons, bring all people under my control, svāhā! Thus, one should offer oblations of clarified butter four times with the complete mantra of Gaṇapati; this is the procedure for the installation of the fire.

Then, with the root mantra, having offered twenty-five oblations of clarified butter (*ājya*) for the purpose of unifying the mouths of the fire and the deity, one should contemplate the identity of one's own self, the fire, and the deity. Having offered eleven oblations of clarified butter with the root mantra for the purpose of joining the channels (*nāḍī-sandhāna*), and having offered one oblation for the deities of the six-limbed enclosure (*ṣaḍaṅga-āvaraṇa-devatā*).
The worship is performed with the Aghora mantra, having placed [the vessel] upon a funeral pyre that has not yet been ignited.

Then follows the oblation of the five products of the cow (*pañcagavyahoma*). Then, with the *astra-mantra*, there is the invocation (*āvāhana*). One should recite the *Mālinī-daṇḍaka*: Aiṃ! O she who is the supreme, supreme Goddess, seated upon the sky, whose form is the sky; O gentle one who has gone to the world of the gods, may you come here into this mandala!
Here, the fire-mandala, together with its limbs, is present.
One should display the nine mudrās, beginning with the invocation (āvāhana) and ending with the yoni.

Then, one should worship with water for the feet (pādya), the respectful offering (argha), water for sipping (ācamanīya), bathing water (snāna), and so forth, as well as with clothing, a sacred thread (yajñopavīta), sandalwood paste, vermilion (sindūra), flowers, incense, and other offerings.

The stream of peace (śāntidhārā) is for the purification of the vessel of clarified butter. Having washed it with the Astra-mantra, one should perform the satiation with the Hṛdaya-mantra. One should sprinkle it with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) using the Kavaca-mantra, and sweep it with the Astra-mantra. One should cause the stream of peace to be poured over the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa).

Then, having washed the vessel for preparing the *caru* and so forth, as in the procedure for the stream of peace (*śāntidhārā*): one should take the grain with the *astra* mantra, pound it with the *kavaca* mantra, place the sun [within it] with the *hṛdaya* mantra, remove the husks with the *astra* mantra, and place it in a copper vessel.

In a fire-pit similar to a lotus, having performed the six-limbed worship (*ṣaḍaṅga*) with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*), one should place the vessel for the *caru* offering. The *caru* is prepared; [then follows] the worship with the six limbs, the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth, and one should display the *dhenumudrā*. Thus is the procedure for the preparation of the *caru*.
