One should offer oblations of clarified butter (*ghṛta-āhuti*) for Gaṇapati, Durgā, and the others, each with their respective mantra. The sequence of oblations is as follows: For the Three Deities: *Thhsrauṃ* to the Goddess Prastaradīpaṭambhakī and the Great Dhvākṣa-Kṣetrapāla, *svāhā*. *Śrīṃ Hrīṃ* to Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha, *svāhā*. (5) *Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ* to Kulagaṇeśvara, *svāhā*. *Yāṃ* to the Yoginīs, *svāhā*.

To Gaṇapati, svāhā! To the Gurus, svāhā! To Kṣetrapāla, svāhā! To Durgā, svāhā! To Brahmā, svāhā! To Praṇīta, svāhā! To Brahmā, svāhā! To Siddheśvara, svāhā! To Śiva, svāhā! To Māyā, svāhā! O Caturvedin! To Indra, svāhā! To Agni, svāhā! To Yama, svāhā!
Svāhā to Nairṛti! Svāhā to Varuṇa! Svāhā to Vāyu! Svāhā to Kubera! Svāhā to Īśāna! Svāhā to Ananta! Svāhā to Brahmā! Siddhāgni!

To the eastern gate: svāhā! To the archway of peace: svāhā! To the auspicious gateway: svāhā! To Nandin: svāhā! To Mahākāla: svāhā! To the Fish: svāhā! To the Ram: svāhā! To the Bull: svāhā! To the Constellation: svāhā! To Gaṇapati: svāhā! To Mahālakṣmī: svāhā! To Sarasvatī: svāhā! To the trident: svāhā!

To Brahmāyaṇī, Svāhā! To Māheśvarī, Svāhā! To Sthāṇu, Svāhā! To Śiva, Svāhā! To Paśupati, Svāhā! To the Kṛta Yuga, Svāhā! To Brahmā, Svāhā! To Soma, Svāhā! To Aṅgāra, Svāhā! To Hetuka Kṣetrapāla, Svāhā! Lāṃ Līṃ Lūṃ Lmlvryūṃ, to Indra, Svāhā! Indra, lord of the gods, wielder of the thunderbolt, possessed of great strength, the deity who is the master of a hundred sacrifices—to that Indra, obeisance!
To the southern gate: svāhā! To the archway of knowledge: svāhā! To the gateway of Śuhotra: svāhā!

To Bhṛṅgin, svāhā! To Vināyaka, svāhā! To the Couple (Mithuna), svāhā! To Karkaṭa, svāhā! To Siṃha, svāhā! To Nakṣatra, svāhā! To Gaṇapati, svāhā! To Mahālakṣmī, svāhā! To Sarasvatī, svāhā! To the Trident (Triśūla), svāhā! To Komārī, svāhā! To Vaiṣṇavī, svāhā! To Ugra, svāhā! To Saṃbhava, svāhā! To Trilocana, svāhā! To Tretāyuga, svāhā! To Siddheśvara, svāhā! To Budha, svāhā!
Svāhā to Bṛhaspati! Svāhā to Agni, Vetāla, and Kṣetrapāla! Svāhā to Yama: māṃ mīṃ mūṃ mmlvryūṃ!
Homage to the Lord Yama, who holds a staff in his hand, the great and powerful overseer of dharma,
whose body resembles a dark cloud, and who appears as Dharmarāja.

To the western gate: svāhā! To the archway of cessation: svāhā! To the auspicious gate: svāhā! To Vṛṣā: svāhā! To Skanda: svāhā! To Kanyā: svāhā! To Tulā: svāhā! To Vicchā: svāhā! To the asterisms: svāhā! To Gaṇapati: svāhā!

Mahālakṣmī, svāhā! Sarasvatī, svāhā! To the trident, svāhā! Vārāhī, svāhā! Aindrāyaṇī, svāhā! To Śiva, svāhā! To Īśvara, svāhā! To Rudra, svāhā! To Śaṅkala, svāhā! To the Dvāpara Yuga, svāhā! To Śiva, svāhā! To Śukra, svāhā! To Śanaiścara, svāhā! To Kālānala-kṣetrapāla, svāhā! Vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vmlvryūṃ, to Varuṇa, svāhā!
I bow to the Lord who is the King of Waters, possessing great strength and having a noose in his hand;
I bow to the King of Nagas, white in color and of great splendor.

To the northern gate, svāhā! To the archway of installation, svāhā! To the gate of health, svāhā! To the Goddess, svāhā! To Caṇḍa, svāhā! To Dhana, svāhā! To Makara, svāhā! To Kumbha, svāhā! To Nakṣatra, svāhā! To Gaṇapati, svāhā! To Mahālakṣmī, svāhā! To Sarasvatī, svāhā! To the Trident, svāhā! To Cāmuṇḍā, svāhā! To Mahālakṣmī, svāhā! To Sambhava, svāhā! To Maheśvara, svāhā! To Mahādeva, svāhā!
Svāhā to the Kali Yuga!
Svāhā to Māyā! Svāhā to Rāhu! Svāhā to Ketu! Svāhā to the one-legged Kṣetrapāla! Sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ smlvryūṃ, svāhā to Kubera!
Obeisance to you, the heroic one, who are proclaimed as Soma among all the Yakṣas and Trāṇas, and who bear a mace and a vessel. Obeisance to you, the most powerful.
To the south-east: RĀṂ RĪṂ RŪṂ RMLVRYŪṂ, svāhā to Agni! Svāhā to the Kṣetrapāla Tripurāntaka!
To the hundred-fold radiant Mahādeva, red-colored and of great luster,
who holds a spear in his hand and possesses great splendor— to that Vaiśvānara, indeed!
To the south-west.
KṢĀṂ KṢĪṂ KṢŪṂ KṢMLVRYŪṂ, svāhā to Nairṛtya! Svāhā to Agnijihva Kṣetrapāla!
[He beheld] the Lord of the Rākṣasas, with blood-red eyes, mounted upon a buffalo, possessing the luster of a blue lotus petal,
holding a sword in his hand, and drinking a flood of blood.
To Vāyavyā: YĀṂ YĪṂ YŪṂ YMLVRYŪṂ VĀYAVYA SVĀHĀ. To Kapālīśa Kṣetrapāla: SVĀHĀ.
I bow to him who is golden-hued with the luster of a deer, who bears a fluttering banner,
who is the very life-force of all beings, and who is seated upon a deer.
With the Īśāna-mantra: Hāṃ Hīṃ Hūṃ Hmlvryūṃ, svāhā to Īśāna; svāhā to the Kṣetrapāla of Terrible Form.
O God, sovereign of all sciences, known by the name Īśāna;
O Mahādeva, wielder of the trident, lord of the three worlds and beyond—homage to you!
The libations: Hrīṃ, svāhā to Viṣṇu; svāhā to the Kṣetrapāla of Hāṭaka.
O Lord Nārāyaṇa, obeisance to you! The sovereign of serpents named Ananta dwells eternally in Pātāla, pervading the universe in every direction.
With the upward [gesture]: Hāṃ, svāhā to Brahmā; svāhā to the immovable Kṣetrapāla.
Salutations to that one who is like Brahmā, the lotus-born, the fourfold-formed, who dwells in the station of the head, and whose nature is eternally the creator of the universe.
To the Yoginī Svāhā.
I bow to the Goddess who pervades the three worlds, who holds a curved knife and a skull-cup, and who crushes all obstacles, together with her two Yoginīs.
Svāhā to the form of Śrī! Hrāṃ, svāhā to the form of Lakṣmī!

Seated upon a lotus throne with her feet extended, possessing eyes as long as lotus petals, with a navel deep in its whorls, bent by the weight of her breasts, and wearing white lower garments— this Goddess Lakṣmī, accompanied by the lords of elephants and hosts of sages, was bathed with golden jars.
May she, who holds a lotus in her hand, be ever present for you, always endowed with every auspiciousness.
KṢĀṂ! To the protector of the realm, svāhā!
Seated upon a human corpse, stationed in the southwest,
presiding over all the planets— homage to you, O Kṣetrapāla!
Gāṃ, to Gaṇapati, svāhā!
I bow to Gaṇeśa, who removes all obstacles, who is mounted upon a mouse, and who must be invoked at the beginning of all undertakings to ward off every impediment.
Svāhā to the form of the Guru.
Possessing the hue of saffron, holding rosaries and books,
they are remembered as the teachers of all, knowing all scriptures and the ultimate reality.
To the one who brings peace, svāhā!
May the sky of peace, the intermediate space, and likewise the earth; may the gems, the medicinal herbs, and all the gods grant peace;
may Brahmā, Vāyu, Agni, and Rudra also grant peace to Bāṇa.

The sun, the moon, and Hari, as well as I myself, am entirely pacified by those for whom peace is attained through the performance of the *śānti-homa* according to the ritual of one's own preceptor, with the offering of the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*).
The descent of Śiva’s power: Oṃ hrāṃ oṃ juṃ saḥ, to Mṛtyuñjaya, the Lord of Immortality, accompanied by the power Mahālakṣmī; saḥ juṃ oṃ svāhā.
O Amṛteśī, O Great Lord, to the destroyer of the suffering of the universe,
whose nature is both transcendent and immanent— salutations to You, O Three-eyed One!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Āditya!
He possesses a thousand rays and great splendor, adorned with jeweled earrings;
his beautiful feet are near [to the devotee], he wears armor, and his body is composed of jewels.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, svāhā to Varuṇa!
Ananta, the lord of the nāga kings, and Mahāpadma and Takṣaka; Vāsuki and Padma, the protectors of the lords of the Kulika family.
O Lord, this Kakkoṭaka and other jewel-treasures are dear to you;
homage to you, the King of Nāgas, homage to the sovereign of Pātāla.
To the Yakṣa, svāhā! To the Yakṣiṇī, svāhā! Praise!
O you who ride upon the lord of beasts, O Lord of the Yakṣas, for the destruction of obstacles—
may you all, together with your vehicles, be girded for battle by the command of Śiva.
Śrī Svāhā.
I bow down to the Goddess Śrī, who dwells upon the body of a sea-monster (makara), who is well-worshipped by the three worlds,
and who holds vermilion and blue lotuses in her two hands.
Lakṣmī Svāhā.
Seated upon the tortoise-throne, radiant as the moon and the white water-lily, and holding a lotus and a mirror— I bow to Goddess Lakṣmī.

Oṃ juṃ saḥ svāhā to Mṛtyuñjaya. [Recite] "The pure and peaceful one, supreme in grace," and so forth. [Perform] the *thaṇḍila* rite with the root mantra. For the removal of baldness, [use] the root mantra.
To Śrī Lakṣmī: O Great Lakṣmī, the source of the lotus of supreme bliss born of Yoga, the crest-jewel among the jewels of women, the embodiment of great auspiciousness;
you whose breasts are the central power (*śakti*), and who are the true bond that adorns the three worlds.
The Yoginī Śrī Kālikā, who bears a digit of the moon on her forehead, possesses the essence of all virtues.

A liṅga made of cow dung. For the propitiation of Mṛtyuñjaya: "O pure one, O peaceful one," and so forth; for the dog-eater Varuṇa, *svāhā*. "Ananta, Takṣaka," and so forth. "Aśitāṅga," and so forth; "Brahmāṇī," and so forth. *Hrāṃ*, to Aśitāṅgabhairava together with the Śakti Brahmanī, *svāhā*. *Hrāṃ*, to Rurubhairava together with the Śakti Kāmeśvarī, *svāhā*.
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Caṇḍabhairava, together with the power Kaumārī.
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Krodhabhairava, together with the Vaiṣṇavī Śakti, Ṭaṃ.
Hrāṃ! To Unmattabhairava, together with his Śakti Vārāhī, svāhā!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Kapālisabhairava, together with the power Indrāyaṇī.
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Bhīṣaṇabhairava, together with Cāmuṇḍā and her Śakti! Yaṃ.
Hrāṃ! To Śaṃhārabhairava, together with the power Mahālakṣmī, svāhā!

Indra and others: Luṃ, svāhā to Indra; Ruṃ, svāhā to Agni; Mūṃ, svāhā to Yama; Kṣūṃ, svāhā to Nairṛtya; Vūṃ, svāhā to Varuṇa; Yūṃ, svāhā to Vāyu; Sūṃ, svāhā to Kubera; Hūṃ, svāhā to Īśāna; Aṃ, svāhā to Ananta; Oṃ, svāhā to Brahmā. Prayāga and others: Hrāṃ, svāhā to the Great Kṣetrapāla of Prayāga; Hrāṃ, svāhā to the Kṣetrapāla of Varuṇa.
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the great Kṣetrapāla of Kolāpura!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the venerable Kṣetrapāla Aṭṭahāsa!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the great field-protector Jayantī!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Caritra Mahākṣetrapāla.
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the great protector of Ekāmraka!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the Kṣetrapāla of Devīkoṭa.
Hetukādi. Hrāṃ, svāhā to Hetuka Kṣetrapāla.
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Tripurāntaka Kṣetrapāla.
Hrāṃ! Svāhā to Agnivetāla Kṣetrapāla!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Agnijihva Kṣetrapāla!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Kālākṣa Kṣetrapāla.
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Kalāli Nakṣatrapāla.
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the one-legged Kṣetrapāla!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the field-protector Bhīmarūpa!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Hāṭaka Kṣetrapāla!
Hrāṃ, svāhā to Gaganakṣatrapāla!
Brahmāṇyādi: Hrīṃ Aṃ Brahmāṇī Devī Svāhā. Hrīṃ Kaṃ Māheśvarī Devī Svāhā. Hrīṃ Caṃ Kaumārī Devī Svāhā. Hrīṃ Ṭaṃ Vaiṣṇavī Devī Svāhā.
Hrīṃ Taṃ Vārāhīdevī Svāhā || Hrīṃ Paṃ Indrāṇīdevī Svāhā || Hrīṃ Yaṃ Cāmuṇḍādevī Svāhā || Hrīṃ Śaṃ Mahālakṣmīdevī Svāhā ||
Brahmā: Hrāṃ, svāhā to Brahmā. Praṇītā: Hrīṃ, svāhā to Viṣṇu.

[O you] who possess the four Vedas. (4) || *Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ svāhā*. (4) || O Guardian of the Sacrificial Pit (*kuṇḍaṅuvalokapāla*): *Luṃ* to Indra, *svāhā*; *Ruṃ* to Agni, *svāhā*; *Muṃ* to Yama, *svāhā*; *Kṣuṃ* to Nairṛtya, *svāhā*; *Vuṃ* to Varuṇa, *svāhā*; *Yuṃ* to Vāyu, *svāhā*; *Suṃ* to Kubera, *svāhā*; *Huṃ* to Īśāna, *svāhā*; *Aṃ* to Ananta, *svāhā*; *Oṃ* to Brahmā, *svāhā*.

O Six Yoginīs! Aiṃ (5)! To Dhāṃ Svāhā! To Dhāmavatī Svāhā! To Dhāmnī Svāhā! To the Vedyāmaṇḍala Svāhā! To Raviprabha Svāhā! To Virājantī Svāhā! O Six Ākinyas! Ḍmlvryūṃ! To Ḍākinī Svāhā! Rmlvryūṃ! To Rākinī Svāhā!
lmlvryūṃ, svāhā to Lākini! kmlvryūṃ, svāhā to Kākini! smlvryūṃ, svāhā to Sākini! hmlvryūṃ, svāhā to Hākini!
Ṣaṭdūtī: Aiṃ (5) Hskhphreṃ Kāli Kāli Hrāṃ Mahākāli Hrīṃ Māṃsaśoṇitabhojani Hūṃ Raktakṛṣṇamukhīdevī Hroṃ Māṃ Māṃ Paśyantu Śatravaḥ Svāhā!

Aiṃ (5). Homage to the Blessed One, O Duṣṭacāmuṇḍāli, consumer of the blood and flesh of enemies, bearer of the skull-bowl and khaṭvāṅga staff! Strike (2), burn (2), pierce (2), cook (2)! Hūṃ (3)! Kill so-and-so (2)! Devour (2)! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Aghore Hrauṃ, O terrible one, Hsphreṃ, O most terrible one, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ, O you who transcend all, O all, O everything, Hskhphreṃ! Homage to you, O you whose form is Rudra! Hsauṃ Svāhā!

Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ, O you who have attained the supreme equanimity, Hrīṃ, O you who have destroyed all afflictions, Hrīṃ, O you who have written [the truth] on the surface of the earth, Hrīṃ, O you who have written it upon all trees, Svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ Guhya Kubjike Hūṃ Phaṭ Hrīṃ Rakte Mahārakte Cāmuṇḍeśvarī Aiṃ Svāhā.

Aiṁ (5) HSKHPHREṂ HSKHPHRĪṂ HRĀṂ HRĪṂ HŪṂ! May all calamities—whether incantations, magical diagrams, powders, applications, or the like—performed, performed in the past, or that will be performed by anyone, be destroyed! Strike them down! O Dāṃṣṭrākalālī! HRĀṂ HRĪṂ HRŪṂ PHRAUṂ PHRŪṂ ŚLĪṂ! O Guhyakubjikā, svāhā!
Ugracaṇḍā: Oṃ hrīṃ rājaprade hsphreṃ ugracaṇḍe raṇamarddanī hūṃ phreṃ, always protect you and me, juṃ sa, O remover of death, namaḥ svāhā!
Vagalāmukhī || Aiṁ (5) Oṃ hlīṃ Vagalāmukhi, paralyze the faces and speech of all the wicked; nail down their tongues (2); destroy their intellect! Hlāṃ oṃ svāhā.
Triśati || Śrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ aiṃ vajravailocanīye hūṃ (2) phaṭ svāhā ||
Hanubhairava: Aiṃ (5) Oṃ rhphrīṃ hūṃ bhañja bhañja rhkṣrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Not with a loose horse. Aiṃ (5) Oṃ hūṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ, svāhā to Nṛtyaśvara Mahābhairava together with his consort Śkṣmlvryīṃ Nṛtyalakṣmī and her power.

The fifth is Vārāhī: Aiṃ (5) Glauṃ Oṃ Namo Bhagavati Vārttārī (2) Vālāhī Vārāhi Mukhi Andherī Nama Rudherī Nama Rudhe Rudhani Nama Jambhe Jambhani Nama Mohe Mohani Nama Sarvaduṣṭānāṃ Sarveṣāṃ Śighraṃ Vasamvuru Kuru Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ṭha (3) Oṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā.
West: Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes, Śkṣmlvryīṃ! To the venerable Paścima Mūlasthāna Bhaṭṭārikā, Svāhā!
With the following [mantra]: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ svāhā. (3)
Kāli || Oṃ phreṃ siddhikalāli hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ svāhā ||

Of Tripurasundarī: Aiṃ (5) KṢHRĪMLHRĪMKLHRĪṂ! To the venerable goddess Mahātripurasundarī, the supreme power whose essence is Brahman, who resides upon the seat of Caryā in the great sacred site of Oḍiyāna within the Wheel of Brahman; Śrī Svāhā!

With five faces: Aiṃ (5) Rjhṛīṃ, O Mahācaṇḍatejasaṃkarṣaṇī Kālī, O Manthānā, svāhā! Phreṃ Āṃ Kroṃ Phroṃ, O Mahāsiddhasamaya Khphreṃ Bhairavī, O Ghoravighoralakṣmī, O Bestower of Boons, svāhā! Āṃ Phiṃ Phrāṃ, O Mahāsṛṣṭicaṇḍalakṣmīśvarī, phaṭ (2) svāhā!
Siddheśvara! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Ānandabhairava Siddheśvara, Svāhā!
Gaṇagorajāsa || (5) Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaḥ glauṃ śrīṃ, svāhā to the Lord of the Host of Rats.

Haṃtākṣā | Gvagrāsa | Oṃ pañcaśvamātraye svāhā | Nandrābhṛ pra (? | Kaumārī | Aiṃ (5) caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ kmlvryūṃ kroṃ kaumārī vicce svāhā | Vārabhāve | Vaiṣṇavī | Oṃ hrīṃ ṭaṃ vaiṣṇavī devī svāhā | Vaiṣṇavī Viṣṇu | Cāśvara | Aiṃ (5) paścimayā | Aiṃ (5) caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ cmlvryūṃ caṇḍeśvarī svāhā | Ṣaṭkambā | Syāmāraktā | Bālabhāve.
Nāśvara || Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to Nṛtyaśvara, Śkṣmlvryīṃ, to Nṛtyalakṣmī, svāhā || Ānandaśakti ||

Tuparaju. Aiṃ (5). In the beginningless great seat (*anādimahāpīṭha*), in the great field of Meru (*merumahākṣetra*), in the house of the Kaulas (*kauligṛha*), O Kubjikā! HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ. O Śrī Kulacakreśvaranātha! HSKHPHREṂ. O Kubjikā! ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ. O Śrī Kulacakreśvarī! Svāhā! [To the one] of red color, four... Thānaraṅkhu. THHSRAUṂ. To the goddess Dambhakī, the lamp upon the rock, and to the great protector of the crossroads (*mahādhvākakṣatrapālāya*), svāhā! [To the one] with reddish-brown hair.

Rājakalāka: Oṃ hrūṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ, to Karaṅkeśvara and Śkṣmlvryīṃ Karaṅkeśvarī together with her Śakti, svāhā! Smoke-colored and blazing. Vaccharā Devī, in the west: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, namaḥ svāhā! Seated upon the letter Ai (aikārāsana). Utphullā.

On the bare ground (thaṇḍilī), there are five offerings (pañcabaliḥ): 1. **Vaṭuka**: *Śrī hrīṃ kulaputra vaṭukanāthāya svāhā*. 2. **Kṣetrapāla**: *Thhsrauṃ prastaradīpa dambhakīdevī mahādhvāka kṣetrapālāya svāhā*. 3. **Yoginī**: *Yāṃ yoginibhyo svāhā*. 4. **Cāmuṇḍā**: *Hskhphreṃ śrīsiddhicāmuṇḍāya svāhā*. 5. **Gaṇa**: *Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaḥ glauṃ kulagaṇeśvarāya svāhā*. [Then follow: *Gaurīputraṃ kumāraṃ tyādi*... [and so forth].

Trideva | Kṣetra | THSRAUṂ! To the Goddess Dambhakī and the Great Dhvākā Kṣetrapāla, svāhā! I bow to the Śadāsaka. Vaṭuka! ŚRĪṂ HRĪṂ! To the noble son Vaṭukanātha, svāhā! O Vaṭukanātha, in the illustrious seat! Gaṇa! GĀṂ GĪṂ GŪṂ GAḤ GLAUṂ! To the Lord of the Kula-gaṇas, svāhā! To Sindurasānda!
With *saguna*. [To] the *kalaśa*: *aiṃ (5) hskṣmlvryūṃ saṃpūrṇakalaśamūrtaye svāhā*. Śrī Svāhā! Lakṣmī Svāhā! For the liberation of Brahmā and the others!
Kumbha: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ svāhā. She is mounted upon a lotus and a corpse.
West: HSKMLVRYŪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Vīrādhipataye ŚKMLVRYĪṂ Gurumaṇḍalabhaṭṭārikāyai SVĀHĀ. The letter U.
Hskṣmlvrayū ānandaśaktibhairavānanda vīrādhipataye śkṣmlvryīṃ aṣṭāviṃśatikarmabhaṭṭārikāyai svāhā || Ṣaṭkaṃbā ||
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda Virādhipati, Śkṣmlvryīṃ! To the venerable Mother of the Root Abode of the Illustrious Western [Tradition], Svāhā! She is dark blue and red.
Tumbeśvarī. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, svāhā to the goddess Śrī Jayatumbeśvarī. Vadhukadyuti.

The Topknot (Śikhā): Aiṃ (5) Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ, svāhā to the Great Bhairava of the Free Will (Svacchanda) at the topknot! Kva-kvā-śaḥ kva-kvā-samī! O Mahākāra! Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ, svāhā to the Great Bhairava Mahākāra, who crushes all enemies! Mahākālaṃ ma!

Ugracaṇḍā || (5) Oṃ hrīṃ rājaprade hskhphreṃ ugracaṇḍī ripumardanī hūṃ phreṃ sadā rakṣa (2) tvāṃ māṃ juṃ sa mṛtyuhare svāhā || Mārkaṇḍeya, the destroyer of calamities. Ugracaṇḍī || (5) Oṃ hrīṃ rājaprade hskhphreṃ ugracaṇḍī ripumardanī hūṃ phreṃ sadā rakṣa (2) tvāṃ māṃ ju sa mṛtyuhare svāhā || The goddess who [slays] Madhu and Kaiṭabha...
Root mantra: Aiṃ (5) Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ svāhā. (108 times). Utphullā. Guhyakālī. Oṃ pheṃ siddhikāli hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ pheṃ namaḥ svāhā. Yā sāntakā.

KLĪṂ HRĪṂ SKLĪṂ SKLHRĪṂ! To the Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, whose essence is Caryānātha, at the Brahma-cakra in the great sacred seat (mahāpīṭha) of Oḍiyāna, the supreme power whose self is the Brahman—Śrī Svāhā! [To] Aindrī and Yaiva-sa. Thus, the *saṃpātāhuti* offering. Kārā-patana-māla-koviye.

The Root Mantra: (108) || One should recite this verse while offering oblations of clarified butter: Aiṃ! May Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, the Lord of the Gods (Indra), Agni, Kāla, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Yama, and Nāga; the hosts of planets, the earth, day, night, the yogas, and the lagnas; the eight Yoginīs beginning with Jala; Gaṇapati, Vaṭuka, Kṣetrapāla, and all others—may they all be peaceful and grant their desired fruits through this full oblation of clarified butter, Svāhā! Mounted upon the Prāṇa and Preta spirits, O Goddess who dwells in the thousand-petaled lotus!
Thus ends the full oblation of clarified butter.

Then follows the purification of the oblation vessel (*homapātra*), as previously described starting with the washing and so forth. Then follows the worship of the Guru. [The ritual] begins with the offering of water for the hands (*hastārgha*) and ends with the offering of flowers. Having donned garments, an upper cloth (*uttarīya*), ornaments, a crown, and a ring, the patron (*yajamāna*) should utter these words:
Adorned with all ornaments, including bracelets and rings.

The ritual of the *kalaśa* and so forth; the union of the three goddesses (*tridevayoginī*).
