Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to Kṣatrapāla! [This is] the gift of Dāteśaviya.
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to this Odyāna-pīṭha! [East]
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to the sacred seat of Jālandhara!
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to the sacred seat of Pūrṇagiri in the west.
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to the sacred seat of Kāmarūpa. [Direction: North.
The Vediyābali (4) and the Lokapālaṅuva (10). These are the outer offerings (bahirbali).

The offering of incense, two lamps, and the bali-oblation; the giving of the dakṣiṇā to the Ācārya; the recitation (vācana); the offering of the bali for the local deities (deśabali) and the ancestors (dukhāpikhā); the worship of the retinue (parivārapūjā). Then, the fulfillment of the gift (dānapūrṇā): one should cause the oblations (āhuti) to be performed—108 oblations with the nine-syllable mantra.
The *śruva* spoon is for the purpose of offering oblations; it is used for pouring the clarified butter, and likewise for the *āghāra* and *anvāghāra* libations.
The sacrificer, Dhaka, Jonaka, Taya; Śruk, Śruva, Ājāva, Vayadaṅga, Nābhi, Cūli, and Dikanta.

The Liturgy: Obeisance to the Śrī Saṃvarta-maṇḍala! To the one who possesses blossoming lotuses! To the one who possesses a thousand-petaled lotus! To the one who roars at the destruction of Time! Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ! [This is] the garland mantra; Svāhā Vauṣaṭ is given. Having prostrated, [perform] the ritual sipping of water (ācamana).
The offering of sandalwood and other such substances.
Then one should recite this verse:
I bow to the leader of the gods, the performer of a hundred sacrifices, who always dwells in the east;
he possesses a body with a complexion like gold,
stands upon the back of the king of serpents, has a thousand eyes, and is eternally praised and worshipped by the sages.
He is the eternal shatterer of the pride of the Dānavas and possesses valor that is a thorn to the six heretical systems.
Indeed, that fire which abides both externally and internally, richly developed with colors, born from the union of various seed-bodies, the Lord in the form of the fire of the hunchbacked one—
blazing intensely red, possessing all rays, faultless light, and ever-shaking.
I bow to the one who holds a sacrificial ladle (śruva) in his hand, who bestows boons, and whose power is the mantra-offering (bali).

This time is like a formidable, excellent rain-cloud; though the Lord, who protects the command of Śambhu, is exceedingly terrifying in appearance, he always remains intent on the welfare of others. He is the life-force that descends into the Dharma, having transcended the conduct of deliberating upon dharma and adharma.
Therefore, that god, the wielder of the staff who eternally removes the sustenance of worldly existence, is always to be saluted by me.
I bow to that Lord of the Gods, who possesses eternal glory, the guardian of the quarters worshipped by night-stalkers,
whose hand is raised with a flaming sword, who moves among the spirits of the dead,
who always destroys the Kali age in the sacrifice of battle, and who is as expansive as the eyes of Śrī Vīra.
O Lord of Sages, salutations to you who are merit itself, the remover of obstacles, and who are bowed to by Rātriñca and Raśa.
In the land of Śuddhavatī, in that most excellent great city,
may the Lord— ever peaceful, always dwelling within the great Makara, the ender of suffering, and the bearer of the noose— protect us;
he who is eternally adorned with strings of pearls and always embellished with white garments.
This god is Varuṇa with a vast countenance; eternal salutations to you two, O Vāsukī.
Victorious is the one who is the cause of breath for the embodied beings of the worlds,
who is beyond the wind, who is the life-force of gods, serpents, and humans, whose form is that of the living soul;
who, though formless, pervades all, who consists of swift movement, and whose limbs are of a golden hue.
To that Vāyu of divine form, with head bowed low, [I offer salutation]: "O Prāṇavāyu, obeisance to you!"

The lords of the yakṣas [worship] the King of Kings, the Lord of Wealth, who has tawny hands, whose garment is a choice horse, who dwells in the northeastern quarter, whose complexion is like molten gold, whose limbs are beautiful, and who is auspiciousness itself; he who is the friend of Śrī, adorned with abundant gold and divine jewels, and the master of grain.
Shall I bow to the lord of men, who is the master of the dissolution of gold?

Iśāna, the lord of the world, who is always embraced on the left by the Daughter of the Mountain; whose complexion and luster are like the king of mountains, white and radiant as the color of cow’s milk;
who has a white radiance, moves upon the lordly bull, and whose body is adorned with serpents.
I bow to that supreme Śiva, who removes fear and calamity and whose form is like the fire at the end of an aeon.

In the beginning, he was in the form of a fish; in the second, he had the body of a noble tortoise; in the third, he was the enemy of the Daityas, Nṛsiṃha, who crushed the strength of Bali like a fire of immeasurable power;
then Rāma, the destroyer of Rāvaṇa, the best of sons; and finally, the incarnation of pure consciousness for the protection of the virtuous.
This Mādhava, the incarnation of Śrī-Śrī-Kalki, renowned throughout the ten directions, is to be praised.
Performing the creation of the three worlds, the teacher of all people, the incarnation of Vedic mantras,

the instructor of various sciences, the bestower of auspiciousness upon the three realms, the eldest of the deities, the primordial Veda, the embodiment of mantra, the one perfected through the attainment of the complete syllables of the Krama-patha which are devoid of letters— [I bow to him].
I indeed bow to that god, the universal form, born from the lotus, possessing four faces and four arms.

For the gods and humans, he has bestowed a great deal of inauspiciousness, obstacles, and various afflictions; yet for his devotees, during the portion of the sacrifice, he grants all prosperity that produces auspiciousness.
[I bow to] Vighneśa, the elephant-faced one, who holds a boon-granting tusk and rests upon a rosary.
I bow to the hand marked with the *kuśa* grass, which possesses the fullness of a *laḍḍūka* fruit and is adorned by the strength of the arm.

This deity has the luster of gold and possesses two arms and two hands; holding a book in his left hand, he is Gīṣpati, the supreme and excellent preceptor of Indra and the other gods, the very embodiment of Brahmā.

Salutations to you, who have approached [the world] amidst various afflictions and planetary influences; who possess rays like the sun; who are eternally gentle; who are born as the bestower of boons; and who are held upon the crown of the head.

Bhairava is the sovereign lord of the fields, whose body is the entire universe; the creator of all, the protection, the cause of the self of protection, the most excellent teacher of all, and the eldest in the circle of Bhairavas.
He is bliss, the lord of the universe, multiplied by the nine rasas, possessing the six qualities, yet the Lord of the qualityless.
Beyond form, formless, accompanied by the hosts of ancestors, O Protector of the Kṣatriyas, protect me!

The Yoginīs, capable of assuming any form at will, endowed with all auspicious qualities, possessing the luster of molten gold, adorned with garlands of intoxicated skeletons, with blood trickling down their necks, and wearing red garments as upper cloths—
holding a sword, a noose, a skull-cup, and a trident, they are well-remembered and exceedingly gracious.
Bestowing the desired fruits upon devotees and practitioners, she is being praised as gracious.

You are the embodiment of the deities; you are filled with the waters of all the celestial rivers and holy fords, such as the Gaṅgā, along with jewels, medicinal herbs, fruits, flowers, an umbrella, and auspicious foliage.
You are the cause of the destruction of obstacles, the remover of the impurities of the Kali age, and the most excellent of all sacrifices.
I bow to him in the form of Kumbha, the auspicious vessel of Śiva and Śakti that purifies all impurities.
O Lord, the Sun [bestows] sovereignty; Mars, supreme majesty; Mercury, intelligence; Jupiter, dignity; Venus, auspiciousness on one's path;
Saturn, the destruction of enemies; Rahu, the loss of desired objects; and Ketu, the son of Simha, [brings about] calamity.
May you, who perform the slaying of Kaiṭabha, be well-disposed and grant your favor.
One should always hold within the center of the moon that which has the color of pure cow's milk, a conch shell, crystal, snow, or camphor, possessing a hundred rays of cool light in all directions;
in the right hand, it is the color of nectar, and in the left, it is a jewel-like vessel.
With his two hands, he displays the gestures of granting fearlessness and bestowing boons, out of devotion and compassion for the world.
With the *kalaśa* [vessel].
This one has been worshipped with oblations by the guardians of the celestial worlds, beginning with Brahmā, and has been bowed to and praised;
you alone, O Jambha, [know] the primordial God who is the conqueror of death—unto Him I go for refuge.
With both hands.
I bow to Siddhilakṣmī, who is mounted upon a lotus and a corpse, resembling crystal in hue, five-faced and three-eyed, enchanting the three worlds, her limbs draped in divine garments;

she carries in her left hands a skull-cup, a trident, a jar, the gesture of granting boons, a great noose, and a severed head, and is endowed with a bell, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a sword, the gesture of fearlessness, and an arrow.
The circle and the sector.
Fair-complexioned, with three eyes and five faces, seated upon a lion, he draws in [beings] while holding a noose, a hook, a bell, and a skull-cup;
he bears the Lord of Nagas and holds a vessel filled with sweetmeats, granting fearlessness and bestowing all things with his right hands.
Salutations to Herambanātha, who possesses beautiful arms and a captivating trident.
[The mantra] for the consumption of the cow: *gogrāsayā*.
Oṃ, salutations to the mother of the five products of the cow—she who is auspicious, benevolent, fragrant, pure, and captivating to the mind; she is the purifier for the destruction of sin.
The young girl.
You are Haṃsī, Pūrvādhikārī, Aruṇā, Tapanībhā, Kālarātrī,
Bhavānī, Tripurā, Kubjikā, Akṣā, Navakadhiyā, Siddhilakṣmī, Parā, Bhāsānā, and Parā; you are the mother of the three worlds, the Sovereign of the Lords of Kings.
I bow to the goddess Kumārī, who, though single in essence, possesses manifold forms, and who is the mother of the three worlds.
The powerful one; the one belonging to Viṣṇu.
Vaiṣṇavī is the illusory power (māyā) of Viṣṇu, the destroyer of the formidable fortresses of the Daityas;
she has limbs of a greenish-yellow hue and is seated upon Garuḍa.
Holding a conch, a discus, and a mace in her hands, adorned with four arms,
she is a great play of jewel-flames, embellished with various gems.
Always possessing green flowers and fragrance, she who eternally wears the color green has no fixed form of existence in heaven, among mortals, or in the netherworld.
O Aṭṭahāsa Mahākṣetra, dweller of the Kadamba tree,
who abides at the Pīṭha in the southwest, O Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you!
And the horse-sacrifice (*aśvamedha*). The six pillars, the attainment of mantra-perfection (*mantrasiddhi*), and so forth. She is blue and red, and so forth.
In her childhood state she is Mahāraudrī, and as a maiden she is fond of red;
she wears garments of red hue, and her body is as crimson as vermilion.
Four-armed, bearing a spear, a thread, and the auspicious vessel of accomplishment,
she is the supreme youthful power, riding upon an excellent peacock.
O Beloved, the goddess Raktapuṣparatā, who delights in blood, flesh, and fat,
is to be worshipped with *kola* fruit in the great field (*mahākṣetra*) where she dwells in the banyan tree.
O Kaumārī, who always resides on the southern seat, salutations to you!
There is no horse-sacrifice.
Adorned with the power of bliss, containing the essence of mantra,
the form of the Supreme Lord who is the cause for realizing all objects and the true nature of reality, and who effects the practice of the eightfold limbs.
I bow to Nāṭeśvara, who bestows success along with the power of action.
The offering of the *tuṣa-rājūya* sacrifice.

The Blessed Lady, dwelling in the center of the seat, seated upon a corpse, beautiful, with red limbs and eyes, holding a trident and a skull-bowl in her hands, the bestower of the essence of cyclic existence,
is always worshipped by Brahmā, Upendra, Surendra, Kinnaras, and men.
I constantly bow my head to that Goddess, the bestower of the attainment of desire and wealth,

who is surrounded by Brahmāṇī and others such as Jayā, who dwells in the sacred field (kṣetra), who is accompanied by [her attendants], the venerable Vīreśvarī, the Mistress of her own family, who is of equal flavor with the Absolute (samarasa), and who holds a trident and a rosary.

May Cakreśvarī protect you— she who, intoxicated and with a slightly clouded orb, pours forth a stream of nectar in the form of words of love, accompanied by drops of the finest wine and other delicacies.
The offering of the *laṃkhubali* at the site.
I perpetually salute Kṣetrapāla Tāmramālā, the essence of all the Kaulikas,
who holds in his hands a skull-topped staff, a sword, a supreme bell, and a *kādyā*.
[He saw] the beloved of the Lord of the Three Worlds standing at the door.
One who has been made a slave by the king.
Smoky in appearance with blazing eyes, his matted hair possesses the luster of lightning;
in one hand he holds a skull-cup and a sword, while in the other he wields a sharp trident and a discus;
he is delighted by the flesh of men and various kinds of corpses, and stands amidst a host of hungry ghosts.
I bow to Ucchiṣṭanātha, together with Mātaṅgī and Śrī, surrounded by his own retinue.

The offering for the goddess Vaccharādevī: "She who is dark-red," and so forth; "the blossoming water-lily," and so forth—these are for the offering. For Palīvālaga: "Brahmāṇī and the others"; "Brahmāṇī, the lotus-moon," and so forth. For Ugracaṇḍā: [the respective mantra].

On the eighth day, having been consecrated by the Blessed Ones such as Śrī Rudracaṇḍā and others, [the goddess] is adorned with the entire circle of the six Yoginīs, headed by Brahmā and others, beginning with Jayā;
on the ninth day and subsequent days, she is worshipped with flowers, sandalwood, incense, lamps, and all manner of offerings.
May that beloved and divine Bhagavatī Caṇḍikā protect you when the tenth lunar day has arrived.
Without having sprinkled [the water] around the fire.
I bow to her whose beautiful cheeks are illuminated by swinging golden earrings, whose face possesses the luster of a shining golden campaka flower, and who resembles the orb of the full moon;
she who has struck down her enemies with her mace and whose flickering tongue moves restlessly.
I remember her whose face was turned away from me, paralyzing my speech with her very glance.
By means of the three powers.

Red, white, and extremely black, possessing the threefold course of the river, the Goddess has three measures; having praised her own self, those who have attained [her] become established in the three aims of life, moving through various states.
Through youth, she becomes powerful and aged; she is the savior from existence, awakened by the three times.
May the mother Vetālī, who possesses a noble womb, who bestows victory, and who is the eternal worship that is a limb of Śiva, be victorious.
By Hanubhairava.
Homage be to Hanurudra and to the Lord of the Kalpa-heroes; homage to Bhairava, the most formidable, and to you, O celibate one! Homage be to you!
Not with a horse.
Salutations to you, the Lord of Dance, who sustains Nandin and Caṇḍī;
O bestower of perfection in dance, grant me good fortune.
On the fifth day, it was carried off by the hair.
Homage to you, O Mahāmāyā, who bears the name Vārāhī;
you are Kolāsyā, the Great Fierce One, who holds the adamantine snout.
By Siddheśvarī.
She has one face and three eyes, with the crescent moon as her crest-ornament;
she has four arms, O Great Goddess, and two hands joined in the añjali gesture.
Seated upon a throne of spirits, she is red in color and intensely radiant;
the Goddess possesses the luster of ten million full moons, blazing with her own great splendor.
Of all those members of the family.
Hymn to the Guru
Salutation to that illustrious Guru, by whom that state was revealed—the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which all that is moving and unmoving is pervaded. (1)
At the end of the stainless Śrīsaṃvarta, the power of bliss is placed in the sequential steps; Subhīmā is the emission according to the rule.
There is a tetrad situated in both Akula and Kula, another pentad, and a hexad.
Then there are four, another pentad, and again four—the sixteen-fold consecration of the Command.
Within the center of the divine eight forms are the syllables Ha, Sa, Kha, Pha, Ra, Ka, La, and Bindu, along with the Puṣpākhya and Mudrā gestures. (2)
The child, the youth, and the elder—the sequence of Vakradevī, who is a digit of Paramaśiva—and Śrīnātha, who is ever-renewed in Candrapurī; the essence is indeed the division of the couple.
There are three incarnations of the Siddhas, and in the first Kali age, his authority was established in Koṅkaṇa.
Their sons and disciples, numbering ninety-eight, were of the intellect of ninefold men. (3)
The lineage, the collection of clans, the complete sequence of steps, the sixteen rays ending with the Krama; these are indeed the remaining mandalas, the pure host of assemblies known as the Lords.
First is the emergence of the mandala, the entire Kula-krama beginning from eighteen.
The purification of the body, which effects the destruction of the impurities of the bound soul through the threefold sequence of ritual action, takes place in the fire of Śiva. (4)

Bow down to that most excellent Guru, the venerable Kujeśa Bhairava, by whom the ground of rest, the expansion, the experience, the conviction, and one's own authority have been unified in the center. (5)

Aiṃ! That power known as Bhaga, which possesses the threefold path, consists of three syllables and has three aspects; Aiṃ! In her [abode], the glorious Oḍiyāna, there is the excellent *kala* situated in the center, brilliantly radiant.
Hrīṃ! In that manifest abode called Jālandhara, in the southern corner indeed, [is she].
In the auspicious Pūrṇapīṭha on the left, he by whom the universe is filled with the fear of bound souls. (6)
Hsphreṁ: before that [is] Kāmarūpa, joined with Madanakalī, and the abode of all siddhas;
Hsoḥ: within the triangle, the entire host of yogas, adorned with the digit (kalā) of Supreme Śiva, has been placed.

In the center of that [earth] is the divine liṅga, which bestows supreme bliss; it is in the form of a bindu, in the form of the letter Kha, the syllable Klīṃ, and its essential nature is eternal bliss. Above that is the churning, divided into six modes. (7)
Glūṃ! For the enjoyment of knowledge, experience the stainless [reality] in that which is to be traversed at the three seats (pīṭha) on the forehead.
Aiṃ! Thus, the entire universe is pervaded by the power of Rudra, the mother of maintenance and dissolution, who is threefold.
Aiṃ! There resides the Goddess of gods, the independent one, the sustainer of the bliss consisting of both Akula and Kula.
Oṃ! She who has become the drop of the Guru’s command, who removes the fear of bound souls, and whose form is the divine current of the Siddhas. (8)

Hsauṃ! I bow to the one known as the illustrious Kubjikā, who is eternally moist, deeply red, the blessed sustainer of the bliss of heat, renowned for making the earth tremble, and whose excellent body is agitated by desire. (9)
The lineage follows the path of Meru; there, the deity is Anvaya. Oṃkāra is the seat of departure, and the Siddhas have been proclaimed by you therein. (10)
The Silent One, the Cave-Dweller, and the Kadamba Tree;
that which is frequented by the convention is called Ambā and Guhavāsinī.
The house is said to be Cāndrapura, the division is Manthānabhairava, and the lineage is the goddess Amarikā; one should arrange these according to the Vāmamārga. 12.
His lineage and spiritual connection are in Āra, while his sphere of authority is in Koṅkaṇa;
his birth was in the place of Brahmaśilā, and his established residence is in Śrīkāmarūpa.
Fame resides in the *ciñciṇī* tree, and success indeed in the *sāraka*; O Goddess of gods, I am pleased with him who knows the sequence of the *tilaka*. (14)

O auspicious lady, one should impart to a worthy disciple the placement (*nyāsa*), the seed-syllables (*kūṭa*), and the sequence (*krama*)— which grant success when worshipped— according to the division of the sixteen supports (*adhāra*).
All these are the three sūtras of Mahāmāyā.
Oṃ, salutations to you, O Great Illusion (Mahāmāyā), whose body is subtle, who are both supreme and non-supreme;
you who are solitary, the pure self, known as Nāda, and garlanded with Bindus. 16.
And when the bodiless one has arisen, she who sustains the universe, the eternal Mahākuṇḍalinī, is established in the midst of the Haṃsa. || 17 ||

She who dwells in the midst of the moon, sun, and fire; she who pervades the void, both supreme and non-supreme; she who abides in the form of the syllable Om; and she who bears the half-moon of the letter Ha.
Subtler than the hundredth part of a hair-tip, infinite, inexhaustible, and imperishable,
it rests upon the filament of the lotus, the support of the half-measure of the letter *Ha*.
O you who are called Sakalā, the Great Illusion, the Giver of Boons, worshipped by the world;
O you who abide in the midst of each and every night, piercing each and every vital point! 20.
O Goddess, the thirty-eight Kalās are located at the tip of the Brahma-channel;
they resemble streaks of lightning and have the coiled form of serpents.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva—
these five great pretas are stationed at the soles of his feet.
O Goddess, mother of the three worlds, salutations to you who are the embodiment of Śakti;
you reside between the Iḍā and Piṅgalā nerves, having the form of a lotus fiber.
The Goddess resides in the center of the Bindu; she is curved and possesses the luster of a half-moon, resembling a drop of frost, and hangs from the limit of the twelve.
Gaurī resides on the body of Umā; she possesses the splendor of the twelve suns.
She is the subtle state within the gross, known as Haṃsa, and she sustains the vital breath.
In the place called Lamba, the supreme goddess moves from south to north;
having emerged at the tip of the nose, she flows as a fine thread in the center.
O Hṛllekhā, you who abide in supreme bliss at the summit of the tāla, where the two bells of sound rub against each other, and who are endowed with the eight qualities. || 27 ||
In the gross and subtle, well-refined pair of sheaths of dharma and adharma;
in the state of effect, cause, and agency; in the triple void whose form is sound (nāda). || 28 ||
In the supreme, beyond the supreme, pure, eternal, and constant consciousness, the Goddess who bears all phonemes is established in the secret place. (29)
The Goddess who delivers the world, who follows the path of conventional reality, who is bodiless, highly fortunate, and the one who carries one across the ocean of saṃsāra. (30)
O Jayā, Vijayā, Ajitā, and Aparājitā; O Tumburu, you who abide in the midst of the seed-syllable, homage to you, the liberator from sin!
The Goddess who effects bondage and liberation is established at the end of the sixteen;
she is the Bhrāmaṇī, endowed with the trident of power (śakti-śūla) and accompanied by the great array (mahā-vyuha).
Bhramaṇī, Bhrāmaṇī, Gaurī, Māyā, Yantrapravāhinī, the goddess Svacchandabhairavī, and Saṃkrodhonmattabhairavī. (33)
The Rudras, who abide in the form of fifty phonemes, have been proclaimed by you:
O Śivā, obeisance to Kāpālinī, who is Ruru in the [letter] called Amṛta and Caṇḍa.
O Ruruṃkṣaṇī, O Mahāmāyā, salutations to you, Jñānabhairavī!
O you with formidable fangs, whose tongue is like lightning, whose eyes are like stars, and whose face is terrifying!
I bow to you, O Goddess of the lords of gods, O Aghorā of terrible form!
O Jvālāmukhī, O Vegeśvarī, O Goddess Umā; salutations to you! (36)
And the Yoginī Śriyādevī, Gaurī, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, the goddess Haṃsavāgīśvarī, Gomukhī, and Śaktimālinī. (37)
Koṣṭhāṅgī, Subhagādevī, Durgā, Kātyāyanī, as well as Nityaklinnā, Raktā, and another known as Ekākṣarā. || 38 ||
You are Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, and Vaiṣṇavī;
you are Vārāhī, Māhendrī, and Cāmuṇḍā with your terrifying countenance. (39)
O Goddess of gods, you are indeed the Mistress of Yoga, endowed with the eight powers (kuśaktis):
Aindrī, Āgneyī, Yāmyā, Nairṛtī, and Vāruṇī. || 40 ||
Vāyavyā, Kauverī, and Aiśānī are proclaimed; likewise Prayāgā, Varuṇākola, Aṭṭahāsā, and Jayantikā. (41)
Caritra, Ekāmrakā, and Devīkoṭa—thus you are eightfold;
likewise Kālī, Umādevī, and Devadūtī—salutations to you! (42)
O Bhadrakālī, the Great Goddess; you are Cāmuṇḍā, the source of terror.
O you who are both great and subtle, O Great Peaceful One, salutations to you whose form is Śakti.
At the end of the word "svāhā" [in the mantra] "bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ," O Goddess, show compassion toward me;
O Mahāmāyā, I who seek knowledge desire to know this. (44)
Those men who recite this hymn at the three junctions of the day obtain their desired wishes and become beloved by women. (45)
Thus ends the hymn to Mahāmāyā on the theme of the essential identity of Śiva and Śakti. (8)
By means of the field.

Tawny-eyed, with red hair, wearing a network of tinkling bells that sound "kiṇi kiṇi," with fangs in his mouth and a cruel disposition, he is the remover of all poisons, holding a vessel in his hand and uttering a roar—
a clearly manifest lion’s roar sounding "ra-ra-ra-ra," the supreme *varvara*, the reality of space.
I bow to Kṣetrapāla, the lord of spirits and ghosts, who removes all fears. || 46 ||
Clad in red garments, with a mass of matted hair blazing tawny,
holding a staff upon which a row of flames flickers, most fierce,
and as fair as the peak of Mount Meru at sunrise.
I bow to Vaṭukanātha, the son of Gaurī. || 47 ||
To Vaṭuka; to Gaṇa.
To the destroyer of the suffering of weariness, who has stilled the fear of cyclic existence, whose body is the end of all obstacles;
to the one with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), who moves through the sky, who bestows all accomplishments and all aims—*gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ*.
*Oṃ glūṃ*, you who are the mudrā known as the Elephant, who move with the wind, and who have a single tusk on the vehicle of the rat.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hāṃ gāṃ! O Gaṇeśa, O two-faced Gaṇa, O Lord of Obstacles, salutations to you! || 48 ||
The ninefold Māyā.

The letter *Ū* is his dancing foot; *Ha*, *Sa*, *Kṣa*, *Ma*, *La*, and *Bha* are his arms; he possesses the fire-linga; he is marked by the wind and the tiger-skin; the crescent moon, the bindu, and the nāda are joined above;
he is the downward-flowing stream of the Gaṅgā; he is the straight, supreme digit; Bhairava, whose form is the mantra.
May the god Navātman, the most excellent teacher of all, Bhairava Śrīkujeśa, [grant his grace]. || 49 ||
The [mantras] beginning with *brahmāṇyā* and so forth.
Brahmāṇī, with a face as gentle as the lotus and the moon; Māheśvarī, who by her playful grace [subdues all]; Kaumārī, who destroys the pride of her enemies; Vaiṣṇavī, whose weapon is the discus;
Vārāhī, whose mouth utters a most terrible "gha-gha" sound like a thundercloud; and Aindrī, whose weapon is the thunderbolt.
May Cāmuṇḍā, Gaṇanātha, Bhairava, the Gaṇas, and the Mothers protect me! || 50 ||
Seated in the center upon the triple throne, their faces radiant with the joy of intoxication, they shine brilliantly within the vajra-lotus;
on the eight petals of Brahmāṇī and the others, in the directions of the vowels and the syllable *praṇava*, and in the sacred fields (*kṣetra*) such as Śrī-Prayāga;
joined with the twenty-eight corners, they flash forth upon the vajra-peaks marked by *ca*, *sa*, *ṣa*, *sa*, *ha*, *sa*, *kha*, and *kha*.
May these thirty-two syllables—consisting of three groups of twenty-eight, accompanied by the sequential steps—protect [us]. (51)
By means of action.

Devoted to the Bhairava of the letter *la* and the flesh (*piśita*), they grant the sword, the accomplishment of mantras, entry into another’s body, movement through the air, or the eye; the paralysis of enemies, victory over hostile forces, the immobilization of all spells, long life, poetic talent, the treasure, the elixir, the pill, the sandals, and every supernatural power—fulfilling every desire. (21)
By means of the western [direction].

Dark-hued and reddish, with three eyes, bent by the weight of her breasts, walking with the gait of an elephant in rut, with lips like the *bimba* fruit, beautiful eyes, and broad hips adorned with a girdle resplendent with jewels;
she is clothed in divine garments, adorned with excellent flowers, and possesses a mass of hair that is dark and curly.
May she known as Sāmeśrī Kubjikā bestow the unfailing, divine stream of the swift flow of gnosis. 53.
I bow to the beautiful three-eyed goddess, radiant as the bandhūka flower, seated upon a lion-throne, the destroyer of all enemies here, adorned with white garments,
possessing eighteen lotus-like hands that are stainless and bestow the fruits of one's desires.
I salute her, the crusher of the demon Mahiṣa; I bow to Tumburu’s Goddess. 54.
To Tumbesvarī.
The topknot.

Where is space? Where is the wind? Where is fire? Where are the waters? Where is the earth? Where is Brahmā? Where is Janārdana? Where is that world? Where is the moon? And where are the gods and the asuras?

Victorious is the Lord Mahābhairava, the master of the yoga of glorious accomplishment, who delights in the dance of the actress that is the end of the aeon, and who is the hero of the drama of divine play. || 55 ||
By Mahākālī.
Mahākāla, the greatly fierce one, with the luster of black collyrium,
possessing a massive form and a huge body, holding a skull-cup and a vessel, wielding a sword and a shield, the three-eyed deity of blazing radiance.
Salutations to you, Mahākāla, the one who brings about the destruction of enemies.
To Ugracaṇḍā.
Mārkaṇḍeya, a knower of Brahman who was like unto Brahmā himself, performed an incarnation to bestow grace upon those struck down by calamity;
he possessed the power of the essence of hymns that gladdened the gods who rejoiced at the destruction of the Daityas.
May this [song] of the goddess Caṇḍikā lead to your welfare. || 58 ||
The Ugracaṇḍī [Tantra].

The Goddess who is the destroyer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, who is the slayer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, who is the intoxicating one who brought about the destruction of the demon Mahiṣa, who takes refuge in Raktabīja;
she who is the crusher of the Daityas Śumbha and Niśumbha, and who is the refuge of the God of gods.
May that goddess Caṇḍī protect me with her right arms; may Jayā protect me. || 59 ||
By the root.
Seated upon the pericarp of a full-blown lotus is the supreme Śrī Siddhilakṣmī,
white as camphor, crystal, and the moon; she is the destroyer of all bonds and the burner of the mire of suffering in the ocean of saṃsāra, remaining forever unshakable.
May she who possesses glorious five lotus-faces, ten arms, and stands upon a corpse protect us. || 60 ||
May the Goddess, who consists of the supreme and the non-supreme, who is the mother of all mantras and possesses incomparable power, grant me success;
I bow to her, the unborn one, the supreme awakening beyond all movement.
I worship here the Goddess Siddhilakṣmī, who has pierced the hearts of the gods with her arrows.
Fulfiller of hopes, remover of sins, dispeller of the flood of the world’s suffering, deliverer from afflictions, slayer of enemies, eternal remover of the delusion of saṃsāra;
you who bring about the highest good, O Cause, Sovereign, and Supreme Life-force that never wavers!
Salutations to you, Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, who is immediately and exceedingly beloved, and who bestows the fruits [of one's desires]. || 62 ||
Mounted upon a mature corpse, endowed with ten arms, five faces, and three eyes,
she dwells within the sovereign heart-lotus after piercing the Brahma-knot;
she resides in the *piṇḍa* state, radiant as a drop (*bindu*), her body composed of nectar, the source of both the creation and liberation of the universe.
I bow to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, who bestows desired fruits and assumes a massive form.

I bow to Siddhilakṣmī, who is mounted upon a lotus and a corpse, resembling crystal in luster, five-faced and three-eyed, enchanting the three worlds, her body draped in divine garments; she carries in her left hands a skull-cup, a trident, a jar, the gesture of granting boons, a great noose, and a severed head, while holding a bell, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a sword, the gesture of fearlessness, and an arrow.
O Śrī Lakṣmī, whose union with each body is the lotus of supreme bliss;
O Bhavā, the crest-jewel among the gems of women; O Mahālakṣmī, the embodiment of great auspiciousness;
you who possess breasts that are the seat of power, and who are the binding ornament of the three worlds.
Śrī Kālikā Yoginī, who holds a digit of the moon sent forth [from her brow], possesses the essence of the qualities. 65.

The Goddess, whose lotus feet are bowed to with devotion by gods, asuras, and others; whose splendor shines like the stainless moon, the seed within all illusions; she who makes the essence of worldly existence fruitful through devotion to her lotus feet.
I bow to the bestower of boons, Jaya Siddhilakṣmī. || 66 ||
She who always dwells in the Karavīra cremation ground for the benefit of humble beings, mounted upon the Rudra of the departed spirits,
white as the moon and snow, five-faced, and indeed unfailing— Amogha.
May this Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, whose arms are auspicious, bestow prosperity. || 67 ||
Aiṁ! Victorious is she who arises from the Vākya-mantra, the bestower of all fulfilled desires, the supreme Śivā who destroys all suffering for those fallen into the ocean of worldly existence;
held by the illustrious Śarva within the lotus-mandala, she bestows the perfection of bliss.
The remainder consists of Śrī, Karuṇā, Pracetasī, Vimalā, Śrīsiddhi, Lakṣmī, and Parā.

Mālinī, consisting of the lineage of the seed-syllable of Māyā, composed of the Kulāmāyā, is the deluding Great Goddess of the Mothers; she possesses the luster of a string of pearls within the Jewel-lineage (Maṇikula),
and she is the bestower of the realization of Māyā, the pride of the wise, and the manifestation of the supreme yoga of the Heart.
By her grace, she bestows the fulfillment of all desires upon one who is devoted to the propitiation of mantras.

The glorious one, radiant as the full moon, pure, bestowing fortune, desire, and peace, the soul of the universe, the sole support of all, the mother of the world, whose nature is the awakening from the states of waking and so forth;
she sprinkles the three worlds with the nectar-water of her compassion.
From time, death, the five elements, and dissolution, the supreme Śrī Siddhilakṣmī is victorious.

From the syllable *kṣauṃ*, she who destroys the flood of misfortunes has caused my task— which was increased by anxiety over wealth— to be accomplished; she, who possesses various forms of knowledge and removes that born of ignorance,
is the book itself, endowed with consciousness through the grace of Śrī, the supreme self whose nature is wisdom.
May the Blessed Goddess, the supreme and most secret Śrīsiddhi, who is eternal, protect me always. || 71 ||

The Supreme [Energy], whose nature is Sound (nāda), emits the syllable *kroṃ* through the hands, eyes, and organs of the Creator of Saṃsāra; she is endowed with the crescent moon in the sky and with the crest-tuft (*śikhā*).
She is eternal, devoid of objects, partless, the bestower of boons, and neither existence nor non-existence.
Victorious is Mātṛkā, the mistress of mantras and sovereign of qualities such as omniscience. 72.
Mounted upon Rudra, the mother of the supreme and the non-supreme, Śrī Siddhilakṣmī is the supreme goddess,
possessing manifold lunar splendors, the illuminator of light, the bestower of perfection and awakening;
she bears weapons of beauty, is endowed with exquisite ornaments, divine, and the soul of the universe.
I remember this Blessed Lady, composed of auspicious compassion, whom I have served. 73.

From the secret center up to the aperture of Brahmā, the sovereign of the abode of Kula manifests her body, enriched with the seeds of the garland of threads—the syllables of the garland-mantra—complete with weapons and limbs.
Having repeatedly become the essence upon the ground of essence, she rests eternally in the peace of the thirty-six [tattvas] through the digit of equanimity.
May that Queen of Vidyās, the Goddess of Accomplishment, flash forth for you so that you may attain the supreme state. (74)
She whose radiance is like ten million moons, blazing with rays that agitate the three worlds;
she whose power was restrained even by Rudra, who pervades the abode of the universe with her majesty;
she who effects the maintenance, creation, and destruction of worldly existence, and who blazes with fierce splendor.
I worship you, Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, whose face is as pure as three eyes. 75.
The secret Kali.
That radiant form which arises from the cavity of the fire of dissolution, situated within the midst of the three paths of the moon, sun, and fire—
let that state, known as the object of the mind, be perceived as dissolved.
She is the essential nature of the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
Consisting of gnosis, encompassing all that is to be, distinct from all phenomena, ever delighted by bliss, and eternally absorbed in the ultimate reality—
she whose form is fashioned within the channels and digits is the nature of mantra.
It consists of seventeen syllables and is characterized by the *khalu* and *chidra* meters. || 77 ||
The supreme hundred-syllable Vidyā, the fierce one who performs the rites of the Kula, whose power is intent upon the three worlds, and who is perfected within the assembly of the Kula;
she who is indeed one yet possesses manifold movements, is to be worshipped by the best of Cakras.
O best of perfected ones, worshipped by Bhairava through association with the virtuous. || 78 ||
O Kālī, you who carry the flow of waves of time divided into its parts;
you whose abode is the Śrīcakra, divided into nine divisions;
you who are the Full Moon, endowed with the digit of the moon, belonging to the Kula, and having the form of the sun.
The supreme accomplishment of consciousness is well-established in the Fire family.
Having attained the state of a sky-farer, she is the supreme moon; she is described as the knower of the great meaning of mantra through the sequence of the wheels (cakras),
devoted to the perfection of association with the virtuous, and the bestower of Kula-siddhi.
I bow to Kālī, whose supreme state is cultivated through her own intrinsic nature.
She who resides in Caṇḍā, in Bhūtabhinnā, in Ravi, Śaśi, and Dahana, in Gotracaṇḍā, and in Rudra;
who is established in the heart, the navel, the throat-cakra, the cavity of the three fires, and at the end of the twelve;
she who performs creation, maintenance, and dissolution; who is joined with Akula and Kula; and who sustains all defects—[to her I bow].
I eternally bow to Kālī, who dwells in the supreme state and whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss.
Belonging to Tripurasundarī.

Bearing the splendor of Indra’s very bow in the middle of her forehead, O Gauri, you possess the beauty of the sun; by means of the *sauṃ*, *klīṃ*, and *kānti* mantras, bring everything under your control through your essential nature.
This very Tripurā, the light within the heart, ever burning like the sun, consisting of both light and speech, may she suddenly sever our sin with her three steps.
Māyā, Kuṇḍalinī, Kriyā, Madhumatī, Kālī, Kalā, Mālinī, Mātaṅgī, Vijayā, Jayā, Bhagavatī, Devī, Śivā,
Śāmbhavī, Śakti, the beloved of Śaṃkara, Trinayanī, Vāgvādinī, and Bhairavī.
Hrīṃ! You are Kālī, the Mother Tripurā, who consists of both the supreme and the non-supreme, and you are Kumārī. || 83 ||
The root mantra is the Pratyāṅgirā.
Salutations to you, O Goddess of the gods, Siddhilakṣmī of great majesty;
O Great Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, Rājalakṣmī, salutations be to you! (84)
She is the Yoginī whose form is accomplishment, whose nature consists of compassion; she possesses manifold forms and resides within the midst of the eight Mātṛkās. (85)
The Goddess, the Sovereign Mother of the World, withdraws the universe in an instant;
she is the Goddess who sustains the world and brings joy to the universe. || 86 ||
The Goddess, the mother of the three worlds, resides in the center of the fire-cakra;
it has six corners, eight petals, and is endowed with four gates.
Siddhi is Lakṣmī, the Great Sovereigness, whose form is a diamond cage;
she resembles snow, the kunda flower, and the moon, and is like pure crystal.
The goddess Nibhā was entirely white, her mind blazing with splendor;
she was adorned with a mass of matted hair and the moon, and her locks were dark and curly.
The three-eyed image is white, possessing ten staff-like arms;
she holds a khaṭvāṅga, a sword, and a trident in her left hands, and a boon-granting gesture, a bell, and [a noose] in her right hands.
In the Muṇḍavāmaka [mandala], she holds a skull-bowl, a trident, and a noose, and displays the gesture of fearlessness;
she is endowed with all ornaments and adorned with gold, jewels, and the like. (91)
Clad in white garments, with a mind delighted by wine, she is mounted upon the shoulder of Rudra; Rudra is like crystal in appearance.
He has one face and three eyes, and his crest is adorned with the crescent moon.
O Great Goddess, he has four arms, with two hands joined in the añjali gesture. || 93 ||
Seated upon a corpse-throne, she is red in color and exceedingly radiant;
the Goddess possesses the luster of ten million full moons and the brilliance of the blazing sun. 94.
The goddess assumes various forms, beautifully adorned with diverse weapons;
she has many faces, many arms, and many feet, and possesses great strength.
The Great Sovereign is of universal form, an incarnation in the form of Lakṣmī;
the Goddess resembles a wish-fulfilling gem, bestowing the fruits of desired objects upon those who think of her. 96.
*Namaḥ*, *svāhā*, *vauṣaṭ*, *hūṃ*, and *vaṣaṭ*—these mantras, O Great Goddess, are the incarnations of the form of mantra. (97)
The Goddess resides in the *ādhāra*, her form coiled like a serpent;
she is the power (*śakti*) who encircles like a snake, moving through that which is inaccessible to the scriptures.
By practicing very gradually, she pierces the door of the universe;
she is the bestower of the great supernatural powers such as atomization (aṇimā) and the granting of all perfections. 99.
Consisting of five elements and joined with the physical body, she bestows royal fortune;
the Goddess, the Supreme Sovereign, increases that fortune by means of the lamp. 100.
O Maheśānī, the gross forms consist of two hundred and ninety [syllables] and so forth;
in the seventeen [syllable-mantras], there are nine, and in the three-syllabled one, fifty-seven.
"O Great Goddess, salutations to you who possess the single syllable and abide in a subtle form!
O Great Goddess, these are the mantras, O Maheśvarī, the Mother of Mantras. (102)
Freed from all sins, his life and health shall increase;
endowed with fortune, he shall become illustrious like a lordly elephant intoxicated with rut.
A single bath at the sacred ford extending as far as the seven seas shall suffice;
by remembering it but once, the mass of their sins will be consumed like a heap of straw. (104)
Having slain this entire world, he is honored by those who know Brahman;
even so is the slayer of a mother, the slayer of a father, the slayer of a Brahmin, and likewise the slayer of an embryo. (105)

Whoever, with a single-minded and concentrated focus, should recite this hymn at the three junctions of the day, [the sins] such as "may it perish" and so forth shall be destroyed; and having remembered [it] once, one should worship. || 106 ||
One is released from bondage and from sins; the shattering of shackles, as well as confinement and mechanical devices, are always paralyzed and liberated. (107)
In a forest that is uneven and terrible, fraught with the danger of lions and tigers;
in a rugged thicket, or amidst fire, or in the fear of spirits and epilepsy.
By means of which one destroys [the poison] through mechanical devices, mantras, and powders—even by a Kulika, when the destruction of the fanged one's venom is possible. (109)
It is the destroyer of spirits, epilepsy, and those belonging to the class of *pakṣa*, as well as of *preta*s and the like;
it destroys even quartan fevers and other ailments through mere remembrance.
And his goals are always accomplished beyond thought;
by her command, she is the pacifier of misfortune and the crusher of suffering and poverty. 111.
Renowned as Lakṣmīśvarī, she brings about manifold enjoyments;
she is Mahālakṣmī, the Great Overpowering One, the bestower of all auspicious fortune. (112)
Her consciousness was intoxicated with the bliss of wine, her eyes were greatly rolling;
her self had become one with bliss, and she manifested the form of the universe.
Brāhmī, Raudrī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, and Ghonaghorakā.
Māhendrī, Carccikā, and Caṇḍikā are indeed the eight Yoginīs. || 114 ||
One should worship the eight goddesses of great accomplishment, who abide in the midst of the accomplished yoginīs, in their various forms with perfumes, garlands, flowers, and other offerings. 115.
One should offer incense combined with camphor and musk;
when she is propitiated, the entire world and even the three realms are worshipped. || 116 ||
One should pierce elephants, horses, buffaloes, goats, and cows;
by this *pratyaṅgirā*, the wise king shall always conquer everything. || 117 ||
What need is there for much speaking here? All things will be accomplished without even being thought of;
for the Goddess, when remembered, is the constant destroyer of suffering and poverty. 118.
Salutations to you, O Great Goddess; salutations to you, whose form is the universe. Salutations to you, Mother of the worlds; salutations to you, Siddhilakṣmī. || 119 ||
Thus ends the hymn to the Illustrious Siddhilakṣmī-Pratyaṅgirā.
By the root.
You are the supreme Kālī, you alone are Siddhilakṣmī; you are the supreme Caṇḍī, you alone are Ugracaṇḍī.
You are the supreme Queen, the Sovereign of the Kings of Kings.
May he who has destroyed all enemies grant all spiritual accomplishments. || 120 ||
By the root.
I speak of no other, I do not gather [anything else], I do not think of another,
I do not remember another, I do not worship another, nor do I take refuge in another; O Honored Lord, I have abandoned everything for Your lotus feet.
O Mother, out of compassion for my own welfare, grant me spiritual accomplishment. || 121 ||
The mantra follows your root [mantra].
Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Caṇḍakāpālinī! Oṃ, homage to Siddhipadmā!
Śrī Jayadratha said:
I bow my head to the Goddess, the Yoginī of all-encompassing accomplishment, by whose arising grace the supreme, innate power emerges. (1)
Therefore, I constantly bow with devotion to Siddhimātṛ, from the radiance of whose feet the supreme expansion arises. (2)
Salutations again and again to Bhavānī, who removes the torment of worldly existence for those seeking refuge; salutations to her who is gladdened by eternally arising bliss. (3)
You abide as the sovereign leader within the entire wheel of families;
having bowed to you, O Blessed One, we praise the mantra Caṇḍakāpālinī. (4)
Having recollected that Goddess through these nine ever-fresh descriptions and by means of the nine syllables, we praise her, the Blessed One, who sustains the vast, throbbing universe. (5)
Since the supreme female ascetic (paramahaṃsinī), who bestows the mass of intense bliss, is the giver of the path to liberation, O Goddess, this entire world is your very essence. (6)
Salutations to the Blessed One, who wears a garland of fire for quenching the heavy afflictions of calamities, and who shatters misfortune, ill omen, and all defilements. (7)
O Goddess, we praise you—the one who enables crossing the ocean of all calamities, the refuge for the three worlds, and the pacifier of enemies everywhere, both here and in the hereafter. (8)
Come, come, O bestower of boons, O laughing goddess, again and again!
Leap, leap, O Mother of the World, you who grant all desires! (9)
You alone are full of flesh, blood, entrails, and fat; you are the one who, both within and without, has smeared all enemies with the oil of Time. 10.
Therefore, O Ānandā, crush, crush those enemies who are arrogant with great ego;
devour, devour them, O Mahādevī, O Maheśvarī! 11.
Pierce, pierce again and again the enemy of desire with the trident;
strike him and cut him in two with the stainless, radiant sword! 12.
Therefore, O Viccā, who possesses the form of Kuṇḍalinī and shines with the syllable *mat*, strive so that you may fulfill all my heart's desires. (13)
For you indeed, O compassionate Goddess, who possesses a most formidable form, are the protector of all mantras and are praised by all the foremost of the gods. (14)
O Goddess, who are affectionate toward those who bow before you, look upon us!
O Mahākālī, salutations to you; O destroyer of Time (Kāla), salutations! 15.
"O Supreme Goddess, be gracious and drive away my enemies from my testicles—that one who brings even the daughters of gods and asuras to the state of being afflicted by passion. (16)

O Māyā-Mahālakṣmī, known as the fourfold digit (catuṣkalā), quickly dispel the blinding darkness of delusion and illuminate the supreme heart-lotus, which is more radiant than the moons of consciousness and whose nature pervades the three worlds. 17.

Having meditated upon the Blessed Lady who bestows desired fruits during meditation, whoever worships you— who have been perfected through worship— with a mind purified by devotion and prostration according to their desire,
shall daily bring about all prosperity and grant it with a heart full of compassion.
I bow to you, the Reality, who is ever-beneficent, who brings about the awakening of the three worlds, and who is ever-arisen.
Whoever recites this hymn composed by Śrī Jayadratha attains all perfections through the grace of the Blessed Lady. (19)
From grass, from a leaf, from a stone, from a bulbous root, from a wall, from water, or from dry land—rise up, rise up and grant me protection; O Lord, there is no other refuge for me. (20)
Thus ends the hymn for the increase of the mantra of Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, composed by the illustrious Jayadratha.
By means of the root of your illusion.
Oṃ, homage to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī!
Aiṁ! Salutations to you, O Great Illusion, who transcends the body and is stainless;
O Pratyaṅgirā, Mother of the World, O Royal Fortune, salutations to you! (1)
The Great White One has a body of color and sets in motion the desires of the practitioner;
she whose body is the syllable is the Great Expansion, arisen from the great siddhi. (2)
That Goddess, who abides as one's own body, is remembered as the bestower of grace upon practitioners;
having pierced through Mahākuṇḍalinī, she pierces the thousand-petaled lotus. (3)
Situated between the iḍā and piṅgalā, she is composed of vital air, moves through the sky, has the form of a lotus fiber, and travels within the center of the suṣumnā. (4)
At the end of sound, she is established in sound; she transcends sound and is stainless.
She dwells in the subtle and the gross, in the most subtle, with an inconceivable form beyond all thought. (5)
O Supreme Śiva, who abides beyond the end of the highest of the high, who is merged in Brahman, whose form and conduct are inconceivable, and who bestows the fruit of inconceivable goals! (6)
The Mother of the Universe dwells alone in Kanavīra;
she is the eternal bestower of the Great Tremor and the performer of the Great Assembly. (7)
The Goddess who resides in the center of the *bindu* is Kuṭilārddhā, known as Candrikā;
she is the Goddess of dissolution at the *dvādaśānta*, dwelling in the sixteen supports. (8)
Intermingled with cause and effect, consisting of consciousness, and situated within the channels, she is established in nine ways in the great wheel at the root of power. (9)
The supreme goddess is bodiless, yet she exists within the body in the form of the vital breath;
her nature is like the flow of nectar, and her supreme form is the syllable Om.
Resembling a flash of lightning, fair-complexioned, and free from both existence and non-existence;
she dwells eternally within the lotus of one's own heart, the Supreme Goddess whose form is peace. 11.
Consisting of the nature of sattva, rajas, and tamas, you are threefold in essence;
O Goddess, you alone are the giver of life to all beings.
You alone create the universe, abiding in manifold ways through your divine play;
you are Mālinī, the supreme goddess, the eternal consort of the cremation ground.
O Cakrasundarī, who pierces the wheel at the heart-center and the wheel of the navel, who is pervaded by the divine through the obstruction of the gateway of the *bindu*—salutations to you! (14)
Resembling ten million suns, as pure as ten million moons, possessing the loveliness of ten million Cupids, and having a form equal to ten million universes. || 15 ||
O you who are without space, without appearance, without stain, and without form;
O Great Illusion known as Sakala, giver of boons, worshipped by the gods! 16.

The letter *kha* and the letter *pha* reside in fire (*vahnistha*), beautiful with the letter *e* between them; O Śivā, you consist of the five syllable-clusters (*pañcapiṇḍa*) within the groups of letters beginning with *ma*.

In the supreme doctrine, she who is of the form of a hut like a serpent, whose nature is the power of sound (nāda-śakti), is eternally situated in the wheel of the point (bindu-cakra) and has Jālandhara as her essential form. 18.
She resides in Turya and Vaituryya-pīṭha, established in Pūrṇa-pīṭha; she dwells in Kāmā, transcends all parts (kalās), and exists as Bhaga in the source of Kāmākhya.
In Śivā, who flows through the central channel with the swelling of the *brahmagranthi*, who is all-pervading, subtle, and the great festival of eternal bliss; (20)
O Mistress of Mantras, O Knower of Mantras, O Vidyā who dwells at the end of the [nine] vowels, O You who abide in the center of the five seats, O Mistress of Meru, O Śarvarī! 21.
She is both Khecarī and Bhūcarī, the carrier of the three powers;
she arises from the fire at the end of time and is the destroyer of even the Destroyer of Time.
Connected with the sequence of Kālikā, she is Kālī in the twelfth maṇḍala;
that goddess is the burner of the three worlds, and she is the thirteenth form.
In the Great Sequence (Mahākrama), which is called the Inexplicable (Anākhyā) and consists of creation, maintenance, and withdrawal,
there is Guhyakālī, known as Radiance (Bhāsā), and Nirvāṇeśī, the Supreme Sovereign.
Jhaṃkāriṇī, Bhairavī, Svarṇakoṭeśvarī, Śivā, Rājarājeśvarī, Caṇḍā, Aghoreśī, and Niśeśvarī. || 25 ||
Sundarī, Tripurā, Padmā, Tārā, Pūrṇeśvarī,
Jayā, Krameśī, Kubjikā, and Ambikā reside in the center of the Krama-maṇḍala.
Through the distinction between the elder and the young, Ugracaṇḍikā is the hunchbacked-eyed one;
she is Brahmāṇī, Raudrī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, and the long-nosed one.
One should worship Vajriṇī, Carccikā, and Lakṣmī as the divine Mothers;
[and likewise] Aśitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodhīśa, and the one known as Martta.
Kapālī, the one known as Bhīṣaṇī, and Saṃhāra as the eighth—these bestow prosperity and accomplishment upon devotees and practitioners. (29)
The great goddess Siddhilakṣmī has been proclaimed by Bhairava;
she is the destroyer of practitioners who harbor hatred and the shatterer of all their ritual actions. (30)
Homage to you, O Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, who acts as the reversal [of all evils];
you swallow Time and the rest, as well as all grahas, bhūtas, and those beginning with ḍākinīs.

I bow to the Goddess Kālasaṅkarṣaṇī, who protects the practitioner; I bow to the Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, who bestows auspiciousness, who protects the world with ease, and who grants the accomplishment of inconceivable goals.

I bow to the Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, who bestows the attainment of sovereignty, who is worthy of protection, who is affectionate toward her devotees, for the sake of accomplishing inconceivable goals. 33.
I pay homage to Pratyaṅgirā, who crushes all enemies, destroys misfortune and affliction, is the very embodiment of the fortune of accomplishment, and bestows victory. (34)
I bow to Pratyaṅgirā, the boat for crossing the ocean of calamities, the supreme bestower of nirvāṇa, the goddess who grants the fortune of success and victory. (35)
I bow to Pratyaṅgirā, who bestows sovereignty, wealth, and prosperity; who grants liberation, destroys suffering, is the fortune of success, and bestows victory. (36)
I pay homage to Pratyaṅgirā, who pacifies wicked enemies, destroys great diseases, is the very embodiment of the fortune of accomplishment, and bestows victory.
I bow to Pratyangirā, who pacifies the evils of the Kali age and bad dreams, who destroys great portents, who is the very fortune of spiritual accomplishment, and who bestows victory.
I bow to Pratyaṅgirā, the bestower of inconceivable success, the sustainer who grants the fruits of desired objects, the Fortune of Siddhi who bestows victory. (39)
I bow to Pratyaṅgirā, who pacifies royal calamities, who destroys death and flight [of enemies], who is the very fortune of success, and who bestows victory. 40.
I bow to Pratyaṅgirā, the mother of kings, the royal fortune who bestows the fruits desired by kings; I pay homage to Siddhilakṣmī. || 41 ||
The Great Vidyā Siddhilakṣmī, the bestower of great accomplishments, [should be worshipped];
one should either recite or cause others to recite this hymn named Pratyaṅgirā. (42)
By reciting it, one may instantly paralyze or shatter enemy armies and the like;
even inconceivable things are accomplished, and through recitation, one attains success. (43)
It pacifies great faults, destroys great diseases, and eliminates the fear of lions, tigers, and malevolent planets, as well as royal calamities. || 44 ||

O Goddess, those practitioners who shall recite this Great Hymn of Worship at the time of worship will find the afflictions caused by planets, as well as those from water and fire, destroyed, and will attain peace. (45)

For them, there is no lack of success; whatever brings satisfaction to the Goddess, there is nothing that will not be accomplished for you, O follower of the Kaula tradition in the teaching of the Kula.
Whatever desire one contemplates, it is accomplished effortlessly;
this is the truth, the absolute truth, O Great Goddess—for in the Kaulika tradition, there is indeed nothing equal to that. 47.
Rising at midnight when the lamps have been lit in the night, if this hymn is recited, everything one has contemplated shall be accomplished. (48)
Furthermore, even without this practice, one attains success through the recitation of this hymn, provided one recites it before a mandala, before an image, or before a painted scroll (paṭa). 49.
This great hymn has been proclaimed as the bestower of the accomplishment of inconceivable goals;
however, it should never be given to those who are devoted to other deities.
"It must be given to one endowed with devotion and who delights in the family initiation (kuladīkṣā);
otherwise, they fall—such is the command of the Supreme Goddess. (51)
Thus ends the hymn on the increase of the mantra of Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, brought down by Śrī Siddhinātha from the Karavīra [Tantra] within the glorious Tridaśaḍāmara.
By means of the root of the staff consisting of three sections.

Aiṁ! (5) Victory, victory, O Mother of the Universe! O You whose lotus-feet possess the splendor of the pollen from the *mandāra* garlands on the crowns of the gods—Hari, Hara, and Hiranyagarbha; O You whose bodily luster is as beautiful as the multitude of moon-like drops of water from the celestial Gaṅgā, which is pure like the golden water of the lotus-eyed Lord; O You of radiant beauty! Victory, victory, O Mahākālī, destroyer of Time (*kāla*), who assemble the circle of the *samaya*, the *yoginī* of the hosts of *siddhas*, the mother of the *vidyādharas*, who are saluted by the gods and sages, and who are praised by the most excellent women!
O Virūpākṣa, O eye [of the world], you who bestow the fortune of perfection upon the Kevārā and Vidhāna tribes when worshipped by the Kadamba Kinnaras!

O bestower of joy upon the Śrāvakas, O sovereign of the three worlds, you who hold in your hand a garland of shimmering, priceless jewels and pearls; O you whose eyes are like the radiance of bones, who wear a necklace of human skulls; O you who are the fulfillment of the burden of bliss, who appear as a debt to those in debt; O you who are the tree and the creeper, the thick Pāṭali flower that has made the entire circle of the quarters its playground; O you who are graced by the sun and moon as your two earrings; O you whose pair of full, firm jar-like breasts is entwined by the creeper of your waist; O you who are adorned with a garland of human heads; O Caṇḍī, you who perform a wild dance in the forest of Vetālas and Kāpālikas, who are intoxicated by the drinking of blood and the tumultuous cries of the Pretas!

In the foremost, firm wheel of *ḍākinīs*, she wanders without fear; she is the wonder that bursts forth from the mass of thoughts, filling the air with the shrieks of the host of *piśācas*. Dwelling in the cremation grounds of the nine directions, she rides upon the shoulders of Rudra. She is the destroyer of the abode of the lotuses of the path of the six *ādhāras*. She is the power of the Kula-nāda, resounding like a serpent in the state of *paśu*; she is the lamp of the radiance of Śakti, the subtlest of all knowledge. She is the sustainer of the stream of nectar from the lunar orb in the blossomed sky of consciousness.

Resembling the ocean of milk, bestowing great supernatural powers (*maharddhi*), the sustainer of all activities; well-cultivated by those who have cultivated the human state; adorned with the entire cycle of the *mātṛkā* letters; perfumed with the fragrance of musk, saffron, and the pollen of the *gurumṛgamada* flower; encircled by garments; adorned with the crescent moon; graced with a mass of matted hair like a fresh garland of *dāmaka-hlāra* flowers; embellished by the various fragrances carried by the wind from golden *keṭakī*, *navamallikā*, *madantikā*, and *mādhya* flowers; and meditated upon by hosts of various *vidyādharas*, gods, humans, *nāgas*, and *kiṃnaras*.

Victory, victory! May the Mother of Victorious Elephants be victorious on the Mountain of the Three Eyes! Victory, victory! She whose mantra consists of more than two hundred syllables including the nine-syllable [mantra], the supreme deity of the *mālā-mantra*, Kālī, Kātyāyanī, Kāpālinī—adorned with a beautiful skull-bowl, trident, *khaṭvāṅga*, bell, severed head, noose, goad, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, she who is filled with human blood, fat, and flesh, and who bears a skull-cup and a skull-topped staff.

The Goddess Siddheśvarī, who holds ten arms, who increases the *virāsana* posture, and who is worshipped by all the sages; she whose lotus feet are saluted by Śiva and Viṣṇu; she who is known as Amā (the New Moon), Umā, and the eternally full Māyā; she who is the Tāraka (the Savior) in the form of the syllables from 'A' to 'Kṣa'; the Mistress of the Sky-voice in the great void of the stainless, formless, and timeless; she who is Kubjikā, Khecarī, Gocarī, Bhūcarī, Digambarī, and Samvarī; she whose nature is the wheel of power (*śakticakra*) and the light of knowledge; she who transcends the qualities (*guṇātīta*), who is eternal, immortal, and the ultimate resting place for the state of dance and enjoyment.

O Goddess who performs the *samayalāsya* (the dance of the pledge) with playful grace, *ṭaṃ ṭaṃ*, surrounded by the great troupe of dancers; O Mistress of Dance, endowed with the full power of all poetic arts and the various bonds of the three qualities (*triguṇa*); O You who flow as the pure stream of accomplishment, prosperity, wisdom, knowledge, and majesty; O You who are the sixteen-syllable and thirty-four-syllable mantra; O You whose forest-like surroundings resound with the humming of bees gathered upon white flowers; O You who perform the *tāṇḍava* within the mandala; O You who are the coiled energy (*kuṇḍalī*) that destroys the opposing side, the enemy, and the contrary winds.

O Mistress of the Island, who causes the ocean of nectar to tremble; O Supreme Goddess, shining forth from the fourfold fire, the eight-petaled lotus, and the outer hexagon; O Śmaśāna-Śakti, O Śivā, you who terrify the Piśācīs with your howling; O Goddess whose splendor is delighted by the loud *kaṭakaṭa* sound of your fierce, wide-eyed gaze; O Heroine seated in the forest posture; O you whose mouth disgorges the female spirits (*pretāṅganā*) and who creates a tumultuous roar as Hara draws them in with his terrifying claws; O you who sport in the mud of the *kola* (boar) and are seated in the bower; O you whose eyes are intent on recitation; O you who delight in the assembly—salutations to you, the Supreme Form.

The Navākṣarī, Saṃcarī, and Sahasrākṣarī [mantras]; Śrīkaṇṭha, Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra, Balabhadra, Vāsuvī, Krodhamuni, Mīnanātha, Jayadratha, Jambālika, Jamadagni, Yamodūcāra, Cānakācārya, Vimalābodha, Vicitrānanda, Devaprabhu, and others; Bhavādi, Trivādi, and the praises offered by the three kinds of gurus; those with joyful hearts; various Vidyādharīs, Gandharvas, Apsarases, daughters of sages, and many daughters of kings.

While the well-conducted deeds of the Samaya-cakra were being sung, Sarasvatī—intent on union with the hosts of Siddhas who had attained the bliss of drinking from the honey-vines of spring; her lotus-like breasts overflowing with the fragrance of the four oceans of passion; her body adorned with the five colors manifested by the *dīpaṃcikā* instrument; her chest pressed by the lotuses of the arms of Lokeśvara and Śrīkaṇṭha; Vṛndārikā, radiant with the bliss of the Lord of the Universe; amidst the multitude of Kalās, fanned by the breeze of the young palm-leaf fans shaken by the intoxicated ones; she was absorbed in the slow, continuous, and gentle flow of the wine.

Victory to the Mother of the World, the Sovereign of All, who wears garlands of flowers born from the wish-fulfilling trees of the beautiful forest; she is the life-restoring herb for the practitioner whose body is scorched by the forest fire of irresistible poverty. She is a river of the nectar of her enchanting mantra-name, with a stream of upward-flowing glances that provide no other refuge to the mindless. Furthermore, O Mother, having set aside the words of other people, look upon me, this helpless one dwelling in the Kadamba forest;
be gracious, O Supreme Goddess, O Most Compassionate One, O Mahābhairavī who assumes a form adored by the best of the thirty gods.

Oṃ! Homage to her who abides in the wheel of all the *siddhi*-yoginīs; homage to her who rejoices as the Mother of Siddhis (*siddhimātṛkā*); who has delivered [beings] from all calamities to awakening; who removes the obstacles of afflicted people; who takes the form of a great fire that brings an end to the suffering of the wilderness; who causes fear to thieves, tigers, and the wicked; whose heart is difficult to resist; who dispels the mass of distress for the heroes fallen into the terrible perils of the impenetrable forest; who is adorned with the various musical instruments—the six seasonal drums, the *mṛdaṅga*, the *ḍamaru*, the *ḍāmara*, and the *ḍiṇḍima*—in a grand display of festive music.

O you who equal the enemy of Smara (Śiva), O you honored by the worlds! O you who are fond of the finest incenses of mahāmāṃsa, mṛgamada, aguru, and camphor, and of great oil! O you who illuminate and shine forth in the pavilion of spring with the jewels of the world! O Caṇḍī, O you whose eyes are like the white lotuses falling from Caṇḍikā! O you whose lotus-eyes are like those of the thousand-eyed Indra! O you whose feet are covered by the garlands of flowers falling from the hands of the multitude of gods, who have offered various salutations with folded palms!

O Mother of all mantras! O you who are affectionate toward those who bow before you! O you whose intoxication is subdued by tranquility! O you who consume the three worlds! O you who shatter the difficult paths of miserable rebirths! O Mistress of the Kula! O destroyer of all calamities! O you who are mixed with human blood, fat, and flesh! O you who cause the life-force of the sacrificial victim to depart! O destroyer of the bonds of bound souls! O Blessed One! O bestower of desired sovereign power upon the practitioners who worship Bhava and upon those great-souled devotees! O creeper-like vine for the tree of the lineage that fulfills every mental wish!
