O Mother, who by nature uprooted the frontal globes of the elephant of Death, forgive my transgression. O Śaktināthā, here I am alone, abandoned by my attendants; I bow down to you, the bestower of boons upon the gods, who have come to this enclosure. I meditate upon you, I gladden you, and I prostrate before you, O Siddhāmbā. O Night, who terrifies those afraid of the night, grant me a place of refuge! Cut, pierce, and strike down the circle of planetary afflictions! Be gracious, be gracious, O Śivā! Forgive, forgive my offense!
Thus ends the *Daṇḍaka-stotra* from the *Śrīsiddhilakṣmī-trikhaṇḍa*.
Having constructed the maṇḍala.
Indra and the other world-protectors, residing in their respective directions and joined with their own respective mudrās,

dwell eternally on earth within the planets beginning with the Sun; likewise, the stars, yogas, lunar days, the Gaṇas, Guru, the Vavaṭukas, and the Mothers reside upon the sacrificial mound (sthāṇḍila) or in the Mātṛkā-mantras.
May Siddhi grant prosperity; may the earth be filled with sacrifices; may there be auspiciousness.
Oṃ, homage to Agni.

I bow to You, who are known as *Tejas*, who illumines the universe, who removes the impurities of worldly existence, who is purifying, the worlds of *bhūr*, *bhuvar*, and *svar*, the all-pervading, omnipresent, praised by the company of sages, radiant, holding a spear in Your hand; who is the inner self of every living being, subtler than the subtlest, the one whose banner is rich with colors, the teacher of all twice-born ones, and the one with beautiful hair— salutations to You.
May all the gods, highly pleased and accompanied by the entire oblation, consume the offerings through the mouth of Agni;
having partaken of the full and auspicious food, may she who bestows all peace and prosperity grant him complete satisfaction and bestow all desired fruits and all perfections.
I bow with devotion to those goddesses; salutations to her who has assumed the forms of all the hosts of gods.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śakra; the blazing Yamaka, the one with the noose of Rākṣasa, the protector of the body, Ananta, Durgā, together with the hosts of grahas and all the nāgas;
Heramba, the assembly of Siddhas who remove sin and fear, and the gods beginning with Candra and Sūrya.
May the Yoginīs, all the gods, together with the hosts of deities, protect you, O all-gods!

The *Ṛgveda* is his first foot, the *Yajurveda* his second foot, the *Sāmaveda* his two hands, and the *Atharvaveda* his second mouth; the *Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa* is his speech, the *Vyāhṛtis* his sacred chant,
the *Gāyatrī* his body, the *Upaniṣads* his eyes, and the *Brahma-sūtras* his tusks.
The Earth becomes the form of Viṣṇu concealed as a Boar in the shape of a sacrifice;
those who are gods, yakṣas, nāgas, the entire host of grahas, bhūtas, rākṣasas, and piśācas;
those which are the years and the months; all the groups of lunar days (tithis), and the constellations (nakṣatras) and their conjunctions (yogas).
May those who are attached to the ear-creepers—Akaca-tataya-yasa-varna-sugriva and Canda—be ever well-pleased; may they grant you the royal fortune that is the state of health and happiness.

Having placed [the seed] within my *kuṇḍa* with the *praṇava* mantra, and having established it in the fire-*kuṇḍas*, the rites beginning with *garbhādhāna* and those starting from the *hṛdaya* [mantra] up to the union with the *śakti* are performed.
Ojā, Pū, Kā, and the altar (vedī), along with the lords of the directions and their retinues, and Bhairava, constitute the eight fields (*kṣetra*).
May Jātavedas protect me, together with the eight Yoginīs, the sacred fields, and the movement of the Vaṭukas.
May the meanings of our mantras be realized; may the deities of the pitcher, the sacrificial mound, the Vaiśvānara fire, and the directions be well-pleased and grant boons;
may there be auspiciousness for the gurus and the Brahmins.
May the king be victorious through righteousness; may he be well-pleased. May the subjects be happy; may there be auspicious prosperity for the land.
May all sentient beings be happy. May the rain-cloud pour forth in due season; may the kingdom be blessed. May there be peace and nourishment for bipeds and quadrupeds.

May the gods send rain in due season; may the earth produce a full harvest of grain; may cows abound in milk and other products; and may the King, whose intellect is free from impurity, protect the world. May the sun shine upon virtuous sons, noble maidens, and women of good family, and may all vice meet its destruction.
May the world truly possess a state of devotion forever; may this very devotion be auspicious.
O King of Kings, Supreme Lord, Most Illustrious Warrior!

May there be the perfection of the sword for Śrī-Śrī-Sumati Jayajitāmitra Mallavartman, the sovereign of our realm; may there be the rise of his majesty; may there be the perfection of mantras for ourselves and others; may there be well-being for bipeds and quadrupeds; may all sentient beings be happy; and may there be the fulfillment of every rite.

May they grant the fruits as prescribed by the scriptures for the sake of the patron’s [name] sacrifice; may the patron’s name be as imperishable as the ocean and vermilion. May there be long life, health, sovereignty, progeny, wealth, prosperity, and the increase of the lineage for [the patron] together with his attendants and retinue.
If there is a defect in the sacrifice, especially that of the preceptor,
or if it is devoid of mantra and mudrā, or due to the fault of reciting the limbs [of the ritual] incorrectly;
One destroys the syllables of the mantra and so forth, especially those beginning with the letter *a*,
by violating purity, moral conduct, and other such rules during the acts of officiating at sacrifices or recitation.
Whatever has been done by embodied beings that is impure due to ignorance of the Vedas and scriptures, or devoid of ritual action—
may you forgive all that and grant auspiciousness and welfare.
The virtuous, ever tranquil, performers of good deeds whose rise of sin has been destroyed,
and kings who always abide in righteousness, protect the earth at all times.

May the clouds rain their waters in due season; may the subjects be delighted; may they rejoice; and may there always be the joy of increasing wealth, kinsmen, friends, and the prosperity of the community.
May there be well-being for all subjects; O Lord of the Earth, protect the world by the path of justice. May there be constant auspiciousness for the Brahmins, and may all the worlds be happy.
May the rain-god Parjanya send rain in due season; may the earth be rich with crops;
may this land be free from agitation, and may the Brahmins be fearless.

Whether performed through ignorance or knowledge, whether left undone or done incorrectly, whatever flaw occurred regarding the mudrās, worship, ritual procedure, the sequence of sacrifice, or the hymns—O Knower of the Unknowable, forgive these faults in this sacrifice and its rites! Even a great sinner, with palms joined in reverence and full of serene faith, [approaches] the Lord who is the sole protector of all worlds; for him, everything becomes entirely complete, like a blazing fire that consumes all.
O Lord of Sacrifice, through the fault of the king and the fault of fickleness in my devotion, the sages have been moved by their power;
whether there has been excess or deficiency in the performance of the mantra-rituals, O God, forgive me, for You are the destroyer of my faults.
You are the refuge of all beings, O Lord of the supreme, who dwells within the moving and the unmoving; you are seen by the inner movement within all creatures.
O Agni, if one has committed any injustice through action, mind, or speech,
and if one's word has been deficient, may that be purified there.
O Supreme Goddess, may whatever is deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, and likewise deficient in devotion, as well as deficient in recitation, fire-offerings, and worship, be forgiven.
Thus ends the verse of aspiration.
With the water of recitation, [one sprinkles] consecrated sandalwood and so forth. [This is] the benediction.

Again, there is the offering according to the number [of deities]. During the homa, one should present a flower-vessel to the preceptor (ācārya) and the others. One should fill the full vessel (pūrṇapātra) with rice and other grains.

The ritual of Nyāsa and so forth: Then, having mentally contemplated Prajāpati as the deity, [one should offer salutations]: "Obeisance to Brahmā; obeisance to Praṇītā; obeisance to the Altar (Vedi); obeisance to Śidhyeśvara; obeisance to Śivā; obeisance to Māyā; obeisance to the World-Protectors: Indra, Agni, Yama, Nairṛtya, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera, Īśāna, Adhas, and Ūrdhva. For subsequent homas, there is the worship of the deities: "Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Tripañca."

Salutation to the four and five deities; to the sacrificial altar; to heaven, to mortals, and to the netherworld; to Gaurī, to Dhārī, and to Skandā; to Sūrya, to the Lord of Yogins, and to the Great Lord of Yogins; to the Tiṣṭubh meters, to the gods, and to the Ṛṣis; to the deity of the oblation, to the consecrated fire, and to all the gods—salutation! Salutation to the three gods!
The offering of fuel-sticks consists of eighteen or sixteen oblations.
With the root mantra, one should perform the worship of the hands and likewise offer oblations.
Lūṃ, svāhā to Indra!
Salutation to that Indra, the lord of the gods, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand, possesses great strength,
and is the sovereign of a hundred sacrifices.
Oṃ hrāṃ rūṃ agne svāhā.
To the hundred-fold radiant Mahādeva, red-colored and of great luster,
who holds a spear in his hand and possesses great splendor— to that Vaiśvānara, indeed.
Oṃ mūṃ, svāhā to Yama.
Salutations to the god Yama, the wielder of the staff, the presiding lord of dharma, possessed of great strength;
salutations to the King of Dharma, whose body resembles a dark cloud at the time of universal dissolution.
Oṃ kṣūṃ, svāhā to Nairṛtya!
[He beheld] the Lord of the Rākṣasas, with blood-red eyes, mounted upon his steed, possessing the luster of a blue lotus petal,
holding a sword in his hand, and drinking a flood of blood.
Oṃ vūṃ, svāhā to Varuṇa!
I bow to the Lord who is the King of Waters, whose nature is the noose in hand, possessed of great strength; the King of Nagas, white in color and of great splendor.
Oṃ yūṃ, svāhā to the northwest.
I bow to Hari, who is golden-hued with a deer-like luster, who bears a fluttering banner,
who is the very life-force of all beings, and who is seated upon a deer.
Sūṃ, svāhā to Kubera!
He is proclaimed as King Soma among all the Yakṣas and Trāṇas;
O heroic one, wielder of the mace and the vessel, salutations to you who are the supreme power.
Oṃ hūṃ, svāhā to Īśāna!
O God, the Lord of all sciences, known by the name Īśāna;
O Mahādeva, wielder of the trident, Sovereign of the three worlds and more—homage to you!
Hrīṃ, svāhā to Viṣṇu.
O Lord, sovereign of the serpents named Ananta, who dwells eternally in the netherworld (pātāla), salutations to you, O Nārāyaṇa! Salutations to you, the All-pervading One!
Oṃ, svāhā to Brahmā!
Salutations to that one who acts as Brahmā, the eternal creator whose nature is the act of creation, who dwells in the place above the fourfold form of Padmayoni.
Śiva-Śakti; Āditya Mṛtyuñjaya on the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila); oblation (āhuti); number of oblations (saṃkhyāhuti).
The officiating priests should recite the Aṅgiras-sūtra; one should cause the officiating priests and others to be fed.
Thus ends the daily ritual.

Then, at night, the offering of the *bali* should be made according to the appropriate ritual procedure. [The mantra: "O Vīra, born of the sacrifice, come quickly! O you who are swift, come quickly! Come to the place of the sacrifice; having offered the *bali*, remain here! Then the Hotṛ and the Ācārya, while holding the *bali* in their hands, should perform three *añjali* gestures toward the *raja-krama-maṇḍala*. Then they should partake of the food of the Ācārya. This concludes the night.

Then, having returned from the two morning sessions, perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and so forth, as well as the worship of the door-vases (*dvāra-kalaśa*), as before. Then, having mentally contemplated each deity in relation to the subjects (*prajā*), [recite] "Brahmā-praṇītā" and so forth. Perform the oblation of eighteen or sixteen fuel-sticks (*samidh*), the oblation of clarified butter (*ghṛta-āhuti*), and the oblation of sesame seeds (*tila-āhuti*) together with clarified butter. Perform the oblations for Brahmā, Praṇītā, the altar (*vedi*), the world-protectors (*lokapāla*), the door-offering (*dvāra-bali*), and so forth, along with the recitation of verses (*śloka*).
The preparation of the sacrificial offering (caru) is as before. The consecration of the water-pot (kalaśa-pratiṣṭhā). The oblation according to the number (saṃkhyā-huti).
In whatever manner one should perform the ritual action.

The ritual for the sacrifice: the preparation of the *caru* oblation, the offering of clarified butter (*ghṛta*), the offering of sesame seeds (*tila*), the consecration of the water-pot (*kalaśa-pratiṣṭhā*), the offerings according to the prescribed number, the root-mantra with its protective deities, the lamp, the protection against metal [weapons], and the invocation (*ārati*). In the northeast of the pavilion, one should construct a bathing pavilion. Therein, the cloth-seats and the *cavakīcoya* [ritual implements] are placed; likewise, there are twelve eight-petaled lotuses and twelve water-pots (*kalaśa*) belonging to the various lineages (*gotra*). In the eastern water-pot are: emerald (*puṣparāga*), ruby (*padmarāga*), topaz (*hera*), pearl (*mūti*), and sun-crystal (*sūryakānti*).

Moonlight || Fullness || Crystal || Worship || Oṃ lūṃ, homage to Indra. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Śikhaṇḍin. The southeast jar: cow’s urine, cow dung, curd, honey, clarified butter, saffron, camphor, musk, worship. Oṃ rūṃ, homage to Agni; hrāṃ śrīṃ, homage to Kaṇṭha.
Dakṣiṇaghaṭa, Vaḍasiṃ, Duṃparavaraṅgata, Jaṃbu, Vyāla, Madhuka, Śilīśa, Pūjana. Oṃ Mūṃ, obeisance to Yama. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Trimūrti.

The Nairṛtya jar: clay from Viṣṇu’s field, clay from the Gaṅgā, clay from the site of an *agnihotra* fire, clay from a mountain peak, clay from an anthill, and clay from a bull’s horn. Worship: Oṃ kṣūṃ, obeisance to Rākṣasa. Oṃ, obeisance to Ekamudra.

The Western Jar: Water from divine wells, snow-melt from the Himalayas, lotus ponds, springs, lakes, rivers, and the ocean—these are the waters for the offering. OṂ VŪṂ VARUṆĀYA NAMAḤ | OṂ HRĀṂ EKANETRĀYA NAMAḤ |
Vāyavya-vessel: śrīkhaṇḍa, aguru, karpūra, kastūrī, kūṭa, jaṭāmāṃsī, musta. For the worship: Oṃ yūṃ vāyavya namaḥ; Oṃ hrāṃ śrīvorttaye namaḥ.
Uttaraghaṭa | Palakā | Tyaṃcchā | Cche | Tyaṃke | Hāmala | Svānavā | Muṃga | Priyaṅgu | Pūjana | Oṃ Śūṃ Kuberāya Namaḥ | Oṃ Hrāṃ Sūkṣmāya Namaḥ.
Īśānaghaṭa, Malisvāna, Hyāṅusahacara, Bhoyu svāna, Jīlisvāna, Cavatra, Kahnevaḍī svāna.

Śaṅkhapuṣpī | Aparājitā | Svāna | Worship: Oṃ Hūṃ, homage to Īśāna; homage to Sadāśiva. To the east of the east: Hnelase, Nānase, Dhāḍe, Kolasa, Udadhiṣajura, Nārikera, Miḍise, Mvāca. Worship: Homage to the Eastern Ocean; homage to Sadyojāta.
To the south of the southern [direction]: Sahadevā, Vaca, Kucilā, Abherahā, Kuhmuri, Guḍagu, Karkkaṭāśṛṅga, Kaṇṭhagiri, Punandana, Pūjana. Salutation to the Southern Ocean; salutation to Vāmadeva.
In the western direction of the west: *manaḥśīla*, *haridhāra*, *hiṅgu*, *rasāñjana*, *ghera*, *gorocana*, *gandhaka*, *valaḍa*, *pūjana*. Homage to the Western Ocean; homage to Aghora.
To the north of the north. Luṃ. Sijela. Nyā. Khaposota. Oho. Kaṃśalaṅa. Ghoṣa. Hmala. Pūjana. Homage to the Northern Ocean. Homage to the Tatpuruṣa.
For nine years and so forth, with the *Succhāya* weapon-mantra, one recites in the presence of the deity.
O God of gods, Lord of the universe, author of creation and destruction!
O Mahādeva, this [image] was fashioned by me with a deluded mind as yours.

Whether it be deficient in limbs, excessive in limbs, maimed, or anywhere incomplete, you ought to forgive all of that; may it become perfect in every respect. May there be pacification of any defects in craftsmanship.

Tila-upatana. Bathing with the *kalaśa* for all the subsequent offerings (12). [Bathing] in the East: with the *ghaṭa* [vessel] using the *astra-mantra*. Southeast, South, Southwest, West, Northwest, North, Northeast, and further East of the East, South of the South, West of the West, and North of the North. Bathing with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) and the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). Bathing with a hundred streams using the root mantra (*mūlamantra*). Thus is the procedure for bathing. Śrīkhaṇḍa.
Camphor, musk, saffron, valerian, ointments and unguents, sandalwood and other fragrant substances, divine vision, flowers, incense, and lamps.

The rising of the deity; the *jōnaka* of the sacrificer (*yajamāna*); the *laṅkhadhāratha* of the sacrificer’s wife (*yajamānī*); at the southwest gate of the pavilion (*maṇḍapa*), [the offering] to the messenger (*dūta*).
To the deity Tūlasat with the *śiras* mantra; to Devathyaṃna with the *śikhā* mantra; to Phāgānaphāyakeṭoṃ with the *kavaca* mantra.

The placement of the Sleep Jar (*nidrā-kalaśa*) upon the head: "Ādhāraśakti," etc., and the weapon-mantra of the eightfold nourishment (*aṣṭapuṣṭikā*). "Salutation to Padmāsana. Having worshipped with the *aghoramūla* and the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), [recite]: "Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the Sleep Jar. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth. [Display] the cow-mudrā (*dhenumudrā*).
Salutation to Śikhaṇḍin. Salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha. Trimūrti, Ekarudra, Ekanetra, Śivottama, Sūkṣma, Ananta—these are the deities for the Vyāghranidrākalaśa worship.

With the root mantra, perform the three-fold recitation (tribhāna). [This is] the visualization (kalpanā). [It concerns] one's own extension (svānataṃne), the deity Bhairava and others who are fond of the linga, and the image (pratimāsa). Having worshipped with the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga)—namely Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Churura, Sanu, and Oṃtha—one should offer oblations (āhuti) when [the deity] has fallen asleep. [One should perform] the Gāyatrī and protect [it] with the Astra mantra.

Devatvaṃ juroṃ. O God who joins the channels! For the purification of this [body] consisting of the five threads, [I offer] Devatvaṃ. Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā—[to the] feet. Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā—[to the] navel. Oṃ svaḥ svāhā—[to the] head.

*Hrāṃ*, svāhā to the *ātmatattva*—[at] the feet. *Hrīṃ*, svāhā to the *vidyātattva*—[at] the navel. *Hrūṃ*, svāhā to the *śivatattva*—[at] the head. Purification by means of the three principles (*tritattva*) together with the mantra: from the feet to the head, from the head to the feet; [this is] purification from the feet to the head. An oblation is made with this mantra at each of these two places. Then, having sprinkled [the area] with water from the *devanidrā-kalaśa* while reciting the *astra-mantra*.
Having placed the five-fold offering (pañcabali) before the deity with the root mantra: *devadaśakriyāmāyajuraḥ oṃ*.

With the *praṇava*, [say] *svāhā*. The visualization of the womb: *oṃ bhūḥ svāhā*. With the root mantra (*mūla*), the rite of conception (*garbhādhāna*). The visualization of the division of all limbs with the root mantra. Root: the visualization of desire (*kāma*). Root: the torso (*piṇḍa*). Root: the bone (*aṣṭhi*). Root: the skin (*tvaca*). Root: the head (*śira*). Root: the hair (*keśa*). Root: the forehead (*lalāṭa*). It endures the sun. Root: the crown (*mukuṭa*). Root: the two eyebrows (*bhrū*). Root: the eyes (*netra*). Root: the gaze (*dṛṣṭi*). Root: the nose (*nāsikā*).

The base of the lips; the base of the teeth; the base of the tongue; the bases of the ears; the bases of the neck; the bases of the shoulders; the bases of the upper arms; the bases of the forearms; the bases of the hands; the base of the heart.

Root: both sides of the abdomen; Root: the chest; Root: the two breasts; Root: the belly; Root: the intestines; Root: the digestive fire; Root: the navel; Root: the bladder; Root: the private parts; Root: the opening at the front of the private parts; Root: semen; Root: both thighs; Root: both knees; Root: the ankles; Root: the feet; Root: the soles of the feet; Root: the toes; Root: the nails of the toes; Root: the body hairs; Root.
Complete in its constituent parts.

Oṃ hrāṃ vaṃ, salutation to Vāmadeva, the northern face. Oṃ bhuvaḥ. Khphreṃ, salutation to the head, which is the abode of the power of satisfaction on the path to nirvāṇa and the bestower of nourishment to the body. Having worshipped [it], and having offered oblations at the end of the svāhā-utterance, [one worships] Puṃ Śravaṇa. Hrāṃ raṃ, salutation to Aghora, the southern face. Oṃ svaḥ.

*Khphreṃ*. O pacifier of calamities and misfortunes, salutation to the power (*śakti*) of the beginningless awakening, to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), to the crest-lock, and to the conceptualization of the body and eyes. Having worshipped [thus], and having offered oblations at the end with *svāhā*, [O] Śrīmanta!

Oṃ hrāṃ yaṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa, the eastern face. Khphreṃ, obeisance to the armor for the rite of birth, the abode of independent power that destroys all misfortunes, enemies, calamities, and afflictions. Having worshipped thus, one should offer oblations ending with svāhā.
The birth-rite (jātakarman) [is performed] with a leaf of the *kāpa* tree.

Oṃ varaṇya || Khphreṃ! To the one who has crossed the ocean of all calamities, whose abode is unimpaired power, Hrāṃ! Salutation to the opening of the eyes. Having worshipped [thus], at the end of *svāhā*, perform the oblation (*homa*). *Bhargaḥ devasya* || Khphreṃ! To the one who crushes all enemies, whose abode is infinite power, Salutation to the weapon (*astra*). [Recite] the root mantra (*mūlamantra*), having worshipped [it], and at the end of *svāhā*, perform the oblation. This is the naming ceremony (*nāmakaraṇa*). As is the name of the deity...
Oṃ sya dhīmahi || Khphreṃ, obeisance to the heart, O Supreme Swan, abode of the power of omniscience!

Having performed worship, and having offered oblations at the end of the *svāhā* [mantra], one partakes of the fruit. (8) *Oṃ dhiyo yo naḥ*. *Khphreṃ*, obeisance to the heart of the Goddess who bestows the path to Nirvāṇa, the abode of the power of satisfaction. Having performed worship, and having offered oblations at the end of the *svāhā* [mantra], one partakes of the food; [this is] the *caru*.

Oṃ pracodayāt || Khphreṃ! Salutation to the Weapon [Astra], the abode of the power of primordial awakening, which pacifies all calamities and adversities. Having worshipped it and offered oblations at the end of "svāhā," perform the piercing of the ear (*karṇavedha*). Luṃ oho mūlu. (8) Oṃ tat savibhu || Khphreṃ! Salutation to the Weapon [Astra], the abode of independent power, which destroys all misfortunes, enemies, and afflictions. Having worshipped it and offered oblations at the end of "svāhā," perform the tonsure ceremony (*cūḍākaraṇa*). Luṃ oho khora. Cākaphaṇini. (8) Oṃ varaṇyaṃ ||

Khphreṃ! Salutation to the upward-facing one, the abode of unimpeded power, who enables the crossing of the ocean of all calamities. Having worshipped [him], and having offered oblations at the end of the *svāhā* mantra, [perform] the binding of the vow (*vratabandhana*), the investiture of the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), and the imparting of the *Gāyatrī*. Just as for the God... (8)... Oṃ Bhargo devasya... Khphreṃ.

*Oṃ sakalaśatrupramathani anantaśaktidhāmne hreṃ piṅgale kavacāya namaḥ.* Having worshipped [the armor], and having offered oblations at the end of *svāhā*, [this is] the initiation (*dīkṣā*). At the end of the mantra: (8) *oṃ sya dhīmahi*. *Khphreṃ sakalaśatrupramathani anantaśaktidhāmne astrāya namaḥ.* Having worshipped [the weapon], and having offered oblations at the end of *svāhā*, [this is] the return ceremony (*samāvartana*).

Oṃ *dhiyo yo naḥ*. Having worshipped with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*), and having offered oblations at the end of the word *svāhā*, [one worships] the household implements. To the one who dispels shadows, to the one who possesses a hundredfold armor, having pierced with the weapon-mantra (*astra*), for the sake of laughter and for the sake of even the palace, in the shadow of the root-navanavṛndāvana, *luṃ* to Indra, obeisance. In the shadow of the leafy tree, having worshipped with the root mantra, and having offered oblations at the end of the word *svāhā*, [this is for] marriage. Oṃ *pracodayāt*.

KH PHREṂ SAKALAŚATUPRAMATHANI ASTRĀYA NAMAḤ. Having worshipped [thus], and having offered oblations at the end of SVĀHĀ, [one performs] the Siṃdūrapātra and the Bhramaṇayātrā. (8) These are the Brahmaśiras and Candra.

[One should perform] the purification of the stone with these [mantras]. Bathing with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) with the root mantra. Sprinkling with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the seat of the Brahmapīṭha. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the form of the Brahmapīṭha. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Brahmapīṭha. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Brahma-stone (brahmaśilā). Oṃ hrāṃ cāṃ, obeisance to the heart. [Offer] twenty-seven oblations (āhuti). The Moon-stone (candraśilā): [Perform] the six limbs beginning with the heart. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the seat of the Pīṭha. Oṃ, obeisance to the form of the Pīṭha.

Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the sacred seat (pīṭha). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the lunar form, the nectar. The worship of the six left limbs. The oblation (āhuti), [verse] 27. Having invoked [the deity], the worship of the Brahma-stone (brahmaśilā).
The formula for the installation of the Brahmaśilā.
Oṃ hrāṃ! O Grandfather, you who are the embodiment of Brahmā in the form of stone, the omniscient one!
Earth, water, fire, air, and space as well.
As long as he remains there, so long may you remain immovable.
And by the command of Śiva, one should remain steadfast precisely because of that very state of firmness.
The firm word of Brahmaśilā.
Oṃ Hrāṃ! May the nectar, which is the very form of immortality, remaining upon the seat of nectar, become firm for him as long as the moon and sun endure.

Sthiravākya: For the worship with vajras, gems, and medicinal herbs. Oṃ hrāṃ laṃ, homage to Indra; [in] the eastern direction. Oṃ hrāṃ naṃdrāya, homage; in the east. Oṃ hrāṃ bhadrāya, homage; in the south. Oṃ hrāṃ jayāya, homage; in the west. Oṃ hrāṃ riraktāya, homage; in the north. Oṃ hrāṃ pūrṇāyai, homage; in the center. Oṃ hrāṃ nandāyai, homage; in the southeast (Agni). Oṃ hrāṃ bhadrāya, homage; in the southwest (Nairṛtya).

Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Jayā; [in the] Vāyavya [direction]. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Riktā; [in the] Īśāna [direction]. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Pūrṇā; [in the] center. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the Heart; [in the] Nairṛtya [direction]. Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to the Head; [in the] Vāyavya [direction]. Oṃ hrāṃ, vauṣaṭ to the Crest-lock; [in the] Īśāna [direction]. Oṃ hrāṃ, hūṃ to the Armor; [in the] Agni [direction]. Oṃ hrāṃ kroṃ, [in the] center.

Oṃ hraḥ astrāya phaṭ! Having struck [the space] in the four directions starting from the east, perform the invocation and so forth, the worship with sandalwood and unbroken rice grains, and the Amṛtadhenu mudrā.
Oṃ hrāṃ sarvoratnoṣadhītyādi || Gṛhṇa baliṃ svāhā || Having gone to the edge of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), nine oblations should be offered. [The] full oblation (pūrṇā).

Then follows the dismissal of the jewels and other materials: *Oṃ hrūṃḥ astrāya phaṭ*. Dismissal. Then, having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and other rites upon the Brahma-stone (*brahmaśilā*) from east to the center, [recite]: *hera*, *luṃ*, *haridhāra*, *chau*, *uśara*. The mantra for the eastern vessel: *Oṃ hrāṃ luṃ ratnadravyadhātu oṣadhī hūṃ phaṭ cirasthito bhava svāhā*. East. (1)

Sūryyakrānti || Śijala || Malaśīla || Hāmala || Mādhava || Oṃ hrāṃ rūṃ ratnadravyadhātoṣadhī hūṃ phaṭ svāhā || Be long-lasting, svāhā! || Āgne || (2) || Nīlaḥ || Kaṃśalaṃṅa || Valaḍa || Māsaḥ || Viṣṇukrāntā || Oṃ hrāṃ muṃ ratnadravyadhātoṣadhī hūṃ phaṭ cirasthito bhava svāhā || Dakṣiṇe || (3) || Indranīlaḥ ||

Oho! Suvarṇamākṣī! Mūṅga! Raktacandana! Oṃ hrāṃ kṣuṃ ratnadravyadhātoṣadhī hūṃ phaṭ! Remain steadfast for a long time, svāhā! [To] Nairṛtya. (4) Mūti! Līḍi! Pādhara! Kaḍagadi! Aṅguli! Oṃ hrāṃ vūṃ ratnadravyadhātoṣadhī hūṃ phaṭ! Remain steadfast for a long time, svāhā! [To] Varuṇa. (5) Puṣparāga! Kaṃśa! Śiru! Tyaṃccho! Śrīkhaṇḍa!

*Hrāṃ yūṃ ratnadravyadhātoṣadhī hūṃ phaṭ cirasthito bhava svāhā.* [Vāyavya] (6). *Padmarāga*. *Hmara*. *Gandhaka*. *Hnāhāvā*. *Duduhvarase*. *Oṃ hrāṃ sūṃ ratnadravyadhātoṣadhī hūṃ phaṭ cirasthito bhava svāhā.* (7). *Vaiḍūrya*. *Nyā*. *Phipati*. *Svaṃdhāvā*. *Kūṭa*. *Oṃ hūṃ ratnadravyadhātoṣadhī hūṃ phaṭ cirasthito bhava svāhā.* [Īśāna].

(8) || Lūṃ || All grains, *pādhara*, *tālaka*, *śaṅkhapuṣpī*, *sahadevā*. Oṃ hrāṃ hrauṃ, O jewels, substances, minerals, and medicinal herbs, hūṃ phaṭ! May you remain for a long time, svāhā! [In the] center. After that, the mantra for performing worship again:
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Naṃdrā—[in the] east. (1) Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Bhadrā—[in the] south. (2) Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Jayā—[in the] west. (3) Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Riktā—[in the] north. (4)
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Nandā. [Direction: Agni (Southeast). Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Bhadrā. [Direction: Nairṛtya (Southwest).
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Jayā; in the northwest. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Riktā; in the northeast. (4)
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Pūrṇā. [In the center. (9) Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vāmā.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Jyeṣṭhā. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Raudrī. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Addhikā.

Oṃ hrāṃ Kālī, obeisance! Oṃ hrāṃ Kalavikarṇī, obeisance! Oṃ hrāṃ Balavikarṇī, obeisance! Oṃ hrāṃ Balapramathanī, obeisance! Oṃ hrāṃ Sarvabhūtādamanī [obeisance]! [From the east to the northeast] (8). [From Vāmā onwards...]

Oṃ hrāṃ lāṃ līṃ lūṃ lmlvryūṃ! To Indra, who holds a thunderbolt in his hand, lord of the gods, whose vehicle is an elephant—[protect] us in the east. Oṃ hrāṃ rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ rmlvryūṃ! To Agni, who holds a spear in his hand...

Salutation to Tejādhipati, who is seated upon a goat; [in the] southeast. (2) Oṃ hrāṃ māṃ mīṃ mūṃ mmlvryūṃ. Salutation to Yama, who holds a staff in his hand, the lord of the pretas, and whose vehicle is a buffalo; [in the] south. (3) Oṃ hrāṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣuṃ kṣmlvryūṃ. Salutation to Nairṛta, the lord of the rākṣasas, who is mounted upon a corpse; [in the] southwest. (4)

Oṃ hrāṃ vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vmlvryūṃ, homage to Varuṇa, who holds a noose in his hand, the lord of the waters, mounted upon a makara. Varuṇa. (5) Oṃ hrāṃ yāṃ yīṃ yūṃ ymlvryūṃ, homage to Vāyu, who holds a banner in his hand, the lord of the wind, mounted upon a deer. Vāyu. (6) Oṃ hrāṃ sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ smlvryūṃ, homage to Vaiśravaṇa, who holds a mace in his hand, mounted upon a ram. Kubera. (7)

Oṃ hrāṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ hmlvryūṃ! Homage to Īśāna, who holds a trident in his hand, the lord of spirits, mounted upon a corpse. Īśāna. (8) Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ haṃ! (9) Homage to Svacchanda Mahābhairava. [In] the center. (9) Oṃ hrāṃ! Homage to the Heart. Oṃ hrīṃ! Svāhā to the Head.

Oṃ hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Hreṃ, hūṃ to the armor (kavaca). Oṃ hroṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes (netratraya). Oṃ hreṃḥ, phaṭ to the weapon (astra). One should display the cow-seal (dhenumudrā).
Thus concludes the worship of the Brahma-stone jewel.

Then, as before, having worshipped with the left-hand rotation (*vāmāvṛtta*), and having again worshipped the heart and other limbs, and having worshipped [the deities] beginning with the invocation (*āvāhana*), one should worship the Lord of the *luṃ* syllable; or else the Lord of the *āśija* water; or else, having performed the pressing of the *toyukāpa*, one should proceed to the *brahmaśilā*.

For the installation of the image: *Ādhāra* (Foundation). *Luṃ*, *karṣamaṃsa*, *yajamananaparāgajuhvanadayake*, *aṅguli*. This is the *pūjā-śakti-mantra-kūṭana*: *ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ SAṂHṚDAYĀYA NAMAḤ*. Having worshipped with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) and so forth, one invokes [the deity] with the *yonimudrā*. The oblation (*āhuti*): (3). The full oblation (*pūrṇā*). For the seats of the deities of the preliminary consecration (*aduvāsana*), the mantra is again: *AIKĀRĀSANĀYA NAMAḤ*. The invocation (*āmantra*): *OṂ ĀDHĀRAŚAKTE NAMAḤ*; *ANANTĀSANĀYA NAMAḤ*.

The bulb, the stalk, the petals, the filaments, and the pericarp. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the lunar disk. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the lord of the lunar disk. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the solar disk. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu, the lord of the solar disk. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the fiery disk. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Rudra, the lord of the fiery disk. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the lunar disk.

Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Īśvara, the lord of the lunar maṇḍala. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the maṇḍala of Śakti. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Sadāśiva, the lord of the maṇḍala of Śakti. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the lotus seat. These constitute the worship of the seats in the center. [Then] the worship of the image and the pedestal. Dharma and so forth (4): in the east, south, west, and north. Adharma and so forth (4): in the southeast, southwest, northwest, and northeast. Oṃ, homage to Vāmā.
Oṃ Jyeṣṭhī, obeisance! Oṃ Hrāṃ Raudrī, obeisance! Oṃ Hrāṃ Ambikā, obeisance! Oṃ Hrāṃ Kālī, obeisance! Oṃ Hrāṃ Balavīryā, obeisance!

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Balapramathanī. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sarvabhūtadamanī. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Manonmanī. [These are worshipped] from the east to the center. Then, Indra and the others: Oṃ lu, obeisance to Indra, and so forth. From the east to the northeast (Īśāna). Having performed worship starting from the heart [of the deity], one should offer oblations up to the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa).
Vase (4): Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the Salt Ocean. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the Milk Ocean. [In the] East.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the ocean of curd. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the ocean of ghee. [To the] right.
Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Ocean of Sugarcane Juice. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Ocean of Honey. In the west.
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Garbhādārṇava. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Śivodārṇava. [In the] north.
Ganges, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Godāvarī. (4) East and so forth.
Śrīkaṇṭha, Śaṅkara, Ananta, Sādākṣa—(4)—[in order] from the east and so forth.
The heart-mantra and so forth (6). The worship of the jar, beginning with the invocation. The installation with the Aghora root-mantra.

Oṃ hrāṃ oṃ aghore hrīṃ thaghore hrīṃ ghora-ghorantare hūṃ phreṃ sarvataḥ sarva sarve hreṃ ju sa hroṃ rudra-rūpe hraṃḥ | May there be a beautiful form for the installation of Śrī Svacchanda Mahābhairava and Sadāśiva. [Recitation of the Svasti-mantra] and the sounding of auspicious musical instruments.
Installation of the pedestal: Oṃ hrāṃ śāṃ kalipuraya namaḥ svāhā. Covering the pedestal. Visualizing the central compartment, one covers the image of Kuliśa.

The Worship of the Pedestal (Pīṭhikā-pūjā) Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Icchā-śakti (the Power of Will). Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jñāna-śakti (the Power of Knowledge). Oṃ hrāṃ hrūṃ, obeisance to Kriyā-śakti (the Power of Action).

The Image. The mantra for worship. Three times on the head. (3) The root-mantra of Aghora. The placement of the face. One should perform the placement by means of the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*). Having offered the essence of the flower, one should offer oblations within the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*). Having touched [the image] in its respective places, one should again perform the placement by means of the five principles (*tattva*): *Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the earth-principle; Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the lord of the earth-principle.*

Salutation to Brahmā. Section (1). Oṃ Hrāṃ, salutation to the element of water (āpa-tattva). Oṃ Hrāṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu, the presiding lord of the element of water. Knees (2). Oṃ Hrāṃ, salutation to the element of fire (teja-tattva). Oṃ Hrāṃ, salutation to Rudra, the presiding lord of the element of fire. Navel (3). Oṃ Hrāṃ, salutation to the element of air (vāyu-tattva). Oṃ Hrāṃ, salutation to Īśvara, the presiding lord of the element of air. Heart (4). Oṃ Hrāṃ, salutation to the element of space (ākāśa-tattva).

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sadāśiva, the lord of the space-element; [this is for] the forehead. (5) Then, having offered a drop of water with a flower, one should go to the edge of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and offer oblations after having asked permission.

Again, having offered the essence of the flowers from the forehead down to the feet, one should perform the placement (*vinyāsa*). Having gone as far as the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), one should offer oblations; this is the sequence of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*).

Having gone near the deity, one should perform the placement [of mantras] with the three principles (tattvas) together with the form (mūrti): Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the principle of the self (ātmatattva); Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the lord of the principle of the self.

Oṃ hrāṃ kṣāṃ, obeisance to the Mūrti. Oṃ hrāṃ kṣmāṃ, obeisance to Sarva, the lord of the Mūrti. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Vahni-mūrti. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Paśupati, the lord of the Vahni-mūrti. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Yajamāna-mūrti. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Ugra, the lord of the Yajamāna-mūrti. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Arka-mūrti. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Rudra, the lord of the Arka-mūrti. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Jala-mūrti.

Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Bhava, the lord of the water-form. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the wind-form. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Īśāna, the lord of the wind-form. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Indra-form. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Mahādeva, the lord of the Indra-form. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Khaṇḍa-form. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Bhīma, the lord of the Khaṇḍa-form. Having performed the placement (vinyāsa) and offered [the oblation] for each taste, from the feet up to the navel is the portion of Brahmā.
Oṃ Hrāṃ! O Brahmā, together with you who are embodied within my heart!
"Free from defects such as missing syllables, as long as this is recited with devotion, for that duration you must remain here by the command of Śiva. [This is] the self-portion (ātmabhāga).

Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the principle of knowledge (vidyā-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Viṣṇu, the lord of the principle of knowledge. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Kṣmā-mūrti. Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Sarva, the lord of Kṣmā-mūrti. Having thus performed the placement (nyāsa) of the eight forms (aṣṭa-mūrti), one should offer flowers and juices, performing the placement from the navel up to the neck: "Oṃ hrāṃ heṃ, O Viṣṇu, together with you, the Lord of Forms (mūrtīśvara), [may this image] be freed from defects such as missing limbs," reciting as far as desired.

"You must remain here for that duration by the command of Śiva. Having gone to the edge of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), one should offer oblations. This is the portion belonging to the *vidyā-tattva*: *Oṃ hrāṃ śivatattvāya namaḥ* | *Oṃ hrāṃ śivatattvādhipataye rudrāya namaḥ* | *Oṃ hrāṃ kṣmā mūrttaye namaḥ* | *Oṃ hrāṃ kṣmā mūrttyādhipataye sarvāya namaḥ* | [The Eight Forms (*aṣṭamūrti*)] Then, having offered the floral essence and performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) from the neck up to the *lalāṭa*: *Oṃ hrāṃ śivatattvam āyatanamūrtiṃ mūrteśvareṇa saha*."
Free from defects such as missing syllables, you must remain here for as long as it takes to recite what is pleasing, by the command of Śiva.
The portion belonging to the Śiva-tattva. Having gone as far as the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should offer oblations. This is the portion belonging to the Śiva-tattva.

Then one should purify with the twenty-six principles (*ṣaḍviṃśatitattva*): Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the earth principle (*pṛthvī-tattva*). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the water principle (*āpa-tattva*). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the fire principle (*tejas-tattva*). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the air principle (*vāyu-tattva*). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the ether principle (*ākāśa-tattva*). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the smell principle (*gandha-tattva*). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Brahma-principle (*brahma-tattva*). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the forms of the earth (*kṣmā-mūrti*). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sarva, the lord of the forms of the earth (*kṣmā-mūrtty-adhipati*). The Form (*Mūrti*).
(8) Having gone as far as the feet and knees, or as far as the sacrificial pits, one should offer the oblation.
The Brahma-portion: (1) Om Hrāṃ, salutation to the principle of taste. Om Hrāṃ, salutation to the principle of form. Om Hrāṃ, salutation to touch.

Homage to the *tattva*! Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the *śabda-tattva* (the principle of sound)! Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the *ghrāṇa-tattva* (the principle of the sense of smell)! Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the *jihvā-tattva* (the principle of the sense of taste)! (6) Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the *viṣṇu-tattva* (the principle of Viṣṇu)! Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to Kṣmāmūrti! Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the Lord of Kṣmāmūrti! [This is] the *mūrti* (form). (8) [Having gone] to the knees... having reached the end of the throat, one should offer oblation. This is the portion of Viṣṇu. (2) Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the *cakṣus-tattva* (the principle of the eye)!

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of skin (tvak-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of hearing (śrotra-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of the generative organ (upastha-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of air (vāyu-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of the feet (pāda-tattva). (6) Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Rudra (rudra-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Earth-form (kṣmā-mūrti). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sarva, the lord of the Earth-form and others. (8) [The offering] for the form is at the navel. Having gone to the end of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should offer oblations. This is the portion of Rudra. (3)

Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the principle of the hands (pāṇi-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the principle of speech (vāk-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the principle of the mind (manas-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the principle of the intellect (buddhi-tattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the principle of ego (ahaṃkāra-tattva).

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Prakṛti. (6) Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Īśvara. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the form of the principle of Earth (Kṣmā). Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Sarva, the lord of the forms of Earth. [This is] the Form (Mūrti). (8) Having gone as far as the heart and the sacrificial pit, one should offer oblations. This is the portion for Īśvara. (4) Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Prakṛti. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Puruṣa. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Rāga. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Niyati.

Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the principle of Ethics (nītitattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the principle of Impurity (aśuddhitattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the principle of Knowledge (vidyātattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the principle of Sadāśiva (sadāśivatattva). Oṃ hrāṃ kṣmī, salutation to the Form (mūrti). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Lord of the Form and all [beings] (kṣmāmūrttyādhipati sarva). [The eight] forms (mūrti): on the forehead. Having gone to the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should offer oblations; this is the portion for Sadāśiva. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the principle of Art (kalātattva). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the principle of Time (kālatattva).

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Medhātattva. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Śuddhavidyātattva. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Īśvaratattva. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Sadāśivatattva. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Śaktitattva. (7) Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Nirañjanaiśvara, the Lord of all principles. [One should place these] upon the head of Īśāna. Having gone to the end of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should offer oblations. O Nirañjana, having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the thirty-six [principles], one should purify the image.

Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to the Śiva-tattva. One should offer oblations as far as the sacrificial pit according to the previously mentioned procedure. [The deities of] the Śiva-tattva are the eight forms (aṣṭamūrti): [the head].
The eightfold form of the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva) [is located] in the heart; it is the Self, the eightfold form (aṣṭamūrtti). [It is] the creation of the foundation (ādhārasṛṣṭi).
One should perform worship at the head with the root mantra.
Perform the placement (nyāsa) on the face; having worshipped with the six limbs beginning with the heart, one should proceed to the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) and offer oblations.

Again, the worship of the pedestal: Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Vāmā, the sovereign of the earth element. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Jyeṣṭhā, the sovereign of the water element. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Kriyā, the sovereign of the fire element. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Jñānā, the sovereign of the air element. Oṃ hrāṃ, obeisance to Icchā, the sovereign of the space element. Having gone to the edge of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should offer oblations.
Furthermore, having worshipped three parts of the pedestal: *Oṃ hrāṃ icchāyai namaḥ*. First.

Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Jñānā; [in the center]. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Kriyā; [on] the upper pedestal (ūrddhapiṇḍikā). One should offer oblations up to the edge of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) for the purpose of establishing the seat of worship (pūjanapīṭhikā).

Jīvanyāsa Oṃ hrāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ śirase svāhā | Oṃ hrūṃ śikhāyai vauṣaṭ | Oṃ hreṃ kavacāya hūṃ | Oṃ hroṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ | Oṃ hraḥ astrāya phaṭ | Oṃ hrāṃ kṣaṃ īśānāya namaḥ | Oṃ hrāṃ yaṃ tatpuruṣāya namaḥ | Oṃ hrāṃ raṃ aghorāya namaḥ | Oṃ hrāṃ vaṃ vāmadevāya namaḥ | Oṃ hrāṃ yaṃ sadyojātāya namaḥ |

Oṃ hrāṃ kṣaṃ, salutation to the face that is both supreme and non-supreme. By means of the root mantra of Aghora: Oṃ oṃ oṃ! Kuṇḍalī, having arisen through the left nostril, having entered the body of Dayāśiva—which consists of all living beings and has the nature of light—by means of the syllables hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, and having meditated upon the state of consciousness as the syllable hūṃ, one should worship right there with the root mantra and the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga), perform the ritual placement (nyāsa), proceed to the edge of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), and offer oblations while reciting the *Śataparījāpya*. Then, one should go into the presence of the deity.
Thus, for the sake of concealing one's own desires, one speaks in this way as if it were the truth.
Then the root mantra for the installation of life-force (prāṇapratiṣṭhā).

Aiṃ (5). Oṃ. For the mantra of the installation of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*): Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra are the seers (*ṛṣi*). The *Ṛg*, *Yajuṣ*, and *Sāman* are the meters (*chandas*), or alternatively, the *Aticchandas* is the meter. The deity is the one named Prāṇa, whose form consists of compassion. This is the ritual application for the purpose of the installation of the vital breaths.

Aiṁ (5) Oṃ Aṃ Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ Āṃ! To the Self consisting of earth, water, fire, air, and ether; Āṃ, salutation to the heart. (1) Aiṁ (5) I Caṃ Chaṃ Jaṃ Jhaṃ Ñaṃ Ī! To the Self consisting of sound, touch, taste, form, and smell; Śirase Svāhā! (2) Aiṁ (5) Oṃ Oṃ Ṭaṃ Ṭhaṃ Ḍaṃ Ḍhaṃ Ṇaṃ Ūṃ! To the Self consisting of ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose; Oṃ, to the crest-lock (śikhā), Ṣaṭ! (3)

Aiṁ (5) Oṃ eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ. To the one whose essence is speech and the organ of generation; Aiṃ, for the armor, Hūṃ. (4) Aiṃ (5) Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ. To the one whose essence is the opening of the mouth, movement, and the bliss of emission; to the three eyes, Vauṣaṭ. (5)

Aiṃ (5) Aṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Kṣaṃ Aḥ, to the Self consisting of mind, intellect, ego, and consciousness, Astāye Phaṭ. (6) Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Āṃ, at the navel, Radha (1). (1) Aiṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ, to the heart, at the navel. (2)
Aiṁ (5) Oṃ Kroṃ, from the head to the heart, *namaḥ*. (3) Aiṁ (5) Oṃ Yaṃ, *namaḥ* to the self of the skin; [place] at the heart.
Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Raṃ, obeisance to the Self of marrow; on the right shoulder. Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Laṃ, obeisance to the Self of flesh; on the hump. Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Vaṃ, obeisance to the Self of fat; on the left side.
Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Śa, salutation to the self of the bones; from the heart to the end of the right foot. Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Ṣa, salutation to the self of the marrow; from the heart to the end of the left foot.
Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Saṃ, salutation to the self of Śukra. [This extends] from the heart to the right foot.
Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Haṃ, salutation to the Self of Prāṇa.
From the heart to the end of the left foot.
Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Kṣaṃ, salutation to the one whose nature is wrath; [this extends] from the heart to the navel.
Having performed the placement (nyāsa) in this manner with the life-force seed-syllable (prāṇabīja), one should meditate upon the deity of the vital breath (prāṇadevatā).
meditative absorption (dhyāna)
Seated upon a red lotus that shines with its own luster within a sea of blood,
she holds in her five hands a noose, a bow made of sugarcane, a goad, and a hook.

May the Supreme Power of Life (Prāṇaśakti), who bears a skull-ornament, who is radiant with three eyes, whose breasts are full and prominent, and whose complexion is like the rising sun— may that Goddess be the bestower of happiness upon us.
Thus ends the section on meditative absorption.

Mantra: Aiṃ (5) Oṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Laṃ Kṣaṃ Haṃ Saṃḥ. O Speech, Breath, Eye, Ear, and Nose of Paramaśiva, come here—Haṃ Saḥ Hsauṃḥ Haṃ Saḥ. May you remain happily for a long time in happiness! Haṃ Saṃ Hsauḥ So'haṃ Haṃ Saḥ Kṣaṃ Luṃ Haṃ Saṃ Ṣaṃ Śaṃ Vaṃ Laṃ Raṃ Yaṃ Krāṃ Hrīṃ Ā Oṃ Svāhā (5) Aiṃ. Dhāra (27). This is the Jīvanyāsa for the completion of the rite.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphroḥ Hsauṃḥ Kṛṣṇa Svāhā. Aghoravajravatīśī.
Thanājīvaliphone.
Aiṃ (5): Grant me vital breath, as well as life-force; grant me longevity, progeny, and wealth.
Grant me the bliss of wisdom and knowledge; grant it to me, even if only for a brief period of time.
Devabhūti for the oblation.

The presiding deity of the five principles (*pañcatattva*). Then, the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) upon the deity, as well as the worship of the deity by the deity. Following that, the worship of Viśvakarman. For the burden of worship consisting of sandalwood, flowers, incense, lamps, the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), flowers, and so forth; for the burden of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) and the burden of the sacrificial materials. The firm oblation (*sthirāhuti*). In the firm enclosure (*sthirahāra*) of the *suvelājulaṅāva*, the officiating priest (*ācārya*) is the master of the altar (*vedi*); the ritual act belongs to the patron (*yajamāna*). Within this firm enclosure, the formula begins: "On this day, in this eon... and so forth.
The month, lunar day, asterism, and weekday.
The statement in the *Thirahāra*.
Aiṃ (5). O Supreme Lord, omniscient one, whose form is knowledge and realization!
For the sake of austerity, for the destruction of evil, and for the merit of the Supreme Person. (1)
For the sake of bringing happiness to the worlds, remain firm upon this comfortable seat;
O Goddess, always be beneficial by turning over [the body] every day. (2)
May it always be worshipped for the sake of the sacrificer, yielding the fruits of all desires;
having performed the placement of the feet, the second [placement] is likewise done with the phonemes. (3)
Bhuvana is the third, Karma is indeed the fourth, Tattva is declared the fifth, and Mantra is the sixty-fourth. (4)
The seventh indeed is the Vinyāsa, and likewise the next is the Para-nyāsa; having thus performed the Nyāsa, the Great Goddess, the Supreme Sovereign, should be installed. (5)

The mantra for the deity is "deveti," and the mantra for the goddess is "devītī"; likewise, at the gateway of the deities, one should place the heart-mantra, the lattice window, and the water-pot. (6)

Having placed the *uṣṇīṣa* at the crest for the rite of installing the deity, one should [place] the two feet, the door, and the window with the heart-mantra of the goddess, as well as the water-pot. (7)
Having placed the *uṣṇīṣa* and the crest (*cūlika*), they know the sequence of the seat of knowledge (*vidyāpīṭha*). "O Goddess, you are established; may this [image] be well-established. (8)
Through the prosperity of Śambhu, the sacrificer also attains his presence; may there be constant welfare for our two-footed beings, and constant welfare for our four-footed beings. (9)
May there be fulfillment of the hopes of all the worlds for us, and likewise may there be prosperity through the kings.
This sacrificer, together with his servants, sons, cattle, and kinsmen—(10).
May all the lords of the gods protect me; salutations, salutations to the giver of all!
As long as the moon and the sun endure, and as long as the earth and the seven oceans remain; (11)
As far as the celestial Gaṅgā extends, so long may you remain firm; be steadfast, and may all be auspicious. (12)
Śrī Saṃvartā. Aiṃ! She who is that Śakti...

Having established *Hskṣmlvryūṃ* and *Śkṣmlvryīṃ*, [perform] the fivefold consecrations (*pañcābhiṣeka*) and so forth, beginning from the south. This is the procedure for the *Sthirahāra*. Thus it is concluded. The sequence of the deities for the installation of the principal deity (*mūladeva*) is as follows: for the principal deity, [offer] to the gracious-faced one (*sumukha*) along with his limbs (*sāṅga*), weapons (*khāṅga*), and ornaments (*adguliyāya*). To all these attendants (*gaṇapāta*), offer oblations (*āhuti*) according to the rite. Offer oblations of parched grain (*lājā*), *dūrvā* grass, and unbroken rice (*akṣata*) to all the deities. Perform one hundred and eight (*108*) oblations with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*). [Offer] one hundred and eight oblations of blooming flowers (*utphullāṃ*). Offer one hundred and eight oblations.
O Lord of Gods, you are established as the great-souled Mahādeva,
possessing the sovereignty over the gods of gods and the fourteen worlds.
Even though established, whatever merit there is has an incalculable fruit;
it is liberated from [all bonds] and must remain by the command of Śiva.
Whatever merit there is, it brings all sovereignty, all prosperity, and progeny;
it is the supreme pacifier of adversaries and the bringer of great peace.
It brings great good fortune and great enjoyment even in this very world,
as well as supreme liberation in the next life and the state of Śiva in the hereafter.
These are the words of consecration: "You are firmly established."

In the northeast corner: [offering] of the remains of the flowers (*nirmālya*), [and] the destruction of the skin of the wind; the bath with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*); the offering of the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*); the three essences (*tritatva*).

*Sodharape* || *Āhuti* together with *pūjana*: Oṃ cāṃ cīṃ cūṃ caṇḍeśvarāya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā || (3) || Then, the *bali*, incense, and lamp. Here, the perfumes and other offerings are established. From "adyādi" up to "yāvaccandraśca" and so forth. The *āhuti* for the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*). The installation of the lion-throne (*siṃghasthāpana*). At the shadow of the main entrance of the temple, the purification (*piṃsvane*) is performed according to the ritual procedure. The ten rites beginning with the bath and the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). The placement of the vital breaths (*jīvanyāsādi*). The worship of the deity (*devārccana*) by means of the root mantra (*mūlamantra*).

Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ siṃghāya svāhā || Incense || Lamp || Here, perfume and so forth || Oblation || Stability || From today onwards || May it be stable, and so forth || Oblation for consecration || Thus is the consecration of Siṃgha. (8) || Directional offerings || Animal sacrifice || Distribution of the regional bali-offering || Oblation || Counted oblations || Fee for the Brahmins || Concluding the ritual sacrifice || Consecration with the water-pot || Benediction with sandalwood paste and other items.
For the purpose of having the Sun as witness; at night, the sacrifice to Kaumārī; the installation of the God and Goddess.

Worship of the deities; offering to the deities; oblation (*āhuti*); as before, the *caru*-oblation; the root mantra for the planets; the fuel-sticks (*samidh*) for the planets, or the selection of verses (*śloka*); the invocation of the planets with the mantras for the armor (*kavaca*), the eye (*netra*), the bow (*dhanus*), the arrow (*bāṇa*), the protection (*rakṣā*), and the crest (*śikhā*).

Having worn the *pehnuya* [garland] with *ajurasa*, one should wear the *jido* [garland] on the forehead. These are the nine types of garlands (*mālā*) to be worn; they should be worn according to the specific ritual action (*karma*) being performed. Whether it be a primary action (*karmma-mālā*) or a secondary action (*okarmma-dhāra*), they must be worn accordingly.

Worship of the Preceptor (ācāryapūjā); offering of regional oblations (deśabali); fire-offerings (āhuti); rites for pacification and nourishment (śāntikapauṣṭika); the ritual procedure for barley, grain, and so forth; the sprinkling of coconut water and other acts; and the bestowing of blessings (āśīrvāda).

Having shaken the sacrificial altar according to the ritual injunctions, [there follows] the consecration of the patron and others, the blessing with sandalwood paste and other substances, and the offering of *svāhā* to the Lord of Sacrifice. At night, there is the concluding rite (*udvāsana*) and the dismissal of the deities. Then, the concluding oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) is performed. Finally, the concluding bath (*avabhṛtha*) is undertaken.

One should offer the specific number of oblations with the tongue-flame mantra (*viśeṣajihvā-vahni*). For the Six Lords (*ṣaṇmānātha*), [offer] with all the limbs. For the hundred thousand-fold offering (*lakṣapola*), [use] *leyā*, *āmalaka*, *kuḍacchi* (1), *phaṃ* (1), and unbroken rice (*akṣata*). For the ninefold five nectars (*pañcāmṛta-navāla*), [use] the womb-essence (*garbhataya*). [Offer] the crest-jewels of those who move in the sky, on the earth, and in the water; the five jewels (*pañcaratna*) according to one's faith; and the *hyāṅu* vessel, the *polaceye* vessel, the three-eyed [image], the ear-banner (*karṇapatākā*), the four gates, the five banners, the red parasol, and red flowers.

The sprinkling of the sacrificer’s pavilion door and so forth; the lamp, iron-protection, sandalwood-paste, and the bestowing of blessings; the offering of *laṃsāsya* and *dutāha*; the circumambulation of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*); and the placement upon the lion-throne. Then, the *hotṛ* priest performs the invocation for the sacrificer. Following that, the *hotṛ* performs the four purificatory rites (*catuḥ-saṃskāra*) beginning with the visual inspection (*anirīkṣaṇa*). [Then follow: the *sodharapa*, the *mālinī*, the *śabdarāśi*, the eight *ghorikās*, the threefold knowledge (*trividyā*), the *granthinyāsa*, the five jewels (*ratnapañcaka*), the twelve limbs (*dvādaśāṅga*), the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), the root-six-limbs (*mūla-ṣaḍaṅga*), and the root-mantra (recited 108 times).

With the *uttarā* [verse], perform the nine-syllable *mālāmantra* and the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) ritual. The nine-fold self (*navātmā*) is the power (*śakti*). Recite the command-mantra (*ājñāmantra*) during the recitation (*japa*). (7) For the *hotṛ*, the supreme meditation on the *muṇḍa*; recite the command-mantra again. Offer one hundred and eight oblations (*āhuti*) of clarified butter (*ghṛta*). With the *śruva* ladle, perform the peace-offering (*śānti-homa*), beginning with the final [mantra] and so forth. As before, perform the *caru*-oblation for pacification (*śāntika*) and nourishment (*pauṣṭika*). [Offer] barley, grain, and so forth. Having performed the rite, whatever is required for the purpose of the sacrifice, offer it as a special oblation.

The morning bath and other daily rites; the worship of the deity through the eastern door and so forth; the worship of the directional jars (dik-kalaśa) as before; and the consecration of the jar (kalaśa-pratiṣṭhā).

The Prāyaścitta Homa preceded by the Mahāvyāhṛtis and the Gāyatrī: Oṃ hrāṃ agnaye svāhā | Oṃ hrāṃ somāya svāhā | Oṃ agniṣomābhyāṃ svāhā | Oṃ hrāṃ agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā | Oṃ bhūḥ agnaye ca pṛthivyai ca mahate ca svāhā | Oṃ bhuvaḥ vāyave ca antarikṣāya ca mahate svāhā | Oṃ svaḥ ādityāya ca dive ca mahate svāhā |

Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! To the moon, to the fields, to the directions, and to the Great One, svāhā! Oṃ! To the one of beautiful form and color, whose fire is hunger, whose deity is Agni, for the vital breath (prāṇa), svāhā! Oṃ! To the one of the color of an indragopa insect, whose fire is the tongue, for drinking, svāhā! Oṃ! To the one with the brilliance of the color of lightning’s filaments, whose fire is radiance, whose deity is Soma, for the diffused breath (vyāna), svāhā! Oṃ! To the one of the color of a lotus filament, whose fire is clarified butter, whose deity is Vāyu, for the upward breath (udāna), svāhā!
Oṃ, to the fire of the flowing stream of cow-dung-colored [ashes], whose deity is Varuṇa, to the Samāna breath, svāhā!
Oṃ, to the one who has transcended form, the unmanifest, the stainless, the supreme Brahman, the immortal, the conscious one—svāhā!

Whatever has been thought, spoken, or done by me—from before this time—through the functions of the vital breath, intellect, and body; during the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep; and through mind, speech, the two hands, the two feet, the abdomen, and the generative organ—all that becomes an offering unto Brahman, Svāhā! Having offered eight oblations with this mantra and having worshipped the Fire as before, [one says]: "For the sake of accomplishing what is deficient or excessive, I offer sesame seeds with ghee. Oṃ Hūṃ, perform [the rite] with all its limbs, Svāhā. (2) Svāhā.

Having thus offered one oblation of sesame seeds: Oṃ! O thousand-rayed one of great splendor, homage to you who bear many forms! Homage be to you, the purifier, the consumer of all, who is omnipresent. You are Rudra; you are the performer of terrible deeds and the slayer of the terrible; homage to you! You are Viṣṇu, you are the guardian of the world; grant me peace through this mantra for the sake of the sacrifice performed according to rule.

On the day of the special ritual: morning bath, daily worship of the deity, [worship] starting from the eastern gate, worship of the directional jars (*dik-kalaśa*) as before, and the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*) of the jar.

The regional offering (*deśabali*); the oblation (*āhuti*); the installation of the patron (*yajamāna-pratiṣṭhā*); the installation of the Hotṛ priest (*hotā-pratiṣṭhā*); the worship of the Preceptor (*ācārya-pūjā*); the rites for peace and prosperity (*śāntika-pauṣṭika*); the barley, grain, and other materials; as before, the ghee lamp and wick; the recitation beginning with "Peaceful is the sky, the atmosphere," etc.; *oṃ bhūḥ svāhā*; *oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā*; *oṃ svaḥ svāhā*; the giving of the fee (*dakṣiṇā*) to the Preceptor; the recitation (*vācana*); the offering of the bali-oblation (*baliharaṇa*); the regional offering (*deśabali*) including the removal of suffering; the consumption of the remains of the sacrificial food (*saṃśava-prāśana*); and the removal of the purifier (*pavitra*) with the Astra-mantra.

The *brahmā* receives the full vessel as a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). An oblation is offered with the root mantra. (108) The *pūrṇāhuti*. Having turned the base of the *śruva* downward, [he performs] the *āsaṃsā*. The blessing of "one or many. The dismissal of the *brahmā* and the *praṇītā* water with the *astra* mantra. The consecration with the *praṇītā* water. The syllable *ukāra*, the seed-syllable of Vāyu, and so forth. The release of the *brahmā*. One should offer the *akṣapātana* with *kuśa* grass from the *upayamana* soaked in clarified butter. The washing of the hands and the *kavaca*.

The Avabhṛtha-bath: Preceded by an auspicious proclamation consisting of umbrellas, chowries, peacock-feather fans, chariots and the like, as well as swords, shields, and other royal regalia, along with the five kinds of musical instruments and the sounds of dance and music, one should proceed to the river for the purpose of the Avabhṛtha-bath.

The ritual bath (*avabhṛthasnāna*) may be performed according to one’s desire. [The materials for the vessel are: bull-hide, deer-skin, a sword, *pholabhelā*, *dhucchegula*, nine water-jars (*kalaśa*), the nine-naveled mandala, the seven types of medicinal herbs (*saptadhī*), five jewels (*pañcaratna*), five sprouts (*pañcapallava*), five grains (*pañcavrīhi*), elephant tusk, bull horn, earth, *gorocana*, lotus, *uphola*, *phosimītha*, white pepper (*śvetamarica*), saffron (*kuṅkuma*), cardamom (*musta*), and *devadāru*—these are for the worship within the jar.
The verses regarding the medicinal herbs for the water-pot (*kalaśa*): *sahā*, *sahadevī*, *balā*, *atibalā*, as well as *damayantī*, *vacā*, *śvetā*, *vyāghradantī*, and *sumaṅgalā*.
Śatavatī, Jayantī, Śatapuṣpā, and Candana.
Priyaṅgu, rocanā, uśīra, amṛtā, and sārikā;
It was beautifully adorned with the sprouts of the aśvattha, plakṣa, bilva, nyagrodha, dhana, sasya, śirīṣa, āmra, and kapittha trees.
Scented with the fragrance of gold, gems, medicinal herbs, bilva flowers, and perfumes.
The domestic priest, having consecrated them with mantras, covered them with white garments.
One should perform the Sāvitrī on both sides, and likewise the Channodevī.
The *Hiraṇyavarṇā* hymn, the *Sukta*, and likewise the *Anuvākyā* and so forth.
The earth shall serve as his footstool, auspicious with its roots of dūrvā grass and elephant-goads;
upon that, there should be a seat made of gold or even silver.
One should arrange those four skins— of the ox, the tiger, the lion, and the deer— in their respective order, beginning from the east.
And the domestic priest should offer oblations according to the ritual procedure of the Caturhotṛ.
By Brahmins standing in the four directions, who had mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas.
The meaning of "together" (sahatya). The worship of the nine jars (navakalaśa-pūjā). The consecration (abhiṣeka).
May the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara consecrate you.
May Vāsudeva, Jagannātha, the all-pervading Saṃkarṣaṇa,
Pradyumna, and Aniruddha grant you victory.
The Lord Ākhaṇḍala, Agni, Yama, and likewise Nairṛti;
Varuṇa, Pavana, the Lord of Wealth (Kubera), and likewise Śiva.
May all the guardians of the directions, together with Brahmā, protect you always.
Rudra, Dharma, Marut, Dakṣa, Ruci, and Śraddhā were the sons of Pṛthivī.
Bhṛgu, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Sanaka, Sanandana,
Sanatkumāra, and likewise the venerable Aṅgiras.
Puraha, Purastya, Marīci, and the lord Kaśyapa— may these presiding deities of progeny, having assembled here, consecrate you.

Therefore, with these aforementioned [auspicious signs], let there be your consecration in the sovereignty of the king of kings; may you rule the entire earth together with its oceans for a very long time, and may your intellect and speech be ever fixed upon righteousness.
One should drink the water of rivers; according to one's ability, the gift of a cow [should be made].

With the *śruva* ladle, [apply] the ash-mark (*bhasmatilaka*) with the *kavaca* mantra. To the southeast corner: *thamataya*. To the *javakhavavāhāsa*, *nugarasataya*, and *casāgharasataye*: for the sake of the patron (*yajamāna*), at the end of all [the rites], for the dismissal of the sacrificial offerings (*balivisarjana*).

Oṃ hrāṃ rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ agnaye svāhā. (3) | Ghee oblation (3). | *Rekva* rice, *reko* two-fold ghee. | *Sekhahoma*. Oṃ hrāṃ rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ svāhā. | *Ghela* *dhavaka* *naluya*. | For the sake of the stream of peace (*śāntidhārā*), [offer] *gheladakvaṃluya*. | *Brahmasiddhi*. Oṃ kṛtaṃ karmaṇe svāhā. Oṃ akṛtāya karmaṇe svāhā. One should offer betel leaf (*tāmbūla*). To the one who wraps the head (*śiroveṣṭakoka*), give the betel nut (*tāmbura*).

Circumambulate the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) three times with the water from the *argha* vessel. Facing the entrance of the path, recite: *Oṃ hrāṃ gaccha gaccha suraśreṣṭha ātmāsaṃsāravāhana | yatra brahmālayadevāstatra gaccha hutāsana ||* "Go, go, O best of gods, you who carry the self through saṃsāra! O consumer of oblations (*hutāsana*), go to where the gods dwell in the abode of Brahmā!"
O Lord, the blessing of Agni; the recitation of blessings with water; the offering of the blessing-fire, sandalwood, and flowers.

Now, the worship of Kumāra: for the purpose of drawing [the mandala], using sandalwood and other substances, one should prepare the gaze, the ear-banner, the five banners, the gateway, the bow, and the garland of *caru* and *dakota*.

[Perform] the purification with one's own shadow. [Perform] the sipping of water (*ācamana*) according to the three principles. [Recite] the formula beginning with *oṃ adyādi*. [Offer] the *arghya* to the Sun. [Recite] the verse beginning with *varṇātaṃ vijatyādi*. [Perform] the salutation to the Guru. [Recite] the verse beginning with *akhaṇḍamaṇḍalākāla*. [Perform] the placement of the wick (*vartiśīnyāsa*).
