"Ādhāraśakti," and so forth. (8) Homage to the one seated upon a peacock throne (Mayūrāsana).
Now, as for meditative concentration (dhyāna).
Kaumārī is the supreme goddess, possessing the brilliance of Nīlalohita;
the goddess wears a mass of matted hair, and another half of her body hangs down. (1)
The goddess Visālavadanā has a face resembling the full moon;
she wears a gentle, divine earring that hangs down on her right side. (2)
Two-armed, she who enjoys desires wears a single garment adorned with jewels;
she is slender-waisted with smooth limbs and elevated breasts. (3)
And in her right hand is a divine mace adorned with various jewels; in her left hand, the goddess holds a beautiful child upon her shoulder. (4)
O beloved, the left leg is cast down and the right foot is raised;
the goddess whose vehicle is a peacock is the supreme Sāṃkarī, the command of all. (5)
Kroṃ! To the form of Kumārī, the flower of meditation, homage!
Thus is the meditation. Threefold añjali.
Aiṃ (5) Caṃ Chaṃ Jaṃ Jhaṃ Ñaṃ Kāṃ Kīṃ Kūṃ KMLVRYŪṂ HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ KROṂ Śrīmahākaumālikā Vicce Śrīpādukāṃ || (3) || Baliḥ || Gāyatrī ||
Aiṃ (5). May we know Kurukumāri; may we meditate upon the mantra of ten million syllables; may that Kauli inspire us. [This is] the offering.
Aiṃ (5) Kroṃ, O Śrīkaumārī Vicce, [I offer] the sandals. Bali.
Hāṃ, [the mantra] for the heart and so forth; the rites of invocation and so forth; the *yonimudrā*; the *aghora*, *vajravatī*, and *sitriya* (3); the *bali* offering.
*Haṃsāśanā* namaḥ, and so forth. (8) *Aṃ* to Brahmāyanī, for Asitāṅga Bhairava, the sandals; *Kaṃ* to Māheśvarī, for Ruru Bhairava, the sandals.

Caṃ, the sandals for Kaumārī together with Caṇḍabhairava. Ṭaṃ, the sandals for Vaiṣṇavī for Krodhabhairava. Taṃ, the sandals for Vārāhī for Unmattabhairava. Paṃ, the sandals for Indrāṇī together with Kapālīśabhairava. Yaṃ, the sandals for Cāmuṇḍā for Bhīṣaṇabhairava. Śaṃ, the sandals for Mahālakṣmī for Saṃhārabhairava.

Namaḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ Caṇḍacogrāyai namaḥ | Śrīṃ hrīṃ Pādukāṃ || Śrī Rudracaṇḍā Devī Pādukāṃ || Śrī Pracaṇḍāyai Pādukāṃ || Śrī Caṇḍogrāyai namaḥ Pādukāṃ || Śrī Caṇḍanāyikāyai Pādukāṃ || Śrī Caṇḍāyai Pādukāṃ || Śrī Caṇḍavatyai Pādukāṃ || Śrī Caṇḍarūpāyai Pādukāṃ || Śrī Aticaṇḍikāyai Pādukāṃ || To these [deities], this is the bali offering. Three añjalis.

Aiṃ (5) Caṃ Chaṃ Jaṃ Jhaṃ Ñaṃ Kāṃ Kīṃ Kūṃ KMLVRYŪṂ HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ KROṂ Śrī Mahākaumarikā Vicce Śrīpādukāṃ || (3) || Baliḥ || Hāṃ to the heart, etc. || Āvāhana, etc. || Yonimudrā || The sacrificial master [performs] the Triyāñjali in the shadow.

The shadow of Nirvāṇa; for you, the one of great power, who shakes [all things]; the invocation and so forth; the Yoni-triśikhā-mudrā; incense; divine fragrance; lamp; excellent light; food offering; food of great flavor; recitation; the three deities; the nine-syllable mantra, five times forty-four [repetitions]; *kmlvryūṃ svāhā*. (54) The thread: the unbroken circle of time; the venerable Saṃvartā; the one who dwells there; I bow to the Lord (three times); the vowel *ū*; the enemy of Brahmā; in the center, the triad; the sword-wielder.

Dark-red; the color of the *bandhūka* flower; where is the Great Kāla in the sky? O Mārkaṇḍeya! That Goddess; the blossoming; Āsāpū; she who is the ender of those [afflictions]; belonging to Indra indeed; the *māyā-kuṇḍa*; homage to you, O God; in the state of childhood; the female swan is the primary authority; you are the Supreme; "just as the wind," etc.; here, the perfumes and so forth; three dots (*bindu-traya*); the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
Worship in the cup. Worship with laughter.

Omniscient One, whose splendor is like that of a maiden, [residing] upon the sacrificial ground, O Maiden! O Goddess, may there be blessings! I bow to the venerable Śrī Vāmā, the Mother of the Universe, the Bestower of Siddhi, who is the Mistress of the New Moon (Darśeśvarī). She is the single form appearing manifold throughout the three worlds; she is Pūrṇeśvarī in the east, Bhūteśī in the north, Gaganopamā in the west, and Naiśeśvarī in the south. Having arrived through knowledge, she is Kuleśvarī among the assembly of Kulas, and the Sovereign Lady of the eastern direction. May there be blessings from my own self!

Aiṃ (5). May the Mother, whose first word [is "Ambā"], who is the Blessed One whose essence is consciousness, who abounds in knowledge and will; likewise Hari, Hara, and Brahmā—the triad of Marīcis; the five radiant Bhairavas; thereafter the five Śrī Yoginīs; and the Sun and Moon—the six stainless Marīcis—may Kujā protect me eternally.

The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) for *likāya*. The dismissal (*visarjana*) of the weapon (*astra*), the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), the water jar (*kalaśa*), and the sacrificial ground (*sthāṇḍila*). The auspicious benediction (*svastika*) for the patron (*yajamāna*). The recitation of the *sataya* [mantra]. The *nivacchana* and other rites. The *hnasaka-nataya*. The consecration with the water jar (*kalaśābhiṣeka*). The syllable *ū*, Vāyu. Sandalwood (*candana*). *Śrīkhaṇḍa-candana*. *Sīdhraṃ muṅayātaya*. O Great Mistress of the World (*vireśvari mahā*), the Enchantress (*mohanī*), the Enchantress of the Three Worlds (*trailokyamohanī*). *Sagvana*. *Sidhārthaṃ dadhipā*. The five threads (*pañcasutrakā*). The *hyāṅukāpaḍakuṇḍayā*.

To the daughter of the *svāna* (dog), the maiden, the granddaughter of the *svāna*; to the blossoming one; to her who is peaceful; and to the one belonging to Indra—salutations to you, O Goddess of the lords of gods! To the queen, the goddess who bestows wealth—having recited these verses, [one should] offer the *svāna* sacrifice. Having offered the *māraka-svāna* sacrifice, the patron (*yajamāna*) should perform the *kuṃbha-hlāya* (water-pot purification) for the lotus-like corpse. For the sake of establishing the sacrificial ground (*sthaṇḍila*), there is the application of Śrī and Lakṣmī. The inspection of the sacrificial ground (*sthaṇḍilāvalokana*) is performed by scattering colored powders (*rajacūrṇa*). The *ārati* (lamp-waving) is performed. For the consecration (*pratiṣṭhāyāya*), the *ārati* is performed.
Established in the foundation; for the sake of the full moon; resembling the full moon; for the sake of being a witness.
The dismissal of Kumārī; thereafter, the offering of the *mālaka* and the *bali* for the destruction of Kumārī.
The *samaya-kāya* is like food and other such things.

[The ritual] with the *kuṃbha* [vessel], the purification of the vessels, the sprinkling of the vessel-remnants, the invocation of the patron (*yajamāna*) and others, the praise (*stuti*), the offering of *sāma* fruits, the seating of the *āgaṇa-kumāris*, the *māraṅ-paṃtaya*, and the *tarpaṇa*. Aiṃ!

May the delighted Bhairava, who dwells upon the seat of the *pretas*, the destroyer of fear, whose form is the mantra; Caṇḍī, seated upon the fierce throne; the *gaṇas*, the preceptors, the *vaṭukas*, the world-protectors (*lokapālas*), the lords of serpents (*phaṇīndras*);
the protectors, the *yakṣas*, the very fierce ones, the entire host of ancestors (*pitṛ-gaṇa*), the Mothers, and the guardians of the field (*kṣetrapālas*)—[may they all be pleased].
May the yoginīs, joined in yoga and moving on land, in water, and through the air, drink this beverage.
May all the deities, the oceans along with their lords of hosts, the yoginīs, and the guardians of the fields (kṣetrapālas), who are established within your body, drink [this].
Vākya: Homage to Śrīnātha! Homage to Śrīsiddhinātha! Homage, repeated homage, to Śrīkujeśanātha!
By means of the water-pot, for the continuity of the body and the alms-bowl, [there is] the division of the space of the occasion. (2)
Tarpaṇa.
I praise her who resides within the Vīracakra in the twenty-eighth maṇḍala of the twenty-eight karmas, endowed with eight groups of eight.
Salutations to you, the sovereign of the universe; salutations to you, the bestower of wisdom.
Salutations to you in the form of Bhairava; salutations to you, the savior from worldly existence.
I bow to this single-formed wheel, consisting of eight groups of eight yoginīs, likewise of vaṭukas, and of Bhairava.
Having divided the body and the stream of the vessel with the *kubhayā* [mantra], one should analyze it; that is its dissolution. (2) || That is its departure. ||
The body shall become indestructible, as well as waterless and stainless.
Possessing great strength and a body of adamant, he is the royal glory under a single parasol.
There shall be constant destruction of enemies, and longevity, prosperity, beauty, and compassion;
there shall be perpetual great nourishment, and it bestows fortune and progeny.
This elixir-water was created for everyone by the God of Gods;
it is a divine, supreme nectar-taste, the medicine for worldly existence, which has been drunk.
May the lineage yoginīs rejoice; may the daughters of the lineage rejoice;
may the illustrious lineage masters rejoice, as well as all others—homage to you!
For the sake of eating whatever food is desired according to the occasion, [I go] to Jayantikā, the cow that grants all desires.
At that time, the Kumbhayāka people were as terrified as if they had fallen into a pit.
For the purpose of satiation: Aiṃ! Victorious is the lotus-foot of the Goddess, which bestows grace, the nectar of liberation, and awakening to the infinite conclusions;
I bow to the host of sixty-four Yoginīs.
I bow my head to the Lord Bhairava, who stands in the midst of the circle of Yoginīs, surrounded by the mandala of Mothers, together with his beloved Bhairavī.
From calamity, from evil, from disease, and from transgressing the rules of conventional conduct—
they ward off all these through union with the divine wheel.

May the Blessed Lord of the Family grant peace to those who worship and protect him, to the ascetics who possess ordinary penance, O Lord of the Senses, and to the country, the kingdom, the city, and the king.

Homage forever to all those Yoginīs who, by the power of their command, reside throughout the three worlds! May the lineages of practitioners rejoice; may the curses of the Siddhas and others fall upon those who violate the observances of the Yoginīs. May that divine will of Śambhu manifest within me, and may the lotus feet of my Guru alone be my supreme deity.
May the practitioners rejoice, may the perfected ones rejoice, and may the Kula-yogins rejoice; may the Sādhakas and Ācāryas, as well as all others who have received Kula initiation, rejoice.
May those without bodies be happy; may those with bodies have happiness.
May that which sustains life—the feet [of the Lord]—be forever gracious. Thus one should recite.

O fair-faced one, come from the place of the remnants for the worship of the Goddess. Come to the remnants; come to the wind-sacrifice. O Goddess who has arrived at the forest of the gods, come to the wind-sacrifice of the gods.

Worship, O fair-faced one! [With the mantra] beginning with "akhaṇḍamaṇḍalākāra" and so forth. The Nyāsa: Aiṃ, salutation to both thumbs. Aiṃ, salutation to both index fingers. Aiṃ, salutation to both middle fingers. Aiṃ, salutation to both ring fingers. Aiṃ, salutation to both little fingers. Aiṃ, salutation to the heart. Aiṃ, svāhā to the head. Aiṃ, vaṣaṭ to the tuft of hair (śikhā). Aiṃ, hūṃ to the armor (kavaca). Aiṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes. Aiṃ, phaṭ to the weapon (astra). Thus, and so forth, is the Kalāga-nyāsa.

The worship of the water-vessel and the argha-vessel; the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) and self-worship (ātmapūjā); the invocation (āvāhana) of Śrī Saṃvartā; the worship of the seats of the three deities, the offering (bali), and the mudrā; the seat of Ādhāraśakti (8); [the mantra] for the corpse-seat of the seat (āsanaśavāsanāya) (2).
Meditative concentration.
Seated upon a corpse, clad in red garments,
adorned with red ornaments, and resplendent with a necklace of *guñjā* seeds.
She is sixteen years of age, slightly flushed with passion, with full and elevated breasts;
holding a skull-cup and a chisel in her hands, she is the embodiment of supreme light.
The best of mantra-knowers should meditate upon her through the union of the left and the right.
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.
Three handfuls of joined palms.
Aiṃ Klīṃ! O Ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālinī, O fair-faced one, O great Piśācinī! Hrīṃ! || (3) ||

This is the *bali* offering for them. [The mantra] "tvāka mahābalina" is used for the shaking [of the vessel]. [The mantras] beginning with "hṛdaya" and so forth are used for the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites.

Mudrā; incense and lamp; food offering (naivedya); recitation (japa); hymn of praise (stotra) beginning with "akhaṇḍamaṇḍalākāra" and "śrīsaṃvartā. [Salutation to] the Goddess Mātaṅgī, who is preceded by the remnants (ucchiṣṭha), the bestower of all accomplishments (sarvasiddhi), the goddess who removes all sins, and who is free from all defects.
Just as calamities— whether stationary, moving, artificial, or born of the body— come to an end when recognized by the Goddess.
O Goddess of gods, it conquers poison residing in one's own limbs or those of others.

Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. May there be peace and prosperity. One or many. O Mother, that which was previously gone. For the purpose of dismissal with the Astra-mantra. For the removal of the offering (bali) by means of the Vātāsati [mantra]. For the removal of blemish.
One should offer betel; this is the *sakare* [offering]. This is the *tāviyamāra*.
Thus ends the sacrificial procedure for the fire established by means of oblations.
May Śrī Siddhilakṣmī be pleased at all times.

Oṃ, salutations; salutations to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī. Then, one should write the *ardharātridīpajāga* (the vigil with the midnight lamp). Then, the consecration of the bronze vessel (*kāṃsasthālī*). The preparation of the sacrificial porridge (*caru*). The ritual rinsing of the mouth (*ācamana*) by means of the three principles (*tritatva*). [The declaration of] "Today and so forth" (*adyādi*). The offering of water (*argha*) to the Sun. Salutation to the Gurus. The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) by means of the root mantra (*mūla*).
The worship of the water vessel and the arghya vessel; the purification of the elements and the self-worship.

The fourfold consecration of the plate: inspection with the root mantra; sprinkling with the weapon mantra; veiling with the armor mantra; and striking with the weapon mantra. Thus is the fourfold consecration.
The seed-syllables of the *thāras* [are arranged] in groups of five *praṇavas* (5). The sacrificial vessel (*carupātra*) is marked with a triangle.
Having placed a portion of sesame and medicinal herbs in a bronze vessel—namely, *oṣadhī*, *bhṛṅgarāja*, and rock salt—and having added a portion of sugar to these, one should set the vessel aside.
Sugar candy, sugar, *sākhala*, medicinal herbs, cardamom, nutmeg, mace, cloves, myrobalan, beleric myrobalan, emblic myrobalan, black pepper, long pepper, dry ginger, and sugar.

Take curd, *kasti*, and water for the *argha* offering. [Offer] the nine substances (9): the water of the Ganges. With these heroic substances (*vīradravya*), perform the ritual sprinkling (*vāraṃhnyāya*). Encircle all dualities with a triangle representing Śiva and Śakti together. Surround it with a garland.

*Kṣecala*, *bhūcala*, *jalacala*, *sekhera*, all *caru*, *aṇḍaja*, *ardhapāka*, *kaṃca*, and *samayāntaka*—in the presence of Bhaṇḍāla. (Three *añjali*s). The *bali* offering. The mudrās for invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth. Dismissal with the *astra-mantra*. To the messenger (*dūta*). The *cakrasavoya*. Having set these aside.

One should draw a triangle within a pitcher (kumbha) containing the syllable *aiṃ*, and fumigate the vessel with Śiva and Śakti. The Guru’s [mantra] is born from the pitcher (*kuṃbhaja*); the deity of this [pitcher] is the one who dwells within. The Yoginī’s [mantra] is filled with bees (*alī*); at the end of the *yāṅatha* [mantra], the Guru’s [mantra] is the final letter of the alphabet, and so forth.

Having placed the Śiva-śakti [liṅga] in the center of the *thaṃne* (the sacred site), having placed it in the worship pavilion (*pūjā-maṇḍapa*), having placed it before the *samaya* [initiates], and having placed the Śiva-śakti before the Guru.
One should serve the Yoginī and so forth at the foot of the tree.
That which arose from the Ocean of Milk and was revealed in Koṅkaṇa—
the mass of innate bliss, fashioned as the supreme nectar.
For the sake of attaining success in the Kula tradition, let the food vessel, which is the supreme single color unifying all colors, be accepted.
I shall serve this supreme Vidyā; I shall serve this supreme Kalā;
I shall serve this supreme Śakti, O Mistress of the Kaulas, who has been accepted by me.
Having offered the sacrificial food (*caru*) and the like, and having dismissed the assembly of Yoginīs and the rest, [one should offer] the liquor (*surā*).
For the offering of flower vessels: as in the hymn of praise to the deity.

Rinsing the mouth with the three principles (tritatvena ācamana). Offering water for honor (arghādi). Offering water for the Sun (sūryārgha). Washing the feet of the heroic people (vīrajanapādaprakṣālana). One should prepare equal parts of vacā, priyaṅgu, surabhī, abhī, uśīra, candana, bālā, māṃsī, and coraka.
Then follows the worship of the Kāli Yoginī, the salutation to the Guru, and the ritual placement (nyāsa) according to tradition.

Water-vessel, *argha*-vessel, purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*), self-worship (*ātmapūjā*). [The mantra for] the seat: "O Support-Energy" (*ādhāraśakti*) and so forth. [The mantra for] the mind: *ai* ointment, sandals.
May this divine śrīkhaṇḍa sandalwood paste, most enchanting with its fragrance and other qualities,
and this forehead ornament known as sandalwood paste, be accepted.
With sindūra: Hrīṃ, the sandals of the hero’s ashes.
O Vīreśvarī, [worship] the Great Hero adorned with the ashes of heroes,
the supreme Goddess who attracts the three worlds, [red] as excellent vermilion.
O Enchantress! [I worship] the sandals of Śrī Sarvajanamohanī.
Mohana (the deluding), Kāmasaṃsiddhi (the accomplishment of desire), Stambha (the paralyzing), Ākarṣaṇa (the attracting), and Jalasta (the water-related).
It bestows auspiciousness upon the eyes, is enchanting, and grants a beautiful gaze.
Jajamakā || Hsphreṁ, [I offer] the sacred thread and the sandals.

The sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*) is the supreme purifier; it was born together with Prajāpati at the beginning of creation. It is the foremost, the first thread, the sacred thread of supreme splendor.
O dogs!
Hsauṁ: various umbrellas, ornaments, flowers, and sandals.
O auspicious lady, this supreme offering of flowers, consisting of various fragrant blossoms and garlands,
bestows good fortune and spiritual success upon the arising of the flowers.
The view; the banner; clothing and so forth; Siṃhalaṅka.
O Goddess, bestower of boons, I offer to you these two silken garments of excellent hue, golden-colored, yellow, and red—rich in splendor; I present them to you.

Worship: *Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ*, the nine-syllable [mantra] of the Seventeenth [Deity]. Offering: Incense, lamp, recitation (*jāpa*), invocation (*āvāhana*), and so forth; the *yonimudrā*. Commitment (*samaya*): The vessel for *hlāya*.
O Goddess, take this sacrificial pap (caruka), which is praised by the Siddhas,
pure like a crystal, and intended for the benefit of the world.
For indeed, the elixir (rasāyana) was created by the gods for everyone, consisting of five [parts].
I bow to Him who is partless, yet born with parts, seated upon a lotus.
"O Hero, accept this Dharma, which is rejoiced in by the Siddhas;
I bow to it at one and the same time as Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and even Cāṇḍālas."
Welcome to you, O Kings of Dharma! You have been created as the singular reality, free from passion and liberated from both hatred and attachment.
O Great Hero, accept this offering, the sacrificial oblation, and the preparation of the cooked rice;
I bow to the lotus-petal, which is both partless and born of all parts.
Sindūra and the sacrificial fee: Aiṃ (3) Khphreṃ. Sindūra, the parasol, the excellent fan, flower garlands, the sacred thread, clothing, incense, and lamps.
Betel leaves, sweetmeats, and fruits—these were all prepared and fully provided for the worship at night.
All the hosts of deities, beginning with Pratyaṅgirā, have been fully worshipped; may this fruit be prosperity and abundant wealth.
May peace always prevail; may the auspiciousness of the Goddess of Fortune grant a vigil free from obstacles for this heroic person; may it be accomplished!
May there be perpetual well-being for us, the people of meritorious realms.
She who is manifold and yet threefold, who has attained the supreme state, and who dwells upon the moon-like seat;
she who is the eternal refuge for Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, all winged beings, and all creatures;
by her power, she is the source of all auspiciousness, [appearing] with a bow in hand and an arrow among the forest deer and the antelope.
Siddhi Gaurīśanātha, whose limbs are dark, red, and rosy, bows down perpetually.

The goddess Caṇḍakālī, who resides in the entire maṇḍala or sacrificial ground of the Krama lineage, together with her host of yoginīs and the assembly of heroes, in the fields, seats, and secondary seats, accompanied by her gurus.

O Lord Śrī Siddhinātha, victory to you! You who remove obstacles in rites such as the lamp-worship and the vigil, you who grant liberation from curses, and you who are the eternal bestower of sovereign fortune that grants all desired fruits.
Here [are] the incense and so forth. These constitute the worship of the Yoginīs.

The Worship of the Three Deities (3) [Seat: "Ādhāraśakti," etc. (8). Sandals for Narāsana; sandals for Mayūrāsana; sandals for Muṇḍāsana. As before, [offer] sandalwood paste and so forth. Three *añjali*s. *Kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ*—sandals for Kṣatrapāla (3). Bali offering.
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, the sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. (3) The offering.
GĀṂ GĪṂ GŪṂ, the sandals to Kulagaṇeśvara. (3) The offering.
The six-limbed [practice]. For the vessel-offering, as before, the verse:
Hymn of Praise.
I perpetually salute Tāmbamāla, the Lord of the Field and protector of the hells, who is the very essence of all the Kaulikas,
and who holds in his hands a skull-topped staff, an excellent sword, and a bell.
Standing at the door of the beloved of the Lord of the Three Worlds.
In the illustrious teaching, he is renowned as Vaṭukanātha; he is the son of Skanda, the enemy of the gods, and the fire-omen (Ketu);
the son of Gaurī, possessing a blazing spear.
May he who rides upon the peacock protect you, clad in garments of deep red.
With a crimson pitcher raised high by the thick spray of vermilion,
possessing a body as beautiful as a mass of clouds,
he bears an excellent axe, sweetmeats, and a rosary of beads.
May Gaṇapati, the bestower of all desired objects, protect you both.
As is fitting: the sacrificial fee. Here, [may] the perfumes and so forth proceed without obstacle. (2)

Siddheśvara Pūjā || Āsana || As before, [recite] "Ādhāraśakti" and so forth (8). [Offer] sandals to the Bull-throne (Vṛṣāsana); sandals to the Lion-throne (Siṃhāsana). As before, [apply] sandalwood paste and other offerings.

Three-fold *añjali* gesture: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, I worship the *śrīpādukā* of Ānandabhairava Siddheśvara. (3) *Bali* offering. Six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) ritual. Mudrās. As before, for the vessel-offering (*pātrahlāya*).
Hymn of Praise.
She has one face and three eyes;
she holds the crescent moon as her crest-ornament; she possesses four arms, O Great Goddess, with two hands joined in the gesture of reverent salutation (añjali).
As previously stated: the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā); here, the perfumes and so forth; may they proceed without obstacle. This concludes the worship of Siddheśvara.

Then, for the Seat of Siddhilakṣmī: as before, beginning with "Ādhāraśakti" and so forth. *Khphreṃ*, for the sandals of Rudrapretāsana, sandalwood and other offerings. Three *añjali*s: *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ pheṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ svāhāḥ*—the sandals (3). The *bali* offering, the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), and the mudrā. As before, for the vessel (*pātra*).
Hymn of Praise.
Seated upon the pericarp of a full-blown lotus is the supreme Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, white as camphor, crystal, the moon, and the *kunda* flower,
free from all defects, a wave that rescues one from the mire of suffering in the ocean of saṃsāra, and forever unshakable.
May she who possesses glorious five lotus-faces and ten arms, seated upon a corpse, protect us.
As is fitting, [this is] the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). Herein are the perfumes and so forth. May they proceed without obstacle.
This is the worship of Siddhilakṣmī. (4)
The *Saradātmā-pūjā* for Thaṃdīrī: "Ādhāraśakti," etc.; the sandals for Padmāsana; the sandals for Narāsana; sandalwood paste and so forth; three *añjali*s.

(5) *Hskṣmlvryūṃ* Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, to the venerable Navātma-gurumaṇḍala-bhaṭṭārikā, the sovereign of heroes, *Śkṣmlvryīṃ*, [I offer] the sandals. (3) || The *bali* offering; the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*); the mudrās; the salutation to the vessel (*pātra*).
Hymn of Praise.
The letter *U* is the foot of Death; *Ha*, *Sa*, *Kṣa*, *Ma*, *La*, and *Bha* are its arms; *Bo* is the awakener; *Agni* (Ra) is the *liṅga*;
it is joined with the tiger-skin of Vāyu (*Ya*), the moon (*I*), and the hand (*Ka*); it is endowed with the *bindu* and *nāda* above;
it is the stream of the pure Gaṅgā, the straight supreme digit (*kalā*); Bhairava is the embodiment of the mantra.
Pāyādeva, Navātmā, Bhairava, Śrīkujeśa, along with the excellent teacher Sakara.

As previously [stated], [this is] the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. May they proceed without obstacle. This concludes the worship of the ninefold self (*navātmā-pūjā*). (5)

Then follows the fivefold offering (*pañcabalipūjā*): "Ādhāraśakti," and so forth. The sandals for the horse-seat (*mayūrasanāya pādukām*). The sandals for the human-seat (*narāsanāya pādukām*). The sandals for the seat with [all] seats (*savāsanāya pādukām*). The sandals for the seat of the hungry ghosts (*pretāsanāya pādukām*). The sandals for the seat of the mouse (*mūsāsanāya pādukām*). Sandalwood and other offerings. Three handfuls of water (*triyāñjali*). *Śrīṃ hrīṃ*, the sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. *Kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣuṃ*, the sandals for Kṣetrapāla.

Yāṃ yīṃ yūṃ, the sandals for the Yoginīs. Hskhphreṃ, the sandals for Śrī Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī. Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ, the sandals for Śrī Kulagaṇeśvara. [Offer] the *thavāna* and the *bali*. [Perform] the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), the invocation and so forth (*āvāhanādi*), the respective mudrās, and the offering to the vessel (*pātrahlāya*).
Hymn of Praise.
One should worship Kumāra, the son of Gaurī, who resembles the sky and the moon; Kṣetrapāla and the Yoginī;
Cāmuṇḍā of fierce form; Gaṇeśa, the remover of obstacles, who has two faces;
and [the goddess] whose limbs are adorned and honored with offerings of flowers, incense, lamps, food, honey, and oblations.
May this rite, which removes obstacles and dispels misfortune for those honored by the Cakreśa, bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
As before, the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) [is given]. Here, [there is] perfume and so forth.
May they proceed without obstacle. This concludes the five-fold offering of bali. (6)

The worship of the Goddess according to one’s own tradition (*svāmnāya-devy-arcana*): [the offering of] the seat; [the recitation of] "Ādhāraśakti," etc.; the *mālaka* seat; sandalwood paste, etc.; three handfuls of water (*tri-añjali*) with the *mālaka*; the offering of the oblation (*bali*); the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*); the invocation (*āvāhana*), etc.; the ritual gestures (*mudrā*); the purification of the vessel (*pātra-hlāya*); the hymn (*stotra*) with the *mālaka*; as is appropriate; the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*); here, the offering of perfumes, etc.; "May they proceed without obstacle. This is the worship of the Goddess according to one’s own tradition. (7)

The ritual worship of the fire-pit (*agnikuṇḍa*) with its attendant rites: "Ādhāraśakti," etc. [Recite]. The seat (*āsana*). The *mālaka*. Sandalwood paste (*candana*), etc. Three handfuls of water (*tri-āñjali*). *Hskṣmlvryūṃ ānandaśaktibhairavānanda vīrādhipataye śkṣmlvryīṃ aṣṭāviṃśatikarmabhaṭṭārikāyai pādukāṃ.* (3) The offering (*bali*). The six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Invocation (*āvāhana*), etc. The mudrās. The vessel-offering (*pātrahlāya*).
Hymn of Praise.
Seated upon a central triple seat, her face radiant with intoxication and joy, she is the blazing union of Vajra and Padma.
Upon the eight petals of Brahma and the others, located in the directions of the gods, she shines in the glorious fields of Prayāga and so forth.
Endowed with twenty-eight squares—va, śa, ṣa, śa, ha, sa, kha, and khe—she radiates from the peak of the vajra.
May she who consists of thirty-two syllables, accompanied by the twenty-eight [deities] and following the sequence of the threefold divisions and the Kula, protect us.
As previously [stated], the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). Here, [offer] perfumes and so forth. May they proceed without obstacle. (8) These are the twenty-eight.

Then follows the worship of Śikhānātha. [Recite] "Ādhāraśakti," and so forth. [Offer] the *pādukā* to the one seated upon the bull (*vṛṣāsana*). [Offer] the *pādukā* to the one seated upon the five corpses (*pañcapretāsana*). As before, perform the worship with sandalwood paste, flowers, and other offerings. [Recite]: *Aghore hrāṃ, ghore hrīṃ, ghoraghorantare hrūṃ phreṃ, sarvataḥ sarva sarve hreṃ juṃ saḥ, hrāṃ rudrarūpe hra, pādukāṃ*.
Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes, śkṣmlvryīṃ, the sandals!
Hsphrāṃ hsphrīṃ hsphrūṃ, [I offer] sandals to Śikhāsvachanda Mahābhairava. (3)

Bali. The six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga). The mudrās for invocation and so forth. As before, [recite] "pātra-samaya-joṅā-vayaḍaye. [Then recite] "carukaṃ gṛhṇate vītyādi" and so on. "O Tattva, by whom have you been contemplated as free from the two-fold appearance?"

Then, offer the vessel of the speech-body: *baliviya baliviya*, *samastamantrapīṭhityādi*, *bali gṛhṇa mahāvīra* and so forth. [Recite] *padmapatraṃ namāmyaham*. Then, offer vermilion as a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*): *sidūra candana viretyādi*.
Hymn of Praise.
Pure, peaceful, and radiant, he possesses a body made of crystal gems with the luster of camphor; he has five faces, five colors, ten arms, and holds spears, weapons, and missiles.

I bow to the Lord Śikhīśa, whose body is adorned with bones, who has three eyes, who consumes with fire, who wears a sacred thread made of serpents, whose form is self-willed, and who removes all fears.
In his hand he holds the skull of Brahmā; on his neck, O Murāri, is a garland of skulls as white as frost;
and upon his entire body he wears a necklace of bones.
Bearing the fear of being obstructed by the raised trident, he manifests repeatedly through his various emanations.
May Śaṅkara, the Kāpālika, protect you at the time of the final dissolution.
As is fitting: the sacrificial fee. Herein are the perfumes and so forth. May they proceed without obstacle. (9)
This is the worship of the entire host (gaṇapūjā).
Then, one should cause the worship of the deity to be performed together with the assembly.

The offering of the *thava* (flower) and the *gurukhāṅāva* (incense). *Ācamana* with the three-fold truth (*tritatva*). *Adyādi*. The *sūryārgha* (offering to the Sun). Homage to the Gurus (*gurunamaskāra*). *Nyāsa*. The water-offering vessel (*jalārghapātra*), purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*), and self-worship (*ātmapūjā*).

Then one should recite the *Māranī*. One should offer the five-fold oblation (*pañcabali*). [The sequence is: the *hṅathvani*, the *lithva thava*, the *jāpa* and *stotra*, beginning with "O son of Gaurī," and so forth, and finally the *tarpaṇa*.

The invocation of Śrī Saṃvartāna. The three deities (3). For the worship of the two, the Moon and the Sun, at this place. Śiva. Sandals for the one seated on the lotus throne. Aśitāṅga and the others (8). Aghora. HSKMLVRYŪṂ. Sandals for the offering of wine to the venerable Kulakumbhabhaṭṭārikā.

Śakti || Pādukā for the Lion Throne || Brahmāṇī and the others (8) || Vajra || ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ, pādukā for the Noble Lady Kulakumbhabhaṭṭārikā || The Six Limbs || These two constitute the worship of the two vases.

For the temple with its limbs and sub-limbs: incense, lamps, recitation (*jāpa*), hymns (*stotra*), and the waving of the bell. To the Yoginīs together with their retinue, grant your command! *Aiṃ*. By the grace of the command of the Gurus, may there be the grace of the command of the circle of the Gaṇas and Yogis; by the grace of the command, may there be the fortune of the accomplishment of the Gaṇas.

Grant me, O you who possess the grace of the command of the Gaṇas and the Gaṇa-deities—the grace of the command! Do so for me! Give, give! Having bestowed the command upon the one with the retinue: [he] wears a necklace of skulls, ornaments of bone, and various other ornaments.
The ritual for the *caru* offering: the preparation of the sacrificial ground (*thaṇḍila*).

The ritual procedure beginning with the offering of water (argha) to the Sun; the recitation of the introductory mantra; the salutation to the Gurus and so forth; the ritual placement (nyāsa) by means of the root mantra; the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) using the water-offering vessel; and the self-worship (ātmapūjā).

The three *balis*. The carving [of the vessel] with the *gāyatrī* mantra. Worship of the great vessel (*mahāpātra*). *Aiṃ*, obeisance to the lotus-seated *Ādhāraśakti*. Above that: obeisance to the stainless (*nirañjana*) lotus-seated one. Worship of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) of the vessel’s seat: *Raṃ*, obeisance to the fire-mandala, whose self consists of the ten *dharma-kalās*.

*Vaṃ*, salutation to the solar disc consisting of twelve digits (*kalā*). *Glūṃ slūṃ plūṃ mlūṃ nlūṃ*, salutation to the sandals for the vessel of supreme nectar (*paramāmṛta-arghapātra*). I worship the five jewels (*pañcaratna*). [The substance: O Goddess, you who possess a beautiful luster like the Bandhūka flower, who are fragrant and delighted by the sound of praise, you are the supreme substance that bestows prosperity (*ṛddhi*) and accomplishment (*siddhi*).

Aiṁ Hskṣmlvryūṁ Śkṣmlvryīṁ, fill the vessel of nine syllables, fill it, svāhā! [Form] the *trikuṭī* mudrā. One should wash [the vessel] with the *aghorāstra* mantra: Aiṁ (5) Vaṃ, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala consisting of sixteen digits.
Aṃ, salutation to the self of the sixteen digits beginning with Amṛtā.
Meditative concentration.
The Goddess, resembling lac-dye in hue, is as red as a pomegranate flower;
she possesses limbs of exquisite form in the bloom of youth, has three eyes, and is in the prime of her youth.
Madirānandacetanī, bearing eighteen arms,
likewise holds a sword, a trident, a thunderbolt, a ḍiṇḍima drum, and a mallet.
In his right hands, he shines with a mace, a lotus, and a supreme vessel;
and [in his left hands] are a pheṭaka, a goad, a bell, a severed head, a khaṭvāṅga, and a jar.
A blue lotus and a radiant drop shine upon her left hand;
she is adorned with divine jewels, sacrificial fire-offerings, and golden ornaments.
O Goddess, you are seated upon a white lotus throne, established in the bound-lotus posture.
Such is the Great Goddess Vāruṇī, possessing a divine form;
she is the Goddess who bestows success through gradual stages, endowed with the power of action (kriyā-śakti).
This Great Knowledge (mahāvidyā) is served as the purifier of atonement and other rites.
The goddess who brings about great peace, the remover of all diseases and afflictions.
Thus, the worship of the vessel brings success to the goddess and yields great fruit.
Na (9) || Sa (17) || Rjjhrīṃ Mahācaṇḍateja Saṃkarṣaṇi Kāli Manthānehaḥ || Caṇḍa (17) ||

Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ. Then, the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) ritual. Oṃ Paramahaṃsinī, beginning with the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). Aiṃ (five times) Hlīṃ Lrūṃ: O you who enter the womb of the enjoyments of the jewel-world, O infinite world, O mover of nectar, O God of infinite bliss, O Mother Anantāmbā, O Yoginī of infinite millions of lakhs, [I worship] the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*). [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth with the *trikhaṇḍā* mudrā. The offering (*bali*) and hymn (*stotra*).
That goddess, whose form begins with the syllable *kā*, who is filled with the enemies of ignorance, who consists of supreme nectar, and whose color is like red vermilion, possesses a divine form;
she is saluted by hosts of the best of gods and by the world-protectors.
That creation, for the sake of the cause of creation, satisfies all the hosts of gods; that goddess is divine water, the bestower of desired fruits and the eternal giver of the fortune of liberation.
This is the Mahāpātrapūjā (the worship of the Great Vessel).
Khecara! Aiṃ (5), salutation to the Viśuddhi-cakra; by means of Khecarī.
O Lord, among the sky-dwellers such as the *ṭiṭṭibha* birds, the sky-dwelling [state] is praised;
yet, although the glory of being a sky-dweller has been described, the actual birth as a sky-dweller does not exist.
Worship: Aiṃ Ymlvryūṃ, the venerable sandals of the Great Siddha Khecarī.
Meditative absorption.
O God, [I meditate upon you] with a face of blue radiance, four arms, and three eyes,
holding a trident, a rosary for recitation, and the skull of Viśvāmitra.
Mounted upon the Lord of Birds, she is established in the Viśuddhi-cakra.
Having meditated upon the sky-faring deity who bestows fortune and good luck.
Aiṃ (3). O Vāgeśvarī! Glūṃ! You who enter the womb of the enjoyments of the world of Ratnaga;
you who move through the nectar of the world of Gaganaloka; O Goddess Gagambā, the bliss of the sky! [I invoke] the sandals of the sixty-four Yoginīs and the sixty-four million *koṭi* of Siddhis.
It emerged from Candradvīpa, radiant and most beautiful.
Obeisance to you, the Lord of Kuṇḍalinī, the bestower of knowledge and realization, and the perfection of success.
Aiṃ (5) Chāṃ Chīṃ, to Mahantārikā; Hrīṃ Glūṃ, O Kalādhi; Sāṃ Sīṃ Sūṃ Smlvryūṃ, to Viśuddha Śākiṇī and the others; Śrī Khaḍgīśānanda Deva Śrī.
Glūṃ! To the form of Khecarī, accept the bali offering, svāhā! Bali. [Perform] the Saṃkṣobhaṇī mudrā. Ymlvryūṃ svāhā (ten times). Japa.
O auspicious one, you who grant the siddhis of moving through the sky and bestow all prosperity;
O Goddess, always grant me the fortune of liberation—homage to You, the Sovereign!
He who eats the boar that moves on the earth—the best of those moving on the earth—and likewise food, [attains the same].
By that [act], the earth-dwelling sin is liberated; therefore, she is called Bhūcarī.
Worship: Aiṃ, to the seat of the Anāhata Cakra (2); obeisance to Bhūcara.
Meditative absorption (dhyāna).
The body is like the color of gold, with four arms and lotus-like hands;
[holding] a book, a rosary for recitation, a staff, and a water-pot.
And he always wears a white sacred thread, which is the supreme essence of the four Vedas.
O you who eternally abide upon a swan, whose very form is Brahman, salutations to you!

Three-fold *añjali* offering: Aiṃ lmlvryūṃ, the sandals for the Great Earth-walker. Aiṃ (5) Māyāya slūṃ, she who enters the womb of the enjoyments of the jewel-like heavenly world; she who moves through the nectar of the heavenly world; O Goddess who grants the bliss of heaven; O Mother of Heaven; Sovereign of millions and billions of Yoginīs; Śrī.
O Lord of Kuṇḍalinī, salutations to you who abide in the center of the remaining nectar at the crest, whose form is the bliss of Kubjikā, and who are united with the mantra of Kālī.

Aiṃ Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhī Bahurūpāyai Hraṃ Mlūṃ! To the one who presides over the mantra, Kāṃ Kūṃ Kaḥ Kmlvryūṃ, to Anāhata-Kākinī, O Guṇapūri, Śrīvidyānandadeva, Śrī! Aiṃ Slūṃ! To the form moving on earth, accept this offering (bali)! Svāhā! Recitation: 10 times.
Obeisance to You, whose form is Brahman— the entire world-dwelling that moves upon the earth, the purifier, the cleanser of the body, the Goddess Lakṣmī who bestows the perfection of creation.
The Worship of Aquatic Creatures: Fishes and other aquatic beings such as the *guha-suśreṣṭha* are known to be of many kinds;
they are liberated from the water-pledge (*jalaśrāpa*) by those who know the third planetary influence (*graha*).
Aiṃ (3). Salutation to the seat of the Svādhiṣṭhāna cakra. Salutation to the aquatic being.
Meditative absorption (dhyāna).
Resembling the moon, snow, and jasmine, with a fish for a face and three eyes,
he holds in his ears the jewel and the discus, and in his hands the conch-vessel containing nectar.
Having meditated upon the wheel situated at the Svādhiṣṭhāna, located on a seat of a crocodile,
and upon the water-dwelling deity, one attains increase in enjoyment, fame, and prosperity.

Three handfuls of water (trayāñjali): Aiṃ Kmlvryūṃ, the sandals for the Great Aquatic Being. Mohanī Plūṃ! O you who dwell within the womb of the enjoyments of the world of jewels, O you who move through the nectar of the world of wind, O Goddess Pavanānanda, O Mother Pavanāmbā, the sandals of the sixteen hundred thousand crores of Siddhas and the sixteen hundred thousand crores of Yoginīs.
O Lord of Kuṇḍalinī, who stands in the center of a red maṇḍala,
established upon a red Kubjikā, and who bestows the knowledge of the command— homage be to you!

Aiṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ varvaraśikhe hlūṃ plūṃ varṇādhya lāṃ līṃ lūṃ laḥ lmlvryūṃ kaṇipura lākinīye mahāpūrī jhaṇṭhīnānandadeva śrīpādukāṃ | Plūṃ, to the one whose form moves in the water, accept this offering (bali), svāhā! Offering. The Sarvākarṣaṇī Mudrā. Recitation: Lmlvryūṃ svāhā.
O auspicious one, salutations to you who are born from the ocean, who are pure, the destroyer of sins, the bestower of the enjoyments of perfection, and whose form is Viṣṇu.
The remaining worship.
The remaining supreme knowledge is for the purpose of the method of arising from the stages.
The remaining [portion] is called *śrāpamukta*; they know the fourth remaining [portion] as *śeṣara*.
Worship: Homage to the seat of the Maṇipūraka cakra.
Meditative absorption.
Red in color and of great splendor, with the face of Saturn and three eyes,
holding a sword and a khaṭvāṅga in his hands, and resting his abode upon a pearl vessel.
Residing in the Maṇipūraka cakra, seated upon the Kalpavṛkṣa tree,
he likewise possesses the form of Śeṣa, bestowing wealth, grain, and enjoyment.
The triple añjali gesture.
Aiṃ Rmlvryūṃ, the sandals for Mahāsekhara.

Aiṃ, for knowledge; Mlūṃ, O you who enter the womb of the enjoyments of the mortal world of jewels; O you who move through the nectar of the mortal world; O Goddess who grants the bliss of mortals; O Mother of Mortals; O you who possess the eight hundred thousand million siddhis; O you who possess the eight hundred thousand million yoginīs; [I worship] the sandal-paste.
O Lord Kuṇḍalinī, salutations to you, who are joined with Ojā, Pūḥ, and the others, who are completely filled by the sequence of the Uddhāra, and from whom the first group of six has emerged.
Aiṃ (5) Hskhphreṃ, to Kubjikā, the Lamp of the Kula; Hrīṃ Mlūṃ, O Padādhye; Māṃ Rāṃ Rīṃ Rūṃ Raḥ Rmlvryūṃ, to Svādhisthāna Rākinī, to the Lord Īśānadeva, the Śrīpādukā.
nlūṃ, accept this offering for the form of Śeṣarāma, svāhā. Japa: rmlvryūṃ svāhā.
O you who possess the form of Rudra, salutations to you, the remainder of all seeds, the increaser of strength and vigor, the giver of enjoyment, and the source of all things.

The offering of all types of sacrificial porridge (*caru*): Aiṁ. (5) Furthermore, the remaining *caru* consists of all [the following]: the wish-fulfilling gem of milk (*kṣīracintāmaṇi*), sugar, ghee, and milk, combined with gold and curd.
It is purifying everywhere, meritorious, holy, and a cleanser of the body;
it is liberated from all sins and is the refuge of all the gods.
Worship: Hsauṃ, the *pādukā* for the seat of the Viśuddhi-cakra; the *pādukā* for the seat of Sarvacaru. (2)
Meditative absorption (dhyāna).
Resembling a dark complexion, with four arms and two eyes.
And she who stands beyond holds a lotus in her hand, while the one with the great bowl is held in her hand.
One should meditate upon the goddess Mahālakṣmī herself, seated atop the grain,
as the divine Lord who bestows all prosperity and who is the sacrificial oblation itself.
Aiṁ, the triad. Kṣmlvryūṁ, the sandals for the Great Embodiment of All Sacrificial Oblations.

Aiṁ Gāyatrī, Nlūṁ! O you who enter the womb of the enjoyments of the world of the Ratna-nāgas, who move through the nectar of the world of the Nāgas, O Goddess who is the joy of the Nāgas, O Mother of the Nāgas, [I worship] the sandals of the forty-four hundred thousand million yogis. [Pādya and other offerings.]
Obeisance to you, O Lord Kuṇḍalin, who are the fourfold, the fivefold, the sixfold, the fourfold, the fivefold, and the fourfold— the illuminator of all the islands.

Aiṃ (5). Homage to the Blessed One at the heart-lotus! Hrīṃ Nlūṃ! O you who are honored at the feet! Ḍāṃ Ḍīṃ Ḍūṃ Ḍaḥ Ḍmlvryūṃ! To the support-ḍākinī Yananipūrī, the deity Mṛtānanda, [I offer] the sandals! Nlūṃ! To the embodiment of all sacrificial offerings, accept the *bali* (2) svāhā! *Bali*! [Seal of] the Enthraller of All.

O Goddess, obeisance to you whose form is Śiva; you are the essence of all sacrificial offerings, purifying, meritorious, holy, the cleanser of the body, and the bestower of the fulfillment of desires.
The Worship of Kālī.
This supreme [practice], mixed with sugar and sesame seeds, brings joy to all;
O Kālī, it liberates one from the curse of time and destroys Time itself.
Worship.
To the one seated upon the wheel of command (ājñācakra), (2) aiṃ (5) khphreṃ, to the sandals of the goddess Kālikā, Kaṃ.
Meditative absorption.
The body resembles blue collyrium; the god has four arms and three eyes, and he holds a sword and a *phetkāra* (bell), as well as two vessels full to the brim.
Always delighting in raw flesh, she is the one who carries across the entire cycle of existence;
O Goddess, established in the Wheel of Time, you are Kālī, the destroyer of Time.
Three handfuls of water: Khphreṃ Kaṃ, the sandals of the goddess Kālikā.
Aiṃ (5) Kāli Kāli Mahākāli—this is the heart mantra.
O God, you who are joined with the lunar orb, yet distinct from fire and sun;
to this twenty-eighth deity, Kuṇḍalīśa, salutations to you!
Aiṃ (5) Khphreṃ! O Kaṅkālikā, accept this bali offering! Svāhā! (2)
Invocation and so forth; the great goad mudrā; recitation and hymn of praise.
Salutations to you, Goddess Kālikā, the bestower of pure nirvāṇa;
you who destroy disease, grief, terrible fear, and the onset of untimely death.
Longevity, merit, good fortune, and prosperity— bestowing all these riches, may the blissful sacrificial pap (caru), permeated by the Kālī mantra, grant me glory.
In this case, there is fragrance and so forth.
The Egg-Born Worship (Aṇḍajapūjā). Homage to the stainless one seated upon the lotus.
Meditation (Dhyāna):
The goddess has a brilliance like millions of moons, three eyes, and four arms; she holds a vessel of abundance and grants boons with gestures of generosity and fearlessness.
Salutations to you, the goddess Kāmasātakā, the power of Brahman.
Hrāṃ lāṃ līṃ lūṃ laṃ mlvryūṃ, the sandal of the power of action (kriyā-śakti).
Three handfuls of water offered with joined palms.
Aghore Hrāṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Saṃ (9). To the Sovereign of the Principle of Self (ātmatattva), to the Supreme Power of Action (kriyāśakti), to the Goddess Nirvāṇacaṇḍikā, Śrī!
Therefore, O Lord of Kuṇḍalinī, salutations to You who are joined with the eight [vowels] preceded by the three [consonants], and who possess the sixty-four [letters] through the letter *bha*.
Aiṁ Lmlvryūṁ! O you who possess the form born from an egg, accept this offering, svāhā! [Perform] the Khecarī mudrā for the invocation.
Hymn of Praise.
The Egg-born goddess is of the nature of Tamas; she causes the paralysis of all things.
There is no disease, grief, or fear; she is the bestower of all spiritual accomplishments.

The worship of the half-cooked offering (ardhapākapūjā): Salutation to the stainless one seated upon the lotus (nirañjana-kamalāsana). To the right: Aiṃ (five times) Rmlvryūṃ, the Śrī-pādukā of the goddess Rājasī.
Meditative absorption.
She has two hands as radiant as ten million suns, possesses three eyes,
holds a vessel of the *bindu* filled with nectar, and displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
O Goddess, whose limbs are adorned with various ornaments, who grants the perfect accomplishment of all desires and wishes,
O Goddess Rāṃ Rajasātaki, the power of Viṣṇu, salutations be unto you!

Aiṃ (5) Rāṃ Rīṃ Rūṃ Raḥ Rmlvryūṃ, the Śrī-pādukā of Kriyā-śakti. Trayāṃ! Paramaghore Hūṃ Ghorāmukhi Vama (2) Piva (2) He (2) Ru (3) Hrīṃ Hsauṃ Phreṃ Phaṭ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ, to the Lord of the Principle of Knowledge (Vidyā-tattva), to the Supreme Jñāna-śakti, to the Supreme Nirvāṇa-śakti, the Śrī-pādukā of the Goddess Nirvāṇakālī.
Oṃ au aṃ aḥ; the inclusion of the letter *ma* signifies that you reside upon the seats of the six cakras.
You are known as the perfect accomplishment of mantra; homage to you, O Lord Kuṇḍalinī!
e rmlvryūṃ, accept this offering for the white-bodied form; svāhā! (2)
The goddess Rājasīdevī, born of Śveta, bestows the state of passion;
she is for the destruction of all obstacles and the liberation from all curses.
The Kaṃca-pūjā: Homage to Nirañjana-kamalāsana; homage to Kaṃbuka-āsana. [In front:]
Meditative absorption.
I bow to the one who has ten arms, three faces, and a chest marked by the fire of his deeds,
who removes fear like the Pārijāta tree, and who is filled with the enemies of ignorance beginning with the letter 'Ka'.
O Goddess who is richly adorned with every erotic grace, who bestows all prosperity, who is peaceful yet characterized by *tamas*, O Śakti of Rudra, salutations to you!

Aiṃ yāṃ yīṃ yūṃ yaḥ ymlvryūṃ, the sandal of the power of will (icchā-śakti). Triyāṃ. Aiṃ hsphreṃ, to the Lord of the Śiva-tattva, to the Aparā power of will, to the Goddess Nirvāṇacaṇḍinī, to the Śrī. The four seats (pīṭhas) are within the body: Oḍḍiyāṇa and Jālandhara, as well as Pūrṇagiri;
likewise, having taken refuge in Kāmarūpa, O Kuṇḍalīśa, salutations to you!
Aiṃ Ymlvryūṃ! O Kaṃbuka-mūrti, accept this bali offering—svāhā! [This is] the invocation and the yoni-mudrā.
The goddess Pākajā is of the nature of Tamas; she bestows the fruit of the accomplishment of desires.
She is liberated from all suffering and is the state that brings about peace for all.
All these are the three charus.
Now follows the end of the observance.
The completion of the sacrifice, the goddess Sādevī, food until the end of the appointed time,
the consecration with blessings, and likewise the heroic feast (vīrabhojya) are the others.
Aiṃ, salutation to Kamarāsana. Aiṃ Kṣmlvryūṃ, salutation to the venerable [deity] Mahāsarvasilayāntaka.
Meditative absorption.
The goddess Sarvavarṇadhārī, with hands granting boons and fearlessness,
three-eyed and possessing great bliss, bestows happiness and the attainment of supernatural powers and accomplishments.
Three handfuls of offerings. The nine-syllable mantra: HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ.
Hymn of Praise.
The Great Goddess Samayāntā always brings about peace and nourishment;
she stands upon a blossoming lotus with her hands, holding a vessel of sindhūra filled with the letters of the Kādi alphabet and radiant with woolen luster.
The Goddess of gods, who is the supreme nectar and the form of divine drink, dwells together with the gods, sages, and perfected beings.
Resembling ten million suns, with a face slightly smiling,
that goddess Mātā Kujeśvarī bestowed the accomplishment of jewels.

Then follows the worship of the jar (*kumbhapūjā*) and the worship of the lamp (*dīpapūjā*). *Ājñācakrāsanāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the seat of the wheel of command). *Aiṃ (5) hskhphreṃ kulāgnaye pādukāṃ* (The sandals for the fire of the Kula; *Aiṃ hskhphreṃ*). *Aiṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ pādukāṃ* (The sandals for [the deity]; *Aiṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ*).
White, red, and deep black, traversing the path of the three worlds, the three goddesses with three measures—
having meditated upon them, [one sees] four hands granting desired boons, holding a power-thread and a *śruva* ladle.

May the God, who has mounted upon the great ram, who is surrounded by seven tongues of flame, who is fond of wine and meat, who is filled with oblations of clarified butter, and who pervades the entire cycle of existence—may He be victorious; [I offer] three *añjali*s.
The limbs of dissolution and the limbs of enjoyment.
Hymn of Praise.

The world, which consists of creation, destruction, and maintenance, possesses splendor dear to all the gods; it is composed of both asuras and suras, serving as the cause for all accomplishments for the seeker who desires success.

I bow to that form of light which is the assistance for all actions, composed of every virtue, present in the beginning, middle, and end, the essence of saṃsāra, and the dispeller of the darkness of ignorance.

Bali: A Caṇḍāyai baliṃ gṛhṇa (2) svāhā! Gho Ghaṇṭāyai baliṃ gṛhṇa (2) svāhā! Re Mahānāsāyai baliṃ gṛhṇa (2) svāhā! Hrāṃ Sumukhāyai baliṃ gṛhṇa (2) svāhā! Tha Durmukhāyai baliṃ gṛhṇa (2) svāhā! Gho Balāyai baliṃ gṛhṇa (2) svāhā! Re Somāyai baliṃ gṛhṇa (2) svāhā! Hrīṃ Prathamāyai baliṃ gṛhṇa (2) svāhā!

Gho! Accept the offering for Ghorā—svāhā! Raṃ! Accept the offering for Somā—svāhā! Gho! Accept the offering for Bhīmā—svāhā! Raṃ! Accept the offering for Mahābalā—svāhā! Ta! Accept the offering for Jayā—svāhā! Re! Accept the offering for Vijayā—svāhā! Hūṃ! Accept the offering for Ajitā—svāhā! Sa! Accept the offering for Aparājitā—svāhā! Rvva! Accept the offering for Mahotkaṭā—svāhā!
To Śuṣkā, accept this offering, svāhā! To Saṃhāriṇī, accept this offering, svāhā! To Aṃbikā, accept this offering, svāhā!

To her who carries away the newborn, accept this offering, svāhā! To her who has terrible eyes, accept this offering, svāhā! Jūṃ! To the goddess Śuṣkaravatī, accept this offering, svāhā! To her who carries away flowers, accept this offering, svāhā! Na! To Asamyā, accept this offering, svāhā! Ma! To Saṃhāriṇī, accept this offering, svāhā! Ste! To Vadrakālī, accept this offering, svāhā! Ru! To Bhadrā, accept this offering, svāhā!
Dra, accept this offering for Rudrā; svāhā! Rū, accept this offering for Bhīmā; svāhā! Pe, accept this offering for Subhākā; svāhā! Hra, accept this offering for Bhadrabhīmā; svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃḥ Hskhphreṃ; having kindled [the fire] with this, one should recite.
May Vighna bestow constant well-being; may Mārtaṇḍabhairava grant well-being;
may all the Yoginīs grant well-being; and may the sacred seats (pīṭhas) and the fields (kṣetras) grant well-being.
The navel-cavity has arisen, enchanting with its power and lamp,
supremely luminous and divine, born of knowledge and higher realization.
The deity of the family fire, who consumes the oblations, is satisfied; may she grant well-being.
All the deities have been worshipped; salutations to you, who are the form of light.
One should wave the three lamps, which are blazing and destroyers of evil;
they indeed burn away all sins committed throughout seven lifetimes.
This lamp is for the three times, dispelling the darkness everywhere.
It illuminates all lamps, purifies the body,
and emerges from the moon-lamp, fulfilling all aspirations.
May there be well-being, peace, constant prosperity, and auspiciousness;
by the mere sight of the island, may all desires be fulfilled.
The Goddess, the Yoginī of the Gaṇas, who brings about all peace, is to be saluted.
Pūjā || Na (9) || HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ || Gāyatrīnaṃ || Bali ||
Hymn of Praise.

You are the form of creation, dissolution, and maintenance; you are the world, the beloved of all gods, and the cause of all perfections. You are the host of asuras and suras, the fulfillment of all desires for practitioners, the imitator of all actions, composed of all virtues, and abiding in the beginning, middle, and end.
I bow to that form of light, which is the cause of the essence of saṃsāra and the dispeller of darkness.
The Jvālinī mudrā.
One should prostrate by touching the ground with the forehead. Rotation is performed with the *saṃvarta* thread. The worshiper is *utphullī*. That which is the fire of destruction (*sāntakāgni*).

The inner radiance and the outer radiance are all manifestations free from affliction; one should abandon the grasping at a body with its afflictions—the intermediate state—and transcend the six supreme [objects].
I consume that lamp which has arisen thereafter— resembling primordial awakening, dispelling the darkness of ignorance, and bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Aiṃ (5) Amṛte (2), svāhā to the one arisen from nectar, Vajrakubjinī!
One should cause [the disciple] to consume it according to the instruction. This is the consumption of the sky-farer (khecara).
I bow to her who is born from the great samaya, arisen from the divine assembly,
endowed with the nine substances, and joined with Kubjī.
The devouring of those who roam the earth.
This offering of remains (nirmālya) is stainless and a purifier for the body;
it should be consumed as a grace, O Kubjikā, beloved of the gods—salutations to you!
The consumption of aquatic creatures.
Fish-meat, great meat, rice, condiments, and sacrificial porridge—the divine sixfold porridge beloved by Kubjikā; salutations to you!
The consumption of the remainder.

O Kubjikā, who is pure through the knowledge of the command, radiant in the discipline of Brahman, merged in the word "Tejo 'si" (Thou art splendor), and joined with the syllable *yuṣ*, salutations to you!
The consumption of all sacrificial oblations.
Having drawn a central triangle, a hexagon, an eight-petaled lotus, an eight-peaked mountain, and four gates in this manner, one should perform worship.

"Aghoravatī asi. With "Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ," perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Therein is a single island; again, the recitation of the fourfold and fivefold [mantras]. This is the circumambulation of the lamp (*dīpabhramaṇa*).

O Goddess, you who are worthy of all salutations, to whom all the gods have gathered; your sight is purifying and meritorious, your touch destroys sin, and you bestow the happiness of worldly enjoyment and liberation, as well as prosperity and fortune.
The act of sitting down.
By this method, a mortal who practices with concentrated mind becomes liberated from all sins and attains the state of one who abides within the range of the Command.
O pierced one, (2) accomplished in the three worlds, emerged from the lamp of the moon, hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

Then follows the wandering of the bowl (*pātrabhramaṇa*), the consumption of the egg-born (*aṇḍajaprāśana*), "Aiṃ! She who is called the power of the womb (*śaktibhaga*)," *santāna*, *saṃvarttā*, the ego-principle of creation (*sarggāhaṃkāra*), and *varṣantī*.
The three circumambulations; the end of the observance; the gratified spirits; the Jayantikā rite; the rice-offering with the mudrā; and the dismissal of the sacrificial offerings.
In the assembly of the Vīracakra, all castes are considered twice-born;
however, once the Cakra has ended, all castes remain distinct from one another.

Food, the end of the skull-cup, betel, and the consecration with the water-pot—these should be held in an unbroken stream before the Deity. The King, knelt upon the ground, [offers] flowers and unbroken rice-grains together with yellow powder, supported by the foundation of the unbroken mandala.
Having propitiated the God of Gods, may there always be long life, sons, fame, glory, the end of obstacles, abundant prosperity, auspiciousness, and well-being.
Salutations to you, whose form is Bhairava, who has manifested in the form of a hero,
joined with Vīraṇī and Bhairavī, the deity among all the gods.
She is Sāṃbhavī, accompanied by her attendants, the Supreme Goddess who manifests all incarnations.
Whether the worship be deficient or excessive, provided it is performed without flaw, it is complete.
O Supreme Lord, may You forgive me in its entirety with Your whole being.
Depart, depart, O all attendants; go to Your respective abodes and dissolve into the source.
Protect, protect me, O Great Goddess, for the sake of victory once again!
The mutual mental attention that gives birth to heroes; three claps of the hands. These are the signs of the accomplished fire, the lamp, and the vigil in the north.

Then follows the procedure for the fourth rite (*caturthī-karma-vidhi*): *Oṃ adyādi* [and so forth]. The patron (*yajamāna*) [offers] a vessel of flowers. The worship of the *Śiva-śakti* pitcher. One should cause the sacrificial rites and other ceremonies to be performed according to the rules. This is the garland of sacrificial procedures.

Now follows the worship of the jar (*kalaśārcana*), salutation to the Guru, the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the *Mṛtyuñjaya* mantra, the worship of the water vessel and the *argha* vessel, purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*), self-worship (*ātmapūjā*), and [the invocation] beginning with "O Support-Power" (*ādhāraśakti*). (8)
She has three eyes and six arms, is peaceful, adorned with matted locks and a crescent moon,
holds a skull-cup in her hand, carries a shield, and is seated in the yogic posture.
Rudra is clothed in a tiger skin, adorned with lordly serpents,
and holds a trident and a rosary in his right hands.
One should depict the god Mṛtyuñjaya, the destroyer of death and disease, holding a skull-bowl and a water-pot in his left hands, while both hands are joined in the yoga-mudrā.
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, homage to Mṛtyuñjaya, who possesses a multitude of hands that grant all things in their entirety. (3)
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to the one accompanied by the power Amṛtasaṃjīvanī. [Bali offering: Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā; salutation to Viṣṇu; salutation to Rudra.

Salutations to Sadāśiva. Salutations to Īśvara. Salutations to the seven oceans beginning with the Gaṅgā. Salutations to the fortnights. Salutations to the months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa. Salutations to the seasons. Salutations to the year. Salutations to the seven oceans beginning with the salt ocean (Kṣāra). Salutations to the lunar days (tithis) beginning with Nandā. Salutations to the asterisms (nakṣatras) beginning with Aśvinī. Salutations to the astrological conjunctions (yogas) beginning with Viṣkambha. Salutations to the auspicious moments (muhūrtas). Salutations to the nine planets beginning with Āditya.

Salutation to Mekhā and the twelve zodiac signs (*dvādaśarāśi*). Salutation to Vasiṣṭha and the seven sages (*saptarṣi*). Salutation to Asvasthāman and the long-lived weapon-deities (*astraciraṃjīvin*). Salutation to Indra and the ten world-protectors (*daśaloka-pāla*). Salutation to Ananta and the eight lineage-nāgas (*aṣṭakulanāga*). [Salutation to] the sandals of the goddess Śrī Rudracaṇḍā, beginning with Rudracaṇḍa. (8) Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ. Salutation to the form of the full water-pot (*saṃpūrṇakalaśamūrti*). Offering (*bali*). Three *añjali* gestures.

Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ. Obeisance to the Great Army of the Kula Tree, to the Deluder, to the deities of the mantras of all sacred sites, to the Kalās and the Tattvas, to the Lord of the Tattvas, to the essence of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra, and to the Tattvas of Ātman, Vidyā, and Śiva: Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ. Obeisance to the venerable form of the Full Jar. [Offer] the bali. [Perform] the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga).

Hnasakana || Śrī Namaḥ || Siṃdhrāmūṅa || Lakṣmī Namaḥ || To Indra, Namaḥ || To Agni, Namaḥ || To Yama, Namaḥ || To Nairṛtya, Namaḥ || To Varuṇa, Namaḥ || To Vāyavya, Namaḥ || To Kubera, Namaḥ || To Īśāna, Namaḥ || To Adhaśchanda, Namaḥ || To Ūrddhachanda, Namaḥ || To Gaṇapati, Namaḥ || To the Gurus, Namaḥ || To Kṣetrapāla and the Yoginīs, Namaḥ || To Yakṣa, Namaḥ ||

Homage to Yakṣaṇī. Śrī Lakṣmī. Nāgarāja. Mṛtyuñjaya. Āditya. Sthaṇḍila. These are the directional jars (digkalaśas). The altar (vedī). Oṃ, homage to Brahmā. Oṃ, homage to Siddheśvara. Oṃ, homage to Śivādevī. Oṃ, homage to Māyādevī. These belong to the altar. The eight pillars (staṃbhāṣṭaka): Oṃ, homage to Gajāsana. Luṃ, homage to Indrastambha. Homage to Chāgāsana. Rūṃ, homage to Agnistambha.

Salutation to the one seated upon a buffalo; *mūṃ*, salutation to the pillar of Yama; salutation to the one seated upon a corpse; *kṣuṃ*, salutation to the pillar of Nairṛti; salutation to the one seated upon Garuḍa; *aṃ*, salutation to the pillar of Ananta; salutation to the one seated upon a makara; *vuṃ*, salutation to the pillar of Varuṇa; salutation to the one seated upon a deer; *yūṃ*, salutation to the pillar of Vāyu; salutation to the one seated upon a rat; *gaṃ*, salutation to the pillar of Gaṇapati; salutation to the one seated upon a horse.

Oṃ, obeisance to the Kubera pillar; obeisance to the bull-seated one; Huṃ, obeisance to the Īśāna pillar; obeisance to the swan-seated one; Oṃ, obeisance to the Brahmā pillar. [These are for] the four corners.

To Duthokāpayā, obeisance to Garuḍāsana. Laṃ, obeisance to Sadyojātastaṃbha; obeisance to Vṛṣāsana. Vaṃ, obeisance to Vāmadevastaṃbha; obeisance to Savāsana. Raṃ, obeisance to Aghorastaṃbha; obeisance to Haṃsāsana. Yaṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣastaṃbha. Thus ends the Octad of Stambhas.
Now follows the section on the eight stakes.

Luṃ, obeisance to Indra. Ruṃ, obeisance to Agni. Muṃ, obeisance to Yama. Kṣuṃ, obeisance to Nairṛtya. Vuṃ, obeisance to Varuṇa. Yuṃ, obeisance to Vāyu. Suṃ, obeisance to Kubera. Hūṃ, obeisance to Īśāna. Thus ends the eightfold *kīlaka*.

Now, the four gates: Salutation to the eastern gate of the Śānti-kalā. Salutation to the southern gate of the Vidyā-kalā. Salutation to the western gate of the Nivṛtti-kalā. Salutation to the northern gate of the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā. Thus, the four gates.
Salutation to Agneya. Salutation to Nandā. Salutation to Bhadrā. Salutation to Jayā. Salutation to Ṛktā. Salutation to Pūrṇā. Thus ends the [salutation] beginning with Nandā.
Just as is the worship of the deity’s stepped mandala.

The *bali* for the root-vessel: Aśitāṅga and the others. (8) Aiṁ (5) Ṭaṁ Ṭhaṁ Ḍaṁ Ḍhaṁ Ṇaṁ KMLVRYŪṂ Śrīvaiṣṇavī Vicce Pādukāṁ. (3) The *bali*. The *hṛdaya* and the others. The great *bali* of Tvaṣṭṛ. The invocation and the others. Dukhā Pikhā. Accept the *bali* from all beings, Svāhā! Vaccharā Devī. The three deities. With the root-mantra of the West. (3) With the nine-syllable mantra. (3)
The bali offering; the heart and other limbs; the great bali for Tvaṣṭṛ; the invocation and so forth; the respective mudrās.

Thāna Laṃkhu. (5) || Aiṃ (5) Thrauṃ! The sandalwood sandals of the goddess Dambhaki at Prastaradvīpa, the great field of darkness. The offering. The heart-mantra and others. The great *tvāka* offering. The invocation and others. The *tarjani* mudrā.

The goddesses of the site; the three deities; the root mantra of the west; the bali offering; the heart-mantra and others; the great bali for Tvaṣṭṛ; the invocation and other rites; their respective mudrās.
The worship of Gaṇa by Godāja. Homage to the one whose vehicle is a rat. Three handfuls of water (triyāñjali). (3) Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ, homage to the Kulagaṇeśvara. The offering (bali).

Now, the worship of the bull and the attendants: Oṃ, obeisance to Nanda; Oṃ, obeisance to Subhadra; Oṃ, obeisance to Subhīma; Oṃ, obeisance to Suśīra; Oṃ, obeisance to Sumanohara. [Thus] the offering of the oblation.

Now, the worship of Kumārī: *namaḥ* to the Peacock Throne (*mayūrāsana*). *caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ kmlvryūṃ caṃ*, *namaḥ* to Caṇḍabhairava accompanied by the maiden (*komārī*). (3 times) The offering (*bali*).
Now, the worship with the *sagona* [offering]. Three *añjali*s. (3)

[Perform] the invocation and so forth with three handfuls of water and the nine-syllable root mantra. [Offer] incense, lamps, recitation, and hymns. I declare my refuge in You alone—the primordial deity Bhairava, known as Mṛtyuñjaya (the Conqueror of Death)—who is worshipped by the guardians of the celestial worlds, headed by Brahmā, and who is praised by those offering oblations and libations.
"O chosen deity, salutations to you," and so forth. Herein lies the offering of perfumes and other items. Thus concludes the worship of the vessel and the bali offerings.

Then, having gone near the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), the Hotṛ priest, facing north, proceeds in order to the seat of the Sacrificial Lion (yajñasiṃhāsana). He performs the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) by means of the three principles (tritatva): *Khphreṃ hrāṃ ātmatattvāya svāhā* *Khphreṃ hrīṃ vidyātattvāya svāhā* *Khphreṃ hrūṃ śivatattvāya svāhā*
The offering to the Sun (sūryārgha). Oṃ, from today onwards... [the formula].
Having extracted the seed-syllable at the end of the vowels, one should place Śiva upon it;
it is adorned by the three fires at its beginning, middle, and end.
Having ignited it with the *varman* mantra, one should extract this [mantra] with the *sāvitrī*;
this is the supreme *kūṭacara*, the Great Mārtaṇḍa Bhairava.
Argha, obeisance! Flower, obeisance! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hreṃ hroṃ hraḥ hrīṃ saḥ, obeisance to the glorious Kulamārttaṇḍa Mahābhairava, together with the Śakti Prakāśa!
Rhrkṣrīṃ, salutation to the illustrious Mahāmārttaṇḍa Bhairava.
Salutation to the Gurus. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsoṃḥ.
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded.
The ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *khphreṃ sakalaśatrupramathani astrāya phaṭ*. (4) The destruction of the enemy's wealth.
Khphreṃ, salutation to Paramahaṃsinī at the thumb.
KHPHREṂ! O Goddess who bestows the path to nirvāṇa, svāhā with the threatening gesture!
KHPHREṂ! O you who pacify the surging of poisons, VOṢAṬ to the central illusion!
KHPHREṂ! O you who crush all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions! HŪṂ to the ring finger!
KHPHREṂ! O you who ferry across the ocean of all calamities, Kaniṣṭhakāya, VAṢAṬ!
KHPHREṂ! O you who crush all enemies, PHAṬ to the weapon-mantra!
Thus is the placement of the hand (kara-nyāsa).
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Yoginīs of Accomplishment; the sandal of the Lord of the Upper Face.
KH PHREṂ NAMAḤ SARVAMĀTRBHYO PŪRVAVAKTRANĀTHA PĀDUKĀM ||
Khphreṃ! Homage to the one who is eternally arisen bliss, the source of joy; O Lord of the southern face, [I worship] your sandals!
KH PHREṂ: To the Mistress of the entire wheel of families, the Lord of the northern face, [I offer] the sandals.
KH PHREṂ! To the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī, the Mistress of the Western Face, [I offer] the sandals.
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Yoginīs of Accomplishment; the sandal of the Lord of the Upper Face.
Thus is the placement of the face.
KH PHREṂ | Homage to the heart of the Supreme Swaness, the state of omniscience.
KH PHREṂ | To Nirvāṇamārgadādevī, svāhā at the head!
KH PHREṂ! O you who destroy the flood of poisons, primordial awakening! VAU PHAṬ for the crest-jewel!
KHPHREṂ! To the independent armor that destroys all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions, HŪṂ!
KHPHREṂ! To the one who crosses the ocean of all calamities, whose power is unimpeded, to the three eyes—VAṢAṬ!
KHPHREṂ! O you who crush all enemies, PHAṬ to the weapon!
Thus concludes the ritual assignment of the limbs (aṅganyāsa).

To the water-vessel: salutations to Samdrāya. To the boar-faced one with flowers and fragrance: salutations. This is the worship of the water-vessel. Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, the sandals for the seat of the water-vessel.

The Dhenu-mudrā. Sprinkling (prokṣaṇa). The Gāyatrī: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, may we know Siddhi-Lakṣmī; may we meditate upon her who possesses ninety [forms]; may that Lakṣmī inspire us. Sprinkling of all things, beginning with oneself.
The worship of the argha vessel: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the pādukā for the seat of the argha vessel.
Hrīṃ śrīṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ, vauṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava.

Having invoked [the deities], perform the mudrās, incense (dhūpa) and so forth, the recitation (japa), and the hymn of praise (stotra). Taking the fire: the fire of the sun’s transgression (*sūryakrānti*), the fire of the nobility (*kṣatrāgni*). The cleansing with mustard seeds and rājikā [black mustard] is performed with the Astra-mantra.
The offering of bali.

and may those beings who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva.
Lamp! Well-illuminated!

Oṃ hrīṃ hrāṃ kraṃ to the flesh-eaters, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! [Offer] three oblations to Kuśavyāṅa, Vakravyāda, and Agnipika. (3) Aiṃ (5) hrāṃ to the flesh-eating fire, svāhā! (3) Aiṃ (5) to the flesh-eating fire, svāhā! [Offer] clarified butter as well. Having offered the bali-oblation to the flesh-eating fire with the Astra-mantra, one should cast it outside.
The ritual sipping of water.
Again, the purification by pure fire. The ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *rāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*, and so forth.

The fourfold ritual action (*catuḥsaṃskāra*): inspection with the Root Mantra; sprinkling with the Weapon Mantra; striking with that [same mantra]; veiling with the Armor Mantra; and sprinkling with the Fire-Gāyatrī: "We know Vaiśvānara, we meditate upon Jātavedas; may Agni inspire us. Having united the consciousness (*caitanya*) in the fire with *Raṃ*, one should contemplate the unity of the fires—the digestive, the lunar, and the earthly. Having consecrated it with the *Praṇava*, one should transform it into nectar using the *vam* syllable and the Cow Mudrā.
Having protected it with the Astra-mantra and enveloped it with the Kavaca-mantra, [one should worship] with "Oṃ Raṃ, obeisance to Vahni," honoring him with perfumes and other offerings.
Having taken up the fire with the nine-syllable mantra.
Aiṁ (5) HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ: having rotated three times within the fire-pit, which is the womb of fuel.

The ritual formula (*vākya*) is as follows: having pronounced the ritual action (*kāryam*), [one says]: *aiṃ (5) hūṃ aiṃ hskhphreṃ agnisthāpanaṃ sumuhūrttāstu agnisthāpanaṃ*. *oṃ kroṃ rīṃ rīṃ rūṃ vahni-caitanyāya svāhā*. *haṃ (9) sa (9) śrīsaṃvarttā utphullāṃ*.
Worship with the six limbs beginning with the heart. Worship of the fire: Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Śrīṃ Gneṃ Hūṃ Śruṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā.
One should recite the words of benediction.
May she who is ever free from obstacles grant well-being; may Mārtaṇḍa likewise grant well-being;
may all the Yoginīs grant well-being; and may the Pīṭhas and Kṣetras grant well-being.
In the east, south, west, and likewise in the northern half above;
she who abides in the sixfold arrival of *svasti* is both hidden and manifest as the deity.
Bhairava and Bhairavī, together with their limbs, [grant] well-being; svah, svah, svah, the wheels!
Their own mantras, their own mudrās, their own weapons, and their retinues— established in the planets, lunar mansions, and zodiac signs— may there be well-being for all beings in the eighth [state].
May there be well-being from the heroic Aprameyā, from the Yoginī, and from the Leader of the Gaṇas;
may there be constant well-being from the King of Mantras, who is the God above all gods.
May the deities of the family fire be satisfied by the oblations and grant well-being;
may the king bring welfare to his subjects, and may there be well-being for the sacrificer at all times.

The five-fold offering (pañcabali): the offering at the edge of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), the offering at the corner of the pit, the offering at the entrance of the pit, the worship of Vaṭuka, Kṣetrapāla, Yoginī, Cāmuṇḍā, and Gaṇeśa; the offering, the ritual gesture (mudrā), the recitation (japa), and the hymn of praise (stotra).
O Three Deities! Having performed the worship of the seat, the offering, and the mudrās; having offered water for sipping with the heart-mantra; and having worshipped the consciousness.
Having covered it with the armor-mantra as fuel: *oṃ hrāṃ citrapiṅgala hana (2) paca (2) daha (2) sarvajñāpaya svāhā*.
I pay homage to that blazing fire, the consumer of oblations, who has appeared;
he is golden-hued, stainless, kindled, and facing in all directions.

Sprinkling with the Astra-mantra. Breaking the dice. The altar as the seat. Aiṃ pādukāṃ | Hrīṃ pādukāṃ | Śrīpādukāṃ | Hsphreṃ pādukāṃ. On the head-knot of the Kuśa-grass bundle, in the east: Brahmaṇe namaḥ. To the one whose form is Brahman (twice). The Heart-mantra (five times): Glūṃ Oḍiyānapīṭha Śrīpā (three times). The offering (bali). In the south: Oṃ Siddheśvarāya (twice). Oṃ Siddhilakṣmīmūrtaye (twice). The Heart-mantra.

(5) *Sūṃ* Jālandhara-pīṭha Śrīpā [duka] || Bali. West: *Oṃ khphreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ* to Śiva (2 times). *Oṃ* to the form of Goddess Śivā (2 times). Heart-mantra: *Oṃ mlūṃ* Kāmarūpa-pīṭha Śrīpā [duka] || Bali.

Kuṇḍaṅuvadvadusa. [This is] the facing of Agni. Aiṁ (5). I worship the sandals of this seat for Brahmā. [This is] Brahmā. Aiṁ (5). Homage to this seat for Praṇītā. [This is] Praṇītā. Aiṁ.
