The consecration of the *praṇīta* water: sprinkling with the water from the *argha* vessel using the *astra-mantra* (*aiṃ*); satiating with the *kavaca-mantra*; wiping with *kuśa* grass using the *astra-mantra*. *Aiṃ (5) hrīṃ*, the sandals for the Amṛtagaṅgā. In the place where speech is stainless and free from sin, the worship of Brahmā: *Aiṃ (5) hrīṃ*, the sandals for Brahmā; *Aiṃ (5) hrauṃ*, the sandals for the Four-Faced One; *Aiṃ (5)*, the sandals for the Creator of Emanation. This is the worship of the *praṇīta* water.
Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ, the sandals of Praṇīta. Hrīṁ, obeisance to Viṣṇu. Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ, the sandals of Paramātman.
To the south, the installation of Brahmā; to the north, the installation of the Praṇīta vessel; and worship as before.
The strewing with *kuśa* grass is performed with the *hṛdaya-mantra*.

The worship of the Fire (*vahnipūjanam*): *Oṃ vaiśvānara jātaveda iha āvaha lohitākṣa sarvakarmāṇi sādhaya svāhā*. Then follows the preparation of the ritual implements (*arthavadāsādhanam*): on the right side, the water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*), the flower-vessel, the three-fold strainers (*tripavitra*) and their cutting instruments, the *prokṣaṇī* vessel, the primary cooking pot (*sthālī*), the vessel for the sacrificial porridge (*caru*), the *śruk* and *śruva* ladles, the cleansing brush (*saṃmārjana*), the under-wood (*upayamana*), two fuel-sticks (*samidh*), the mortar and pestle, the sun-seed (*sūrya*) and other sesame seeds, rice grains, the rosary for recitation (*jāpyamālā*), the vessel for the priestly fee (*dakṣiṇā*), pairs of items, and the suspension cord (*ālaṃbana*).
With the heart.

The cutting of the *pavitra* [strainer] is performed with the *astra-mantra*; the binding of the *pavitra* with the *hṛdaya-mantra*. Having washed the *prokṣaṇī* vessel with the *astra-mantra*, one performs the libation (*pratarpaṇa*) with the *hṛdaya-mantra*. The *pañcagavya* is prepared with the *kavaca-mantra*; the sweeping (*saṃmārjana*) with the *astra-mantra*; the filling with water with the *hṛdaya-mantra*; the stirring with the *pavitra* and the *śiras-mantra*; and the three circumambulations of the courtyard with the *netra-mantra*. One should sprinkle all the ritual materials and oneself with the *mūla-mantra*. Then, having placed the *prokṣaṇī* between the fire and the *praṇītā* vessel—

Then follows the purification of the *śruk* and *śruva* ladles, consisting of the four consecrations: (4) washing with the *astra-mantra*, satiating with the *hṛdaya-mantra*, and wiping with the *astra-mantra*.

Having sprinkled [the materials] with *prokṣaṇī* water while reciting the *Kavaca* mantra, one performs the purification by means of the *tritatva*. With the root of the *kuśa* grass, one joins the root of the *śruva* ladle; with the middle part, the middle; and with the tip, the tip. One wraps them in the reverse order of their growth (*lomaviloma*). One encircles the necks with a triple thread. Then, using purified *kuśa* grass as a seat, one settles upon it.

One should consecrate the vessel for clarified butter (ājyasthālī) and the vessel for the fourfold offerings (carusthālī). Having washed them with the Astra-mantra, one should perform the satiation with the Hṛdaya-mantra and the wiping with the Astra-mantra.

Taking the clarified butter (*ghṛta*), perform the four purificatory rites beginning with inspection (*nirīkṣaṇa*). Place it in the vessel of clarified butter while reciting the *Hṛdaya-mantra*. Purify the fire while reciting the *Hṛdaya-mantra*. Sprinkle [the butter] three times with the tips of two *kuśa* blades while reciting the *Hṛdaya-mantra*. Stir the clarified butter three times from left to right while reciting the *Hṛdaya-mantra*.
Having pierced the mouth of the deer with a weapon, he was struck by a hunter from a nearby thicket.

With the *hṛdaya* mantra, one performs the satiation (*pratarpaṇa*); with the *kavaca*, the sprinkling (*abhyukṣaṇa*); with the *śikhā*, the stirring of the clarified butter (*ājyāloḍana*); with the *astra*, the floating over [the vessel] twice with two *kuśa*-grains; with the *hṛdaya*, the immersion (*saṃplavana*); and with the *kavaca*, the sprinkling of oneself (*ātmānam abhyukṣaṇa*).
Worship: sandalwood paste and so forth. Aiṃ (5) obeisance to the five *praṇavas*.
The Dhenu-mudrā; the inspection of the clarified butter (ājya).
Having seen that clarified butter (ājya) removes sin, clarified butter is the supreme remover of sin;
all the hosts of gods reside in clarified butter, for everything is established in clarified butter.

And the *prokṣaṇī* waters are prepared as before. Stirring with the head-mantra and the *pavitra*; three times toward the north with the eye-mantra; sprinkling the fire with the root mantra; circling the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with the armor-mantra—(3)—one should offer oblations into the fire: *oṃ bhuvapataye svāhā*, *oṃ bhuvanapataye svāhā*, *oṃ bhūtānāṃ pataye svāhā*. Having placed the remaining water into the *praṇīta* vessel, one [offers] the *sāvitra* and the sword of knowledge (*jñānakhaḍga*).

Then, the worship of the *śruk* and *śruva* ladles: *Hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ khphreṃ*, [I worship] the *śrīpādukā* of Siddheśvara Mahābhairava. *Śruk*: [I worship] the *śrīpādukā* of Śrīsiddhilakṣmī. *Śruva*: *Oṃ hsauṃ*, obeisance to Śiva and Śakti.
Taking the *upayamana* kuśa grass with the Astra mantra; the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*); the Yoni-mudrā.

The ritual of the ten fire-offerings: Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to the rite of conception with the Heart-mantra. Aiṃ (5) Pūṃ Svāhā to the rite of hearing [the sacred words]. Aiṃ (5) With the Śiras-mantra, Svāhā to the rite of parting the hair. Aiṃ (5) With the Śikhā-mantra, Svāhā to the rite of birth.

Aiṃ (5). With the mouth of the higher and lower [energies], for the first feeding of solid food, svāhā!

Aiṃ (5), with the eastern face, for the piercing of the ears, svāhā!

Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to the Fourth Face, which is both transcendent and immanent.
The installation of the fire (agnipratiṣṭhā) should be performed with the nine-syllable [mantra] of five faces; it is full of fire.

Aiṁ (5). From the rite of conception onwards, through the tenfold series of sacraments, fully endowed with ritual acts, adorned with all ornaments, possessing every excellence, and accompanied by the seven-tongued fire—O Lord Śrī Bhairava, may this fire, together with the nine-fold accomplishment, be eternally well-established through the offering of clarified butter with the *jālāmuṣṭi* mudrā according to the prescribed rule.

O Lord, may the fire of Śrī Bhairava— endowed with its own installation and other rites from the beginning, increased tenfold by perfect rituals, adorned with all ornaments, possessing every quality, and indeed accompanied by the seven tongues of flame— be forever well-established when offered oblations of a handful of parched grain with ghee, together with the nine-fold accomplishment (siddhi) and according to the prescribed rule.
The dismissal of the fire’s parents. Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the ten-fold duties of the Agnīdhra.
Meditative absorption.
Mounted upon Aries, one should offer eighteen or sixteen fuel-sticks with the Mūla mantra.
Having placed one [syllable] with the *praṇava* and one in the *praṇīta*, there is the meditative cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

The perfected fire (siddhāgni) is surrounded by the eight Bhairavas, such as Asitāṅga and others; the eight cremation grounds, such as Karavīra and others; the six Ḍākinīs and the six Yoginīs and others; and encircled by Brahmāṇī and the rest.

The striking together of the wheels: Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to Sadyojāta. Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to Vāmadeva. Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to Aghora. Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to Tatpuruṣa. Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to Īśāna. The joining of the faces: Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to Sadyojāta and Vāmadeva. Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to Vāmadeva and Aghora.
Aiṃ (5) Aghorāya Tatpuruṣāya Svāhā. Aiṃ (5) Tatpuruṣāya Īśānāya Svāhā. Aiṃ (5) Īśānāya Sadyojātāya Svāhā. Thus is the joining of the faces.
Aiṁ (5). Svāhā to Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa, and Īśāna. This is the unification of the faces.
To Agni, svāhā! Aiṃ (5) To Agni, the maker of well-being, svāhā! The destruction of the eyes. Aiṃ (5) To Agni and Soma, svāhā! The removal of saliva. The oblation for the tongue.
Aiṃ (5) Prūṃ, svāhā to Rājadāyī. [East] (1).
Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to the mother of Śrudāghada! [This is] in the southeast. (2)
Aiṃ (5) Vrūṃ, svāhā to Mṛtyudāyā! [In the south. (3)
Aiṃ (5) Śrūṃ, svāhā to Śatrukālikā. [Direction: Nairṛtya. (4) ||
Aiṃ (5) Vrūṃ, svāhā to Vaśikā; in the west. (5) ||
Aiṁ (5) Prūṁ, svāhā to Uccāṭanī! In the northwestern direction. (6)
Aiṃ (5) Hrūṃ, svāhā to Arthapadā in the northern direction. (7) ||
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ, svāhā to Muktidāyā. [In the] Īśāna [direction]. (8)
Aiṃ (5) Kṣrīṃ, salutation to Sarvasiddhi.

Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Sūrya. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Candra. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Yogīśvara. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Mahāyogīśvara. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Tṛṣṭubs. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Ṛṣis. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Ā-Ṛṣis. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to all [the Ṛṣis]. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Devas. Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the Tridevas.
Homage to the gods in the north; *svadhā* to the ancestors in the south.
Oṃ, svāhā to Indra! Oṃ, svāhā to this for Indra!
The Eye-Oblation (*cakṣuhoma*): Taking clarified butter from the southern portion with the *hṛdaya-mantra*, [offer it] into the right eye: *oṃ hrāṃ agnaye svāhā*. This is for Agni.
In the left eye, from the left side: *oṃ hrāṃ somāya svāhā*. This is for Soma. In the third eye, from the middle part: *oṃ hrāṃ agniṣomābhyāṃ svāhā*. This is for Agni and Soma.
Taking the clarified butter along with the strainer into the mouth of the fire: *Oṃ hrāṃ agnaye sviṣṭikṛtaye svāhā*. This is for Agni Sviṣṭikṛt.
The Tongue-Homage: Aiṃ (5) Plūṃ, svāhā to Rājadāyī. [Offer] in the east. (1) ||
Aiṃ (5) Llūṃ, svāhā to the Mother who burns away all afflictions. [This is] the Āgneya [mantra]. (2)
Aiṃ (5) Vlūṃ, svāhā to Mṛtyudāyī. [In the south. (3) ||
Aiṃ (5) Ślūṃ, svāhā to Śatrukārikā! [Direction: Nairṛtya. (4) ||
Aiṁ (5) ṣlūṁ, svāhā to Vaśikā. [This is] in the western direction. (5) ||
Aiṁ (5) Slūṁ, svāhā to Uccāṭanī in the northwest (6).
Aiṃ (5) Hrūṃ, svāhā to Arthapradāyā in the north. (7) ||
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ, svāhā to Muktidāyā. [In the] Īśāna [direction]. (8) ||
Aiṃ (5) Kṣrīṃ, svāhā to the Giver of All Siddhis. [In the center. (9)
Thus ends [the section on] Navajihvā.
The tongue is the junction. Aiṃ (5) Ylūṃ, svāhā to Rājadāyī; Llūṃ, svāhā to Dāghadājananī.
Aiṃ (5) Llūṃ, svāhā to the Mother of Fever, Vlūṃ, svāhā to the Giver of Death!
Aiṃ (5) Vlūṃ, svāhā to Mṛtyudāyā; Ślūṃ, svāhā to Śatrukārikā.
Aiṃ (5) Ślūṃ, svāhā to Śatrukārikā; Ṣlūṃ, svāhā to Vaśikā.
Aiṃ (5) Ṣlūṃ, svāhā to Vaśikā; Slūṃ, svāhā to Uccāṭanī.
Aiṃ (5) Slūṃ, svāhā to Uccāṭanī, Hrūṃ, svāhā to Arthapradā.
Aiṃ (5) Hrūṃ, svāhā to her who bestows wealth; Hrīṃ, svāhā to her who bestows liberation.
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ, obeisance to the Giver of Liberation; Kṣlīṃ, obeisance to the Giver of All Siddhis; Svāhā!
Astrāya phaṭ svāhā! This is the severing of the nine tongues.
The placement of a single tongue.
Aiṃ (5) Kṣmīṃ, svāhā to the giver of all accomplishments!
aiṃ (5) hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ khphreṃ svāhā ||
Then follows the sprinkling of the mouth: *oṃ haṃ sadyojātāya svāhā* | [This is performed] in the west, accompanied by the renunciation (*tyāga*).
Oṃ hiṃ vāmadevāya svāhā || [In the] north. Oṃ hūṃ aghorāya svāhā || [In the] south.
Oṃ heṃ, svāhā to Tatpuruṣa; in the east. Oṃ hoṃ, svāhā to Īśāna; in the center.
Having thus worshipped and offered an oblation of clarified butter ending with "svāhā," the sprinkling (abhighāra) is performed.
Then follows the connection.
Oṃ hāṃ hiṃ, svāhā to Sadyojāta and Vāmadeva. [Offerings to] the west and the north.
Oṃ hiṃ hūṃ, svāhā to Vādeva and Aghora. [The offering] to the north and the south.
Oṃ hūṃ heṃ, svāhā to Aghora and Tatpuruṣa. [Offer] to the south-east.
Oṃ heṃ hoṃ, svāhā to Tatpuruṣa and Īśāna! A stream of ghee [is poured] from the east into the center.

Likewise, for the purpose of unifying with that face: *Oṃ hāṃ hiṃ hūṃ heṃ hoṃ, svāhā to Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa, and Īśāna.* Then, for the sake of bestowing the faces, [one should recite] from the center of the *ṅāva* (the syllable *ṅa*) while pouring a stream of clarified butter, starting from the southeast (*āgneya*) and ending at the northeast (*vāgvīśa*). From the southwest (*asura*) to the northeast (*vāgvīśa*).
Likewise, there is the inclusion of all faces within the face that is desired.
The full verse begins with “nivasita-kanavīra,” and so forth.
Aiṃ (5) Rāṃ Rīṃ Rūṃ: [I meditate upon] the red-colored Bhairava, three-eyed and fiery, possessing seven tongues;
seated there is Siddhilakṣmī, holding in her four hands a spear, a sacrificial ladle (*śruva*), and so forth;
with one face, she stands upon a corpse; O Unborn One, having kindled the blazing fire, contemplate the dawn.
I come as the bringer of peace, the lord who dwells in the ten directions, Agni, the god.

Then the Vedic oblations (*vedāhuti*): *oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe svāhā*. [Accompanied by] the renunciation (*tyāga*). Likewise: *oṃ hrāṃ pṛthivyai svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ agnaye svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ prajāpataye svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ devebhyaḥ svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ ṛṣibhyaḥ svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ chandobhyaḥ svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ śraddhāyai svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ medhāyai svāhā*; *oṃ hrāṃ sadasaspataye svāhā*.
Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to Sadasaspati! Oṃ hrāṃ, svāhā to Antaka!
Oṃ hrāṃ siddheśvarāya svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ antarikṣāya svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ vāyave svāhā || Oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe svāhā, and so forth. (9)

Oṃ hrāṃ śivāya svāhā | Oṃ hrāṃ dive svāhā | Oṃ hrāṃ sūryāya svāhā | Oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe svāhā, and so forth. (9) Oṃ hrāṃ māyāyai svāhā | Oṃ hrāṃ digbhyaḥ svāhā | Oṃ hrāṃ candramase svāhā | Oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe svāhā, and so forth. (9) Then follows the offering of fifteen oblations: Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā | This is for Agni. Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā | This is for Vāyu. Oṃ svaḥ svāhā | This is for Sūrya.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā! This [is offered] to Prajāpati.

Oṃ vaiśvānara-jātaveda, come here, O red-eyed one, accomplish all rites, svāhā! (3) This is for Agni. The six limbs: Oṃ sahasrārciṣe, svāhā to the heart. [Renunciation] Oṃ svasti pūrṇāya, svāhā to the head. Oṃ uttiṣṭhapuruṣāya, svāhā to the crest-lock. Oṃ dhūmavyāpine, svāhā to the armor. Oṃ saptajihvāya, svāhā to the eyes. Oṃ dhanurdharāya, phaṭ to the weapon. [Renunciation with the mantra.]
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye varada (2) sarvajanaṃ me vaśamānaya svāhā. With this mantra of Gaṇapati, one should offer oblations of clarified butter four times.

Then, with the root mantra, having offered twenty-five oblations of clarified butter (ājyāhuti) for the purpose of unifying the mouths of the fire and the deity, one should contemplate the identity of one's own self, the fire, and the deity.

Having offered oblations eleven times with clarified butter using the root mantra for the purpose of joining the channels (*nāḍī-saṃdhāna*), and having given one oblation each to the deities of the six limbs and the surrounding enclosure (*ṣaḍaṅga-āvaraṇa-devatā*), the worship is performed with the Aghora mantra. Having placed [the offerings] into the *praṇītā* vessel containing the remnants, the *pañcagavya* oblation is performed with the Astra mantra.
Now, regarding the invocation: one should recite the Mālanī-daṇḍaka.
Aiṃ (5). May that Goddess Parāparā, who dwells in the sky and whose nature is space, who has gone to the world of the gods and is gentle, come here into this maṇḍala.
Here, within this fire-mandala, he is indeed present along with his limbs.
One should display the nine mudrās, beginning with the invocation (āvāhana) and ending with the vulva (yoni).

Then, one should worship [the deity] with water for the feet (*pādya*), the guest-offering (*argha*), water for sipping (*ācamanīya*), bathing water (*snāna*), and so forth, as well as with clothing, a sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), sandalwood paste, vermilion (*sindūra*), flowers, incense, and other offerings. [This is done] with the nine-syllable mantra: *aiṃ (5) haṃ (9) saṃ (9)*. [Recite] "O Śrī Saṃvartā! O Āsāpuraṇi! O Pāpā... and so on. Thus ends the fire-worship (*agnipūjā*).
Then follows the preparation of the caru: having taken the grain with the Astra-mantra.

The threshing is performed with the *kavaca* mantra; placing the winnowing basket with the *hṛdaya* mantra; the removal of the chaff with the *astra* mantra; placing [the grain] in a copper vessel; sprinkling it with water while reciting the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) three times; covering it with a cloth while reciting the *śiras* mantra; one should then mutter the *gāyatrī*. The worship consists of the root mantra, the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), the invocation (*āvāhana*), and so forth, ending with the *dhenumudrā*. The sacrificial porridge (*caru*) is divided into three parts: for the deity, for the fire, and for the sacrificer. Thus is the preparation of the *caru*.

Then: the oblation of ghee; the three deities; the Yoginīs; Asitāṅga and others; Brahmāṇī and others (8); Indra and others (10); Prayāga and others (8); Hetuka and others (10); Brahmāṇī and others (8); the one consecrated by Brahmā; the four Vedīs (4); the Guardians of the World of the Kuṇḍaṅo (10); the five offerings; the water-pot; Śiva-Śakti; Indra and others (10).

The Gaṇas, Gurus, Kṣetras, Yoginīs, Yakṣas, Yakṣiṇīs, Śrī Lakṣmī, Nāgas, Mṛtyuñjaya, Āditya, the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila), the water-pot (kalaśa), the jar (kumbha), the five offerings (pañcabali), the three deities (trideva), the Yoginī, the altar (vedī), the pillars (stambha) of Indra and others (10), the seats (pīṭha), the [faces] of Sadyojāta and others (4), the stakes (kīlaka) of Indra and others (8), the four gates (catudvāra), the [four kalās]: Śānti, Vidyā, Nivṛtti, and Pratiṣṭhā, Nandā and others (5), the Krama-maṇḍala, the qualified (saguṇa), the offering (bali), and the pit for the removal of suffering (dukhāpikhā).

The Gaṇa, Gogrāsa, and Kumārī; who is he? The six Yoginīs (6), the six Ḍākinīs (6), the six Dūtīs (6); Ugracaṇḍā, Vagalāmukhī, Triśakti Hanubhairava, Nāśvara, Pañcamī Vārāhī; the West, the North, Kālī, Tripurasundarī; the five-faced (5) Siddheśvara, Deśapātana, Kālāpātana; the outer courtyard of the gate, Thavadeguriyā, the five Duvaṇeyāṅābis; with the root mantra (108).
The speech is filled with oblations of clarified butter.
Aiṁ (5). To Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa; the Lord of the Gods, Agni; Kāla, Rakṣas, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Yakṣendra, the foremost of the Nāgas, the host of planets, the Earth, and the conjunctions of day and night;
to the eight Yoginīs beginning with Jala; to Gaṇapati, Vaṭuka, Kṣetrapāla, and all others—[I offer salutation].
May all beings attain peace; may they grant their desired fruits through this oblation of clarified butter, svāhā!
"O Goddess, mounted upon a *prāṇa*-spirit and seated upon a thousand-petaled lotus"—thus [is the mantra for] the full oblation of clarified butter (*ghṛtāhuti-pūrṇā*).
The descent of clarified butter.
Now, the purification of the oblation vessel: sprinkling with the Astra-mantra; heating with the Kavaca-mantra.

The sweeping with the Astra-mantra; the Svastika-arrangement for the conscious mind; with the five-fold *praṇava* and the nine-syllabled mantra; on each day (*ghāsara*), [it is performed] day after day.

Sesame, rice, unbroken grains (*akṣata*), barley, *dudhari*, ghee, *kasti*, *sākhala*, bark, honey, red cloth, *pugi* fruit (1), *jāmbīra* fruit (1), *bimba* fruit (1), *śrīphala* fruit (1), *nālikera* coconut, and excellent *sādava* (1). Two types of fuel sticks (2). A rosary (*akṣamālā*). A water-vessel (*kyāmakhāniku*) (2). One hundred vessels. The *Gāyatrī* mantra is to be recited ten times (10). The root mantra and the *mālā-mantra* are to be recited five times. Worship with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*).
The sacrificer, holding the oblation vessel, [recites] the formula.
For you two are the protectors and the foundation of the sacrifice; thus, the sacrificial rite shall be free from obstacles.
Here in this world they enjoy pleasures, and in the next world they attain the state of Śiva.
For the sacrificer and all others, there is the arising of auspiciousness in the royal lotus;
it brings about all peace and grants satisfaction to all the gods.
"So be it"; and having accepted [it], I shall perform every rite for pacification.
She is Lakṣmī, the destroyer of all evils and the bestower of the accomplishment of all goals.
Having been saluted by the sacrificer.
Resolution: May there be the fulfillment of this resolution for an unlimited number of oblations to Agni Vaiśvānara.
Aiṃ (5). Since you are the purifying and supreme splendor of Agni, I therefore establish you within my heart-lotus and offer libations to you. Having thus prayed to Agni:
As with the sesame oblation: the three deities, the sacrificial fire, Asitāṅga and the others, and Brahmāṇī and the others.
Brahmāpraṇīta; Caturvedī; Kuṇḍaṅova Lokapāra; Pañcabali.

Kalaśa, Śiva-Śakti, Indra and the other [guardians], Gaṇa, Guru, Kṣetrapāla, Yoginī, Yakṣa-Yakṣiṇī, Śrī-Lakṣmī, Nāga, Mṛtyuñjaya, Āditya, Sthāṇḍila-kalaśa, and Kumbha—having offered oblations to these with their respective mantras and having bowed to them, perform the hymn of praise.

The five *balis*, the three deities, the *yoginīs*, the altar (*vedī*), the pillars, Indra and the others (10)—the *pīṭhas*. Sadyojāta and the others (4)—the *duṭhus*. The *kīlakas*, Indra and the others. The four gates (4): Śānti, Vidyā, Nivṛtti, and Pratiṣṭhā; Nandā and the others. The *Kramamaṇḍala*, the *saguṇa-bali*, the *dukha*, the *pikhā*, the *gaṇa*, the *gogrāsa*, Komārī, Kevo, the six *yoginīs*, the six *ḍākinīs*, the six *dūtīs*, and Ugracaṇḍā.

Vagalāmukhī, Triśakti, Hanubhairava, Nāśvara Pañcamī, Vārāhī, Paścimakālī, Uttarakālī, Tripurasundarī, Pañcavaktra, Siddheśvara, Deśāpātana, Kālāpātana, and Bahirdvārāṅgaṇa—these are the deities of the courtyard. Then, for the inner [courtyard], there are two [deities] to be invoked. (5)
The consecration of the ritual jar.
The root mantra for the *saṃkṣāhuti* is the nine-syllable *mālāmantra*. [Recite it] one hundred and eight times. Place the *uparaphakoviya* above.
Thus, one should perform the final oblation of sesame seeds with the following formula:

Aiṃ (5): Śakra and the other world-protectors, together with the ancestors, the Mothers, the eight Bhairavas, the Rakṣasas, Bhūtas, Piśācas, Vaṭukas, the lords of mountains, Pretas, Nāgas, and Yakṣas.

O Goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, surrounded by a host of deities, stationed upon the sacrificial ground within the mandala, may you grant us constant peace; may [the oblations] be offered with sesame seeds to our satisfaction and with the performance of the full oblation, svāhā!
"Crushing all enemies"—thus [ends] the sesame-oblation; the *caru*-oblation; the portion for Agni.
Then, according to the ritual procedure, the sacrificer should touch the hand of the preceptor within the pavilion.
The sentence.
Oṃ! Having previously well-established the five deities beginning with Nandā, who are well-pleased and bestowers of happiness, I now dismiss them today.
The remnants of the sacrifice, having been honored, have been consumed by you as caru;
may the Lord Śiva be pleased with the divine Caṇḍeśvara.
It constantly brings about peace and nourishment, increases sons and grandsons,
and grants the king victory as well as the fruit of all spiritual accomplishments.
Oṃ: when [the world] is created, it is created in me; when it stands, it stands in me;
when it is emitted, it is emitted in me; when it goes, it goes in me.

Oṃ hrāṃ ślīṃ paśūṃ hūṃ phaṭ, obeisance to the Pāśupata weapon. With this, there is the dismissal [of the deity]. [The dismissal] of the pavilion, the four altars, the eight pillars, the ritual pegs, the fire, the sequential mandala, and ending with the root vessel—this is the dismissal.

The offering of food (naivedya) and other items; worship with the remains of offerings (nirmālya); the pavilion (maṇḍapa), the ritual pegs (kīlaka), and so forth; worshipping with the remains of offerings; the ritual assignments (nyāsa) and so forth; the worship of the heart and other limbs; and the worship with the two [mantras] of the root Pāśupata.
Oṃ hrāṃ cāṃ cīṃ cūṃ ceṃ coṃ caṃ, [the six limbs]. Oṃ hrāṃ cāṃ cīṃ cūṃ cmlvryūṃ, obeisance to the venerable Mahāpāśupata Nirmālyacaṇḍeśvara.
Worship with the root-mantra of Mahāpāśupata; [offering] sandalwood and other substances, incense, lamps, and food offerings; oblations; and recitation.
Hymn of Praise.
The remains of the sacrifice, honored by you, have been consumed;
may the Lord Śiva be pleased with the divine Caṇḍeśvara.
It constantly brings about peace and nourishment, increases one's sons and grandsons,
grants victory to kings, and bestows the fruit of all spiritual accomplishments.

The ritual commitments (*samaya*) and so forth; the food offering (*naivedya*); the dismissal of the remains of the offerings (*nirmālya-visarjana*). One should place these together in their proper locations. One should offer the colored powders, the pavilion (*maṇḍapa*), and other such items.
The impurity-removing bath; the ritual bathing and so forth; [offering] to the venerable Siddhilakṣmīdevī together with her limbs and sub-limbs; incense, lamps, recitation, and hymns of praise.

Offerings are made to the five Sūtrakāna deities and to the Ācāryas and Najoṅāvas. The five-fold bali offering. The three deities. An offering is made with the mantra of the eight syllables of Ādinātha. Having recited the hymn of praise to the eight syllables, the consecration of the parched grain is performed with the root nine-syllable mantra. (108)

You are established. The foundation. For the sake of bowing with the *śruva* ladle. For the completion of the ritual action. Worship of the sword (*khaḍga*). Worship of the sacrificial animal (*paśu*). Satiating the sacrificial animal. The animal sacrifice (*paśuyāga*). *Hiphaya*.
From Māṃśalākā, [the route is] Karaṇa, Ḷnepā (2), Madācakaṃ, Javakhava, Lāhātanapā (2), Śvaṃco, Syāṃco, Luṃgotra, Cetalā, Antā; having gone to Kuṇḍasanīpa.

Head-massaging with meat; bathing with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta); bathing with the weapon-mantra (astramantra) using liquor; the four purificatory rites (catuḥsaṃskāra); washing the arghya-vessel; pouring Ganges water; pouring liquor; camphor; saffron; turmeric; ghee; liquor; pouring.

Place the shadow [image] upon the head. Take hold of the heart; apply red sandalwood paste; perform the *japa* while fixing the gaze; let the ear-banner flutter. Sprinkle the five jewels (*pañcaratna*) with the mantra *aiṃ glūṃ slūṃ plūṃ mlūṃ nlūṃ pādukāṃ*. Offer a garland of flowers. Offer a garland of unbroken rice (*akṣata*). Offer parched grain (*pūya*). Offer three umbrellas (*chatra*). Offer an umbrella made of leaves. Thus, place the shadow [image].

The Fivefold Offering of the Lamps (Pañcadhālāpūjā): To the East: *Ajrara Aiṃ Khphreṃ Pādukāṃ*. To the South: *Rakta Hrīṃ Pādukāṃ*. To the West: *Kṣīla Śrīṃ Pādukāṃ*. To the North: *Gandha Hsphreṃ Pādukāṃ*. In the center of the *ali*: *Cintāmaṇi Samaya Aiṃ (5) Hsauṃ Pādukāṃ*. *Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hraiṃ Hrauṃ Hraḥ*—Worship with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*).

The worship of the head with meat; the fourfold purification (*catuḥsaṃskāra*); the worship of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*); the recitation of the garland-mantra (*mālāmantra*); (10) the retention of the nine-syllable mantra; the invocation and other rites; and the *dhenu* and *yoni* mudrās.

Regarding the reciter for the patron: the statement is that goat meat destroys fever; when combined with *pṛṇuta* (or *pṛṇu*), it cures old age. When combined with milk, peace (*śānti*) arises; through curd, nourishment (*puṣṭi*) is produced.
[The word] "paṃcadharāhlāya" [is] the statement.
A stream of milk in the middle bestows the fruit of destroying obstacles;
a stream of blood in the south, however, bestows the removal of disease.
Milk poured from the western stream bestows the fruit of increased longevity; poured from the northern stream of fragrant water, it bestows the fruit of increased prosperity.
In the flow of the vital breath (prāṇa), the middle hero [should offer] the stream of clarified butter;
when the five streams are established, the sacrificial rites are accomplished.

The meat-oblation (*māṃsāhuti*) is as follows: it consists of the offering of ghee and sesame seeds to the three deities beginning with Agnisad. Then, there is the number of oblations for the root mantra, performed either with the *mālā* mantra or with the nine-syllable mantra—namely one hundred and eight (*108*).

Recite *ḷlā-java-yāja-vasaṃ* six times; recite *ḷlā-kha-vayā-kha-vasaṃ* six times. Recite the two *madācaka* mantras. At the end of one's own [name], recite *cetalā* nine times. Recite *lugvada* nine times. This is the mantra for the head (*śira*). This is the mantra for the limbs (*aṅga*). (10) The nine-syllable [mantra]: (108) Regarding the rosary (*mālā*): Do not recite it while walking. At the tip of the mouth, offer the *alibali* oblation together with ghee; this is the root practice.

The *śruva* ladles are filled with oblations of meat; in the fivefold stream, there are four [ladles] for the *turya*, and *śruva* ladles for the clarified butter (*ghṛta*). They are full in the speech. *Aiṃ*. The door of the directions and its arrangement, together with the *gaṇas* and *vaṭukas*, on the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) or in the mandala, in the field (*kṣetra*), the seat (*pīṭha*), and the secondary seat (*upapīṭha*)—the mandala accompanied by the hosts of *gaṇas* in the *siddhacakra*.

May the Goddess Siddhilakṣmī protect me— she who is satisfied by ghee, the full oblation, the offering of wine, the five nectars, and the like, and who is joined with all the gods and the fire-mouthed [deities].

Regarding the offering of *purodāsa* (sacrificial cake) and other items: *selā*, *ghera*, *jhāmarasa*, *gorasohāna*, cumin (*jīra*), black pepper (*maraca*), cloves (*lavāṅga*), *mustakaśūra*, and nutmeg (*jilaphola*)—this is the procedure for these *purodāsa* offerings.

Indeed, in the streams, there is the *agola* [offering] for the Sage (*Samuni*). Because of the state of being struck by the *lābali* and the *śakra-koṭa*, and because of the state of being submerged in the stream, it is like a powerful arrow. In the *ca-phumaḍhe*, there is the fire-seed (*agni-taṇḍu*). From the five streams of the joy of the obstructors of the time and the city, the throat is opened. By the teacher, the offering is made to the Sage; the libation (*tarpaṇa*) is for the satisfied spirits, the departed, and so forth. The Sage is offered to at the time of the ritual procedure (*cepana*).
Thus is the oblation of meat.

The firm foundation for the sacrificer; an oblation with the nine-syllable mantra. (54) || The blossoming lotus; for the sake of the fourfold state; the nine-syllable mantra with the *śruva* ladle. (54) ||

May the Goddess Siddhilakṣmī protect me—she who is established at the cardinal gates along with the Gaṇas and Vaṭukas upon the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila) or in the mandala; she who resides in the sacred fields (kṣetra), seats (pīṭha), and secondary seats (upapīṭha), accompanied by her retinue within the Gaṇa-mandala and the Siddhacakra; she who is invoked, joined with the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti), accompanied by wine and offerings, and endowed with the five drinks and other requisites; she by whom all the gods are satisfied, and who is united with the Fire-mouthed deity.
For the sake of making the ladles inclined toward oneself at the end of the day.
The *śāntika* oblation: recite the nine-syllable mantra 108 times. Having prepared the sacrificial vessel along with the *uṅga* and fuel sticks, offer them.
Aiṃ (5). May the peace of heaven, the atmosphere, and the earth; the ocean of peaceful jewels; all the gods; the Creator, the wind, fire, and Rudra;
the lords of the forest; the sun, the moon, and Hari; and I myself—may all these grant peace.
And having performed the oblation for those [deities] according to the ritual of one's own guru, [one performs] the peace-oblation and the full oblation with "svāhā."

[Recite] the nine-syllable mantra one hundred and eight times. Having offered the sacrificial ladle (*sruva*) along with the *samidh* fuel sticks, [offer them] into the fire. Aiṃ! May the eight auspicious deities—the god named Mṛtyuñjaya, Hari, Vidhi, Kamalā, Pārvatī, Skanda, the Mothers, Jiṣṇu, Herambanātha, Manasija, and the Lord of the Moon—bestow upon you nourishment, wealth, sons, and strength at all times. Through this sacrifice performed with the *puṣṭi-homa* offering according to the ritual instructions from the mouth of the Guru, may there be fulfillment through *svāhā*.
The worship of the preceptor; having performed the expiatory fire-offering (prāyaścitta-homa).
Oṃ hrāṃ laṃ, svāhā to Sadyojāta, the purifier of transgressions.
Oṃ hrāṃ vaṃ, svāhā to Vāmadeva, the northern face, for the sake of expiation.
Oṃ hrāṃ raṃ, to Aghora, the southern face, for the sake of expiation, svāhā!
Oṃ hrāṃ yaṃ, svāhā to the eastern face, Tatpuruṣa, who is the expiation for transgressions.
Oṃ hrāṃ kṣāṃ, to Īśāna, the upward-facing one, for the purification of transgressions, svāhā!
Thus [ends] the expiatory oblation.
The vow rooted in the fire-oblation is for two years and six months; it is for two years and six months.

Barley, grain, salt, fuel sticks, molasses-rice, the *bimba* fruit and so forth, the mantra for recitation and application, the twenty-seven nine-syllable mantras, the twenty-seven garland mantras, and the twenty-seven command mantras.

One should recite these [mantras] one hundred times: *japalapejā* (1), *jāmbila* (1), *ko* (1), *kimba* (1), *ko* (1), *sādavagvaya* (1), *ko* (1), *vailva* (1), *laṃko* (1), *nālikerasādava* (1), *ko* (1). [Offerings include: curd-rice (*dadhnodana*), *vadali* fruit, *priyaṅgu*, *sumukha*, *śatapuṣpa*, white sesame, black sesame, mustard seeds, the three pungents (*trikaṭu*), the three myrobalans (*triphalā*), *rūpakesala*, lotus filaments (*padmakesara*), sandalwood grains (100), and *guguriguri* (110).
All kinds of herbs; aguru; śrīkhaṇḍa; camphor; musk; bulbs; roots; fruits; cooked food; sugarcane.

One should offer one hundred and eight oblations of *dūrvā* grass, unbroken rice (*akṣata*), and milk. [108] The resolve regarding food (*annasaṃkalpa*). For the maintenance of the ghee lamp, there is the fire-ritual (*agni-saṃskāra*). For the recitation of the *Gāyatrī*, [there are] three [units]. [110] For the *Nepusarasasataya*. Then, having offered the *kheśocaka* twice, one offers with the nine-syllable mantra. With the nine-syllable mantra, there is an oblation of ghee. [10] [Offerings] to Indra and the others, ten [deities]. One should place the ghee-oblation and the maintenance-vessel in the center. Aiṃ (5). Peace: heaven, the intermediate space, and the earth as well.

May Śānti, Annapati, the Viśvedevas, Vidhi, Pavana, Vahni, Rudra, Bṛhaspati, Ravi, Śaśin, and Hari—may all these, including myself, attain peace through this oblation of *svāhā*, offered with full devotion according to the ritual prescribed by one’s own preceptor.

The *Vyāhṛti-homa*: *oṃ bhūḥ svāhā* | *oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā* | *oṃ svaḥ svāhā* | *oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā*. The *Ācārya-āhuti* (oblation for the Preceptor): *oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ ācāryasya mantrasiddhirastu svāhā*. (54) *aiṃ (5) nūnebhyaḥ svāhā*. *aiṃ (5) nūnātiriktaṃ juhomi svāhā*. *aiṃ (5) atiriktaṃ juhomi svāhā*. *aiṃ (5) anājñātaṃ yadājñātaṃ tatsarvaṃ kriyate mama svāhā*.

"To Kuṇḍayā, for the sake of the installation of the fire. Thus ends the offering of the inner oblation (*antarbali*) and the outer oblation (*bahirbalipradāna*). The outer oblation consists of the *pāṭava*, *sapantaka*, *oṅachoya*, and *mālā*. This is the mantra for worship.
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to the Rudras! [East] Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to the Mothers! [South] Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to the Gaṇas! [West] Aiṃ (5) Yakṣebhyaḥ svāhā! [North]

Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to the Planets, Svāhā! [To the northeast. Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to the Asuras, Svāhā! [To the southeast. Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to the Rakṣasas, Svāhā! [To the southwest. Aiṃ (5) to the Nāgas, Svāhā! [To the northwest.]
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to the fields! [In the center. Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to the lunar mansions! [In the northeast.]
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to the Viśvedevas; [in the] southeast. Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to the Kṣetrapālas; in the southwest. Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to Varuṇa; between the blue and the yellow [regions].
Thus concludes the internal offering.

Now, for the outer oblation (*bali*) to Indra and the other [deities]: Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to Indra, Svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to Agni, Svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to Yama, Svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to Nairṛtya, Svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to Varuṇa, Svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to Pavana, Svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to Kubera, Svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to Īśāna, Svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to Brahmā, Svāhā! Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ to Viṣṇu, Svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to Kṣetrapāla! Dātesaviya. Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ, svāhā to Odyānapīṭha! Pūrvva.

Aiṁ (5) Hrāṁ, svāhā to the sacred seat of Jālandhara. [South] Aiṁ (5), svāhā to the sacred seat of Pūrṇagiri. [West] Aiṁ (5) Hrāṁ, svāhā to the sacred seat of Kāmarūpa. [North] The bali offering for the altar (vedi). (4) The bali offering for the world-protectors (lokapāla) and the fire-pit (agnikuṇḍa). (10) The bali offering for all these. The presentation of incense, two lamps, and the bali offering.

The giving of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇādāna*); the recitation (*vācana*); the regional offering (*deśabali*); the dismissal (*visarjana*); the purification through the worship of the retinue (*parivārapūjācchoya*); the proclamation of the *saṃśrava*; and the excellent purifier (*pavitra*).

Now, regarding the *pūrṇā* [offering]: one should offer the oblation at the proper time. The oblation consists of nine syllables. (108) Having poured the clarified butter from the *sruva* ladle into the *ghara*, one should place it in the *svānamāla* vessel; having thus prepared the *sruva* for the offering, one should then perform the pouring.

To the one whose lineage is that of the sacrificer, the husband, and the son; to the one possessing the *śruk* and *śruva* ladles, the *jūṅgava* staff, and the topknot (*nābhicūlin*); to the one with a beautiful face. [The] statement: "O Śrī Saṃvarta! O you of full-blown [lotuses]! O you who possess a thousand lotuses! O you who roar like the dark [clouds of] time! (5) *aiṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ* — with this mantra of the garland, offer *svāhā* and *vauṣaṭ*. Having prostrated, offer water for sipping (*ācamana*), sandalwood paste, and betel leaf. With the *śruva* ladle, [offer] to the husband.

Having turned [the vessel] face down—thus is the *pūrṇā* offering—one should recite the *āsaṃsā* verse. In the case of the bestower of the mandala, one should recite it according to one's own tradition. Now, in the venerable *Śrī-Śrī-Śrī-Siddhāgni-yajña*, one should recite the *āsaṃsā* verse: *Oṃ namaḥ śrīsiddhāśvara-mahābhairavāya*.
For the purpose of praise: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃḥ.
With the *kalaśa* [vessel].
This sacrificial fire has been bowed to and praised by Brahmā and the other gods, as well as by the guardians of the celestial realms;
you alone, O Jambhava, have sought refuge in the primordial god, the conqueror of death, whose eyes are like lotus seeds.
By the world-protectors, Indra and the others.
Indra and the other world-protectors, each presiding over their respective directions and joined with their own mudrās,
dwell upon the earth forever in the forms of deities along with the planets beginning with the Sun.
The constellations, sacrifices, the very sharp ones, the Gaṇas, Gurus, Vaṭukas, and the Mothers reside either on the sacrificial ground or upon the altar.
May Siddhi grant prosperity; may the earth be filled with sacrifices; may there be auspiciousness.
May all those deities who are established in auspicious forms within the various stages of the sacrifice, in every direction and intermediate quarter—

whether situated in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), in the midst of the fire, encompassed by the mandala, or upon the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*)— may they all be gods who grant desired fruits, appearing in the form of satisfaction through mantra.
Forgive the faults committed through the performance of the sacrificial rites when they were devoid of the proper mudrās and mantras.

May Jātavedas protect me—He who is established by me in the fire-pits at the junctions of the day (saṃdhyā) through the fire-mantra and the Praṇava; He whose rites begin with the impregnation (garbhādhāna) and proceed from the heart-mantra onwards, joined with the Śaktis; He who is O, Jā, Pū, and Kā, the altar, the lords of the directions with their hosts, Bhairava, the Rāṣṭra, the Kṣetra, the eight Yoginīs, along with the Kṣetrapāla and the movement of Vaṭuka.
May Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śakra; the blazing Yama, Varuṇa, and the Lord of the Rākṣasas; Vāyu, Lakṣmī, and Ananta along with Durgā and the hosts of planetary deities;
Heramba, the assemblies of Siddhas who remove the fear of misfortune, the Moon, Sun, and Fire-gods;
the Yoginīs and all the gods together with the foremost of deities—may all these gods protect you!

The form of an unbroken circle; the venerable Saṃvartā; the trident; Mahāmāyā; the three deities; the syllable *Ū* as dance; the Brahmāṇī group; the three-fold terror in the center; the sword in the left [hand].
Dark green and red.

Having the luster of the *bandhūka* flower; where, where is the *āśā*? To Mahākāla; Mārkaṇḍeya; that Goddess who...; with full-blown lotuses; the fulfiller of hopes; she who is like the fire of destruction; *tāhāka*; as if of Indra; the illusory coiled one (*māyā-kuṇḍalī*); salutations to you, O God; you are the Supreme.
These are the [mantras] of all the Āmnāyas; [this is] of Siddheśvara.
O Great Goddess, she has one face and three eyes, with the crescent moon as her crest-ornament;
she has four arms, and two of her hands are joined in the añjali gesture.
By the root.
Seated upon the pericarp of a full-blown lotus is the supreme Śrī Siddhilakṣmī,
white as camphor, crystal, and the moon, who removes all bonds and eternally burns away the mire of suffering in the ocean of saṃsāra with unwavering constancy.
May she, whose glorious five lotus-faces and ten arms rest upon a corpse, protect us.
Oṃ, homage to Agni.

I bow to You, who are named *Teja* (the Radiant), the universal forbearance that removes the impurities of worldly existence, the purifier of the three worlds—*Bhūr*, *Bhuvaḥ*, and *Svaḥ*; who pervades all, is praised by the assembly of sages, and is luminous with a trident in hand; who is the inner self within every living being, the subtlest of the subtle, the banner enriched with the most excellent colors, the preceptor of all twice-born ones, and the one with radiant hair.
May the deities of all the sacrificial altars, beginning with Vaiśvānara and the guardians of the directions, be pleased by the meaning of our mantra and grant us boons.

For the purpose of the sacrifice consisting of offerings of fire and flesh for the sake of the accomplishment of the goddess Śrīsiddhilakṣmī—the eldest of the West, the eldest, the great illusionist—and for the goddesses Śrīguhyakālikā and Tripurasundarī, may the Kṣetrapāla of his own station, Brahmāṇī and the others, the Great Bhairava Asitāṅga, together with the Yoginīs such as Jayā from Prayāga and other sites, along with Gaṇa, Vaṭuka, and Hetuka, together with their limbs, their retinues, and the world-protectors such as Indra in the cardinal and intermediate directions, be well-pleased and granters of boons.
May the venerable Siddhāgnibhaṭṭārakas grant the fruits as prescribed in the scriptures.

May there be auspiciousness for the cows, the preceptors, and the Brahmins; may there be success in the mantras of the teachers; may the king be victorious in righteousness; may the subjects be happy; may there be prosperity in the land;
may all sentient beings be happy; and may the rain fall in due season.
May there be peace for bipeds and quadrupeds; may there be prosperity.

May there be the perfection of the sword for our King of Kings, Supreme Lord, Most Venerable Sovereign of the Realm, the illustrious Śrī-Śrī-Sumati-Jayajitāmitra-Malla-deva; may his majesty increase; may there be the perfection of mantras for ourselves and others; may there be auspiciousness for bipeds and quadrupeds; may all sentient beings be happy; and may all rites be fulfilled.
May there be an increase in progeny for the sacrificer and his wives, with their vermilion unshaken.
May there be long life, health, sovereignty, progeny, wealth, prosperity, and the increase of the lineage for the patron, along with his attendants and retinue.
May the virtuous be ever peaceful; may kings, whose rise of sin has been destroyed and who are ever uplifted by righteousness, protect the earth;
and may the clouds rain their offspring [water] at the proper time, bringing joy to the subjects.
May there always be joy for the increase of wealth, and constant delight for kinsmen, friends, and the assembly of relatives.

May there be well-being for all subjects; may you, O Lord of the Earth, protect the world by the path of justice. May there be constant auspiciousness for cows and Brahmins, and may all people be happy.
May the rain-cloud pour forth in due season; may the earth abound with grain;
may this land be free from agitation, and may the Brahmins live without fear.

O sole Lord of all the worlds, whatever has been done out of ignorance or knowledge, whether left undone or performed, whether beautifully or harshly executed—whether it be the ritual of sealing, worship, the sequence of sacrifice, or a hymn of praise—whatever fault exists in each and every sacrifice, and even the oblation that was not offered, [may it be purified]. *Note: The final line of the source text appears to be incomplete or syntactically truncated; the translation above provides the logical resolution based on the context of the preceding verses.*
Everything was indeed complete; the fire-god, with palms joined in reverence, was exceedingly well-pleased.

O Lord, forgive me for my faults—my ignorance of men and kings, my devotion, my fickle nature, and the influence of my entreaties; like a sacrificial rite where the mantra is deficient or excessive, may you, the destroyer of faults, be patient with me.
You are the refuge of all beings, established throughout the moving and the unmoving;
having perceived the movement within all beings, you are the Supreme Goddess.
O Fire-god, whatever has been done there in that city by action, mind, or speech— whether it was performed according to the rules or left undone through a deficiency of words— [all that remains].
O Supreme Goddess, may whatever is deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, deficient in devotion, and likewise deficient in recitation, fire-offerings, and worship, be forgiven.
I am a sinner, one of evil deeds, evil-natured, and born of evil;
protect me, O Goddess of the lords of gods, O Hara who removes all sins!
May this entire ritual procedure for worship, consisting of the offering of perfumes, flowers, incense, and lamps, be completely fulfilled here.
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the *Āsaṃsā-stotra* of the illustrious *Śrīsiddhāgnihoma*.
Blessing; the disciple-offering; the root nine-syllable mantra. (3)

The *brahmāpraṇītā* [rite]: the dismissal of the weapons from the altar (*vedi*). Having loosened the knot of *kuśa* grass on the altar for the *praṇītā* consecration, it is cast away for the purpose of drawing lines.

The letter *ū* is Vāyu; Brahmā is the vermilion (*siṃdūra*). Having offered the oblation, one should apply a tilaka of ashes with the *śruva* ladle. With the mantra "Oṃ caturvā sadhvapahyāṅāva agnikonasakāya," at the end of which is "yajavasvava vāhāsa nugarasa vasogharasataya," the sacrificer (*yajamāna*) offers the entire oblation.

The dismissal of Bali: *Oṃ hrāṃ rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ agnaye svāhā* (three times). Three oblations of clarified butter (*ghṛtāhuti*). One handful of rice and two portions of clarified butter for the cock that encircles the head. Offering of betel-leaf (*tāmbūla*). The sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) is sprinkled three times with water from the *argha* vessel. Having turned one's face toward the path (*adhvamukhaṃ kṛtvā*).
Oṃ hrāṃ! Go, go, O best of gods; O fire, carry my self to where the abode of Brahmā and the gods are located. Go there!
O Lord, the blessing of fire: the bestowal of fire, sandalwood, and flowers with the water from the ritual jar as a benediction.
The garland of worship for the Youthful Lord, which purifies the rite of consecration; may the deity grant blessings! O Mother, you who exist as a single form yet manifoldly;

O Pūrṇeśvarī in the east, O Bhūteśī, O Blessed One comparable to the sky in the north, O Naugeśvarī in the south, O Kuleśvarī of Jñānāga in the west, and O Chāruṇī, the Mistress of the direction in the northeast.
I bow to the auspicious Vāmā, the mother of the universe, O Goddess Darśeśvarī, the bestower of spiritual accomplishments.

The Doctrine of the Sword of One's Own Self. Aiṃ. (5) May Ambā, whose state has been previously described, who is the very essence of the form of consciousness, and who abounds in knowledge and will; likewise Hari, Hara, and Brahmā—the triad of rays;
the fivefold solar and lunar [rays]; and thereafter the fivefold Śrī-yoginīs; and may Kuja protect me eternally—the pure sixfold rays including the Moon and the Sun.

The ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *likāya*. For the dismissal of the weapon-mantra (*astra*), the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), and the water-pot (*kalaśa*). For the water for sipping (*ācamanīya*). The return of the patron (*yajamāna*) and so forth. The sprinkling with the *hanasaka* mantra. The consecration with the water-pot (*kalaśābhiṣeka*). The syllable *Ū*, Vāyu, the *canda*, *śrīkhaṇḍa*, *sīṃdhara*, and *muṅavāyāvatayā gurīyātaya*. O Great Mistress of Heroes (*vīreśvarī*), the Enchantress (*mohinī*), the Enchantress of the Three Worlds (*trailokyamohanī*). [Offerings of] wine, meat, curd, and milk. The five threads (*pañcasūtraka*). For the bath (*snānataya*). The fully blossomed (*utphullā*). That which is Peace (*yā śānti*).
The Aindrī and Cāyī [mantras]: "Obeisance to you, O God Śī. The goddess Rājyadā and Dhanadā—these six lines are to be recited; the Mārakoṣṭā is to be recited.
Aversion; established, firmly grounded; with the manner of the full moon; resembling the full moon.

For the sake of witness: May the garland-wearing Bali accept the offering; may the daughter of Kumāra (Kauśikī) accept the morsel of food for the cows; may Mālakosaka and Tācchodyajuḥ accept [the offerings].
The worship of Kaumāra; the consumption of food and other offerings according to the rules as desired.
The stalks of the lotus.
The Gvāraviya.
Thus ends the procedure for the fourth rite of the established fire.

Now, the procedure for the flow of ashes (bhasmapravāha-vidhi). [The offering] to the preceptor (ācārya) at the *baliviya* [altar]; [the offering] to Naluyikā; [the offering] to Jalasiṣata; [the offering] to Trinetra; [the offering] to Hākuchatra with garlands and flowers. For the preceptor there is the *homayā* (fire sacrifice); for the patron (*yajamāna*) there is the flower-vessel. The formula (*vākya*).
From this day forward, for the sacrificer [named] so-and-so, the sacrificial ashes shall serve the purpose of purifying the river's current.

The water-offering for the Sun; for the sake of the *pāśahoma* in the heat; according to the rule with the mantra; the worship of the *kalaśa*; the oblation of clarified butter (*ghṛtāhuti*); the oblation of sesame seeds (*tilāhuti*); the consecration of the *kalaśa*; the numbered oblations (*saṃkhyāhuti*).
The sword-worship, the animal sacrifice, and the oblation of the head are as before.
The Nalupūjā; the Caṇḍayānyāsa; "Ca" for *astrāya* and so forth; the *āsana*: "O Ādhāraśakti," and so forth.
Meditative absorption.
Oṃ! [I bow to the deity] born from Rudra and Agni, fierce, with the luster of collyrium, terrifying, holding an axe and a trident, formidable, four-faced, and four-armed.
With great flames from the courtyard of his mouth, twelve red eyes,
adorned with a crown of matted hair and a crescent moon, and wearing a serpent as a bracelet;
He wears a serpent as his sacred thread, along with a rosary and a water-pot;
he is seated upon a white lotus, his throne blazing with devotion.
Oṃ cāṃ cīṃ cūṃ to Caṇḍeśvara, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. (3)

Thus, with three *añjali* gestures; having worshipped with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*): "Oṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍeśvara; Oṃ, obeisance to Deva. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth; the *triśūla-mudrā*; incense, lamp, recitation (*japa*), and hymn (*stotra*).
Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍeśvara!
By the command of Śiva, may they offer you food to be licked, pure end-products of digestion, drinks, and so forth, as well as betel, flowers for the ears, ointments, floral remains, and unguents.
"Whatever was done in excess or deficiency through delusion has now been made complete and equal for me.
Having thus informed Caṇḍeśa, and having confessed his transgression, by virtue of that vow—
They say the *liṅga* is in space and the earth is its pedestal;
it is called the *liṅga* because it is the abode of all beings and that into which they dissolve.

Herein: perfumes and so forth; the oblation; (10); the rite for pacification (*śāntika*); the rite for nourishment (*puṣṭika*); the final offering (*pūrṇā*); the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) consisting of the root-mantra (*mūlamantra*).
The benediction for the duration of worldly existence; the dismissal of Bali.
The Consecration with the Vase; Nalūṣa.
Sandalwood and other [unguents], semen, wine, meat, the dismissal of the deities, and the performance of fire offerings (homa) constitute austerity.
Having gone to the river || from today onwards || [this is] the statement ||
Oṃ hrāṃ! Having well established me as the worshiper, may the five deities beginning with Nandā depart today with well-pleased minds; I now perform their dismissal.
O Caṇḍī, you have honored, licked, and rolled about the remains of the offerings;
O Caṇḍeśvarā, be well-pleased and remain with a gracious mind.
One should cause [the disciple] to proceed with the Astra-mantra; having performed the ritual bath and other preliminary rites.

Again, at the site of the sacrifice: the worship of the *śāntika* water-pot (*kalaśa*), the flower-vessel, the *arghya* offering to the Sun, the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and so forth; thus is the worship of the water-pot according to the prescribed rite.

The *bali* offering, the *gaṇa* offering, the *gogrāsa*, the worship of Kumārī, incense, lamps, recitation (*japa*), and hymns (*stotra*). For the *ācārya*, there is the *śāntika-bali*. As before, up until the time of the animal sacrifice (*paśuyāga*), there is the worship of the *ācārya*, the formal dedication of food (*anna-saṃkalpa*), the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) of the patron (*yajamāna*), sandalwood paste and other offerings, the *sagvana* (hymn), the benediction (*āśīrvāda*), the removal of obstacles, and the taking of the sun as witness. With the completion of the full sacrifice (*pūrṇā-yajña*), the ritual is concluded. Thus ends the *Bhasmapravāha*.

Now, regarding the ritual for the annual festival (*varṣavardhana*) on the day of the sacrifice: [the following items are required]: two jars for Śiva and Śakti; one jar for the *tāhāgha*; one jar for the *goḍa*; the offering of the sacrificial oblation (*balipātana*); the feeding of cows (*gogrāsa*); the worship of Kumhara; the *bhujāvana* rite; the *melānabali* offering; the worship with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) for the local deity (*sagvanadeva*); and rice grains (*akṣata*), two fruits, and a dog’s head (*svāna eḍamāḍhe*). All these are for the annual festival. The patron (*yajamāna*) should offer a vessel of flowers to the petitioner. The formula is as follows:
Just as for the purpose of the festival celebrating the King’s birthday, the hoisting of the banner, and the performance of sacrifices.
One should cause the sacrifice to be performed as before.
In accordance with the prescribed rule and mantra, one should perform the worship of the jar (kalaśa) dedicated to Śiva and Śakti.

The worship of the image and the ritual jar (*mūrttikalaśapūjā*). The sequence of the deities, beginning with the invocation (*āvāhana*), followed by incense (*dhūpa*), lamp (*dīpa*), recitation (*japa*), and hymns (*stotra*). The hymn to the deity according to the gems and medicinal herbs (*ratnoṣadhī*). Herein [are included] the perfumes and other offerings (*gandhādi*). Then, at the conclusion of the accomplishment of the meaningful words (*arthapadāsādhanānta*), there is the offering of clarified butter (*ghṛtāhuti*) in full measure with their respective mantras. Next, one should offer oblations of sesame seeds (*tilāhuti*). Having performed the "casting out of all parts" (*sakaleṅa vosyata kṛtvāya*), the "raising of the banner" (*dhvajātvāya*) by means of the triple essence (*tritatvena*). The "falling away of the place" (*deśāpātana*) and the "falling away of time" (*kālāpātanaviya*). The consecration of the ritual jar (*kalaśapratiṣṭhā*). The numerical oblation (*saṃkhyāhuti*).

The dismissal of the anthropomorphic pitcher (mūrttikalaśa) and the banner (dhvaja). For the deity, the five nectars bath (pañcāmṛtasnāna), the bathing in the river (yātavane snāna), and so forth; the decoration of the anthropomorphic pitcher. Worship of the God and Goddess according to one's capacity.

The donor, the patron, the reciter, and the preceptor should recite the *svastivācana* and offer the banner to the God and Goddess. Having circumambulated the God and Goddess three times with the banner, they should place the banner at the end [of the procession]. The formula is: "Today, in the Varāha-kalpa... and so forth. This offering of the banner (*dhvajādāna*) should be given.

With *kuśa* grass, sesame seeds, water, flowers, banners, and *jona* leaves; on this day, during the Vārāha-kalpa, in the [current] month, asterism, and so forth—for the sake of attaining the fruits as prescribed in the ritual of raising the banner for the increase of the years of the illustrious [Name] Devī, the patroness, I offer this banner.
Oṃ! O Bhavānī, Queen of the Gods of gods, Sovereign of the three worlds, four-armed one;
may Maheśvarī be pleased by this offering of a banner according to my capacity.
One should give a white great banner, having fashioned it with five parts of cow-hide,
complete with bells and adorned with a peacock-feather parasol.
By means of this very celestial chariot, situated above all the gods,
he rejoices in the abode of the deities for one thousand years.
One should arrange a multitude of banners according to the dimensions of the temple,
or otherwise, one should offer eight banners in the cardinal and intermediate directions.
For as many thousands of years as there are threads, including the shuttle, in the cloth,
for that many years one is honored in the world of Śiva.
The goddess resides in the messenger; she resides in the banner; she resides in the desire for stability; she resides in the auspicious vessel; she resides in those unbroken grains and two fruits.

In the Svānamāḍha, there is the *digpūjā* (worship of the directions). Offerings are made with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) for each respective deity. Recite the hymns (*stotra*) along with the verses (*śloka*). Perform one hundred and eight recitations (*japa*) of the root mantra. The consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*) follows the previous sequence, including the offering of meat (*māṃsāhuti*). There is the consecration of the patron (*yajamāna-pratiṣṭhā*), the worship of the preceptor (*ācārya-pūjā*), the rites for peace (*śāntika*) and prosperity (*pauṣṭika*), and the offering of barley, grain, and other materials. Thus concludes the ritual fire sacrifice (*vidhi-homa*). Then follow the vigil of the young girls (*kumāri-jāga*) and the purification of the patron (*nirmmacchana*).

The consecration of the jar with Śiva-Śakti; sandalwood paste and other offerings; the benediction with all qualities; the presence of witnesses; the waving of lights (ārati) for the Lord himself along with his attendants in the courtyard; and the offering to the dog. [Thus ends the ritual procedure for the lowering of the banner and the celebration of the annual festival.]
Īśāna. Herein is Mṛtyuñjaya: Oṃ juṃ saḥ, obeisance to Sadāśiva, the Great Bhairava, the Lord of Immortality.

O Agni! Navātma-mantra: (5) Haṃ (9) to the venerable Navātma-gurumaṇḍala-bhaṭṭārikā, the consort of Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes, who is the power of bliss (ānanda-śakti), [I offer] the sandals (pādukā). Saṃ (9).
Nairṛtya: The mantra of Dakṣiṇāmūrti.
Oṃ Hrīṃ! Obeisance to you, Dakṣiṇāmūrti, who dwells at the foot of the banyan tree, whose limbs are entirely absorbed in meditation; obeisance to Rudra, to Śambhu, Hrīṃ Oṃ!
Vāyavya || The Cintāmaṇi mantra || Ṛkṣmyrūṃ ||
East: Pāśupata-weapon mantra: Oṃ ślīṃ paśuṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
South: The Piṅgalā Astra mantra: Ḷ Kṣīṃ, to the Piṅgalā Astra of form, phaṭ!
Uttara: The Aghorāstra Mantra: Hrīṃ sphura (2) prasphura (2) ghora ghora-tara-tanu rūpa-caṭa (2) pracaṭa (2) kaha (2) vama (2) vaddhā (2) ghātaya (2) hūṃ phaṭ.
West: The Śivāstra Mantra: Oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ oṃ namaḥ śivāya astrāya phaṭ.
One should recite the mantra of Mṛtyujit in the northeast, the Navātman in the southeast,
Dakṣiṇāmūrti in the southwest, and Cintāmaṇi in the northwest.
One should recite the Pāśupata weapon-mantra in the east, the Piṅgala weapon-mantra in the south,
the Aghora weapon-mantra in the north, and likewise the Śiva weapon-mantra in the west.
One should cast [the oblation]. Ritual sipping (upasparśana). Again, the consecration with pure fire. The ritual placement (nyāsa): *rāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*, and so forth.

The fourfold ritual action (*catuḥsaṃskāra*): inspection with the root mantra; sprinkling with the weapon mantra; striking with that [same weapon mantra]; veiling with the armor mantra; and sprinkling with the Fire-Gāyatrī: "We know Vaiśvānara, we meditate upon Jātavedas; may Agni inspire us. Having joined the consciousness (*caitanya*) into the fire with the syllable *Raṃ*, one should contemplate the unification of the gastric, the lunar, and the earthly fires as one. Having consecrated it with the *praṇava* (Oṃ), one should transform it into nectar using the *vam* syllable and the cow-seal (*dhenumudrā*).

Having protected [the fire] with the Astra-mantra and enveloped it with the Kavaca-mantra; having worshipped it with perfumes and other offerings while reciting "Oṃ Raṃ Vahnyai Namaḥ"; and having taken up the fire with the nine-syllable mantra; [one performs] the threefold rotation of the fuel with "Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ Indhana Bhramaṇa Tṛdhāvṛtti"; and the installation of the fire with "Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ Aiṃ Hskhphreṃ Agnisthāpanaṃ."

Hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ Śrī Saṃvartā. With the mantra *ūtphulāṃ*, [worship] the speech. Perform the worship with the six limbs, beginning with the heart: Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Gneṃ Hūṃ Śruṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā.
The word *svasti* is used in the speech regarding the *paḍapa*.
May she who is ever free from obstacles grant well-being; may Mārtaṇḍa likewise grant well-being;
may all the Yoginīs grant well-being; and may the sacred seats (pīṭhas) of one’s own field grant well-being.
In the east, south, west, north, above, and likewise below—
may the sixfold *svasti* (well-being) abide, with its deities both concealed and manifest.
Bhairava and Bhairavī, together with their limbs, [grant] well-being; svah, svah, svah, the wheels!
May their own mantras, their own mudrās, their weapons, and their retinues— abiding in the planets, constellations, and zodiac signs— grant well-being and prosperity to all.
May there be well-being for the heroes, the immeasurable ones, the yoginīs, and the leaders of the hosts;
may there be well-being for the God of gods and the King of Mantras, without interruption.
May the deities of the family fire be satisfied by the offerings and grant well-being;
may the king always grant well-being to his subjects, and may there be well-being for the sacrificer at all times.

Now, regarding the five-fold bali offering: the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), the protective cord (khavalāsa), the bali offering within the sacrificial pit, the student (vaṭu), the field (kṣetra), the Yoginīs, Cāmuṇḍā, the Gaṇas, the recitation (japa), the hymn of praise (stotra), the three deities (trideva), the worship of the seat (āsanapūjana), the bali, and the mudrās.
Aiṁ (5), the heart mantra:
pādukāṃ to the monkey-faced one.
The strewing with kuśa grass.

Then, when the purpose is to perform the ritual means (*sādhana*): on the right side, there is a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*), a flower-vessel, three blades for cutting the *pavitra*, two *pavitra* strainers, the *prokṣaṇī* sprinkling-vessel, the clarified butter vessel (*ājyasthālī*), the oblation-pot (*carusthālī*), saline soil (*udūṣara*), a broom of *muñja* grass, *kuśa* grass, the *upayamana* (supporting) *kuśa* grass, fuel-sticks (*samidh*), the *śruk* and *śruva* ladles, clarified butter, sesame seeds, rice, a winnowing-basket (*sūrpa*), a black antelope skin (*kṛṣṇājina*), and pairs of items for the commencement. [The purification] is performed with the *Hṛdaya-mantra*. The cutting of the *pavitra* is done with the *Astra-mantra*. The binding of the *pavitra* is done with the *Hṛdaya-mantra*.

Having washed the *prokṣaṇī* vessel with the *astra-mantra*, one should perform the satiation with the *hṛdaya-mantra*. Cleansing is performed with the *astra-mantra*, and filling [the vessel] with water with the *hṛdaya-mantra*. Stirring with the *śiras-mantra* and the *pavitra* grass, one should offer three oblations of water toward the north with the *netra-mantra*. One should sprinkle all the ritual materials and oneself with the *mūla-mantra*. Then, having placed the *prokṣaṇī* between the fire and the *praṇītā* vessel, [one prepares] the *śruk* ladle.

Purification with the *śruva* ladle; sprinkling with the *astra-mantra*; heating with the root (*mūla*) mantra; sprinkling again with the *astra-mantra*; purification with the *tritatva*; preparation of the clarified butter (*ghṛta*); sprinkling the vessel for the clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*) and the sacrificial porridge (*caru*) with clarified butter using the *astra-mantra*; installation with the *kavaca-mantra*. Aiṃ (5) [with] the heart-mantra, [one offers] the oblation of clarified butter. Regarding the preparation of the sacrificial porridge (*caru*) for the establishment sacrifice (*pratiṣṭhāmakha*): Aiṃ (5) [with] the *astra-mantra*, [one offers] to Puṣpākai; Aiṃ (5) [with] the *kavaca-mantra*, to Sūrya; Aiṃ (5) [with] the heart-mantra, to Hāya.

Aiṁ (5). Worship with sandalwood and other offerings. Aiṁ (5). Sprinkle the head-mantra with ghee and *caru* oblation. Recite the heart-mantra over the *kuśa* grass and the water vessel. Recite the weapon-mantra (*astra*) for the purification of the mouth. Recite the weapon-mantra four times for the sprinkling.
With the armor mantra, the heat mantra, the ghee mantra, and the *caru* mantra, [one should perform the rite] five times with the *aiṃ* mantra and the weapon mantra (*astramantra*).
Having placed the *śruva* ladle and the vessel of clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*) on his right side.

Aiṁ (5): Purification by sprinkling with *kuśa* grass using the Weapon mantra. Aiṁ (5): Sprinkling toward oneself using the Heart mantra. Sprinkling [the site]. Sprinkling upon oneself using the Armor mantra.

The mantra for beholding the clarified butter (ājya): Aiṃ (5) O clarified butter, destroyer of sin! Having seen me, O auspicious clarified butter that removes obstacles! Clarified butter is not to be taken away by even the gods;
everything is established in clarified butter.

The *prokṣaṇī* waters are treated as before. Stirring with the *pavitra* [strainer] using the head-mantra; three upward splashes using the eye-mantra; sprinkling with the *tritatva* mantra; and placing the remaining water into the *praṇītā* vessel. Then, for the sake of the sacrificial ladles (*śruva*) and the clarified butter pots (*ājyasthālī*), [one performs the purification] upon the *kuśa* grass seats. With the *kāsvatuna* mantra, together with the *śruva* ladle. (3) (5) With the *hṛdayamantra*.

The worship of the *śruva* ladle, the *ājyasthālī* vessel, and the *śruk* ladle: *Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ Khphreṃ Siddheśvaramahābhairava Śrīpādukāṃ.* [Worship of] the *śruk* ladle. *Śrīsiddhilakṣmī Śrīpādukāṃ.* [Worship of] the *śruva* ladle. *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ* with the five *praṇavas*. [This is] the worship of the *ājyasthālī* vessel. [Perform] the six-limbed [worship], the *yonimudrā*, the veiling (*avaguṇṭhana*), the armor (*kavaca*), and the protection with the weapon-mantra (*rakṣāstra*). With the offering of abandonment (*tyāga*), perform the oblation of clarified butter (*ghṛtāhuti*): *Aiṃ (5) Sadyojātāya Svāhā.*
Aiṃ (5) Vāmadevāya svāhā. Aiṃ (5) Aghorāya svāhā. Aiṃ (5) Tatpuruṣāya svāhā. Aiṃ (5) Īśānāya svāhā. Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Ātmatattvāya svāhā. Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Vidyātattvāya svāhā. Aiṃ (5) Hrūṃ Śivatattvāya svāhā.
The rite of cremation by fire.
Aiṃ (5), with the heart-mantra, for the rite of conception, svāhā!
Aiṁ (5) svāhā to the rite for the birth of a male child. Aiṁ (5) svāhā to the parting of the hair on the head with the mantra.

Aiṃ (5) with the *śikhā* [mantra], for the rite of birth (*jātakarman*), svāhā! Aiṃ (5) with the *kavaca* [mantra], for the rite of emerging [from the womb] (*niḥkramana*), svāhā! Aiṃ (5) hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ khphreṃ; to the one named Agnisvarūpa, the illustrious Siddhāgni—[to him] for the rite of naming (*nāmakaraṇa*), svāhā! to the illustrious Siddhāgni, svāhā!

Aiṃ (5) To the upward-facing mouth, for the consumption of fruit, svāhā! Aiṃ (5) To the upper and lower-facing mouths, for the consumption of food, svāhā! Aiṃ (5) To the eastern-facing mouth, for the tonsure ceremony, svāhā! Aiṃ (5) To the eastern-facing mouth, for the piercing of the ears, svāhā! Aiṃ (5) To the southern-facing mouth, for the making of the *vaṭu* (initiation), svāhā! Aiṃ (5) To the northern-facing mouth, for the release from vows (*vratamokṣaṇa*), svāhā! Aiṃ (5) To the western-facing mouth, for marriage, svāhā!

Aiṃ (5) Svāhā to the Fourth Face, which is both supreme and non-supreme. The installation of the fire should be performed. The fire is filled with the nine-syllable [mantra] and the five-faced [deity]. Aiṃ (5) Hā to the Embryo. Thus is the tenfold ritual of the fire.
O Agni, dismissal of the parents. Aiṁ (5) Hrāṁ, salutation to Vāgīśvara. Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ, salutation to Vāgīśvarī. [This is] the worship. Offer an oblation with these.
Meditation on the fire.
One should visualize the Fire-god seated upon a ram, pervading all, holding a spear in his hand,
situated within the sacrificial pit with his face turned toward the north, blazing like a second sun.
The tongue shall be of seven colors; the *śruva* ladle and other implements are in the right hand, while the wife, Svāhā, stands in the left during rites for peace (*śāntikarma*).
Oṃ, homage to the flower of meditation upon Agni.

Meditation: Bhairava, Aśitāṅga and the others, surrounded by the eight fields such as Karavīra and the eight cremation grounds, encircled by the six Ḍākinīs, the six Yoginīs, and the [eight] Brahmāṇīs, and the fire of the Siddhas.
Having offered eighteen or sixteen fuel-sticks as oblations, having offered one with the *praṇava*, and having placed one in the *praṇītā* water-vessel.
Having asked Brahmā with the three-fold effort and the *kuśa* grasses: "Oṃ, obeisance to Prajāpati, svāhā!"—this is the offering into the *prokṣaṇī* vessel: "This [is for] Manu Prajāpati."
In the initiation ceremony (upanayana), the binding of kusha grass around the left hand.
Oṃ Hrīṃ! Homage to Indra, who holds a thunderbolt in his hand, the lord of the gods, whose seat is Airāvata.

Then, having mentally contemplated Prajāpati as the presiding deity, [one performs] the worship of the Praṇītā vessel, the Vedis, and the World-Guardians (Lokapālas), followed by the worship of the deities during the subsequent fire-offerings (homas): Oṃ, obeisance to Brahmā. Oṃ, obeisance to the Praṇītā. Oṃ, obeisance to Oḍiyāna. Oṃ, obeisance to Jālandhara. Oṃ, obeisance to Pūrṇagiri. Oṃ, obeisance to Kāmarūpa. Oṃ, obeisance to Indra. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni. Oṃ, obeisance to Yamā. Oṃ, obeisance to Nairṛtya. Oṃ, obeisance to Varuṇa.

Oṃ, obeisance to Vāyu. Oṃ, obeisance to Kubera. Oṃ, obeisance to Īśāna. Oṃ, obeisance to the Upper Direction. Oṃ, obeisance to the Lower Direction. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Tripaṃca. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Catuḥpaṃca. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Devāga. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to the Cardinal Directions. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to the Intermediate Directions. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Svarga. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Martya. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Pātāla. Oṃ Hrāṃ, obeisance to Gaurī.
